title: Travis Kelce moves past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in TD catches by a tight end
summary: For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone.
full_text: For the first time since Sept. 27, Travis Kelce has gotten back into the end zone. And Kelce has also secured another milestone in his storied career. Kelce capped the Chiefs’ first drive with an 8-yard touchdown catch, giving Kansas City an early 7-0 lead over Arizona. The score also moved Kelce past Rob Gronkowski for No. 3 all-time in touchdowns by a tight end. Only Antonio Gates and Tony Gonzalez are ahead of Kelce on the list. The possession lasted 11 plays and went 72 yards to the end zone, taking 5:14 off the clock. Patrick Mahomes was 4-of-5 on the drive for 36 yards, converting a pair of third downs. He hit Rashee Rice for a 15-yard gain on one third down and the touchdown to Kelce was the second. Rookie Emmett Johnson is once again off to a strong start, taking six carries for 36 yards while also catching a screen for an 8-yard gain.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cooper DeJean: DK Metcalf "just missed" poking me in the eye
summary: Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close.
full_text: Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean says Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf didn’t poke him in the eye on Sunday, but came pretty close. “ Just missed ,” DeJean said, via the Philadelphia Inquirer . Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game after multiple incidents and two personal foul penalties, but DeJean said nothing that happened during the game could explain what had Metcalf so upset. “We were just competing,” DeJean said. “Things like that happen in football. It wasn’t anything crazy, and no one was really saying anything. It was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off me, things like that, and then it obviously carried over to whatever that was when he got thrown out.” Metcalf had just one catch for two yards before he was kicked out, and DeJean suspects that Metcalf is mostly upset with his own production. “He wasn’t getting the ball a whole lot during that game," DeJean said. "Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me.”
author: Michael David Smith

title: Malik Nabers on sideline moment: I was just trying to watch the game
summary: Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers.
full_text: Late in Sunday's win over the Jaguars, video of the Giants' sideline showed quarterback Jameis Winston trying to restrain receiver Malik Nabers. Nabers eventually worked his way past Winston and moved toward the edge of the field. So what was happening? "I vaguely remember it," Nabers told reporters, via Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic . "But, I mean, I just remember me saying, 'I'm good. I'm good. I wanna get back to watching the defense play.' And that was really all, I think. Everything was going on, I was just telling the offense, 'Let's go, let's go,' I think. Jameis kind of [was] trying to calm me down, but I was fine. So I was just telling him, 'I'm good. I'm good. I just wanna watch the game ." The fact that Nabers navigated past Winston and got into position to watch the game seems to confirm Nabers's explanation. He just wanted to watch the game. The problem is that Winston's reaction to Nabers's initial movement created the impression that something else was happening. No quotes on the situation have emerged from Winston. It would be interesting to know why he thought Nabers needed to be restrained at a time when restraint ultimately wasn't necessary. Either way, the moment went viral — and more people will see that video and draw possibly inaccurate conclusions than will hear Nabers's explanation.
author: Mike Florio

title: Officials deny Jaguars TD on sensational catch by Parker Washington
summary: Washington appeared to make a superb touchdown catch, but the officials and the replay office ruled it incomplete.
full_text: ' Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington made a leaping grab in the back of the end zone, got his feet down in bounds, and controlled the ball as he fell to the ground in the fourth quarter today against the Giants. Or so it appeared. The officials ruled it incomplete, and after the Jaguars challenged, the replay review ruled that Washington did not make the catch. The ruling of incomplete pass stood, and the Jaguars settled for a field goal that cut the Giants' lead to 20-9. It was a highly questionable call, questioned even by former NFL referee Gene Steratore, the CBS rules analyst who said on the game broadcast that he thought it was a catch. Washington is having a sensational season, and that was perhaps his greatest play yet — or at least it would have been, if it had been ruled a catch. The Giants previously got a touchdown on a Jameis Winston quarterback sneak, even though replays appeared to show Winston's helmet hit the ground before the ball crossed the goal line. Now there have been two controversial touchdown calls, both in the Giants' favor.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Evans TD and Parker Washington non-TD raise more questions about NFL catch rules
summary: Two big plays on Sunday renewed questions about what is and is not a catch in the NFL.
full_text: ' Few topics in the NFL cause more heated debates than what is or is not a catch. Two more big debates happened on Sunday, with two touchdown catch rulings that both appeared to be wrong on the field, and not corrected by replay. On Sunday afternoon, Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington caught a pass and had control with both feet down in the end zone, but it was ruled incomplete. On Sunday night, 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans didn't have full control with both feet down as he went out of bounds in the end zone, but it was ruled a touchdown. In the Jaguars game, former NFL referee Gene Steratore broke the play down and explained that while there was some minor movement of the football as Washington went to the ground, Washington had the ball with both feet down and never lost control. "When Parker Washington, after the bobble, possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he's falling," Steratore said on the CBS broadcast. "Then I had the left foot touch. I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think he lost possession of the football. I have possession, right foot down, tap with the left foot, yes, the ball moves a little, but the right hand, in my opinion, continues to keep that secure enough, that I would say in my opinion he's still controlling that football. I think it's a touchdown." In the 49ers game, former NFL referee Terry McAulay said Evans was juggling the ball while running across the end zone and didn't have control of it until his final step, with only one foot down in bounds. "I don't see him get final control until he's got one foot down," McAulay said. "The ball rolls around on his wrist. I don't see it pinned to his body. When he gets control, there's only one foot down. I think they should've reviewed it and reversed it to incomplete." Even if the NFL wants to insist that its officials got both calls right on the field, and that the replay review process was correct to uphold those calls, the league still needs to acknowledge that it has a problem on its hands if the catch rule is so confusing that even former referees who now work as on-air officiating analysts aren't seeing what the on-field officials and the replay officials are seeing.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jesse Minter: The only thing you can do is get up off the mat again
summary: It has been a rough stretch for first-year head coach Jesse Minter and the Ravens, who have now lost six games in a row after falling to the Panthers on Sunday.
full_text: '' It has been a rough stretch for first-year head coach Jesse Minter and the Ravens, who have now lost six games in a row after falling to the Panthers on Sunday. After a back-and-forth game that ended up in a loss, Minter said that every loss is tough. “The last two weeks, our team has battled their butts off and put the team in position to have a chance to win. We haven’t gotten it done,” Minter said, via transcript from the team. “And so again, you’re going to look back. We’re going to come in tomorrow. We’re going to look at all these different plays and say, '[It] could’ve been this play, or it could’ve been that play. Can’t do that.' It’s a one-play-at-a-time game, and we didn’t get it done.” “The only thing you can do is get up off the mat again,” Minter added. “[It was] two really tough, gut-wrenching type of games, but again, it’s an opportunity. Every day’s an opportunity to bounce back. Every day is an opportunity to improve. We’ll go right back to work.” Now a few games behind in the AFC North, the Ravens will be on the road again to face the Texans in Week 12 before a Week 13 bye.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers come back to beat Ravens in a wild game in Carolina
summary: In a crazy, back-and-forth game, the Panthers ended up on top, 35-33.
full_text: The Panthers and Ravens played a highly entertaining game today at Carolina, going back and forth until the closing seconds, when an ill-advised Jacoby Brissett interception ended the Ravens' hopes. Brissett played well for most of the game, but when he attempted to make a play in the final 30 seconds, he scrambled around before heaving the ball deep downfield, where it was intercepted by the Panthers, sealing a 35-33 win. Other than that interception, Brissett was solid, completing 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown. Derrick Henry and Justice Hill both had rushing touchdowns for the Ravens, but Henry went into the locker room late in the game for a concussion evaluation. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young shook off some early struggles and finished 22 of 30 for 254 yards, with two touchdowns and an interception. Chuba Hubbard had an excellent game for the Panthers, running 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns. With the win, the Panthers improve to 5-5 and remain atop the NFC South. The Ravens fall to 4-7.
author: Michael David Smith

title: DK Metcalf should have been ejected earlier than he was, for contact with official
summary: There's another factor that could fuel a Metcalf suspension.
full_text: As it turns out, Steelers receiver DK Metcalf should have been ejected before he was ejected. It happened in connection with the first of two personal fouls that prompted his disqualification. After being separated from Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean following a play that began with 12:52 to play in the third quarter, umpire Mark Pellis pushed Metcalf away from the fray. Pellis had his hand on Metcalf's chest. Metcalf can be seen slapping Pellis's forearm away. From Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1(e): "Under no circumstance is a player allowed to shove, push, or strike an official in an offensive, disrespectful, or unsportsmanlike manner. The player shall be disqualified from the game, and any such action must be reported to the Commissioner, who may impose further discipline." Metcalf should have been disqualified then and there, because "shall" means "must." It wasn't part of a broader fray, with Metcalf not knowing whose arm he was striking. It was Metcalf and Pellis, and no one else. Later in the quarter, Metcalf drew a second personal foul and was ejected. As the league considers the next step for potential discipline of Metcalf, his contact with Pellis should be a factor in determining whether to suspend Metcalf for Friday's game against the Broncos — if not longer.
author: Mike Florio

title: Emeka Egbuka has taken a big step back in Year 2
summary: Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka had just two catches for 18 yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
full_text: Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka had just two catches for 18 yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions. During his breakout rookie season last year, that would have been a surprisingly bad game for Egbuka. This year, there's nothing surprising when Egbuka has a bad game. Last year Egubka played all 17 games and finished the season with 63 catches for 938 yards and two touchdowns. This year Egbuka has missed two games with a foot injury, and 10 games into the season he has just 33 catches for 296 yards and two touchdowns. Egbuka's average has dropped from 14.9 yards per catch last season to 9.0 yards per catch this season. Last year Egbuka had 20 catches of 20 or more yards, and three catches of 40 or more yards. This year Egbuka has three catches of 20 or more yards, and no catches of 40 or more yards. Last year Egbuka had 34 receiving first downs. This year Egbuka has 14 receiving first downs. It's been more than a full year since Egbuka gained even 65 receiving yards in a season. The last time he topped 65 yards was Week 10 of 2025. Of course, Egbuka is far from the only part of the Bucs' passing game that has severely regressed this season. Baker Mayfield is having his worst year, and undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels started three games when Mayfield was out. It's fair to question whether the fault lies with Egbuka, or with the quarterbacks throwing to Egbuka. Either way, after being one of the NFL's best rookies in 2025, Egbuka has been one of the NFL's biggest Year 2 disappointments in 2026.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Giants earn their most impressive win of the season with upset of Jaguars
summary: The NFC East leaders surprised the AFC South leaders today.
full_text: The NFC East-leading Giants made a statement today against the Jaguars. In a game that few expected the Giants to win, New York took a 10-3 first quarter lead and never relinquished it, turning in an impressive performance and beating the Jaguars 23-18. The Giants were aided by two highly controversial touchdown calls: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston got a fourth-and-goal tush push touchdown despite his helmet appearing to be down before the ball crossed the goal line, and Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington was denied a touchdown catch despite appearing to have possession with his feet down in bounds. But the two controversies shouldn't overshadow that this Giants team is far better than anyone expected. They're 6-3-1 and in total control of the NFC East, and today they earned their most impressive win yet. The Jaguars fall to 7-3, and despite the loss they're still the overwhelming favorites to win the AFC South. This loss will hurt in the AFC playoff seeding, however, as they're now long shots to earn the No. 1 seed. Both the Giants and the Jaguars look like playoff teams. This was a hard-fought game between two opponents that expect to still be playing well into January. And maybe February.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean Payton honored Tom Jackson's family with a game ball after win over Raiders
summary: The entire NFL world was saddened to learn about the passing of Denver and ESPN legend Tom Jackson over the weekend.
full_text: ' The entire NFL world was saddened to learn about the passing of Denver and ESPN legend Tom Jackson over the weekend. After the Broncos defeated the division-rival Raiders on Sunday, head coach Sean Payton presented Jackson's family with a game ball. “I think I’d be remiss if we didn’t start by honoring Tom Jackson tonight,” Payton said in his postgame press conference, via transcript from the team. “A lot of these players — as a coach, you’re always teaching. A lot of these players certainly won’t remember him as a player, maybe not as an ESPN media member. He got a game ball tonight, his family, as part of the rich [team] history. Obviously, [a] tough loss for everyone.” A member of the Broncos Ring of Fame, Jackson played 191 games across 14 years for the franchise from 1973-1986.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Quinnen Williams: We executed better on defense, but we still gave up 30 points
summary: The Cowboys defense was under the microscope all week due to the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and hand them to assistant Mike Pettine, but defensive tackle Quinnen Williams pointed to something else playing a leading role in the unit's performance on Sunday.
full_text: The Cowboys defense was under the microscope all week due to the decision to strip defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties and hand them to assistant Mike Pettine, but defensive tackle Quinnen Williams pointed to something else playing a leading role in the unit's performance on Sunday. Dallas did not allow a touchdown in the first half while building a 27-9 lead over the Titans and ended the day as 51-30 winners. Williams, who had two sacks and a forced fumble in the win, "no matter who called the call, no matter what call, the players on the field had to execute" and that he was "super proud" of the way that the group responded on Sunday. Williams's pride in the performance did not obscure the fact that it was far from perfect. "We still gave up 30 points ," Williams said, via the team's website. "So we definitely got to go watch the film and learn from it and get better, because we know the defense we can be and we have a long way to go, and we have to take steps forward to get there." The Titans are a one-win team, which makes them exactly the kind of opponent you want to see when trying to right the ship. The Cowboys have another losing team on deck with the Eagles coming to town on Thanksgiving and they'll have to keep pushing to improve to make Sunday's win a sign of things to come rather than a momentary blip for an underwhelming unit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Tomlin: DK Metcalf lacks "professional maturity"
summary: Steelers need to send a message to Metcalf after Sunday's ejection.
full_text: Current Steelers coach Mike McCarthy has some decisions to make regarding receiver DK Metcalf. His former coach likely wouldn't hesitate to send an unmistakable message. Mike Tomlin made his thoughts on Metcalf clear during halftime of Sunday night's NBC game, after Metcalf was ejected from the Week 11 loss to the Eagles. "It's one thing to struggle in terms of production, and he certainly is struggling," Tomlin said. "But it's another thing to complicate it by showing lack of professional maturity. And that's what he showed. He was frustrated and so he did some things that are outside the lines of the game, and certainly he paid the consequence today, but he's probably gonna continue to pay the consequence, whether it's from New York or whether it's in-house." A league-imposed suspension is possible, and last year's two-game suspension for an altercation with a fan in Detroit could be a factor in such an outcome. The team could choose to suspend Metcalf, or to make him a healthy scratch for Friday's game against the Broncos. The fact that Metcalf's production has lagged this year makes it much easier to take a stand. And that's how it always works. There's a sliding scale, where in-house consequences become more likely the less impactful the player is. Currently, Metcalf isn't impactful. As the Steelers find themselves at 6-4 and staring at games against the Broncos, Texans, and Jaguars, taking an aggressive stance as to Metcalf could give the team a much-needed kick in the ass. If, of course, the locker room will react positively to the team suspending or benching Metcalf. His " good friend " Aaron Rodgers will need to be on board. Even though Rodgers isn't the player he once was, he has tremendous influence over his teammates. And that's one of the problems that flows from keeping Rodgers around for the first year of McCarthy's tenure. A certain amount of the coach's authority has been delegated to Rodgers. If that authority is going to be exercised against Metcalf, Rodgers needs to approve it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Abdul Carter: I showed I'm the best in the world
summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said last week that he was confident sacks would start to come for linebacker Abdul Carter and he was proven correct on Sunday.
full_text: '' Giants head coach John Harbaugh said last week that he was confident sacks would start to come for linebacker Abdul Carter and he was proven correct on Sunday. Advanced stats have graded Carter well as a pass rusher all season, but he came into Sunday's game against the Jaguars with two sacks and eight quarterback hits on the year. Carter doubled his sack total against Jacksonville, hit Trevor Lawrence five times and was credited with 12 pressures to help the Giants to a 23-18 win that maintained their breathing room ahead of the Cowboys in the NFC East. After the game, Carter was asked what he showed during the victory. "I'm the best in the world ," Carter said. Others will have other opinions about that question, but the Giants will be happy to reap the benefits of Carter's continued efforts to prove that point in the weeks, months and years to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jevón Holland on controversial Parker Washington call: "Shoutout Vegas"
summary: Back when the NFL hated gambling, it feared that widespread legalized sports betting would prompt fans to think the fix is in.
full_text: ''' Back when the NFL hated gambling, it feared that widespread legalized sports betting would prompt fans to think the fix is in. Although the league has done its best to ignore the fact that its fears were accurate, not everyone has gotten the memo. Giants safety Jevón Holland went there on Sunday, regarding the decision that Jaguars receiver Parker Washington failed to catch what would have been a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. “The game’s over? That might have been a catch,” Holland said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post. “That was a hell of a play. When they called it out, I was like, ‘Alright.’ Shoutout Vegas , man. I don’t know.” Holland was surely joke. On the topic of suggesting that something fishy was happening, however, the NFL may not have a sense of humor. It's precisely the kind of comment to which the tinfoil-hat crowd will cling. Even if Holland doesn't mean it, those who want to think the fix is in will seize on the statement of evidence that the fix is in. As we've said time and again, the fix isn't in. However, the NFL needs to be far more concerned about that perception than it is.
author: Mike Florio

title: George Kittle's second TD gives 49ers 14-7 lead
summary: Once again, George Kittle has made it into the end zone.
full_text: ' Once again, George Kittle has made it into the end zone. Kittle caught his second touchdown of the night on an 8-yard pass from Brock Purdy, putting the 49ers back ahead 14-7 with 14:13 left in the second quarter. It took San Francisco just five plays to go 67 yards and score. The big play on the drive came on second-and-10 from the Minnesota 48, with Purdy beating a blitz to fire a strike down the middle to Mike Evans for a 34-yard gain. After a Christian McCaffrey 6-yard run, Purdy connected with Kittle for the tight end’s seventh touchdown of the season. Notably, Kittle has now passed Terrell Owens to become No. 2 all-time in 49ers franchise history in receiving yards. Only Jerry Rice has more receiving yards than Kittle, as the star tight end continues to thrive in his long career.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bryce Young's 14 game-winning drives tied for most by any player 25 or younger since at least 1950
summary: Panthers quarterback Bryce Young showed a knack for leading game-winning drives while leading the Panthers to a division title last season and he's gotten back into the groove the last couple of weeks.
full_text: '' Panthers quarterback Bryce Young showed a knack for leading game-winning drives while leading the Panthers to a division title last season and he's gotten back into the groove the last couple of weeks. Young led the Panthers to a game-winning field goal in the final 30 seconds against the Saints in Week 10 and then got them into position for another Ryan Fitzgerald kick with 1:41 to play against the Ravens on Sunday. The defense closed out the 35-33 win from there, which means that Young has now led 14 game-winning drives since entering the league in 2023. That's the second-most by any quarterback since Young entered the league and, per the NFL, he is tied with Dak Prescott and Justin Herbert for the most game-winning drives by any player 25 years of age or younger since at least 1950. "Game on the line, nobody else I want with the ball ," Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Sunday, via the team's website. "Bryce Young's going to go there. He's going to be, he's going to be in control. He's going to be focused, locked into the moment, and that's what he looked like on that drive." Young was 39-of-60 for 454 yards, two touchdowns and an interception over the last two games and the wins have given the Panthers a two-game lead in the division heading into Week 12. If they can keep rolling against the Buccaneers next Sunday, another playoff berth will feel even likelier in Carolina.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sunday Night Football: 49ers move to 9-1 with dominant 35-10 victory over Vikings
summary: George Kittle caught two touchdowns as San Francisco became the first team to score at least 30 points against Minnesota in 2026.
full_text: '' Are the 49ers the best team in the league? Sunday night’s victory over the Vikings makes for a great argument that they are. San Francisco put together a dominant performance against Minnesota, coming away with a 35-10 victory in Mexico City. The 49ers were impressive on both offense and defense, but the result from the former was particularly notable. It’s the first time Minnesota has allowed 30 points all year, with only two teams reaching 20 points prior to Sunday’s contest. Quarterback Brock Purdy had an excellent night, finishing 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns. Head coach Kyle Shanahan took him out of the game midway through the fourth quarter with the contest effectively decided. George Kittle caught the first two touchdowns of the night, with Mike Evans catching Purdy’s third late in the second quarter. The 49ers then scored again on Ji’Ayir Brown’s pick-six off Kirk Cousins to hold a 28-10 lead at halftime. Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter to cap a 13-play, 98-yard drive that put the game out of reach. McCaffrey finished with 49 yards on 12 carries with a TD. He also caught two passes for 13 yards. Evans had six catches for 109 yards with a score, Keenan Allen caught three passes for 38 yards, and Kittle finished with three receptions for 34 yards with two TDs. On the other side, Kirk Cousins was frustrated by the 49ers’ pressure throughout the game as the Vikings couldn’t get much going on offense. Cousins ended the matchup 26-of-38 for 235 yards with a pick. He was taken out late in the contest, as Carson Wentz came in for mop-up duty. Justin Jefferson led the Vikings with 86 yards on seven catches. It didn’t help that Minnesota was missing left tackle Christian Darrisaw for much of the contest. He suffered a shoulder injury in the second quarter and did not return. The 49ers also lost an offensive lineman, as right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a serious lower-leg injury in the first half. He was carted off in an air cast after players were visibly upset by the nature of his injury. With the win, the 49ers move to 9-1 and are in the driver’s seat for the NFC’s No. 1 seed. They will host the division-rival Seahawks next Sunday afternoon. The Vikings fall to 7-3 after starting the season 6-0, having lost three of their last four. They will be back at home in Week 12 to face the Falcons.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Vrabel: Amy Adams Strunk didn't want to pay A.J. Brown
summary: One of the most compelling pieces of draft-room video came in 2022, when the Titans unexpectedly traded receiver A.J.
full_text: One of the most compelling pieces of draft-room video came in 2022, when the Titans unexpectedly traded receiver A.J. Brown to the Eagles and coach Mike Vrabel's discomfort with the move was manifested by the repeated jerking of his head. Now that Brown and Vrabel have been reunited in New England, after an offseason process that had the Rams tap out due to concerns about Brown's knee, chatter has surfaced that the Titans made the trade because they'd been told by doctors that Brown's knee — as of 2022 — had only two years left. On Monday morning, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel addressed that narrative during his weekly appearance on WEEI. Was Brown traded because the Titans believed his knee had a short shelf life? "No, the owner didn’t want to pay A.J. Brown 25 million dollars," Vrabel said, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. "That's what it was. He went to Philly, and I mean, A.J. has participated in quite a handful of games and has missed a few since he went to Philly." Brown played four years with the Eagles. He missed six regular-season games. He had four straight 1,000-yard seasons. He qualified for two Pro Bowls. He was an Associated Press second-team All-Pro three times. The real question isn't whether Brown had two years left in his knee in 2022. It's whether the knee had enough to justify trading for him and paying him in 2026. The Rams decided it wasn't. The Patriots decided it was. The fact that Brown has missed six games due to injury has brought the knee problem back into focus, opening the door for revisionist history as to why the Titans traded him. "But by all indications, unfortunately, after the training camp that he had, I wouldn't have anticipated anything," Vrabel said. "And then injuries are part of the game. He gets rolled up on [in the season opener]. And then gets dragged down the other day, and that was unfortunate. So we'll just keep trying to get him healthy and whenever he can get back out there to help us, I know that he will." Currently, Brown has a hamstring injury. Vrabel made it clear on Monday that Brown will miss at least the Week 12 game at the Chargers. Nothing about Brown's current condition — as it relates to his knee or any other body part — changes the fact that the Titans made a huge mistake when they decided not to give Brown a second contract, to trade him to a team that would, and to replace him with a first-round pick that was used on receiver Treylon Burks. In three years with the Titans, Burks had 53 catches for 699 yards and one touchdown. During those same three years, Brown had 261 catches for 4,031 yards and 25 touchdowns with the Eagles. And two Super Bowl appearances and a Super Bowl win. Regardless of whether the Patriots made a good decision to trade for Brown in 2026, there can be no credible dispute that the Titans made a horrible decision to trade him in 2022.
author: Mike Florio

title: Christian McCaffrey touchdown gives 49ers 35-10 lead in fourth quarter
summary: It's just about all but over in Mexico City. 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey capped a 13-play, 98-yard drive with a 6-yard touchdown to give San Francisco a 35-10 lead with 13:26 left in the fourth quarter.
full_text: It's just about all but over in Mexico City. 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey capped a 13-play, 98-yard drive with a 6-yard touchdown to give San Francisco a 35-10 lead with 13:26 left in the fourth quarter. Minnesota had put San Francisco on the 2-yard line with a well-covered punt. But San Francisco was nevertheless able to methodically make its way down the field, converting three third downs on the way to the end zone. Newly acquired Keenan Allen caught two of the third-down conversions, moving the chains on third-and-4 with an 8-yard catch and on third-and-9 with a 13-yard reception. The drive covered 7:04 across the third and fourth quarters, putting Minnesota in an even more unfavorable position as the team tries to get back in it. McCaffrey now has 11 rushing touchdowns this season along with three receiving TDs.
author: Myles Simmons

title: David Bailey is first player with 9.5 sacks, six forced fumbles in first 10 NFL games
summary: The Jets haven't won a lot of games this season, but they picked a winner when they drafted linebacker David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in this year's draft.
full_text: '' The Jets haven't won a lot of games this season, but they picked a winner when they drafted linebacker David Bailey with the No. 2 pick in this year's draft. Bailey had two sacks of Justin Herbert in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers and he forced a fumble on one of those takedowns. That moved Bailey up to 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles on the season, which makes him the first player to notch those numbers in the first 10 games of his career — Bailey missed one game due to injury — since sacks became an official stat in 1982. "I’m not surprised and you guys ask me that all the time and I’m going to keep telling you the same thing. We expect that from him," head coach Aaron Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "I think he’s close to 10 sacks right now. The thing that’s really sticking out to me is the fact that he’s doing everything he can to get the ball back to the offense. He has maybe six or seven forced fumbles this year. I don’t know where that is as far as record, but it has to be somewhere up there. Listen, any time he’s on the field he gives us a chance for something big to happen. He’s a big-time playmaker. I call guys like him ‘pressure players.’ He’s able to make big plays at a time of need and he does a good job at that.” Bailey is now the betting favorite to be the league's defensive rookie of the year and he provides reason for optimism about the future amid another rough season for the Jets.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saquon Barkley: I won't be 100 percent healthy this season, but will keep playing
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said after beating the Steelers on Sunday that he's not completely healthy and won't be completely healthy this season, but he has no desire to shut it down.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said after beating the Steelers on Sunday that he's not completely healthy and won't be completely healthy this season, but he has no desire to shut it down. Despite the Eagles being 3-7 and seemingly going nowhere, Barkley said he'll play through whatever is ailing him the rest of the way. "I don't think I'm ever going to get to 100 percent again for the rest of the season. That's just how football works," Barkley said. "Got to get ready for the Thanksgiving game. That's our job." Barkley appeared to injure his shoulder at one point in the game, but he wouldn't answer directly when asked about it and indicated that he'll be good to go after three days. "I won't really get into that. I just look forward to rehabbing this week and getting back on Thursday," Barkley said. After snapping a seven-game losing streak, Barkley is enthusiastic about trying to win two in a row in Dallas on Thursday. "Playing on Thanksgiving is something we always dream about as kids, against the Dallas Cowboys," Barkley said. Barkley is going to play as long as he physically can.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel: No timetable for Drake Maye, he won't be available this week
summary: Word late last week was that Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fractured his fibula and that he could miss the rest of the season, but head coach Mike Vrabel isn't looking that far ahead.
full_text: ' Word late last week was that Patriots quarterback Drake Maye fractured his fibula and that he could miss the rest of the season, but head coach Mike Vrabel isn't looking that far ahead. The Patriots had a bye in Week 11, so there was no chance for head coach Mike Vrabel to discuss Maye's diagnosis in the days after he was injured against the Lions. On Monday, Vrabel made an appearance on WEEI and he was asked how knowing the extent of the injury affects the team's preparation for the rest of the campaign. "Won’t be available, so I don’t think it necessarily matters," Vrabel said. "We’ll see how he progresses and how long that takes. I don’t think there’s any timetable right now." Vrabel repeated that Maye "won’t be available this week" when asked a followup about whether he believes it will be a short term absence. Tommy DeVito is in line to start with Behren Morton as the backup and Vrabel did not indicate that a move to add another quarterback is imminent.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dak Prescott on facing Joe Milton: He's still a Cowboy, I hope he helps us out
summary: After the Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30 on Sunday, their quarterback Dak Prescott was asked about the team's Thanksgiving Day opponents.
full_text: After the Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30 on Sunday, their quarterback Dak Prescott was asked about the team's Thanksgiving Day opponents. Prescott was specifically asked about former teammate Joe Milton quarterbacking their NFC East rivals to a win over the Steelers and how he feels about the chance to face his former backup. Milton spent last season in Dallas and was on their practice squad before signing with Eagles in October. "Very excited. It’ll be fun," Prescott said. "Joe knows how I feel about it . He’s still a Cowboy and I’m hoping he helps us out.” Milton probably has a different view on whether or not he's still a Cowboy and it's a safe bet that neither he nor the Eagles will be in any mood to help out their longtime adversaries on Thursday afternoon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fernando Mendoza: This week was an improvement, but still a lot to work on
summary: Sunday's game in Denver opened poorly for the Raiders as the Broncos built up a 17-0 lead while the road team punted on its first three possessions, but things got better from there.
full_text: Sunday's game in Denver opened poorly for the Raiders as the Broncos built up a 17-0 lead while the road team punted on its first three possessions, but things got better from there. The Raiders cut the lead to 17-10 on a perfectly thrown pass by Fernando Mendoza to running back Ashton Jeanty on a wheel route and then tied the game when the rookie quarterback hooked up with tight end Ian Thomas for another score in the third quarter. Things swung back Denver's way from there and they iced the 38-24 win with a Ja'Quan McMillan interception return for a touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Mendoza ended the day 18-of-37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns and that pick. After the game, he said he felt "a lot more comfortable" than he did in his first start while also noting room for growth in future starts. "I believe I saw the field better ," Mendoza said. "I believe that my accuracy was better this week than last week, stepping into throws rather than drifting back. Don’t get me wrong, although I believe it was an improvement there are a lot of things I need to improve on for next week.” Among the things Mendoza and the Raiders will need to work on is the rookie having six passes batted down by Broncos defenders during the loss. He'll try to be crisper in his Sunday Night Football debut in Cleveland next weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: J.J. McCarthy: Offense took late Jags FG personally, we can't give them that confidence
summary: One of the biggest moments in Sunday's game between the Giants and Jaguars came with just over three minutes to play when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen elected to kick a field goal rather than go for it from New York's 9-yard-line.
full_text: '' One of the biggest moments in Sunday's game between the Giants and Jaguars came with just over three minutes to play when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen elected to kick a field goal rather than go for it from New York's 9-yard-line. The kick cut the Giants' lead to five points and Coen said after the game that going for it would have been a "hope play" that presented more risk than giving the ball back to the Giants. That reasoning was built around the Giants going without a first down on their previous four possessions, but the Giants got two to close out the game after the ensuing kickoff. After the 23-18 win was in the books, Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy acknowledged that the Giants offense took that both as a shot at them and as a reminder that the unit needs to do more than they did in the second half on Sunday. "As an offense, we took that personal for sure," McCarthy said, via a transcript from the team. "But the prior drives, obviously that was something that they felt comfortable with doing. We can't get into that position. We can't give them that confidence to go out there and kick the field goal. The next time we get in those situations where we're up, we have to finish the job and find every way we can this week to make sure we do that the next time." The win was McCarthy's third in four starts for the Giants and that record makes it easier to swallow any of the rough patches that the offense has hit over the course of those games. They'll try for a smoother effort across the board in Indianapolis next Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Allen did not have a rushing attempt in Sunday's win
summary: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has built his career on being a two-way threat with the ball in his hands, but he did not play that way against the Dolphins on Sunday.
full_text: '' Bills quarterback Josh Allen has built his career on being a two-way threat with the ball in his hands, but he did not play that way against the Dolphins on Sunday. Allen is one of the most feared running quarterbacks in the league and is 14th in NFL history with 90 rushing touchdowns for his career, so it was a surprise to realize that he did not run the ball once in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins. It is the fourth time that Allen has started a game and not run the ball a single time, but the other three were token starts in the final weekend of the regular season to keep his consecutive starts streak alive. Allen had one carry in a 41-7 win over the Titans in 2022 and he's had seven starts with two carries in his career. While Allen wound up with 304 passing yards, it wasn't a stellar day for him throwing the ball either as a pair of interceptions helped keep the Bills from putting an early wrap on their one-win visitors from Miami. He'll need to be sharper putting the ball in the air against the Chiefs on Thursday and it seems like a good bet that he'll find ways to impact the game as a runner as well.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cam Skattebo on unretiring the backflip: When energy calls for it, it calls for it
summary: Cam Skattebo said during the week that he was retiring his celebratory backflip because he didn't want to risk a similar injury to the one suffered by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in Week 10, but the retirement proved to be a very brief one.
full_text: '' Cam Skattebo said during the week that he was retiring his celebratory backflip because he didn't want to risk a similar injury to the one suffered by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in Week 10, but the retirement proved to be a very brief one. After Skattebo iced the Giants' win over the Jaguars with a first down run on Sunday, he flexed his muscles and then did a backflip to the delight of fans at MetLife Stadium. Skattebo told reporters in the locker room that he was swept up in the energy of the moment. "When energy calls for it , it calls for it," Skattebo said, via SNY. "My teammates — I do whatever I can to bring my energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. When that happens, it’s second nature and it’s hard to hold back from." The backflip wasn't the only callback to past games for Skattebo. He also lost a fumble in the second half, but head coach John Harbaugh did not bench him as he did after a fumble in overtime against the Commanders earlier in the season. That made it easier for the coach to chuckle about the way Skattebo punctuated the victory. "He couldn't help himself, could he? He just couldn't help himself," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. There was no injury and the Giants' win leaves them on top of the NFC East, so there was little reason for Harbaugh to make either the fumble or the backflip the focus of attention after the game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs has 52 career rushing TDs, ties Barry Sanders for most before turning 25
summary: Two Lions running backs now share the NFL record for the most rushing touchdowns before turning 25 years old.
full_text: Two Lions running backs now share the NFL record for the most rushing touchdowns before turning 25 years old. Jahmyr Gibbs scored his 51st and 52nd career rushing touchdowns on Sunday against the Buccaneers, which ties him with Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns by a player under the age of 25 in NFL history. Gibbs doesn't turn 25 until after this season, so if he scores just one more rushing touchdown this year, he'll move ahead of Sanders and have the record to himself. It's safe to say Gibbs will score at least one more in the Lions' seven remaining games. Sunday was Gibbs' 18th game with multiple touchdowns, and he now has 62 total touchdowns in 59 career games. Gibbs is the betting favorite to win the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year award. He has 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 touchdowns this season, both leading the league.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers lose right tackle Colton McKivitz for season with fractured, dislocated ankle
summary: The 49ers lost starting right tackle Colton McKivitz for the season on Sunday night with a serious ankle injury.
full_text: ' The 49ers lost starting right tackle Colton McKivitz for the season on Sunday night with a serious ankle injury. Coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed the injury after the game and said it was particularly hard for the 49ers to see McKivitz get hurt because of how well respected he is within the locker room. "That was really crushing. Colton's had an unbelievable year. We care about all our guys, but it was tough to see Colton go down like that," Shanahan said. Shanahan said McKivitz appears to have the same injury that 49ers linebacker Fred Warner suffered last year. Warner had that injury in Week 6 and missed the rest of the season, so McKivitz will certainly not be able to play again this season after suffering the injury in Week 11. "We think it's broken and dislocated, similar to Fred's last year," Shanahan said. McKivitz suffered the injury midway through the second quarter and was replaced by Vederian Lowe. Shanahan said Lowe played well for the rest of the game and the 49ers will be counting on him to play well for the rest of the season.

title: Parker Washington non-catch controversy: Jevón Holland says 'Shout out Vegas,' NFL says call was correct
summary: Holland's tongue-in-cheek comment likely won't sit well at the league office
full_text:
Seemingly everyone has an opinion about Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington's controversial non-catch heard 'round the world from Jacksonville's 23-18 Week 11 loss to the Giants , but New York safety Jevón Holland's certainly isn't the best look.
First, here's the play in question.
"I did not think he lost possession of the football ... I think it's a touchdown fellas." @GeneSteratore disagrees with the call of INCOMPLETE after review pic.twitter.com/b2T3eoe5my
The Jaguars settled for a field goal to make it 20-9, then scored a touchdown to cut the deficit to 23-18 (after a failed two-point conversion). Obviously, the non-catch loomed large, and Holland — perhaps tongue-in-cheek — suggested that if the game hadn't been close, the NFL might have flipped the call.
"The game's over -- that might have been a catch," Holland said post-game, per The Athletic's Dan Duggan . "That was a hell of a play. I thought he got his foot down. I was like, 'Damn.' But then they called it out, and I was like, 'Shit, all right.' Shout-out Vegas. I don't know."
Holland's comment likely will not go over well at league offices, which certainly want to avoid any link between sports betting influencing games or calls. To be clear, Holland was relieved when the call went New York's way.
NFL vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth said officials made the correct calls both initially and in upholding the call after Liam Coen's challenge. Even though Washington got two feet in bounds, Butterworth said, the ball was moving when he made contact with the ground.
"He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch," Butterworth said via the pool report.
Parker said he "felt good about it" being a catch but emphasized that regardless of the call, the team needed to (and still needs to) move on. Teammates didn't exactly feel the same way, with safety Antonio Johnson saying the team was "devastated" to hear the call wouldn't be overturned, per ESPN .
NFL on CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore, play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz, and lead analyst J.J. Watt all believed it should have been a touchdown, while most Giants — Holland not included — believed the officials got it right.
"He was out. Clear as day," said cornerback Dru Phillips, who was covering Washington on the play, per ESPN . "And he bobbled the ball, too. So, it wouldn't have been a catch regardless."
Even if the NFL didn't agree with Phillips on the first part, the second part was the deciding factor.
"The ball moved," John Harbaugh said in his post-game press conference. "The same exact one as Malik [Nabers] had [earlier in the game]."

title: Commanders vs. Bengals prediction: Cincinnati looks to extend lead in AFC North in 'MNF' matchup
summary: How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Monday night contest in DC
full_text:
In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals .
Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival New York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks.
Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night.
Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL . Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media.
Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease.
Ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him.
The Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment.
Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample , though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two.
Washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league.
However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins.
Jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams .
Without Terry McLaurin , Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs , rookie Antonio Williams , Treylon Burks , Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo.
Diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position.
The Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year.
The Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler , each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football.
With big Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins , Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground.
The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. Pick: Bengals 31, Commanders 20

full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
We fell for it again. Everyone underrated Houston . How could college basketball be so blind? Kelvin Sampson is as reliable as anyone in this sport and seems to own the nation's best team following the Cougars' run to the Players Era 8 title. At the very least, Sampson owns his most dangerous offense to date .
Our Cameron Salerno projects that Houston will move up to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 rankings when they are released later today.
We also foresee Indiana moving into the top 25 for the first time in this young season thanks to a 2-0 week in which it beat No. 20 Arkansas and Kentucky . The 14-point win over Kentucky not only cemented the Hoosiers' case to crack the rankings but also emphasized the Wildcats' flaws. It also pointed the microscope on Mark Pope and his less-than-accurate explanation of his team's lack of experience .
Here is the tier in which we project the Hoosiers to land:
18. BYU (5-0) 19. Gonzaga (3-1) 20. Indiana (6-0) 21. Louisville (3-1) 22. Nebraska (6-0)
Don't forget about Oregon . Three early-season losses dropped the Ducks out of the rankings and playoff picture, but with Dylan Raiola kicking the offense into gear, they trounced Michigan State and are squarely in the hunt for the Big Ten Championship Game and CFP. Losses from UCLA and Indiana helped their cause and made them one of the most fortunate teams of the week .
Elsewhere in the Big Ten, Ohio State is trending sharply in the other direction and on Saturday tumbled right out of playoff consideration. It has to be a devastating feeling to be on the wrong end of Nebraska snapping a 31-game losing streak against ranked opponents. It is hardly a consolation for losing a fourth game for the first time since 2011, but at least Jeremiah Smith put up monster numbers on the Cornhuskers. Nebraska coach Matt Rhule is ready to declare the Heisman Trophy race over , and our Brandon Marcello says that is not an overreaction .
While Ryan Day slogs through the worst year of his career, Josh Heupel is pulling off his best coaching job to date . His Tennessee squad downed LSU by two touchdowns for a revenge win over Lane Kiffin and earned a "B+" on our Week 12 report card for the victory.

title: Cover 32: AFC contender is at risk of missing playoffs entirely, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 11
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all of the biggest items from Week 11 in the NFL, including DK Metcalf's ejection and Brock Purdy's stellar day against the Vikings defense
full_text:
The record has been scratched amid Aaron Rodgers ' "Last Dance."
For the first half of the 2026 season, the Pittsburgh Steelers seemed well on their way to making it back to the postseason and giving Rodgers, who is playing in his final season in the NFL , one last kick at the can. The club entered its Week 9 bye at 6-2 on the season and riding a four-game winning streak. Upon their return to action, however, their season has gone sideways.
Pittsburgh has now dropped two straight games, including a 19-16 defeat to the Joe Milton-led Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. Whatever the issues that have led to this skid are, the Steelers need to get them corrected in a relatively quick fashion, as it's not hyperbole to say their season is teetering.
The Week 11 loss dropped them to 6-4 on the season and has them falling from the No. 6 seed down to the No. 7 seed. Despite being on the bye, the Cleveland Browns leapt over them thanks to a tiebreaker. After splitting the regular-season series, Cleveland currently possesses the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh due to its superior record within the AFC North (4-3 vs. 3-3).
On top of jockeying for position with the Browns, the Steelers now need to concern themselves with a few AFC teams just outside the current playoff picture. While their season has been turnt upside down following the fractured fibula to Drake Maye , the Patriots (5-5) are a game behind Pittsburgh and own the head-to-head tiebreaker thanks to a win back in Week 2.
Speaking of tiebreakers, the Steelers' main competition for a wild card spot could end up being the surging Texans. Houston is 4-6 after Week 11, but has been lurking, especially as C.J. Stroud has been enjoying a career year under center. These two AFC clubs will square off in just a couple of weeks from Pittsburgh in Week 13.
Before then, the Steelers will host the Denver Broncos , while the Houston Texans will host the Baltimore Ravens. At DraftKings Sportsbook, Pittsburgh is a 2.5-point underdog at home next week, and the Texans are a 6.5-point favorite. If those games go according to the spread, this Week 13 contest sets up Houston with an opportunity to move to 6-6 and gain the head-to-head tiebreaker with a win over the Steelers, who'd tumble down the standings and possibly out of the playoff picture entirely.
Pittsburgh would then finish out the season with games against the Jaguars (road), Ravens (twice), Panthers , and Titans (road). While that's not a gauntlet, no game is guaranteed given the way the Steelers have been playing post-bye.
Right now, Mike McCarthy's club sits at +138 to miss the playoffs. That feels like one of the best bets you can make in the futures market coming out of Week 11.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Carter was a man possessed in New York's win over the Jaguars. Coming into this game, the former first-round pick had two sacks on the season, and he ended up matching that total with two sacks on Trevor Lawrence on Sunday. Carter led the team with eight pressures and was a big reason why the Jaguars offense was off-kilter for the bulk of the afternoon.
Abdul Carter is taking over 😤 JAXvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/v6djuFIjYZ
Simmons continues to pay dividends for the Bears after the Bears acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Titans. The defensive lineman tallied three sacks in the win over the Saints . That gives Simmons five sacks since coming over to Chicago. He's just the third player in NFL history to have at least five sacks and three wins in his first three games with any franchise.
This Jeffery Simmons guy is pretty good at football 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/jdGX4RdikK
The Cowboys offense exploded for 51 points in a dominant win over the Titans. Prescott accounted for five touchdowns on the afternoon, the fourth time in his career he's notched at least five scores. He's also the fifth player in NFL history with multiple games of at least 300 yards passing, four passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown in a career.
6 drives 6 TDs THE COWBOYS' OFFENSE IS ELECTRIC TENvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4FQeNa6kbk
Kelce turned back the clock in Kansas City's 34-7 win over the Cardinals . He was Patrick Mahomes ' most targeted weapon in the winning effort and finished with a team-high 74 yards to go along with two touchdowns. Kelce is the fourth-oldest player with at least two touchdown receptions in a game in NFL history. Those scores also got him to 90 career touchdowns, which is the fourth-most by a tight end in NFL history.
Kelce gets his second touchdown of the first half! AZvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VOaPtsJiBo
Coleman would not be denied as the rookie back was the key cog of Denver's offense in the 38-24 win over the Raiders. He hit paydirt three times on Sunday and extended his touchdown streak to three-straight games. Coleman is the first Bronco with at least 100 yards rushing and three rushing touchdowns since Mike Anderson (2005 vs. Jets ).
Hat trick for Jonah Coleman ‼️ LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FQNYZWdwKH
Purdy sliced up what has been the best defense in the NFL in the Vikings en route to a 35-10 win in Mexico City. Against Brian Flores' blitzes on Sunday night, Purdy completed 16 of his 18 pass attempts for 195 yards and two touchdowns, which resulted in a 148.8 passer rating. This performance could very well propel him atop the MVP odds and has San Francisco on a clear road to the No. 1 seed in the NFC.
What a throw by Brock Purdy! MINvsSF on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EbcQmS99j1
On the one hand, Jameson Williams ' 57-yard touchdown catch was worth celebrating. It broke open the game for Detroit en route to their win over the Buccaneers . That said, a backflip probably wasn't the way to go, especially when the Lions are merely a week removed from Aidan Hutchinson suffering a season-ending ACL tear after celebrating a sack.
Aidan Hutchinson had a season ending injury celebrating last week… So naturally his teammate Jameson Williams does this after scoring pic.twitter.com/aw490Oacbq
You could feel everyone in Detroit tense up as he leaped in the air.
Justice Hill was about to add to Baltimore's lead in the early stages of the second quarter as the Ravens back ripped off what looked to be a 37-yard touchdown. However, just before crossing the goal line, Hill has the ball knocked free. It then flew through the back of the end zone for a touchback.
TD turns into a touchback! Panthers ball! BALvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qpWNoHVtvw
Hill would redeem himself with a touchdown run later in the quarter, but that was a killer in what proved to be a 35-33 defeat at the hands of the Panthers.
One of the wildest plays of the weekend came in Dallas where rookie wideout Carnell Tate wisely realized he was untouched on a short throw by Cam Ward . After making the catch, the Titans receiver quickly got up and ran 59 yards to the house for a touchdown. Upon review, no Cowboys defender touched him while he was on the ground, so it was a remarkable heads-up play by Tate.
The awareness by Tate for the TD‼️ 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/iI11vKXeap
The Steelers receiver was ejected from the Week 11 loss to the Eagles after poking the eye of Philadelphia defensive back Cooper DeJean . Metcalf already had one unsportsmanlike penalty to his name for the game, and that infraction then sent him packing in the third quarter. This was the third ejection of Metcalf's career.
DK Metcalf has been ejected in Philly CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J
Before his ejection, Metcalf caught just one of his four targets for 2 yards in what has been a forgetful season for the veteran pass catcher.

full_text:
If there is any truth to the adage that the NFL season does not truly start until Thanksgiving, then now is the time to start taking the playoff race seriously. As the calendar turns to Week 12 and a loaded holiday slate, all seven seeds in both conferences are up for grabs, and there are a number of teams beyond the current cut line that could not only make their way into the bracket but also compete for home-field advantage in the postseason.
Anyone that aims to lock up a first-round bye in the NFC has to get through the San Francisco 49ers , which is a daunting task considering how dominant they appeared on the Week 11 edition of "Sunday Night Football."
And in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars learned a difficult lesson on Sunday about how slim the margins are in the race for the No. 1 seed when they suffered a costly setback against the New York Giants .
With seven weeks of regular-season action to go, here is a snapshot of the playoff picture in both NFL conferences.
Remaining schedule: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots , at Packers , vs. Bears , at Broncos, at Dolphins , vs. Jets
The only blemish on the Bills' resume is a three-point divisional loss to the Patriots, but that should not come back to bite them in the AFC East race as they hold a commanding four-game lead. It does make them vulnerable in the battle for the conference's No. 1 seed, though. The schedule is about to stiffen up following a four-game stretch in which Josh Allen feasted on beleaguered opponents and the defense corrected its early-season woes by allowing no more than 12 points in any of those contests.
Remaining schedule: at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders , vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers
That the Broncos fended off Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders was critical for Denver's chances of winning the AFC West. Sean Payton's squad holds a tiebreaker over the Chiefs thanks to their higher win percentage against common opponents. It was a rare win by double digits for a team that is prolific at squeaking out victories by a one-score margin and increased the win streak to six games, which is tied for the longest in the conference.
Remaining schedule: at Commanders , vs. Saints , at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers , at Colts , vs. Ravens , vs. Browns
Regardless of what occurs on "Monday Night Football," the Bengals cannot slip out of line for a top-four seed. They stand a game and a half clear of the Browns and Steelers in the AFC North. As one of the hottest teams in the league, they take an offense that is seemingly unstoppable into the Week 11 finale against the Commanders.
Remaining schedule: vs. Titans , at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans , at Cowboys , vs. Commanders, at Colts
Trevor Lawrence endured uncharacteristic struggles in a loss to the Giants that halted the Jaguars' momentum. In each of their previous four games, they scored at least 31 points. They managed only 18 against New York. The AFC South is still theirs by a three-game margin, so the defeat only has implications for seeding inside the top four. This team went all-in at the trade deadline and would thus figure to be disappointed with anything less than the No. 1 seed, but so long as everything comes together in the postseason, one loss in Week 11 will not haunt them.
Remaining schedule: at Bills, at Rams , at Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, at Chargers, vs. Raiders
The battle with the Broncos to secure home-field advantage in the Wild Card round could come down to the last week of the season. The Chiefs have done nearly everything they can to lock up one of those prized seeds yet find themselves on the outside looking in due to Denver's tiebreaker in the division. Kansas City has been mauling overmatched opponents of late and needs that to translate to the much stiffer competition that lies ahead over the next five weeks.
Remaining schedule: vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons , at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, at Bengals
The Browns hold a tiebreaker over the Steelers for the No. 6 seed because of their divisional win percentage. They split the regular-season series with Pittsburgh and won their only other AFC North contest, 13-10, over the Baltimore Ravens. Among the more pleasant surprises of the entire NFL season is what first-year coach Todd Monken continues to achieve in turning Deshaun Watson back into a serviceable starting quarterback and how defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg constructed a competitive group following the offseason Myles Garrett trade.
Remaining schedule: vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens
It was only three weeks ago that the Steelers held sole possession of the AFC North lead. Everything since then has been a disaster. They no-showed a week ago in a primetime loss to the Bengals and, on Sunday, were on the wrong side of the Eagles , who snapped a seven-game losing streak. That in-state loss marked a new low for the 2026 Steelers. They remain on the right side of the postseason cut line, but it is a tenuous position.
No team outside the top seven is better than 5-5, and that lone .500 team will be without its quarterback until further notice. The Patriots (5-5) would be the top contender to move up the ladder if Drake Maye were healthy, but in his absence, the door is open for teams a little further down. That includes the Texans (4-6), who could become just the second team in NFL history to start a season 0-4 and reach the playoffs. The pickings are slim behind them, as the Ravens (4-7) and Raiders (4-7) are operating with a backup quarterback and rookie signal-caller, respectively.
Remaining schedule: vs. Seahawks , at Giants, vs. Rams, at Chargers, at Chiefs, vs. Eagles, at Cardinals
If a decisive win over a fellow championship contender and a 35-point outburst against the NFL's top defense does not cement the 49ers as Super Bowl favorites, then nothing will. San Francisco is undoubtedly the team to beat. Mike Evans ' return in the Mexico City Game injected even more life into the offense and gives Kyle Shanahan yet another weapon to deploy in the weeks to come as he unleashes an unstoppable attack on the rest of the league. The NFC is the 49ers' to lose.
Remaining schedule: vs. Bears, at Falcons, vs. Titans, at Vikings, vs. Giants, at Bears, at Packers
The Lions hold a tiebreaker over the Bears for the NFC North lead with the greater win percentage in division games, but that will not matter in just a few days when the head-to-head result between the two on Thanksgiving determines who has the inside track to home-field advantage in the Wild Card round. Detroit, as it stands, is the top threat to the 49ers at the top of the conference and owns the kind of offensive star power it would take to unseat them from the NFC's catbird seat should they square off in the postseason.
Remaining schedule: at Colts, vs. 49ers, at Seahawks, vs. Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, vs. Eagles
The Giants passed their biggest test of the year on Sunday when they took down the Jaguars in a colossal 23-18 victory. Every other win on their ledger is against a sub-.500 team, so the Week 11 triumph was by far the most impressive and legitimized their division lead. They remain the only NFC East team with a winning record and own a defense that seems capable of keeping them in control of their own destiny in the hunt for a top-four playoff seed.
Remaining schedule: at Buccaneers , at Vikings, vs. Saints, vs. Bengals, at Steelers, vs. Seahawks, vs. Falcons
Such is the state of the NFC South that the Panthers are merely .500 yet own a two-game lead over the rest of the division. Every other team is 3-7. There exists a realistic path for Carolina to move up to the No. 3 seed since the NFC East is nearly as weak as their own division, but that is probably the ceiling. Back-to-back wins and Chuba Hubbard's emergence as a prominent bell-cow running back have the Panthers trending the right way.
