title: NFL Week 12 early odds: Bills favored over Chiefs for Thanksgiving showdown, Steelers home underdogs
summary: The Bears are road favorites for their Thanksgiving matchup in Detroit
full_text:
How about a little football to pair with your turkey and stuffing? The NFL is about to embark on its Thanksgiving slate, and this year is particularly jam-packed with action.
It begins on Wednesday night when the Packers and Rams kick off the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. Then, we have our traditional Thanksgiving triple header, the Black Friday game and the Sunday slate before we wrap things up in Tampa on Monday night. That's five windows of games over a six-day span. If that's not something to be thankful for, I don't know what is.
Of course, with the games kicking off a bit earlier this week, it's even more important to get situated on the betting front. That's especially true given that some of these games that we'll watch over the holiday carry massive stakes. That includes an NFC North matchup on Thanksgiving, with the Chicago Bears currently listed as road favorites over the Detroit Lions .
We'll get into that game and the rest of the slate as we take our first glimpses of the Week 12 odds.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Packers at Rams (Wednesday)
Eagles at Cowboys (Thursday)
Chiefs at Bills (Thursday)
Broncos at Steelers (Friday)
Broncos -152, Steelers +128
Falcons +269, Vikings -333
Titans +720, Jaguars -1124
Patriots +100, Chargers -119
Commanders -352, Cardinals +283
Panthers at Buccaneers (Monday)
Panthers +131, Buccaneers -155
Both of these clubs are coming off of their bye week, so the rest disparity will be the same. Los Angeles opened as a 3.5-point favorite for this Thanksgiving Eve game but have since lost the hook and are laying a field goal. Green Bay and LA are 6-4 ATS this season, but the Rams are 2-3 ATS at SoFi Stadium. The Packers are 3-2 ATS on the road. The total dipped down to 44.5 after opening at 45.5. This season, the Under is 7-3 in Packers games.
Chicago opened as a 2.5-point road favorite in Detroit, and that's held coming out of Sunday's action. The Bears are 6-4 ATS this season, which includes a 3-1 ATS record on the road. Specifically, as a road favorite, Chicago is 2-1 ATS. As for the Lions, they're 2-2-1 ATS at Ford Field. They have yet to be a home underdog this season. Points are expected to come in bunches as the total sits at 55.5, which is the largest of the slate. However, the Over is just 3-2 in Lions home games this season.
Dallas is coming off a win in which it scored 51 points against the Titans and will now try to inch closer in the NFC East standings when it hosts the Eagles. The Cowboys are an 8.5-point favorite and will look to improve on their 5-6 ATS record on the season. At AT&T Stadium, Dallas is 2-3 ATS. As for the Eagles, they're 2-8 ATS this season, which includes a 0-3 ATS record on the road. Philadelphia is the only team in the NFL without an ATS road victory this season.
Buffalo opened as a 3-point favorite at home against the Chiefs, and that's held up after both clubs won in Week 11. The Bills are 4-1 ATS at home this season, and their 11.6 average margin of victory is the fourth-highest in the league. The Chiefs haven't been the strongest team to back when they're outside of Arrowhead Stadium, coming into Week 12 with a 2-3 ATS record on the road.
The Broncos opened as a 1.5-point road favorite against Pittsburgh, but that has since jumped up even higher to Denver -3. Faith has been dwindling in the Steelers as they've dropped two straight games coming off of their bye week. At home, Pittsburgh is a perfect 4-0 ATS, which includes a cover in their lone game as a home dog this season. That pristine record will be put to the test, however, as the Broncos are 3-0 ATS this season as a road favorite.
Houston will have the rest advantage in this game after playing last Thursday while Baltimore played on Sunday. That, in part, is why the Texans are laying 6.5 points in this matchup. However, Houston hasn't been a slam dunk at home this season, coming into this game with a 1-4 ATS record. The Ravens are 3-2 ATS on the road. The total for this game has ticked up to 46.5 after opening at 44.5. The Over is 7-4 in Ravens games this season.
Cincinnati is a 10.5-point favorite after this line initially opened at Bengals -10. Of course, this line could fluctuate again depending on how Cincinnati's game against the Commanders on Monday night pans out. That said, Cincinnati is 5-4 ATS this season, which includes a 2-2 ATS record at home. As for the Saints, New Orleans is a perfect 4-0 ATS on the road. They are the only team in the NFL that has yet to record an ATS road loss.
Minnesota is a touchdown favorite at home over the Falcons. It'll be at a bit of a disadvantage in terms of rest, however. On top of the Vikings coming off of an international game in Mexico City, they'll be hosting an Atlanta team that was on the bye in Week 11. The Vikings are 1-3 ATS at home this season, while the Falcons are 2-2 ATS on the road. With the total sitting at 42.5, it's worth noting the Under is 3-1 in Vikings home games.
New York is a 6.5-point road favorite against the Colts in Week 12. Indianapolis will be starting Anthony Richardson for this game after releasing Daniel Jones following their Week 11 loss to the Texans. The Giants covered their lone game as a road favorite this season and are 3-1 ATS on the road overall. The Colts are 2-3 ATS at home, which includes a 2-1 ATS record as a home underdog.
The Jets picked up the hook after opening as a 3-point favorite. Miami is 2-2 ATS this season as a home underdog, while New York is 3-2-1 ATS on the road. This will mark the first time this season that the Jets are a road favorite.
Jacksonville is the biggest favorite of Week 12, laying 14.5 points to the Titans at home. The Jaguars are 6-4 ATS on the season overall, which includes a 3-0 ATS record at home. Liam Coen's team is also 2-0 ATS following a loss this season and has an average margin of victory of 32 points in those games.  Tennessee is 4-6 ATS this season overall and 3-2 ATS on the road.
The Chargers opened as a 3.5-point favorite over the Patriots, but this line has since inched toward New England. Now, LA is laying just 1.5 points. Of course, the Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for this game after Drake Maye suffered a fractured fibula in Week 10 prior to the bye. Meanwhile, the Chargers are dealing with questions at quarterback themselves as Justin Herbert is in concussion protocol. If Herbert cannot play, backup DJ Uiagalelei would get the nod. The Patriots are 1-3-1 ATS on the road this season, while the Chargers are 0-5 ATS at home.
San Francisco is a slim 2.5-point favorite over the Seahawks, who were on the bye in Week 11. The Niners are 3-2 ATS at Levi's Stadium this season, while Seattle is 2-2 ATS on the road. The total for this game is 46.5, and the Under is 6-4 in Seahawks games this season.
This line could see some movement depending on the outcome of Washington's Week 11 game on Monday night. That said, the Commanders are a 7-point favorite on the road against Arizona. Washington is 3-1 ATS on the road this season, but it has yet to be favored on the road. The Cardinals are 0-4 at State Farm Stadium.
Cleveland was on the bye in Week 11, so it'll have a rest advantage over a Raiders team that was just in Denver. The Browns are laying 4.5 points in this AFC matchup and looking to stay perfect at home, where they've covered all four of their games. This season, Las Vegas is 3-3 on the road.
The Bucs were a 3.5-point favorite at the open but have dropped the hook. Now, they're merely laying a field goal in what is a pivotal NFC South matchup with the Panthers. Carolina is 3-2 ATS on the road this season, while Tampa Bay is 1-4 ATS at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Steelers gave DK Metcalf $150 million, traded George Pickens. Now they're paying for both decisions
summary: The Steelers wanted a more dependable receiver. Instead, Metcalf has delivered disappointing production and familiar distractions.
full_text:
There was a time the Steelers were really, really good at drafting and developing wide receivers. Hines Ward, Plaxico Burress, Santonio Holmes , Mike Wallace , Emmanuel Sanders , Antonio Brown , JuJu Smith-Schuster , Diontae Johnson , George Pickens . Of those nine names, two were first-round picks, six were Day 2 picks, and Brown was a sixth-rounder.
In fact, since drafting Pickens with the 52nd overall pick in 2022, Pittsburgh has selected exactly three receivers: Roman Wilson (third round, '24), Germie Bernard (second round, '26) and Kaden Wetjen (fourth round, '26). The philosophy, it seems, is less about developing receivers than trading for established players and paying a premium to do so. (By the way, as we've written previously, these struggles have not been limited to just pass catchers .)
Consider what the Steelers have done the last two offseasons. In March 2025, they traded a second-round pick as part of a package to acquire DK Metcalf , then gave him a five-year, $150 million contract. A year later, they traded for Michael Pittman Jr. and signed him to a three-year, $59 million deal.
That's $209 million in total contract commitments to two receivers, and through 11 weeks of the 2026 season, they have combined for 523 yards and two touchdowns. Pittman has played just three games because of injuries, while Metcalf has as many touchdown receptions this season as games he's been suspended since arriving in Pittsburgh. (Two. The answer for both is two.) And that doesn't include Sunday's ejection in Philadelphia , which could mean we'll have to update the "Days since DK was suspended" sign once again when the league is done with him.
It's also not a stretch to suggest that the Steelers are worse off at receiver than they were before all this started.
Early in his career, Metcalf was one of the NFL's most dangerous targets. In 2020, his second season in Seattle, he caught 83 passes for 1,303 yards and 10 touchdowns. He was always a straight-line player – but he consistently won with his physicality, size and 4.3 speed.
That was six years ago. He had two more 1,000-plus-yard seasons in Seattle, but 2020 turned out to be his most productive year in the league. He's been an unrecognizable shell of that player in this season.
So far this season, Metcalf is averaging 43.4 yards per game, and his 1.16 yards per route is easily the lowest of his career. For perspective, he averaged more than two yards per route in both 2020 and 2023.
Put another way: The Steelers paid $30 million annually for a receiver who has combined for 1,280 yards in 25 games. Here's where it gets worse: Among 16 veteran receivers we looked at who were acquired via trade or free agency between 2022 and 2025, Metcalf gave his team the least production for its money in his first season. Stefon Diggs , Jerry Jeudy and Darnell Mooney all provided considerably more bang for the buck, despite signing smaller contracts.
Let's dig a little further. For every $1 million in annual salary, Metcalf averaged just 1.89 receiving yards per game in 2025. Jeudy, who made $17.5 million annually, averaged 72.3 yards per game, or 4.13 yards for every $1 million. Mooney was even better: 62 yards per game on a $13 million annual deal, more than twice the production per dollar Pittsburgh got from Metcalf.
And it's gotten worse in 2026. Metcalf is now averaging just 1.45 receiving yards per game for every $1 million. In other words, the Steelers are paying the same price for 23% less production than they got a year ago.
If the Metcalf trade was supposed to solve Pittsburgh's WR1 problem, acquiring Pittman was supposed to address everything else. The Steelers needed someone who could consistently get open, move the chains and take some pressure off Metcalf.
Pittman had been a dependable receiver in Indianapolis, including a 109-catch, 1,152-yard season in 2023. But his production declined over the next two years, and injuries have limited him to seven catches for 89 yards since arriving in Pittsburgh.
Injuries happen, sure. And the Steelers gave up next to nothing to acquire him, essentially moving down 16 spots in the 2026 draft, from No. 214 to No. 230. The financial commitment, however, is another matter. The organization now has two expensive veteran receivers and little in the way of production to show for it.
So while Pittsburgh was overpaying for Metcalf in 2025, Washington acquired Deebo Samuel from San Francisco for a fifth-round pick. Samuel caught 72 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns last season and added value as a runner.
New England took a different approach, signing Stefon Diggs to a three-year, $63.5 million contract. Diggs responded with 85 receptions for 1,013 yards, despite coming off a season-ending knee injury in 2024.
Neither receiver required anything close to the combination of draft capital and long-term financial commitment Metcalf received.
(Same 5 yr/$150M contract)
Hindsight, you might say, is 20/20, and anybody can cherry-pick examples that worked out after the fact. Fair enough. But we don't know many folks who thought at the time that Metcalf was worth $30 million a year. Or that Michael Pittman, who is a possession receiver at best when he's healthy, had earned a new deal.
And we'll grant you this: None of this means Diggs or Samuel would've produced the same numbers in Pittsburgh, which now seems like where passing offenses go to die. But it's difficult to ignore the financial flexibility those teams maintained while getting meaningful contributions from those veteran additions.
And then there's Pickens, which might be the most hilariously frustrating part of this saga for Steelers fans.
The team had understandably grown tired of Pickens' mood swings, which often manifested themselves as inconsistent effort and dumb penalties. So two months after acquiring Metcalf, the Steelers traded Pickens to Dallas rather than deal with the nonsense for another season.
Pickens responded with 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns in 2025. He already has 780 yards and six touchdowns through 10 games in 2026. Metcalf, meanwhile, is one of the NFL's most ineffective receivers, and the cherry on top is that he's been a bigger headache in Pittsburgh than Pickens ever was. Last December, the NFL suspended him for two games after a physical confrontation with a fan in Detroit. And then, on Sunday, Metcalf was ejected after getting into it with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean .
So let's recap: Pittsburgh moved on from Pickens because he was a pain in the ass, then paid Metcalf $150 million to be invisible as a playmaker and front-and-center as a distraction. Make it make sense.
Now the Steelers have committed another $59 million to Pittman, who has spent most Sundays this fall on the sidelines in sweats. Aaron Rodgers is done after the season, which means that whoever is under center in 2027 could inherit one of the worst offenses in the league .
For all the money and draft picks the Steelers have wasted trying to fix their receiver room, perhaps the most damning indictment is this: A franchise that once set the standard for finding and developing young receivers now seems incapable of doing either.

title: Vikings utilize NFL's obscure fair-catch kick rule to attempt 71-yard field goal against 49ers
summary: If made, Will Reichard's field goal would have made NFL history
full_text:
The game between the Vikings and the 49ers got a little confusing toward the end of the first half on Sunday night when Minnesota decided to take advantage of an obscure NFL rule known as the fair-catch kick.
With 11 seconds left to play in the first half, the 49ers were facing a fourth-and-19 from their own 11-yard line, which was an obvious punting situation for San Francisco. Vikings returner Myles Price called for a fair catch on the play, and that's where the rarely used fair-catch kick came in.
Basically, the rule goes like this: If a team fair catches a punt, they're allowed to attempt a free kick on the next play. The kick isn't a typical field goal, either. The defense has to line up 10 yards off the ball — similar to a kickoff — and the defense is NOT allowed to try to block the kick. The "free kick" is more like a kickoff, except the kicker has to attempt the field goal off the ground, and there's also a holder (the kicker also has the option to dropkick the ball, but that almost never happens).
Here's how the NFL describes the rule :
"After a fair catch, the receiving team has the option to put the ball in play by a snap or a fair-catch kick (field goal attempt), with fair-catch kick lines established ten yards apart. All general rules apply as for a field goal attempt from scrimmage. The clock starts when the ball is kicked. (No tee permitted.)"
Now that you know how the rule works, let's get back to the game. Price actually called for a fair catch from his own 40-yard line, which meant that if the Vikings wanted to take advantage of the rule, they would have to attempt a 71-YARD FIELD GOAL. With the game being played in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet, that adds about five yards to a kicker's natural distance, so the Vikings decided to send out Will Reichard for the potentially record-setting kick.
According to the broadcast, Reichard hit from 68 yards in warm-ups, so the Vikings thought he could hit from 71, and it ALMOST HAPPENED. Reichard's kick only fell about a yard short.
Will Reichard comes up just short on a 71-yard fair catch free kick in Mexico City. Mike Tirico with the SNF call for NBC. 🏈🎙️ pic.twitter.com/q3BDFyVWBP
If the kick had gone in, it would have counted in the record book as the longest field goal in NFL history. But since he missed, Cam Little still holds the record at 68 yards.
There have only been 10 field goal attempts ever from 70 yards or longer, and Little actually had one of them back in Week 3 when he just barely missed a kick against the Patriots . Out of the other nine attempts, four of them came on a fair-catch kick, including Reichards'.
The fair-catch kick is rare: There have only been 21 attempts ever in the Super Bowl era, and only one kicker has actually made one over the past 40 years ( Cameron Dicker in December 2024 ). Reichard had a chance at NFL history on Sunday night, but he came up about a yard short. Reichard also missed a 55-yard attempt in the first half.
author: John Breech

title: Cam Skattebo flips: Giants RB celebrates game-clinching drive with backflip days after retiring it
summary: Skattebo said he'd retire his celebration in the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
full_text:
After Lions star Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL going airborne while celebrating a sack in Week 10, Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he'd retire his signature backflip celebration .
It proved a very short retirement.
Skattebo delivered the game-clinching first down in the Giants' 23-18 upset win over the Jaguars and celebrated ... with a backflip.
Skattebo first down and a backflip! JAXvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JuwVc6smEv
It was a huge win for the Giants, who moved to 6-3-1 to remain two games up on the Cowboys (5-6) in the NFC East. Dallas won earlier Sunday.
It was also a huge sigh of relief for Skattebo, who had a crucial fumble that contributed to Jacksonville's late rally. Overall, Skattebo finished with 14 carries for 34 yards.
John Harbaugh had long been against Skattebo's flipping — Skattebo notably failed on a backflip over the offseason, months after his rookie year ended with a serious ankle injury (not suffered on a flip). He was pleased to hear about Skattebo's intention not to backflip earlier in the week.
"I support his decision, and I hope he scores a lot of touchdowns," Harbaugh said. "I hope he gets an opportunity to prove it real soon. That'd be great."
After Skattebo reneged, Harbaugh didn't exactly look pleased on the sideline.
Cam Skattebo hit a backflip after saying he wasn't going to do it 👀 Check out John Harbaugh's reaction on the sidelines 😭 pic.twitter.com/Z1ucuQzvE7
After the game, though, Skattebo explained that the charged atmosphere and the significance of the first down played huge roles.
"When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo said. "My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. So when that happens, it's second nature, and it's hard to hold back from."
Cam Skattebo on doing a backflip today, days after tabling celebration: “I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul.” pic.twitter.com/vc6qRxfk9u
Harbaugh, meanwhile, offered a bit of a wry/forced/half smile and said, "Yeah, he couldn't help himself, could he? Just couldn't help himself."
He couldn't help himself, could he" 😭 John Harbaugh on Cam Skattebo's backflip pic.twitter.com/hN1dC75Fxo
For now, though, Harbaugh will at least be relieved Skattebo made up for his mistake with a big run and didn't get hurt celebrating. Only time will tell if this was a one-off or if the backflip celebration — like Skattebo on that crucial play — cannot be contained.

title: NFL Week 11 winners and losers: Cowboys offense makes history in get-right win, Steelers slump
summary: Dallas scored on all but one possession in a bounce-back victory, while Pittsburgh's postseason hopes took a hit
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have to light up the scoreboard to win games in 2026, and they did just that in Week 11. The superstars on their offense showed up emphatically in a "gotta have it" kind of game against the Tennessee Titans and, for at least one week, deflected some of the deserved scrutiny that has been trained on the defense all season.
Dallas, therefore, is among the biggest winners of the week across the NFL this week. Sunday's schedule was one where heavy favorites had little to gain but everything to lose, and to the Cowboys' credit, they not only avoided disaster but also took care of business in emphatic fashion. They were not the only team to do so, but they needed that kind of win more than any of the other franchises that entered the week on the right side of a lopsided point spread.
But at the same time, the Pittsburgh Steelers were among the teams to feel the sting of failing to live up to expectations against a beleaguered opponent.
Here are the greatest winners and losers from Sunday's Week 11 action.
The defense is still an issue even after Christian Parker's demotion from play-caller, as evidenced by the 30 points it surrendered to the lowly Titans and the breakdown that allowed Carnell Tate to score one of the strangest touchdowns of the year . But when a team can score at will, what happens on the other side of the ball hardly matters. That was the case for the Cowboys in a 51-30 drubbing of the Titans .
Dallas needed a win in this spot, and they got it in the worst way. A season that is already slipping through its fingers would have only gotten more depressing with a loss to a one-win team. Behind a nearly perfect game from Dak Prescott , CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Javonte Williams and the rest of the offense, the Cowboys avoided disaster by a healthy margin and notched their third win in five games, keeping them very much alive in the NFC East race.
The Cowboys scored on all of their possessions except the final one when they knelt out the clock. They found the end zone seven times and scored a touchdown on each of their first six drives, the franchise's longest run of consecutive possessions ending in a touchdown to open a game in the play-by-play era. Some of that success had to do with the Titans' bleak defensive situation—their 13 straight drives with points allowed dating back to Week 10 were the most in a single season since at least 2000, per NFL research— but just as much with the star power on their own offense.
In the process, Lamb became the first receiver in Cowboys history with six consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. He and Pickens both crossed the 100-yard mark in the blowout.
The last time the Steelers beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the City of Brotherly Love? 1965. Granted, as members of opposite conferences, the in-state rivals only play every few years. But this is a losing streak that now spans 12 games after Sunday's 19-16 result , which went in favor of the Eagles.
This was the kind of matchup that was supposed to help the Steelers bounce back from last week's no-show against the Cincinnati Bengals and work their way back toward the top of the AFC North. Instead, they lost to a team that hadn't won a game since September and started Joe Milton at quarterback. It is far too early to call it a devastating loss, but if the Steelers finish the season a game short of a playoff berth, it is a contest they will look back on as one they should have gotten.
The Carolina Panthers survived a shootout with the Baltimore Ravens that stands competitively among the most entertaining and chaotic games of the season. There were seven lead changes in the contest, including four in a back-and-forth second quarter and two in the final period. The Panthers were responsible for that final go-ahead play: A 37-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald with 1:44 to play. The kick put the NFC South leaders up 35-33.
On a day when every other team in the division either lost or was on a bye, the Panthers capitalized on their opportunity to distance themselves from the pack. They now stand two games clear of the three other squads, all with 3-7 records.
A loss would not have cost Carolina its division lead, but it would have been a difficult pill to swallow, given the Ravens hadn't even led in a game since Oct. 25, before the multiple advantages they held on Sunday. But by taking care of business at home against the reeling Ravens, Carolina improved to .500 on the year and is now looking like a more respectable division leader.
High yardage total aside, Trevor Lawrence had a day to forget. His 301 passing yards were more a product of the large passing volume required of him in a loss than anything else. The New York Giants defense had him pressing in a 23-18 loss and forced him into a number of errors including two interceptions, a pick on a 2-point attempt, three sacks and a whopping 22 incompletions.
Rarely have the Jacksonville Jaguars found themselves in negative game scripts this season. Lawrence was fantastic in one of them (when he threw four touchdowns in a loss to the Houston Texans ) but struggled in two others.
It took until the fourth quarter for Lawrence to lead the Jaguars to a touchdown, but by that point, it was too late. The Giants had already done enough damage in building a 14-point lead. Jacksonville needed Lawrence's typical MVP-caliber passing ability to shine in order to pull off the comeback but did not get it. And as a result, they are behind pace in the battle for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
This deep into such a lengthy and legendary career, Travis Kelce routinely reaches landmarks on team and league leaderboards. Sunday was another historic day for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end. Kelce scored two touchdowns in the 34-7 rout of the Arizona Cardinals and thus hauled in multiple scoring passes for the first time in 47 games. Ending that prolonged drought also moved Kelce up a spot on the NFL tight end career touchdown list.
What better day to make history than the same day on which Kelce became the fourth player in Chiefs history to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead Stadium? That is some serious longevity.
As if the loss to the Eagles was not bad enough for DK Metcalf and the Steelers, the wide receiver made his day even worse with an inexcusable decision. Metcalf had been jawing at Philadelphia defenders all game and took it to another level when he poked Cooper DeJean in the eye a little more than halfway through the third quarter. That exchange drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty (Metcalf's second of the game) and prompted his ejection from the game .
DK Metcalf has been ejected in Philly CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J
Metcalf did not back up his trash talk with his performance. He caught just one pass for 2 yards across four targets.
The NFL fined Metcalf earlier this season for taunting in the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Browns . He also served a two-game suspension last season for getting into a physical altercation with a fan.
The Chicago Bears ' trade deadline blockbuster continues to age to perfection. Jeffery Simmons has been nothing but a superstar since his arrival in the Windy City and turned in his best performance as a Bear in the 21-13 win over the New Orleans Saints . Simmons racked up three sacks for the second time in his career, also recording three tackles for loss in a game for the fourth time. He led a vicious pass rush that got home on Tyler Shough six times.
Each of general manager Ryan Poles' moves ahead of and during the season contributed to where the Bears stand as a contender for the NFC's No. 1 seed. The Simmons trade is the latest and most stupendous example, but Poles made several other transactions that have been just as impactful. The Garrett Bradbury trade added a reliable starter to the middle of the offensive line, and sending DJ Moore out of town for two draft picks opened the door for Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze to flourish as a prolific…

title: Justin Herbert in concussion protocol after loss to Jets: Chargers QB played entire game
summary: Herbert took some big shots late in the game but did not exit
full_text:
Justin Herbert is in the NFL's concussion protocol after the Chargers ' 27-24 loss to the Jets , per the team. It's unclear when Herbert suffered the injury, as he played the whole game, but concussion-like symptoms can appear well after the collisions that cause the concussions themselves.
Because he entered concussion protocol, Herbert did not address the media after the game.
Herbert went 15-for-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 32 yards and a score as well. He took six sacks, though, and has now taken an NFL-high 39 sacks this season.
Herbert has been an ironman, especially considering the hits he has taken in his career behind a seemingly ever-shaky offensive line. Only one injury has forced Herbert to miss a game in his career: A fractured finger on his throwing hand required surgery and cost him the final four contests of the 2023 campaign.
The Chargers (1-9) have had a miserable season, with the much-hyped pairing of Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel failing to mesh. Herbert has thrown just eight touchdown passes compared to 11 interceptions and is on pace for career worsts nearly across the board. He had played his first two turnover-free games of the season — last week in a win over the Ravens and Sunday against New York — but now could miss time depending on how concussion protocol progresses.
If entering the protocol does force Herbert to miss time, the Chargers would turn to DJ Uiagalelei . He has played in one NFL game, in mop-up duty against the Texans in Week 9 . He went 2-for-7 for 24 yards and a touchdown. Los Angeles also has Jake Browning on the practice squad.

title: DK Metcalf's bad season just got worse. What happens now for Steelers embattled receiver?
summary: It's safe for Metcalf to be considered the worst trade acquisition in Steelers history. Now he faces a possible suspension and an uncertain future in Pittsburgh
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made their bed before the trade deadline, and now, they're lying in it.
Sitting at 6-2 at the trade deadline, the Steelers' general manager, Omar Khan, decided not to strengthen his receiving corps or defensive backfield, two areas that could have used reinforcements. Since the deadline, the Steelers have lost consecutive games in embarrassing fashion, and one of their biggest mistakes continues to get exposed: DK Metcalf .
After Philadelphia's 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday, it's safe to say Pittsburgh would have benefitted by getting someone — anyone — at the trade deadline on defense.
Metcalf, the poster child of Pittsburgh's receiving woes, hit a new low on Sunday when he was ejected after committing his second unnecessary conduct penalty of the third quarter. Metcalf had 15 times more penalty yards — yes, 15, 1...5 — than receiving yards (30 to 2) when he was tossed after poking Cooper DeJean in the eye.
DK Metcalf has been ejected in Philly CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/johlxzOD1J
Two weeks ago, the Steelers were considered a shoo-in to make the playoffs. That is anything but the case at the moment. Many questions now surround the 2026 Steelers, starting with their embattled receiver.
After the game, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy was critical of Metcalf, although he didn't say whether he plans to discipline his receiver. "We need him in those games," McCarthy said . "That's not acceptable to get thrown out a game."
Postgame, quarterback Aaron Rodgers added , "I mean that was disappointing. Obviously, we love DK, and I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening, but yeah, we can't have two of those [penalties]."
Metcalf will undoubtedly face further discipline by the NFL . He will surely get fined and may even face a suspension as a repeat offender . Metcalf was fined earlier this season for unnecessary roughness. He was suspended for the final two games of the 2025 regular season after getting into a physical altercation with a Lions fan.
If the NFL decides to suspend Metcalf, he will miss Pittsburgh's upcoming home game against the Broncos on Black Friday. Metcalf could possibly miss the Steelers' Week 13 game against a Texans team that has closed the gap on Pittsburgh in the AFC playoff standings.
If the Steelers lose next week as well, Houston will pass Pittsburgh in the standings if it wins next week and then defeats the Steelers in Week 13. If that happens, the Steelers face an uphill battle just to make the playoffs.
The irony in a possible Metcalf suspension is the fact that he has had little impact when he's been on the field. He came into Sunday's game with just 35 catches for 432 yards and two touchdowns this season. Metcalf's 12.3 yards per reception, 6.2 yards per target and 40.0% success rate on the year would all be career lows if the season ended today.
This follows a season where Metcalf had just 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns in 2025, a career low in receptions and yardage, plus the second-fewest-touchdowns in a season of his career. Following his return from last year's two-game suspension, Metcalf dropped a key pass in the early portions of Pittsburgh's eventual 30-6 loss to Houston in the opening round of the playoffs. It was emblematic of Metcalf's time in Pittsburgh up to that point and ever since.
Metcalf should already be considered the worst trade acquisition in Steelers history. After sending a second-round pick to Seattle, the Steelers gave Metcalf a four-year, $132 million contract. That contract was surprising then, and it's downright laughable now.
What does Metcalf's career in Pittsburgh look like? At this point, it's hard to imagine the Steelers keeping him on board. He's failed to produce as a No. 1 receiver, and his on-field antics haven't helped his cause, either.
It should be pointed out that Metcalf hasn't had much help. They tried to give him more room to work when they acquired Michael Pittman from the Colts this offseason in another trade that has aged horribly. A foot injury has prevented Pittman from making an impact.
A lack of supporting cast, however, does not explain Metcalf's failure to make routine plays. He has seldom come down with contested catches and doesn't appear to be too willing to fight for extra yards. For example, he was tackled a yard short of the sticks on Pittsburgh's first possession Sunday. The Steelers turned it over on downs a play later.
Metcalf's mistakes have also led to turnovers, such as Denzel Ward's interception in Week 8 after Metcalf couldn't come down with Rodgers' deep pass.
If Metcalf's struggles continue during the final weeks of this season, the Steelers will probably try to free themselves of his contract this offseason. They'd likely be willing to trade him for as little as a sixth- or seventh-round pick if a team is willing to take on his salary.
The most likely scenario is the Steelers cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027. While doing so would force the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money, it would save $26.5 million against the cap.
Until then, however, the Steelers will have to continue to lie in the bed they've made. That might mean continuing to give Metcalf opportunities. It might also mean giving other receivers (including Max Hurleman , who caught a touchdown pass on Sunday in what was his regular-season debut) more opportunities to make plays in the coming weeks.
Regardless, the Steelers have to find a way to get more production of their receivers, or their season will end without a playoff win for a 10th straight year.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Week 11 overreactions: Jesse Minter one-and-done? Offensive Player of the Year award winner emerging?
summary: Plus, the Steelers are once again facing a familiar end to their season
full_text:
Thanksgiving week is a true NFL feast — one game Wednesday, three games Thursday, one game Friday and 11 games Sunday — but Week 11 provided a hearty appetizer with several surprises sprinkled in.
How about the most entertaining game being between the Panthers and the Ravens ? Carolina prevailed 35-33 in a game that featured eight lead changes, five turnovers and a kickoff return touchdown. Ryan Fitzgerald hit a game-winning field goal, and the Panthers extended their lead atop the NFC South thanks to a Buccaneers loss in Detroit. Who says two sub-.500 teams playing one another isn't fun?
What decidedly hasn't been fun is the Ravens' season. Baltimore is 4-7 after starting 4-1, and there are major long-term questions for what had been a bastion of winning and stability for years.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Lots of the Ravens' issues are out of first-year coach Jesse Minter's control. The Lamar Jackson injuries, obviously, threw the season way off course. Baltimore has used four different starting quarterbacks. This week, Minter sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home after his comments about Baltimore . Even Sunday's game was another example of the things Minter can't control going wrong. Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell.
But there are plenty of issues Minter has been responsible for—or at least hasn't fixed—this year. Regarded as a defensive whiz after two years as the Chargers ' defensive coordinator, he now oversees a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in yards per game and yards per play, and in the bottom 10 in yards per pass attempt and takeaways. Simply put, it's been underwhelming at best for a team expected to contend for a championship.
Instead of improving as it acclimated to Minter's system, the unit has gotten worse: Baltimore has allowed at least 5.3 yards per play in five straight games, the longest streak in franchise history.
But the Ravens won't fire Minter at season's end. There are big-picture questions about Jackson and the entire roster, but Minter should get an offseason to tweak and improve his defense and fit it better to his defenders. A second brand-new start in two seasons would be very un-Baltimore-like, though one could say this season has been very un-Baltimore-like, too.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Even after a truly awful 19-16 loss to the zombie Eagles , the Steelers are in good shape for the playoffs. They're still 6-4. The only team within one game is the 5-5 Patriots , who won't have Drake Maye until the tail end of the season at the earliest. The 4-6 Texans are within shouting distance but have significant ground to make up. A Week 13 game between Houston and Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh has massive implications.
Regardless, the Steelers are what they have been for years: a low-ceiling operation with a mediocre offense and a solid, opportunistic defense. Thus, their season will end as all their recent seasons have: without a playoff win. Pittsburgh hasn't won a playoff game since January 2017. It's lost seven straight postseason games.
The Steelers are 2-4 on the road, with the offense averaging 17 points. Guess where Pittsburgh would play its playoff opener if it makes the postseason? Aaron Rodgers almost never pushes the ball downfield, and when he does, it's often on perimeter throws with little chance of being completed. When teams lock down on the running game and short passes, this offense has no answer. Pittsburgh is 2-4 when it runs for under 4.9 yards per carry.
What's the definition of insanity? Doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results? Sorry if you feel insane, Steelers fans.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
It wasn't always pretty, but Jahmyr Gibbs ground out 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in the Lions ' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. He's up to 1,502 yards from scrimmage this season and on pace to finish with 2,553. That would break Chris Johnson 's all-time record of 2,509 from 2009.
That, one would think, would clinch an Offensive Player of the Year award for Gibbs. Even if he doesn't break the record, Gibbs would be a deserving winner, so long as he keeps producing. He's had at least 110 yards from scrimmage in all but two games. He had 168 in a win over the Vikings , 58 more than any other running back versus Minnesota this season. Gibbs won't win MVP, because it'll go to a quarterback, but he deserves this major award.
Overreaction or reality: Reality
Baker Mayfield had yet another rough outing. Yes, the two touchdowns to zero interceptions is a good ratio, but he had just 187 passing yards on 33 attempts, and he took four sacks. The sacks are a gigantic issue, as he currently sports an 11.2% sack rate, one of the worst marks in the league.
Injuries and age have sapped Mayfield's improvisational ability, but that's how he plays: a scrambling, improvising gunslinger. It can be exciting, but it can also lead to some really rough moments, and Tampa Bay is getting the latter. Keep in mind, the Buccaneers extended Mayfield with a three-year, $165 million deal just before the season began , after it seemed like an extension wouldn't happen.
Tampa Bay must be wishing it hadn't made the deal. Mayfield is constantly banged up — he's dealing with plantar fasciitis in addition to the thumb injury that caused him to miss several games already this year — and he can't physically make his play style work. How the Buccaneers overcome this is TBD, because there are no realistic easy answers. The defense, plus the awful NFC South, means the team won't be picking super early any time soon. Tampa Bay, like Pittsburgh, is stuck in no-man's-land.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
Almost every very good team has a bad loss. They happen. The Jaguars ' 23-18 loss to the Giants was a bad one — not because the Giants are bad, but because the Jaguars looked bad.
The offensive line got dominated all game. Left tackle Walker Little , already filling in for Anton Harrison (torn ACL), also left the game. Center Robert Hainsey (knee sprain) missed the game and is week-to-week, and guard Patrick Mekari (back) hasn't played this season. The depleted unit had fits with Abdul Carter on the edge and with D.J. Reader on the interior. The team had no push in the run game, which had its worst success rate of the season.
Trevor Lawrence took three sacks and threw the ball 47 times, often after narrowly escaping pressure. Ultimately, his valiant attempt to put the team on his back proved unsuccessful. Lawrence was pressured 22 times, per initial PFF tracking.
Jacksonville lost 9.6 expected points on dropbacks, by far its worst performance of the year. In fact, it has only been below zero one other time. Jacksonville also had nine offensive penalties, four by offensive linemen.
The defense settled in, but several errant J.J. McCarthy passes when he had open targets really helped in that regard. Pricy trade-deadline acquisition Jordan Davis had one assisted tackle. For someone acquired for a first-round pick and a second-round pick, that's not enough. Jacksonville did not turn McCarthy over and sacked him just once.
Are the Jaguars in huge trouble? No. But this isn't a loss to chalk up to as "one of those days." Liam Coen has his work cut out for him.
Overreaction or reality: Overreaction
The Jets ended a five-game losing streak with a tidy 27-24 win over the Chargers. How tidy?
If the teams are bad and the result is meaningless for the playoff picture, it's nice for the game to be either 1.) super entertaining, or 2.) super quick. Thank you for the latter, New York and Los Angeles.
Anyway, it was nice to see Aaron Glenn overjoyed with the victory. They all matter and should feel meaningful, even if they come amid another lost season. The coaches and players work too hard for that to not be the case.
Still, in the…

title: DK Metcalf ejected: Steelers WR tossed after poking Cooper DeJean in the eye, could face suspension

full_text:
DK Metcalf's forgettable 2026 season hit a new low during Sunday's game between the Steelers and Eagles .
Metcalf was ejected from the game after he appeared to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye in the third quarter. It was Metcalf's second unsportsmanlike penalty of the game, which led to his ejection. His first unnecessary roughness penalty occurred early in the third quarter after he got into a shoving match with the Eagles' defense.
Sunday's ejection marks Metcalf's third of his eight-season career since 2019, which puts him in jeopardy of being suspended as a repeat offender. His first ejection came in Week 10 of the 2021 season in a 17-0 loss at the Green Bay Packers when Metcalf grabbed Packers safety Henry Black's facemask during an altercation. That led to him being ejected for fighting, and he was fined $6,949 at the time.
#Seahawks WR DK Metcalf has been ejected after this altercation with #Packers DB Henry Black. pic.twitter.com/Ry1jdhIOpd
In Week 14 of the 2023 season, Metcalf fought San Francisco 49ers All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner. He body slammed Warner into the turf before grabbing the linebacker's facemask when fighting. He was ejected in the Seahawks' 28-16 defeat that day and fined $19,123 for fighting. The eight-year veteran was fined $11,941 by the NFL for taunting following Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Browns . He was suspended for the final two regular-season games of the 2025 season after getting into a physical altercation with a Lions fan, an incident in which Metcalf was sued but ultimately not charged .  Metcalf returned for Pittsburgh's AFC wild card game against the Texans , but he had a costly drop early in the game that set the tone for Pittsburgh's 30-6 loss. The NFL league office will certainly be reviewing his latest interaction with DeJean to determine his latest fine amount and/or whether or not a suspension is warranted.
"They say it's going to a good cause, so I might as well win Walter Payton Man of the Year," Metcalf said this summer when asked if he is tired of giving money to the NFL via fines. "So no, I'm not tired of it."
Metcalf appeared to be frustrated with the Eagles' physicality downfield on Sunday. Philadelphia's secondary blanketed him on an incomplete pass moments before his altercation with DeJean.

Metcalf's 12.3 yards per reception, 6.2 yards per target and 40.0% success rate on the year would all be career lows if the season ended today.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans ends in historic scorigami after late Tennessee touchdown
summary: The Cowboys' 51-30 victory became the 1,101st unique final score in NFL history after a late Titans touchdown
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and Tennessee Titans played one of the wildest games of Week 11, and it ended with the two teams combining to make some NFL history. The Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30, which is notable because it marked the first time that exact final score occurred in the NFL's 107-year history.
The scorigami only happened because the Titans scored a garbage-time touchdown with less than one minute in the game. With Tennessee trailing 51-23, Cam Ward hit Calvin Ridley for a 12-yard touchdown pass, and at that point, the Titans decided to kick the extra point. If the kick had missed, there wouldn't have been a scorigami, because 51-29 has happened before, but Joey Slye's kick went through and that ultimately gave us the 1,101st final score in NFL history.
TEN 30 - DAL 51 | 0:31 left in 4th 👀 Scorigami Watch 100% chance, most likely Scorigami: 51-30
If the Titans hadn't gotten into the end zone on their final drive, the game wouldn't have ended in a scorigami, because 51-23 has happened before. If the Titans had successfully gone for two, we also wouldn't have gotten a scorigami, because 51-31 has happened before.
For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen and that was certainly the case here. The main thing that happened is that the Cowboys offense went off. Dak Prescott totaled five touchdowns on a day when the Cowboys scored seven. If you throw in a Brandon Aubrey field goal, that's how the Cowboys got to 51, and any time you see a team put up at least 50 points, there's always a solid chance of a scorigami.
The Cowboys missed a two-point conversion in this game, but that didn't matter, because even if they had hit it, 53-30 would have also been a scorigami.
On the Titans' end, the garbage-time touchdown played a big part in the scorigami, but the only reason Tennessee got to 30 points is that they scored one of the craziest touchdowns of the season.
Nobody touched Carnell Tate and he scores! TENvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cQ7sadUDLH
That's Carnell Tate going 59 yards for a score after not being touched by the Cowboys' defense .
This marks the second straight week that the Cowboys have been involved in a scorigami. They also had a unique final score in their 46-40 loss to the 49ers . This marks the first time since 2016 that a team has been involved in scorigami in back-to-back games (the 49ers did it in Weeks 2 and 3 that season).
Not to be outdone, this is also Tennessee's second scorigami of the season. The Titans were also involved in one back in a 43-36 loss to the Bengals in Week 8. This means the Titans' last two road games have both ended in a scorigami.
Overall, there have been six scorigamis this year, already more than we saw in the entire 2025 season (five). This is turning into the year of the scorigami.
author: John Breech

title: Derrick Henry injury: Ravens star RB clears concussion protocol after leaving game post-TD
summary: Baltimore avoids yet another key loss to injury
full_text:
Running back Derrick Henry left the Ravens ' eventual 35-33 loss to the Panthers to be evaluated for a concussion and did not return, but he cleared protocol after leaving the field, per the Baltimore Banner's Giana Han .
Henry suffered the injury on a touchdown run that gave Baltimore a late lead. His head hit the ground hard as he landed in the end zone.
TOUCHDOWN @KingHenry_2 !!! Tune on on FOX. pic.twitter.com/71Uo8Gzbdo
The Panthers scored a go-ahead field goal on their next possession, and Tyrel Dodson sealed the deal by picking off Jacoby Brissett— the fourth quarterback to start a game for Baltimore this season—on a desperation heave.
Henry ran 13 times for 94 yards—his most since Week 5, and a stark improvement from last week when he had 10 carries for 10 yards—but it was in yet another losing effort. Baltimore has lost six straight games after starting the season 4-1.
It's been a difficult year for Baltimore in its first season under new coach Jesse Minter. Lamar Jackson has appeared in just five games due to ankle and thumb injuries; the latter is currently sidelining him and will likely keep him out for several more weeks, if not the rest of the season.
Henry has 198 carries for 793 yards and 11 touchdowns this season. His 4.0 yards per carry are on pace for a career low.
Should Henry miss time, the Ravens would feature Justice Hill more. Typically a change-of-pace receiving back, Hill had 96 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown in the loss. Baltimore also has running backs Rasheen Ali and Adam Randall on the roster.

title: Could former Colts QB Daniel Jones be claimed today? Clear waivers? The Cardinals are said to be in the mix
summary: The Indianapolis Colts shocked everybody in the NFL when they outright released their starting quarterback Daniel Jones after a lackluster performance against the Houston Texans. Jones had signed a two-year $88 million extension in the spring of this year. The contract was the largest two-year deal in NFL history. Jones, age 29, will find out […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts throws the ball during the first half against the Miami Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts shocked everybody in the NFL when they outright released their starting quarterback Daniel Jones after a lackluster performance against the Houston Texans. Jones had signed a two-year $88 million extension in the spring of this year. The contract was the largest two-year deal in NFL history. Jones, age 29, will find out on Monday at 4 p.m. ET if he clears waivers. Any team that claims him will have to continue his contract. If he clears waivers, any club can then sign him to the NFL veteran minimum, similar to what occurred with former Cardinals QB Kyler Murray when he inked a similar deal with the Minnesota Vikings. RELATED: SHOULD THE CARDINALS BE INTERESTED IN JONES? It is estimated that Jones might wait to sign with another team, according to ESPN . He may want to get the right opportunity with the right team instead of just signing with any club in order to get back on the field immediately. Teams that have interest include the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots, and Arizona. Jones is expected to have options. Apparently, the Colts did not want to keep him in a state of flux once they decided not to play him anymore this season. If the Cardinals really want Jones, they must put in a claim for him, which currently own the #7 waiver claim spot. But his huge contract will accompany him. If he clears waivers, the Colts will have to pay all of the remaining salary due to him. What has been the big mystery is why Indy didn’t trade him before the NFL trade deadline and gotten something for him instead of just releasing him outright and receiving nothing in return. Jones had trade value and several NFL clubs were seeking an experienced signalcaller. Jones (6’-5”, 230 pounds) led the league this year in interceptions with 13, so there’s that. But he has plenty of experience during his eight seasons in the league. This season, he was named the starter for Week 1. Jones started all 11 games for a listless offensive unit which has been selling off their key players. Their offensive line is absolutely porous. This year, Jones hasn’t had any time to throw and has paltry production such as 144 (twice) yards, 108 (twice), 143, and 166 in games. He has thrown seven touchdowns against 13 interceptions. Jones was taken with the sixth overall selection in the 2019 NFL Draft by the New York Football Giants after a standout career at Duke. He was supposed to be the future after Eli Manning retired. In 2022, Jones made NFL history by becoming the first player ever with 300+ passing yards, 2+ touchdown passes, and 70+ rushing yards in a playoff game. For his eight-year career, Jones’ stats: 94 games with 93 starts, 1,903 completions on 2,976 attempts for 19,657 yards, converted 979 first downs, 96 TDs, 68 picks, a 63.9% completion ratio, sacked 257 times, an 84.1 QB rating, and a 35-57-1 starting win-loss record. He is a very good runner with 478 carries for 2,441 yards with another 21 scores. By claiming Jones, it could mean the Cardinals would have a capable quarterback for their remaining games this season who would compete with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck in training camp next year.

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Chiefs Winners & Losers: Arizona taken to the woodshed – again
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs, who are one of the best teams in the AFC as well as in the league. They have a great offense. Perhaps they are looking beyond the matchup against the Cardinals since they are playing the one-loss Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day. The […]
full_text: LB Jack Gibbens #50 of the Arizona Cardinals (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs, who are one of the best teams in the AFC as well as in the league. They have a great offense. Perhaps they are looking beyond the matchup against the Cardinals since they are playing the one-loss Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day. The Cardinals came into this game starting their fourth quarterback of the young season. The NFL record is five, so, there’s that. RELATED: CARDINALS GET BLOWN OUT IN LOSS Arizona At the final gun, the Cardinals were never in the game as they were beaten pretty badly in the first half, then allowed the Chiefs to coast to a 34-7 win. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS LB Jack Gibbens – Mr. Dependable for the Cardinals had another good day along the defense as he led all defenders with 10 total tackles. Stopped RB Emmett Johnson for just a two yard gain in the first quarter that ended up being three points instead of six. As WR Xavier Worthy was rumbling downfield in the third quarter, Gibbens came from behind to tackle the receiver after a 20-yard gain that could have been a touchdown. On a third-and-five with 2:31 left in the game, Gibbens nailed RB Nate Carter for just a two-yard gain, which forced a punt. P Blake Gillikin – Probably the offense’s MVP today. Had three punts downed inside the 20 with one on the three and another at the one yard line. Six punts for 241 yards with a 40.2 average and a long of 55 yards. He was more focused on pinning the Chiefs deep than his net average. Nice work. WR Harrison Wallace III – Somebody has to be listed as having a great game, so here is the undrafted rookie playing well despite not being named the starter and coming up with good plays. In the first quarter with Arizona driving on a third-six, Wallace turned a short pass into a 25-yard gain to the KC 26-yard line. He got 10 yards in the third quarter and then on the same drive facing a third-and-five, he caught the short pass to the right for 10 more yards to keep the drive going. Led all receivers with 7 targets, 4 receptions for 57 yards, and a 14.3 yards per catch average. Nice day at the office. Third-and-two stop – It looked like Kansas City was going to run away with this game when they faced a third-and-two with 7:36 left in Quarter 3. The ball was handed to RB Emmett Johnson who was stuffed by DTs Walter Nolen and Roy Lopez for no gain that led to a punt. 9 ➡️ 80 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/hnnKqCZBGg — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 22, 2026 Second drive of the game – KR Max Melton got a decent return to set up Arizona at the Cardinals’ 37. Two short passes gained a first down. Then Wallace hauled in the 25-yarder to the Chiefs’ 48. A sack, then two short passes and two short runs placed the ball at the KC eight yard line as TE Trey McBride converted a third-and-five by gaining six. QB Josh Johnson found WR Simi Fehoko crossing in the end zone for six. The score was now 14-7 Kansas City. It just felt good at that moment, didn’t it? ——————————————————————————— GEEKS Covering #87 – With TE Travis Kelce being the Chiefs main pass catcher and a fav target of QB Patrick Mahomes, it would make sense for DC Nick Rallis to come up with a great gameplan to eliminate the talented tight end from the game, right? So, whose responsibility was to cover Kelce? Well, nobody. We don't know about you, but we're feeling like a 22-yard TD reception by @tkelce 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/A2dYZcQJXo — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 22, 2026 And nobody covered him all game. That was the gameplan? Passes to Kelce moved the chains all first half, not to mention he scored two touchdowns, both he was wide open. On his first touchdown in the first quarter, LB Mack Wilson was trailing Kelce the entire time so all Mahomes had to do was zip it in there. With 2:27 left in the first quarter, Kelce gained 13 yards but was not covered. He caught a ball that got 14 early in the second quarter, and was tackled after getting good running yardage but no coverage on the pass. 13 yards on a TE screen. Another TD catch that he was open in the second quarter. Kelce was not challenged all day, and chipped, then released and found open areas all game long. 7 targets, 6 catches for 74 yards and two touchdowns. CB Kei’Trel Clark – With 7:14 remaining before the half, Clark played well off WR Josh Downs, then bit on the arm cock of Mahomes. Downs then simply ran past Clark for a 26-yard gain. In the first quarter, Clark dropped a sure interception. He gave up nine yards in the second quarter to RB Emmett Johnson by yet again, giving a large cushion and 13-yards to WR Josh Downs on a third-and-10. That drive ended in another Chiefs TD. Five total tackles, mostly from chasing down the receiver after he made a large gain. Offense first half – The Chiefs had 152 yards on offense in the first quarter and 295 at the half. The Cardinals had 13 yards on offense in the first quarter and 78 yards in the first half. 21 first downs for KC, five for Arizona. Nine rushing yards for the Cardinals whereas the Chiefs had 69. Trey McBride three catches for 17 yards. Time of possession: Kansas City – 20:06, Arizona – 9:54. Score: 27-7. Yeah, all of this in just two quarters. Fourth and one play – As the second quarter was winding down, the Cardinals had a third-and-2 at their own 36 yard line behind just 17-7. A Bam Knight run made just one yard. Run out the punt team, right? Their own 37 yard line, correct? Down just 10 points, correcto? That would be a negative. Instead, a jet sweep by WR Simi Fehoko was ordered who gained nothing. It was Fehoko’s first carry of the year by the way. Turnover of downs, and a subsequent Chiefs TD in just three downs that moved the scoreboard to 24-7. One word: completely dumb. Okay, that’s two words. Best quote of the game – As the Chiefs moved up and down the field and scored on all five possessions in the first half, TV announcer Ian Eagle stated, “The Chiefs are doing whatever they want.” Let’s finish this thing 🤝 pic.twitter.com/IJYbLNSafZ — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 22, 2026 RT Josh Fryar – The backup tackle had no answer for #56, DE George Karlaftis, who was in the offensive backfield all game it seemed. Johnson was sacked three times, as Karlaftis had 2.5 sacks, 4 tackles, 2 tackles for loss, and a whopping 5 QB hits. Fryar just could not stop the outside speed of Karlaftis. His sack with 11:08 left in the third quarter killed a good drive which ended in yet another Gillikin punt. Last three games – The Cardinals offensive production in the final three games: 3 points, 6 points, and 7 points. With the escalation, does that mean this offense is improving? ———————————————————————————– Bird Seed – Always remember you’re unique, just like everyone else CB/KR Max Melton – Had two good kickoff returns, one for 37 yards while the other was for 36 yards. E$ runs it in for his 5th TD of the season (and 4th game in a row)! pic.twitter.com/VA599QZpGb — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 22, 2026 Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson – At Nebraska, Johnson was a First Team All-American and was named the “Big 10 RB of the Year” plus voted First Team All-Big 10. He was taken in the fifth round. Instead of taking an elite pass rusher with the third overall pick, or an offensive tackle, the Cardinals took Notre Dame RB Jeremiyah Love, who is on IR with repetitive ankle issues and has played sparingly. Johnson just ran for his second consecutive 100-yard game where he scored in both contests and has a rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. title: Can Michael Penix be fixed by the Atlanta Falcons?
summary: The 2026 Atlanta Falcons have a 3-7 record, a 1-5 home record, a -57 point differential, a -0.14 offensive EPA per play… and because they reside in the NFC South, they are actually one good run away from competing for the division. But if they are going to find that good run, they’ll need to […]
full_text: Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images | Getty Images The 2026 Atlanta Falcons have a 3-7 record, a 1-5 home record, a -57 point differential, a -0.14 offensive EPA per play… and because they reside in the NFC South, they are actually one good run away from competing for the division. But if they are going to find that good run, they’ll need to fix whatever the heck has happened to quarterback Michael Penix Jr. of late. Penix returned to the field in Week 3 after recovering from the partially torn ACL he suffered in November 2025, and things went rather well for a while. Weeks 3-7, to be exact. After that, everything fell apart. Attempts Completions Completion % Pass Yards Yards per Attempt TD INT Sacks Passer Rating EPA per Dropback Pressure Rate (%) Weeks 3-7 144 96 66.7 1157 8 9 1 9 109.1 0.112 29.3 Weeks 8-10 98 51 52 573 5.8 1 6 3 47.7 -0.402 31.8 It’s unexpected, to say the least. After a Week 7 performance against the San Francisco 49ers in which he completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions, a passer rating of 118.9, and an EPA per pass of +0.26 — and was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his trouble in a 29-20 Falcons win — Penix fell off in ways nobody could have imagined. The first bad trip came in Atlanta’s 16-0 Week 8 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Both teams were playing in monsoon conditions, but that doesn’t excuse what was Penix’s worst game as a professional quarterback. He completed 8 of 24 passes for 125 yards, no touchdowns, four interceptions, a passer rating of 12.0, and an EPA per pass of -1.09. And then, in losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Kansas City Chiefs in Weeks 9 and 10, Penix combined for 43 completions on 74 attempts for 448 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, a passer rating of 69.0, and an EPA per pass of -0.34. Okay, so… what happened? First, let’s go back to that 49ers win and see what Penix was doing right. He was throwing accurately within the timing of the routes, he was going through his progressions, he was using play-action like a boss, he was rolling out to great effect, and he looked calm and ready no matter the circumstances. This is the Penix we expected, right? Michael Penix Jr. on October 25. Your NFC Offensive Player of the Week. Where did THIS guy go? pic.twitter.com/Zgb4rx4tZV — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 21, 2026 “We knew with this defense, they don’t really give up too many explosives,” Penix said after the 49ers game. “They do a good job with that. So for us, I just had to be smart and find my checkdowns, find the guys that [were] open, and obviously deliver a good ball for them. So, that’s all it was about. Just making sure we didn’t make any mistakes. Just go out there and play our brand of football.” Quick game was a big part of the plan. Penix completed 16 of 20 passes with 2.5 seconds or less in the pocket for 144 yards, two touchdowns, and a passer rating of 130.0. Head coach Kevin Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees gave him the answers to the test with a lot of defined first reads, and that gave Penix the confidence he needed. Now, fast-forward to Week 8 against the Bucs. It wasn’t just the weather that held Penix back — Tampa Bay head coach Todd Bowles and his staff did an absolutely marvelous job of changing the picture from pre- to post-snap, and Penix never really got the hang of it. Linebacker Alex Anzalone grabbed two of Penix’s four picks with these disguised looks, where Penix was expecting Anzalone to be in one place… and Anzalone was in another place when Penix decided to throw the ball. If you can't see late linebacker drops well enough to react in that split millisecond, you are not going to have a very bright future as an NFL quarterback. pic.twitter.com/PByVFaFVpU — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 21, 2026 The Bucs also flipped their safeties from single-high to two-high post-snap and vice versa, and they capped Penix’s underneath reads. Total clampdown. This is what you would expect from a defense that currently ranks first in DVOA . “Yeah, the first one was a good play,” Penix said postgame of Anzalone’s two interceptions. “My back was to him, I turned around, threw the ball and he just dropped underneath Drake [London]. The second one, that’s a good play again – there are no excuses. I’ve got to protect the ball. They didn’t do anything special.” These things are indeed nothing special in today’s NFL, but if you can’t live in the world of coverage switches and simulated pressures, the NFL is going to spit you out and move along. The Bucs blitzed at a 36% rate and only generated pressure 24% of the time. Which tells you that the plan was more about confusing Penix with spacing, as opposed to just going after him all the time. Penix threw three of his interceptions from a clean pocket. What’s to learn from this? Penix needs a quicker second-reaction plan when defenders switch and drop post-snap. Atlanta’s 34-17 loss to the Bengals in Week 9 saw a better Penix — hey, it couldn’t be much worse. He completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards, one touchdown, one interception, a passer rating of 74.9, and an EPA per pass of -0.1. Cincinnati’s defense did a great job of plastering Penix’s targets in space, and he responded the right way: When the defense gives you holes in the middle of the field, take off and run. Penix did so three times on scrambles for 50 yards. It wasn’t enough to keep up with Joe Burrow playing at his usual nuclear level, but it did provide a bit of a spark. The Bengals had a coverage-first plan against Michael Penix Jr., so Penix did the smart thing: He used his legs to advance things. pic.twitter.com/w46WK1EfwN — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 21, 2026 “I felt good out there,” he said of using his legs when other options weren’t available. “Whenever I found a lane, I was able to scramble and get a couple first downs. I get that a lot about me not really scrambling much. Today that’s what I felt like we needed in those situations, so I took advantage of it.” What’s to learn from this? Penix needs to use his mobility more often when the need arises. Tethering him to the pocket doesn’t always work. Then, there was the Week 10 disaster against the Chiefs. Game script put this in Penix’s hands, as Kansas City had a 28-3 (sorry) fourth-quarter lead — the Falcons were never really in this one. Penix completed 23 of 43 passes in the 35-13 loss for 286 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of 64.7, and an EPA per pass of -0.5. As the pass-heavy necessities became clear, Penix had some issues. And those issues were not helped by the route concepts. Penix has a tendency to speed up his process when things go sideways, and that was the case in this game. He missed first-read flat routes, he threw off-time and off-target too often, and he generally didn’t seem in sync. What Penix has from a route combination perspective is pretty rudimentary. There’s a lot of four verts, some simple two-man crossers, and a lot of iso routes where one pattern doesn’t help another. If you compare the Stefanski/Rees passing game to what Ben Johnson, Sean McVay, and Kyle Shanahan put on the field, there’s a cohesiveness to their offenses that the Falcons simply do not have, and Penix would benefit from the designed openings you get from those types of offenses. Stefanski has moved Rees from the booth to the field, and he’s getting more and more questions from the media about a possible coordinator change. “I think it’s just very important that you pull everything apart in a bye week when you look at it,” Stefanski said on Nov. 17, as the bye week began. “You get under the hood, and you find out areas that need our attention. Now you do that every week. I think the misnomer is that you wait till the bye week to do self-scout; you’re doing it every week. But with the amount of time that you have, and you’re not game planning for the next week, you can really put a fresh set of…

title: NFC South standings: Falcons move ahead of the Saints on Atlanta’s bye week
summary: The Falcons are on their bye this week, but play continued in Week 11 for the rest of the NFC South — and it did shake up the standings a bit in a good way for the Falcons. The Panthers were the only NFC South team to win on Sunday, escaping with a narrow 2-point […]
full_text: Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images | Getty Images The Falcons are on their bye this week, but play continued in Week 11 for the rest of the NFC South — and it did shake up the standings a bit in a good way for the Falcons. The Panthers were the only NFC South team to win on Sunday, escaping with a narrow 2-point win over the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens and moving their record to 5-5. Carolina stays on top of the NFC South, and thanks to the other two teams losing, the Panthers extend their division lead to two games. The Buccaneers were facing the Lions in Detroit, and they lost 31-21. The Saints faced off against the Chicago Bears, and they lost 13-21. That evens up the Bucs, Saints, and Falcons at 3-7 through 11 weeks, and thanks to Atlanta’s head-to-head tiebreaker over New Orleans, the Saints drop down to the basement of this weird division. The Falcons are still eligible for the 2026 NFL playoffs, though I would not hold your breath. Fanduel Sportsbook has Atlanta’s odds to make the playoffs at +700, and while the Panthers’ two-game lead isn’t insurmountable with seven games left to play, I don’t think anyone who’s watched the Falcons play over the past few weeks is holding their breath for that outcome.
