summary: The Cleveland Browns get to enjoy their bye week with no chance of being knocked out of their current NFL playoff position. Sunday’s slate of games is far from exciting for general NFL fans, with a few games that Browns fans will pay attention to because of playoff scenarios. There isn’t even “Rams Watch” for […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns get to enjoy their bye week with no chance of being knocked out of their current NFL playoff position . Sunday’s slate of games is far from exciting for general NFL fans, with a few games that Browns fans will pay attention to because of playoff scenarios. There isn’t even “Rams Watch” for 2027 NFL draft reasons , as the Los Angeles Rams join Cleveland and four other teams on a bye this week. Looking back at the Browns big Week 10 victory , which set the NFL to flex Week 12’s matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders to Sunday Night Football , three players have a little less money in their pockets. The league’s weekly tradition of handing down fines almost a week later continued for Week 10, with two Texans and one Browns player fined for their actions: DT Sam Kamara – Unnecessary Roughness – Use of Helmet – $6,750 WR Nico Collins – Unsportsmanlike Conduct – Violent Gesture – $14,926 DB MJ Stewart – Unnecessary Roughness – Facemask – $11,667 The “violent gesture” Collins was fined for was this celebration, which was also penalized in the game: The NFL fined Texans WR Nico Collins $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (violent gesture) while celebrating Dalton Schultz’s touchdown last week in Cleveland. Collins was also flagged. pic.twitter.com/TEn8qM8NvK — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 21, 2026 For the season so far, the NFL has levied 263 fines, on just over one percent of plays run this season.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans Stock Report: Dak Prescott provides masterclass performance
summary: A win is a win. That gets old fast, especially when you don’t have one that feels like a big one, but it is true for the Dallas Cowboys of this moment nevertheless. Dallas took care of business and then some against the Tennessee Titans, and with Thanksgiving Day ahead, they will now have a […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A win is a win. That gets old fast, especially when you don’t have one that feels like a big one, but it is true for the Dallas Cowboys of this moment nevertheless. Dallas took care of business and then some against the Tennessee Titans, and with Thanksgiving Day ahead, they will now have a chance to build upon it as the stretch run of the season approaches. Before we get too far ahead of ourselves we need to properly put away what we just witnessed. The Tennessee Titans are not a good team, but they are still an NFL team. The Cowboys did what you are supposed to do against teams of this variety and vanquished them with ease. Our stock report as a result of it all is fully positive. Happy holidays and what not! Stock Up: Mike Pettine Sunday was Mike Pettine’s first time calling defensive plays in literally a handful of years. He was obviously around the Cowboys for a few weeks before it, but like everybody involved he also had to manage the awkwardness that was last week and the Christian Parker situation. We hardly witnessed the most unbelievable defensive performance ever, but outside of one silly moment (it was very silly) where Dallas let up, they were mostly a professional football team on defense. Ultimatley the point here is that it was improvement. The bar was low. All that jazz. Stock Up: Brian Schottenheimer The Cowboys offense scored on literally every single possession. There are a lot of people who deserve credit for that and the offensive play-caller is certainly one of them. What’s more is that this past week was difficult for the Cowboys as mentioned. Brian Schottenheimer made a change, a messy one to be clear, but he was proven right in the smallest sample size possible. Everyone needed a win like the Cowboys just got, Brian Schottenheimer most of all. Stock Up: Dak Prescott We can talk about the state of the NFC East and all that stuff, but so long as Dak Prescott is playing the way that he is then the Dallas Cowboys have a chance if they get in. The quarterback position matters that much. Obviously dak’s stat line was incredible, but his disposition is what really stood out to me. Dak charged up the middle and into the teeth of the Tennessee defense early on for a fourth-down conversion. He lowered his shoulder to reach the endzone on his rushing touchdown. He dove for a first down after that. Prescott appears to recognize more than anybody how precious time is, how it is fleeting, and that capitalizing on his right now is of the utmost importance. He played like that on Sunday. Stock Up: Javonte Williams The Cowboys offense has been so prolific as of late and a lot of it has been action through the air. As a result of the fanfare we tend to lose sight of how the run game is working out, and while it is not the most stout in the NFL it is in very capable hands with Javonte Williams. He was on the other sideline on Sunday, but the Cowboys never reached a real point of stability with Tony Pollard. That was obviously partly the team’s fault. I say that to say Williams is arguably the most stable backfield presence that Dallas has had since the peak of the Ezekiel Elliott days. It feels like it has been forever since they have been this reliable in this way. Stock Up: Every pass catcher CeeDee Lamb. George Pickens. Javonte Williams (again). Brevyn Spann-Ford. Sunday was an absolute party if you were a pass-catcher on the Cowboys roster. It is great to see how many options exist. We pay so much attention to Lamb and Picken exclusively, but the group at large is top-notch. Stock Up: Brevyn Spann-Ford At the risk of being redundant, Spann-Ford deserves his own shout out. It remains to be seen what the full future is going to hold for the tight end position on the Cowboys with regards to him and Jake Ferguson, but his role continues to grow and develop. He is TE1 right now. Stock Up: James Houston The Cowboys got to Cam Ward a handful of times on Sunday and a pair of them belonged to James Houston. We have certainly seen Houston flash at different points in the past, and many have long argued that he could be most successful when part of a bevy of pass rushers. Sunday was actual proof of that. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams Another pair of sacks belonged to Quinnen Williams, not to mention the forced fumble that he caused to put even more ice on top of the game at the end. Williams has been the most dominant defensive player on the Cowboys in a while. Obviously the peak of a certain player traded away was quite special, but Williams is coming close to that territory. If you have been around long enough to pine for presence along the interior, it is an incredible joy that Dallas actually has it. Quinnen rules. Stock Up: Aggression in general It is easy to be aggressive when things are not going your way, but it is harder to keep the disposition when they do not. Early in the game the Cowboys had a chance to go for two after a penalty on Tennessee after a touchdown, and they did not get it. Recent history has shown that Schottenheimer takes his foot off of the gas in those instances. That was not the case here. The Cowboys showed up on Sunday to vanquish the Titans at all possible costs. That is what we want to see be the disposition of the team at every waking moment. Stock Up: Shemar James We have obviously hyped up a lot of different Cowboys linebackers over time, and that is far from my intention here. It is worth saying though that Shemar James has been playing quite well. James is also handling more work and responsibility while thriving which is impressive to see. The Cowboys need their Day 3 picks to produce into players like that long-term and James being someone of that variety would go such a long way.

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys win over the Titans
summary: Every now and then, the Dallas Cowboys remind us that they have some serious talent. Facing a struggling Tennessee Titans squad, the Cowboys took care of business in a convincing 51-30 victory that was relatively stress-free, something fans haven’t had in a while. Beating up on a bad team won’t make everything better, but it […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Every now and then, the Dallas Cowboys remind us that they have some serious talent. Facing a struggling Tennessee Titans squad, the Cowboys took care of business in a convincing 51-30 victory that was relatively stress-free, something fans haven’t had in a while. Beating up on a bad team won’t make everything better, but it is hard to complain when they pull off a 20+ point win. The Cowboys lit it up from start to finish, leaving fans with a lot of things to be happy about. Here are 10 thoughts on the Cowboys’ win on Sunday. 1. Unstoppable offense The offense was phenomenal on Sunday. Yes, it came against a bad Titans defense, but you really couldn’t have asked this unit to do much more than it did. Dallas scored on every single offensive possession of the afternoon, minus the final kneel down, totaling an eye-popping 51 points. Dak Prescott was brilliant the pocket, completing 85% of his passes while spreading the wealth effortlessly. Both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens feasted on the Tennessee secondary, with each receiver eclipsing the 100-yard mark. When the passing game operates with that kind of rhythm and efficiency, this offense looks impossible to stop. 2. Historic opening The Cowboys won the coin toss and arrogantly elected to take the ball first. Usually, that’s not a favorable decision, but when the offense responds by scoring a touchdown on its first six possessions, we can’t complain too much. This marked the first time in Cowboys history that the offense has ever opened a game with six straight touchdown drives. 3. Weird two-point call The Cowboys are just so weird sometimes. After scoring their first touchdown of the game, Titans defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers got flagged for a personal foul. Dallas wisely accepted the penalty to move the ball up to the one-yard line and opted to go for two, which made sense. What didn’t make sense was unwisely lining up in the shotgun with four wide receivers and throwing the ball. They didn’t convert. It was a bizarre decision to go that route, though it was about the only thing the Cowboys’ offense did wrong in the game. 4. Backfield depth The Cowboys previously found a nice complementary runner in Tyler Goodson, who put together a strong 77-yard performance before getting hurt against the Colts a couple of weeks ago. Last week, the coaching staff tried to fill that void with Israel Abanikanda, but he managed only eight yards rushing. This week, Jashaun Corbin stepped up and rushed for 34 yards at an impressive 6.4 yards per carry. Beyond running the ball well, Corbin also made a crucial play in pass protection by picking up a blitz that allowed Dak to connect deep with Pickens, setting up a 1st-and-goal inside the five-yard line. 5. More backups chip in It was also a nice showing for the depth players in the tight end room. Brevyn Spann-Ford hauled in his first touchdown catch of the season, while backup tight end James Mitchell showed up early in the game with a couple of receptions, totaling 40 yards. It wasn’t anything major, but it is encouraging to see that the team’s primary blocking tight ends can sneak out into routes and help move the chains when needed. 6. Home sack streak There are not a lot of good things one can say about the Cowboys defense this year, so we have to give credit where it is due. One clear positive is that this unit has been doing a great job creating more pressure on opposing quarterbacks. After a slow start to the year, the pass rush has recently picked up steam. The Cowboys have now recorded five sacks in three straight home games, marking the first time that has happened in Dallas since the 2008 season. 7. Quinnen dominates again Quinnen Williams continues to ball out, showing up once again as his usual disruptive self in the middle of the defensive line. He set the tone early by starting the game with deflected passes at the line of scrimmage, doing it not once, but twice. He also blew up a play with a nice tackle for a loss deep in the Titans’ backfield. Williams also got in on the sack party with two takedowns of his own, including a strip-sack that forced a fumble and resulted in a huge return for the defense. 8. Houston is a problem Edge rusher James Houston is officially on a November heater. After not playing more than 10 snaps in any of the team’s first seven games, he has now logged at least 20 snaps in each of the last four contests. More importantly, he has made every bit of that extra playing time count. Houston has racked up 3.5 sacks over his last four games, fueled by a two-sack effort against the Titans on Sunday. He easily could have had a third sack on the day had cornerback Joey Porter Jr. not wiped it out with a facemask penalty. 9. Can’t touch this For weeks now, the Cowboys defense has flirted with disaster by failing to touch a downed receiver before he gets back up and starts running. On Sunday, they finally got bit. After Carnell Tate fell to the ground after making a catch, the defense just casually walked over to him and touched him, but not before he lifted himself off the ground. Strangely, this team does things like this, and it’s a glaring symptom of poor discipline and an inability to finish plays. Even in a blowout win, this defense just can’t seem to help itself when it comes to mental lapses. 10. Fluky 30 It is tough to know how to feel about letting one of the worst offenses in football put up 30 points. Should we be happy? Did the Mike Pettine play-calling switch actually help? The defense didn’t allow a single touchdown in the first half. Tennessee’s first touchdown was heavily aided by a 38-yard pass interference penalty that set up a quarterback sneak, and their second came on the play where everyone forgot to touch Carnell Tate. Their final score came with 30 seconds left on a fourth-down desperation heave by Cam Ward across the field against Dallas backups, making the final tally look much worse than the actual defensive performance.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas offense is nearly perfect, defense improves in win
summary: The Dallas Cowboys, coming off a historically bad defensive performance, needed a win against a lowly Tennessee Titans team going into a short week. And to their credit, the Cowboys did just that. The offense was nearly perfect, hanging 51 points and getting production out of all their major contributors. Dak Prescott, in particular, was […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys, coming off a historically bad defensive performance, needed a win against a lowly Tennessee Titans team going into a short week. And to their credit, the Cowboys did just that. The offense was nearly perfect, hanging 51 points and getting production out of all their major contributors. Dak Prescott, in particular, was superb, with an 85% completion percentage, 325 yards, and five total touchdowns. The defense, now being called by Mike Pettine, did enough. It was not a dominant defensive performance, but they had some big plays and gave the offense the opportunities they needed. Are the Cowboys Back on Track after 51-30 Win Over Titans? – Mark Heaney, Inside The Star Just one week after the 49ers made the Cowboys’ defense look like a JV high school football team, Dallas absolutely dismantles the Titans. But this was to be expected; was this enough to inspire confidence? They gave up 30 after allowing a staggering 46 last week, but 30 is still pretty rough. There were certainly improvements, and I am not trying to dismiss that, but a lot of the positives and negatives were things we’ve seen before from this team. Quinnen Williams and James Houston, for example, played out of their minds once again, but that’s not new. Don’t Forget These 5: Barron’s tackle before halftime – Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com In a game the Cowboys thoroughly won, there were plenty of plays that one can point to. And finally, there were some big defensive plays to be impressed with. Houston’s sack keeps Cowboys in control – The Titans had scored two touchdowns on their first two drives of the third quarter, but couldn’t really dig into the lead because of the Dallas offense. But on Tennessee’s third drive, edge rusher James Houston helped close the door with yet another sack on third-and-10 near midfield, forcing a punt. Dismember the Titans: Cowboys offense perfect, defense enough in 51-30 win – K.D. Drummond, Cowboys Wire There are two sides of the coin that Dallas has become all too familiar with. The offense was superb, and 51 points is about as good as it gets. The defense had issues, but there were some positives. Prescott, who suffered an injury to his hand but kept playing, threw for four scores and ran in another to add to his five-TD performance last week. He’s been on fire. In today’s contest, he got both CeeDee Lamb (11 receptions, 132 yards, 1 TD) and George Pickens (7 receptions, 102 yards, 1 TD) over the century mark. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . 6 instant reactions as Cowboys drop 50-burger on Titans in Week 11- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat It has been a season of ups and downs for the Cowboys. Here are some of the takeawys from the game. DeMarvion Overshown’s usage is confounding Anyone else notice that it was Justin Barron who replaced Dee Winters at off-ball linebacker in the second quarter after Winters was helped off the field? Barron is a fine depth player, but he shouldn’t be taking snaps away from DeMarvion Overshown. Dak Prescott Injury Concerns Surface With Hand Issue At Post-Game Press Conference- Josh Sanchez, Sports Illustrated The concerning aspect of this hand injury is that Dallas is facing a short week. And if the Cowboys have any hope of competing this season, it rests in the hands of their QB1. When asked about his hand, Prescott said that “ it bent back on a bad hit he took in the second half.” However, Prescott says that he is fine and that it’s a “blessing” that he wasn’t more seriously injured. Considering the quick turnaround he and the Cowboys have for Week 12, it’s great that he isn’t showing any concern. Cowboys vs. Titans: 5 winners and 3 losers from the game- Mike Poland, Blogging The Boys Luckily, against the lowly Titans, there were more winners than losers. After the way the season has gone, a convincing win is more than appreciated. Winner: Quinnen Williams Quinnen Williams continues to look like the centerpiece Dallas hoped it was acquiring. Williams recorded a sack of Cam Ward in the second quarter, getting through the interior to drop him for a loss.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 11
summary: The Cowboys don’t have a lot of time to enjoy their 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11. They play again in just a few days on Thanksgiving, when the host their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, at AT&T Stadium. Despite their focus having to shift quickly to their next opponent, they should […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cowboys don’t have a lot of time to enjoy their 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11. They play again in just a few days on Thanksgiving, when the host their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles, at AT&T Stadium. Despite their focus having to shift quickly to their next opponent, they should feel pretty good about earning the “W” Sunday afternoon against the Titans. For the most part, the Cowboys pretty much dominated the game from start to finish. This is still a team that has a lot to work on, especially defensively, but earning the victory against the Titans should be a confidence booster for them moving forward. As always though, it was a mixed bag of good, bad, and ugly for Dallas in Week 11. THE GOOD – Cowboys defense? It’s difficult to gauge how much, if any, the Cowboys defense improved in the Week 11 against the Titans. It’s also difficult to know how much of that is due to Mike Pettine taking over the play-calling duties or the fact they were playing an inferior opponent. Whatever the case, they did look at least a little better Sunday afternoon. They are still giving up too many big plays and are still struggling in run defense, but they also seem to be showing flashes of improvement. The coverage seemed more coherent and they are getting a good pass rush. Hopefully this will continue to the point where they are at least an average unit. So for this week we’ll give them a good. THE BAD – Injuries The Cowboys didn’t escape unscathed Sunday afternoon against the Titans. Dallas’ defense has had to overcome its fair share of injuries all season long and took another hit on the injury front Sunday. LB Dee Winters exited the game with the knee injury. Later CB Cobie Durant left with a neck injury after sustaining friendly fire from DeMarvion Overshown, neither returned. The extent of their injuries is unknown at this time, but there’s a good chance both could miss next week’s game and beyond. Dallas is unfortunately already thin at both positions. THE UGLY – What Dak Prescott did to the Titans defense Dak Prescott and the Cowboys offense exploded on Sunday. They dropped 51 points on Tennessee by scoring a touchdown on nearly every possession, discarding the last kneel down. The one time they didn’t score a TD still resulted in three points off a Brandon Aubrey field goal. With the help of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, Dak Prescott shredded Tennessee secondary, completing 28 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns. It was a near-perfect outing for them and made the Titans defense look ugly.

Sure, the Titans may have one of the league’s […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys beat the Tennessee Titans 51-30 this week. Here’s what we learned. The offense has found its way Dak Prescott played one of the absolute best games of his career this week against the Titans scoring five total touchdowns and throwing for 325 yards. Sure, the Titans may have one of the league’s worst defense, but you can only play the schedule you have. After putting up 40 points against a tough 49ers defense, the Cowboys scored nonstop touchdowns on every drive until being held to a field goal in the fourth quarter. They’d score yet another touchdown after that field goal after a gift from the defense. The GOTI offense took over on the ground and through the air, finally taking advantage of a weak opponent. I can’t help but wonder if their offensive performance against the 49ers has a catapult effect on the season for Dak and company. Offensive and defensive synergy After halftime, the defense looked like it could turn into the pumpkin we’ve seen time after time. They did give up 30 points in the end, but 14 came on extremely wacky plays. Holding the Titans to nine in the first half allowed the Cowboys offense to run up the score and never look back. This was finally a week where the offense and defense worked in unison – scoring touchdowns while forcing field goals and punts. The receivers for Dallas had a field day, Prescott was nearly flawless, while the defense never allowed Cam Ward and the Titans get comfortable. With performances from the two sides of the ball completely synergized, this was a refreshing week for the Cowboys and their fans. Did Mike Pettine make a difference or was it “just the Titans”? This week, Mike Pettine replaced Christian Parker as the defensive play-caller against Tennessee. We saw double mug looks from the linebackers, sometimes coming and sometimes bailing. The quarterback pressures and sacks continued to stack up, assisted by blitzes but also tighter coverage in the secondary. Dallas really didn’t allow the Titans’ passing game to get going until late when they needed to force long, clock chewing drives. Cam Ward went into halftime with 55 yards through the air. He finished the third quarter with 154 total yards passing with 59 coming on the odd Carnell Tate catch-and-run, not being ruled down and scoring a touchdown. But even into the fourth quarter, the Dallas defense forced chaos resulting in turnovers and sacks. Did Mike Pettine really call a much cleaner game or was this just luck of the draw in facing a weak opponent?

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: 5 winners and 3 losers from the game
summary: The Dallas Cowboys entered Sunday knowing there was very little margin left for error in their season. Against the Tennessee Titans, the offense responded in emphatic fashion. Dallas moved the football almost at will and built a commanding advantage, although some familiar discipline and defensive problems prevented the performance from being completely clean. Either way, […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys entered Sunday knowing there was very little margin left for error in their season. Against the Tennessee Titans, the offense responded in emphatic fashion. Dallas moved the football almost at will and built a commanding advantage, although some familiar discipline and defensive problems prevented the performance from being completely clean. Either way, the Cowboys get the home victory winning 51-30. Here are today’s winners and losers from the win at home. Winner: Dak Prescott Dak Prescott completely controlled this game. Prescott went 28-of-33 for 302 yards and four touchdown passes, while also adding a rushing touchdown himself. He also connected on a franchise-record 19 consecutive passes. He has found answers at every level of the field and, most importantly, hasn’t given Tennessee anything through turnovers. The efficiency was absolutely outstanding. Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams for touchdowns and repeatedly punished Tennessee when it tried to bring pressure or crowd the line. A testament to his control in this game, Prescott hit eight different receivers in this game and rushed three times for 10 yards. Winner: Javonte Williams Javonte Williams hasn’t produced a massive rushing total, but he keeps finding the end zone. Williams scored Dallas’ opening touchdown from one yard before later catching an 11-yard touchdown pass from Prescott in the third quarter. That gives Dallas another example of why Williams has become such an important part of this offense. He’s capable of doing the dirty work around the goal line while also contributing as a receiver when defenses focus too heavily on Lamb and Pickens. Plus he still provides quality pass protection. Winner: Cowboys wide receiver corps This was a great example of just how difficult the Cowboys receiver room can be to defend when everybody contributes. It starts with CeeDee Lamb, who produced another monster afternoon with 11 catches for 132 yards and a touchdown. Tennessee knew where the football was going and still couldn’t stop him. Lamb consistently moved the chains, produced yards after the catch and scored from eight yards out in the second quarter. Then there was George Pickens, who gave Dallas the complementary threat it needs opposite Lamb. Pickens reached seven receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown, averaging 14.6 yards per catch. His 10-yard touchdown in the second quarter helped Dallas build a 27-6 advantage. He also added a six-yard rushing attempt, showing how Dallas continues finding different ways to get the football into his hands. And then there’s KaVontae Turpin. His contribution didn’t come through the traditional passing game, but he’s still part of what makes this receiver room so difficult to defend. Dallas gave Turpin two designed rushing attempts and he turned them into 41 yards and a touchdown, including a 22-yard score around the left side. Winner: James Houston James Houston made the most of his opportunities. His biggest play came late in the first quarter when he exploded off the edge and dropped Cam Ward for an eight-yard sack on third down, immediately ending Tennessee’s possession. Houston had already created pressure on the previous snap and consistently looked disruptive when Dallas allowed him to attack. He actually got to Ward again during the second quarter for what would have been a 13-yard sack, only for a Joey Porter Jr. facemask penalty to wipe the play away. The sack didn’t count statistically, but the rep still showed Houston beating his blocker and finishing at the quarterback. He finally got that sack back later in the game. Houston keeps making the argument that he deserves more opportunities to provide it, and a day with two sacks that could have been three is a good starting point for that argument. Winner: Quinnen Williams Quinnen Williams continues to look like the centerpiece Dallas hoped it was acquiring. Williams recorded a sack of Cam Ward in the second quarter, getting through the interior to drop him for a loss. He also produced one of his best run-defense snaps of the afternoon by exploding into the backfield and dropping former Cowboy Tony Pollard for a two-yard loss. Williams also affected the passing game without always appearing in the sack column, including forcing an incompletion on third down later in the second quarter. He also tipped to balls at the line of scrimmage. The high point of what he did today, however, was the great strip-sack late in the game. Other than an interception, Williams marked off every major defensive statistical category today, and no one does that by accident. Loser: Explosive pass defense Mike Pettine’s first game calling the defense has produced some encouraging moments. The explosive-play problem hasn’t disappeared. The clearest example came in the third quarter when rookie Carnell Tate got loose for a 59-yard touchdown, immediately answering a Dallas score and allowing Tennessee to remain within striking distance. The Cowboys can produce several excellent defensive snaps, generate pressure and force an opponent behind schedule, only for a lapse in concentration to wipe all of it away. That has been the story of this defense throughout the season. Loser: Cowboys penalties This is the part of Dallas’ performance that Brian Schottenheimer will hate when he watches the film. The Cowboys committed 11 penalties for 128 yards, that’s far too much free yardage against anyone, never mind for a team that has spent most of the season fighting its own discipline problems. George Pickens’ third-quarter taunting penalty was particularly unnecessary. Prescott had just scored to extend Dallas’ advantage, yet Pickens immediately gave away 15 yards after the play. Dallas has been good enough offensively to overcome the penalties today, but a different team on a different day this is bad. Loser: Christian Parker The Cowboys defense wasn’t suddenly dominant against Tennessee, but it looked different this week, and that isn’t a particularly good look for Christian Parker. Tennessee still created explosive plays and scored points, but their touchdowns during the meat of the game came from a long pass interference penalty, and the failure to touch Tate down on what should have been a medium gain. What stood out, though, was how much more unified the unit appeared. Communication looked cleaner, players seemed more certain of their assignments and there appeared to be less confusion before the snap. Dallas also generated pressure at important moments and generally looked more organized despite Pettine only recently joining the staff. If the defense immediately looks calmer and more connected in the very first game after somebody else takes over the play-calling, questions are naturally going to be asked about what was happening before. Pettine hasn’t fixed the Cowboys defense in one afternoon, but even a noticeable step toward looking like a coherent unit is a huge jump from what was happening.

title: Cowboys win over Titans made NFL history in this way
summary: History has happened, folks. The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Tennessee Titans on Sunday by a final score of 51-30 and this is significant because of the score specificially. For anyone unaware… when an NFL score happens that has never occurred before it is a Scorigami. 51-30 had quite literally never happened before across all of […]
full_text: Nov 22, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates with wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (88) after scoring a rushing touchdown against the Tennessee Titans during the third quarter at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect History has happened, folks. The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Tennessee Titans on Sunday by a final score of 51-30 and this is significant because of the score specificially. For anyone unaware… when an NFL score happens that has never occurred before it is a Scorigami. 51-30 had quite literally never happened before across all of NFL history which means that you can file the paperwork with the proper historians because this one has made its way in. TEN 30 – DAL 51 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1101st unique score in NFL history, and the 6th of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/5lHdwXYvME — Scorigami (@ScorigamiGuy) November 22, 2026 Interestingly, the Cowboys have been a part of back to back Scorigamis as their loss to the San Francisco 49ers (46-40) also produced a score that had never been seen before. Given that we can speak to being on the winning and losing ends of these in recent memory… the winning side is certainly a lot more fun. Perhaps the Cowboys can make it three in a row on Thanksgiving Day against the Philadelphia Eagles?

title: Game balls for the Broncos’ win over Raiders in Week 11
summary: The Denver Broncos had a bit of a scare at home against the Las Vegas Raiders, but when it mattered the most they made the plays to pull away and secure the win against their AFC West rival. At 8-2, they’ve also moved into the second seed in the AFC and first place over the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Ja'quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with fans after intercepting a pass for a touchdown during the fourth quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos had a bit of a scare at home against the Las Vegas Raiders, but when it mattered the most they made the plays to pull away and secure the win against their AFC West rival. At 8-2, they’ve also moved into the second seed in the AFC and first place over the Kansas City Chiefs after tiebreakers. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . It was a weird game — also a quintessential Broncos’ game. This team is a momentum-driven team. Given that reality, they pushed out early to a 17-0 lead by early in the second quarter dominating the Raiders on both sides of the ball. However from there, both sides of the ball went into hibernation ceding momentum entirely to the visiting team. The Raiders would fight their way back to a 17-17 tie with five minutes left in the third quarter. That would wake the Broncos back up who would then lead two touchdown drives of their own to extend their lead back to two touchdowns. Vegas wasn’t dead yet and still had a chance to lead a game-tying drive, but Ja’Quan McMillian shut it down entirely with his pick six. All in all, it was quite the fun game. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to from the Broncos win over the Raiders: Bo Nix Bo Nix finished 19/35 for 225 yards with a touchdown and an interception. The box score stats don’t look impressive, because they lack context. Nix was slinging the ball out there and was on target. The issue were several egregious drops that could have been big plays and one perfect deep ball that would have been a walk-in touchdown. Instead, Troy Franklin somehow let it bounce off the top of his helmet. Taking in that context, there were a lot of yards and big plays left out there. I see a Bo Nix that is dealing and at a perfect time for a stretch run heading into late November. – Tim Lynch TOUCHDOWN ADAM TRAUTMAN 🐟 pic.twitter.com/4a6mbO64gd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 Ja’Quan McMillian Ja’Quan McMillian is just him. How many times has he been the guy who comes up with the big play to put a game away? Add one more. With the Broncos trying to hold off the Raiders in the 4th quarter his pick-6 was the final nail in the coffin. The play was special too, reading the pass, reacting, and then grabbing the ball out of the air behind himself one-handed. A thing of beauty. And on a day to honor Tom Jackson, the ultimate Raider Hater, it was a touch of therapy for Broncos Country. – Adam Malnati JA'QUAN MCMILLAN PICK 6 PAY THAT MAN pic.twitter.com/vi1YeYD5Hg — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 Jonah Coleman The Broncos have their running back. It’s clear that Coleman brings an element to the offense that makes it … run. The rookie had not one, not two, but three touchdowns in Denver’s 38-24 win over the Raiders. Coleman also finished with a game-high 111 yards rushing on 24 carries for an average of 4.6 yards per carry. He also added four receptions for 18 yards. Coleman is the first Broncos running back to rush for 100 or more yards in 19 games. Have a day, rookie. – Ian St. Clair JONAH COLEMAN WITH THE HAT TRICK 3 RUSHING TOUCHDOWNS pic.twitter.com/TEtshWvf0Q — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 Jonathon Cooper Jonathon Cooper only had two tackles , but they were both TFL. He also led the team with three qb pressures and two sacks. He threw in a batted pass as well. He had one of the best games of his career and earned a game ball from me. This was his fifth career game with two sacks, which is his career high. This was also his fifth career game with two TFL, also his career high. – Joe Mahoney Zach Allen Zach Allen put on a show on the defensive line for the Broncos this week. He was in on a sack, had two quarterback hits, and 3 passes batted down. He was a constant force of frustration for Mendoza. – Sadaraine Evan Engram Evan Engram hasn’t made the impact Broncos Country was hoping for when they signed him during the 2025 offseason. However, he had a great game against the Raiders. Egram was their leading receiver with 6 receptions for 74 yards and had numerous catches move the chains. Perhaps this is a sign for more things to come for the veteran tight end. If Denver can continue to find ways to get him involved, their offense could be much better down the stretch. – Chris Hart Tom Jackson The historical game ball goes to one of the all-time greats in NFL history. Adding his time as a Denver Broncos and his decades broadcasting with ESPN, there are few people who have contributed more to the NFL sport than Tom Jackson. And his Raider Hater spirit could not have been stronger in that stadium and on the field — helping to inspire the Mile High Magic. A win over the Raiders was Broncos’ Country’s Mile High Salute to No. 57. If the crowd were quiet enough, you probably heard TJ whisper, “it’s all over fat man” then crack that huge smile. Rest in peace. – Laurie Lattimore Volkmann Moment of silence for #Broncos legend Tom Jackson pic.twitter.com/KHUkZ7KvVS — Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) November 22, 2026 Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Raiders game? Share in the comments section below.

title: The Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars: The Broncos race for AFC dominance
summary: With Denver’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, the Broncos again find themselves atop the AFC West and the 2nd seed in the AFC. As Denver looks around the NFL at their closest competition, it’s clear that with just 7-weeks to go in the regular season that their main concerns are the Bills, […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 19 : A Denver Broncos fan shows off a replica Super Bowl ring for the camera during team warmups before the Broncos played the Cincinnati Bengals during the game at Sports Authority Field at Mile high in Denver, Colo., November 19, 2017. (Photo by Marc Piscotty/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With Denver’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, the Broncos again find themselves atop the AFC West and the 2nd seed in the AFC. As Denver looks around the NFL at their closest competition, it’s clear that with just 7-weeks to go in the regular season that their main concerns are the Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars. The current #1 seed in the AFC is the Buffalo Bills (9-1). Their remaining 7 opponents are Kansas City (8-2), New England (5-5), Green Bay (6-4), Chicago (8-2), Denver (8-2), Miami (1-9), and the New York Jets (3-8). With a combined record of 39-32 and a win percentage of 54.92%, the Bills actually have the 2nd toughest road ahead of them. Obviously, the Christmas Day game in Denver looms extra large since control of the AFC at large will likely be at stake. The Chiefs (8-2) were the AFC West’s seat warmer for the week following the Broncos bye. At 8-2 on the season, Denver’s handling of business against the Raiders re-annointed them the AFC West leaders due to the many layers of tie-breaking procedures. Buffalo (9-1), Los Angeles Rams (6-4), Cincinnati (7-2), New England (6-6), San Francisco (9-1), Los Angeles Chargers (1-9), and Las Vegas (4-7) will close out the Chiefs regular season. At 42-30 and a win percentage of 58.33%, it’s imperative that Denver maintain their winning ways while remaining hopeful that the Chiefs will find a way to lose at least one or two of those tougher matchups. Even though Denver beat them in week 2, the Jaguars (7-3) are proving to be a scrappy and dangerous team coming down the stretch. Yes, they did somehow lost to the Giants on Sunday, but with 7 games to play they could very well challenge the Broncos again before the season is over. Their remaining opponents, Tennessee (1-9), Chicago (8-2), Pittsburgh (6-4), Houston (4-6), Dallas (5-6), Washington (3-5-1), and Indianapolis (3-8) have a combined record of 30-40-1 and a win percentage of 42.25%. While winning the AFC seems less likely considering their loss on Sunday, the Jaguars are poised to pounce on the Bills, Chiefs, or Broncos should any of them stumble down the stretch. At 8-2, the Denver Broncos have the ‘easiest’ remaining schedule between now and the playoffs. Pittsburgh (6-4), Miami (1-9), Jets (3-8), Las Vegas, (4-7), Buffalo (9-1), New England (6-6), and the Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) have a combined record of 30-44 and a win percentage of 40.54%. Having beaten the Jaguars and split with the Chiefs, the Broncos find themselves in a terrific position to steal the 1-seed in the AFC from the Bills in their Mile High matchup on Christmas Day. 7-games left to play is too many to predict or discount just who will be the AFC’s top seed. On paper, the Broncos appear to have done all their heavy lifting to start the season. The Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars schedules stiffen, but is that something Denver can rely on looking forward? Can Denver take care of business when it matters most? Sure, it’s important that Denver beat teams whose seasons are already all but over, but the real determination will come from that Bills game on Christmas Day. It’s looking more and more like it will decide home field advantage throughout the playoffs and is shaping up to be a game that the Broncos absolutely have to have if they’re going to right the wrongs from their almost-Super Bowl season last year. Laid out in front of us, Broncos Country is looking like they’re poised to enjoy another deep run into the playoffs this season. While out rivals have a tougher road ahead of them, the Broncos can’t be distracted by what others are doing, lest they lose sight of the 7 remaining tasks in front of them. It’s going to be terrific fun watching all this play out until the regular season’s closing bell rings. Go Broncos.

title: Winners and Losers from the Broncos’ 38-24 victory over the Raiders
summary: In honor of the late and great Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos defeated the Las Vegas Raiders at home, infront of the Mile High Crowd. Now, the game shouldn’t have been as close as it was at times, but the Broncos won a rare two-score game and improved their record to 8-2 and retook the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with fans after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Denver Broncos won 38-24. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images In honor of the late and great Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos defeated the Las Vegas Raiders at home, infront of the Mile High Crowd. Now, the game shouldn’t have been as close as it was at times, but the Broncos won a rare two-score game and improved their record to 8-2 and retook the lead in the AFC West. Rookie Jonah Coleman had three rushing touchdowns and topped 100 yards on the ground, and Ja’Quan McMillian had the game sealing pick 6 of rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza late in the 4th quarter. The Broncos had a 17-0 lead at one point but allowed the Raiders to tie it up at 17-17 due to some poor defensive plays and errors on the offensive side of the ball. Honestly, they even left more points on the field and should have been up 24-10 at halftime if Troy Franklin had not doinked the ball off his helmet. More on that later. With all that said, here are your winners and losers from the Denver Broncos’ 38-24 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman had a breakout party vs. the Raiders. Coleman topped 100 yards for the first time in his career and had a hat trick with three rushing touchdowns. In total, Coleman had 24 carries for 111 yards and 3 rushing touchdowns while adding 4 receptions for 18 yards. That is 28 touches for 129 yards and 3 touchdowns. That’s impressive. JONAH COLEMAN WITH THE HAT TRICK 3 RUSHING TOUCHDOWNS pic.twitter.com/TEtshWvf0Q — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 After a trade deadline period that featured the Broncos being connected to Jonathan Taylor and Tony Pollard, Coleman emerged from the bye week and proved to the team and the fans that he is the guy. He averaged 4.6 yards per carry, ran hard, and was tough to bring down. He ran through and over Raiders defenders, stiffed armed DBs, and had a nose for the end zone. If the Broncos want to have success in January, they need a run game like this. Add in the explosive element of RJ Harvey, who will be returning in a few weeks, and the Broncos could have a solid 1-2 punch in the backfield. This was one of the best Broncos rushing performances in a long time. Love to see it. WINNER – CB Ja’Quan McMillian (PAY THAT MAN) The Broncos signed CB Riley Moss to a four-year extension this week, but pending free agent slot corner Ja’Quan McMillian once again proved his worth to the team with a big-time play vs. the Raiders. It was late in the 4th quarter and the Raiders. led by rookie number one overall pick Fernando Mendoza, had a chance to tie the game up, or even for the win with a two-point conversion. Well, Ja’Quan McMillian, who is known for his clutch plays, did it again. He made an impressive one-handed interception and took back for a touchdown. Yet another late-game INT and pick 6 that sealed a victory for the Broncos. JA'QUAN MCMILLAN PICK 6 PAY THAT MAN pic.twitter.com/vi1YeYD5Hg — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 Say it with me everyone. PAY. THAT. MAN. Hear me Broncos? Do not let this man leave the building. WINNER – TE Evan Engram Engram, who was supposed to be a gamechanger for the Broncos offense, has been mostly non-existent, including this season. However, the veteran tight end showed up and showed up in a big way tonight. He led the offense with 6 receptions for 74 yards and made multiple big time plays for the Broncos passing offense. If we can get this sort of production from Engram more often, that could be a gamechanger for this offense. I have my doubts that this will happen, but it was good to see and I am hopeful it continues. LOSER – WR Troy Franklin DOINK Troy Franklin's deep ball woes continue 🤦 pic.twitter.com/ZoVha29Gsc — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 Troy Franklin has had his issues with tracking a deep ball and that, unfortunately, continued tonight vs. the Raiders. He got open, wide open actually, and had a walk in touchdown due to a beautiful Bo Nix pass. It was all there for a big-time score for the Broncos to retake the momentum and control of the game before halftime. All he had to do was make the catch and… DOINK Right off the helmet. If you’re going to be a situational deep threat wide receiver, you need to make these plays. We have seen Franklin struggle with the deep ball throughout his short career and this one might be his worst blunder of the bunch. WINNER – QB Bo Nix His stat line does not look all that impressive, but he should have at least three touchdown passes. He finished the game going 19 of 35 for 225 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 hailmary INT. If you add in Marvin Mims getting touched down at the 1 yard line (near TD) and Franklin’s drop, you’re looking at a near 300 yard 3 touchdown game. These box scores never tell the entire story and that is the case with Bo Nix. FLEA FLICKER TO BIG PLAY MARVIN MIMS pic.twitter.com/Me3sZzt6KX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 I thought this was Nix’s best game of the season. He looked in command of the offense, threw the ball down the field and did it well, looked confident, and moved the ball up-and-down the field. This has been the storyline with Nix throughout his young career. Starts slow, for whatever reason, gets a bye week, and comes out firing. His best games last season came post bye week and I think we’ll see that again this season. LOSER – Denver Broncos defense/Vance Joseph This has been a glaring red flag for me the past three games. The Broncos defense is allowing big plays, giving up first downs on third/fourth and long, and keep letting teams get back into the game. That happened again tonight vs. rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza making his second career start. The defense started out hot, but errors, poor plays, and bad play calls allowed them to get back in the game. How many times have we seen a running back wheel route kill this defense? Why is edge rusher Que Robinson one on one with Ashton Jeanty down the field? Also, the run game continues to allow chunk plays. They allowed a wide open running lane for Jeanty to go 45 yards untouched. This is a Raiders rushing offense that has been struggling and yet, they had success vs. the Broncos. They allowed another first down on third and long, which has been annoying me personally, and had a blown coverage late in the game that could have went for a long walk in touchdown if Mendoza threw a better ball. Despite this, they had sacks, swatted the ball, and had a pick 6 which is great, but these issues remain. Plenty of good, but the bad keeps showing up and has shown up in multiple games in a row now. WINNER – OL Matt Peart, LOSER – OL Ben Powers I am bunching these two together because the Broncos rotated the two in and out at left guard tonight. Powers has started at left guard all season, but today, Peart got the start. However, Powers still played and had multiple series in a row out there before being replaced by Peart. So, it’s a win for Peart to get the start and extended playing time, but he was still being subbed out. Meanwhile, Powers lost his starting gig, for at least one week, but still saw plenty of playing time. I am interested to see the snap counts and discuess this situation out more tomorrow. WINNER – Sacks and pass deflections While I said the defense was a loser due to their issues with big plays and on third/fourth and longs, the defense still made some impact plays in this one. They had 5 sacks in total. Two by Jonathon Cooper, 1 by Alex Singleton, 1 by Malcolm Roach, and half sacks by Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto. Also, Allen had multiple pass deflections while DJ Jones and Malcolm Roach also were able to get their mits on the…

summary: The Denver Broncos came out of their bye week and took an early 17-0 lead on the Raiders. However, this team can never do anything easy, and they allowed the Raiders to tie it up. However, the Broncos leaned on three Jonah Coleman touchdowns and a game-ending Ja’Quan McMillian to end it and improve to […]

title: Instant reaction: Broncos kick into high gear on offense to take down Raiders
summary: With heavy hearts after the news of Tom Jackson’s passing, the Denver Broncos took the field this afternoon. The Broncos battled the Las Vegas Raiders today in a key Week 11 divisional matchup. After four quarters of play, the Broncos were victorious and defeated the Raiders 38-24. Here are some instant reactions from today’s victory. […]
full_text: Nov 22, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) waits for the snap against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With heavy hearts after the news of Tom Jackson’s passing, the Denver Broncos took the field this afternoon. The Broncos battled the Las Vegas Raiders today in a key Week 11 divisional matchup. After four quarters of play, the Broncos were victorious and defeated the Raiders 38-24. Here are some instant reactions from today’s victory. Bo Nix’s numbers weren’t great, but he played better than his state line suggests An extra week of rest, recuperation, and preparation was much needed for the Broncos. In the first half of the season, they struggled to be consistent on offense. In order to be a championship contender, improving their efficiency and productivity in that respect is an absolute must. A lot of that means improved play from quarterback Bo Nix. Today’s matchup against the Raiders provided them with that opportunity. Las Vegas entered today’s game being one of the worst defenses in the NFL across the board. That’s why I was hopeful this would be a big chance for Nix to play at a high level . All things considered, I was pleased with his performance. The third-year signal caller looked a lot more confident and showed tremendous poise in the pocket. He was routinely stepping up and making throws on time. He delivered a handful of passes over the middle of the field and big plays down the field. Unfortunately, a handful of drops on well-placed throws held back his overall numbers. This was probably the highest number of drops Denver’s receiving corps had all season long. Had Troy Franklin, Jaylen Waddle, and a few others held onto the ball, Nix’s productivity would have been way higher. He would finish the game going 19-of-35 for 225 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception. But make no mistake, Broncos Country. He played a lot better than what the stat line showed. Fans should be confident that the usual second half of the season rise will happen. In my opinion, his group of receivers have to step up and start helping him out more. A lot of yards and potential points were left on the field due to the drops. Jonah Coleman and Evan Engram shine on offense Having a strong running attack will be mission critical as the Broncos embark on the final stretch of the regular season. Today, rookie running back Jonah Coleman put together a praise-worthy performance. Coleman’s ground game prowess was the heart and soul of Denver’s offensive endeavors. His tough-nosed running and tackle breaking ability was key for their efforts in the second half to earn the victory. He rushed the ball 24 times and finished with 111 yards and 3 touchdowns. There is no doubt he is Denver’s bell cow back moving forward. He had a special day, and I couldn’t be more thrilled for him. On a side note, I’d like to give tight end Evan Engram some love. That hasn’t happened often in post-game analysis since he joined the team last year. In the first nine games of the season, Engram didn’t have much of an impact . Prior to today’s contest, he had just 17 catches for 169 yards and 1 touchdown. Today? He was the team’s leading receiver with six receptions for 74 yards. A lot of those catches moved the chains. If Coleman and Engram can continue to shine, I think Denver’s offense can take flight to new levels and be much better in the final trek of the season. Broncos’ defense struggles again to combat the splash plays; but deal with deal with a pick-six to end the game Denver’s defense hasn’t been playing at an elite level this season. They’ve been good, but they haven’t been great. Your mileage may vary, but I believe they have experienced some regression. In today’s matchup, they didn’t have to account for star tight end Brock Bowers. However, they struggled to find a way to combat second-year running back Ashton Jeanty. Jeanty had two huge plays in the first half. A 46-yard run that put them in scoring position. That was followed up on the next drive with a 68-yard wheel route receiving touchdown beating Que Robinson in coverage. Late in the fourth quarter, busted coverage allowed a 39-yard reception to wide receiver Tre Tucker. Surrendering third-and-longs and giving up explosive plays have been the two biggest issues for Vance Joseph’s defense by far. That continued even after the bye week. I know he likes being aggressive with his playcalling, but sometimes that aggressiveness puts them in precarious situations. On the flip side, kudos to Ja’Quan McMillian for his game-sealing pick-six of rookie Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter. That’s a big play Denver’s defense needed to put the Raiders away for good. Even so, Joseph and his players have a lot to clean up moving forward.

title: Broncos seal win with Ja’Quan McMillian clutch pick six in final minutes vs. Raiders
summary: The Denver Broncos always find a way to make it interesting. They should have been up multiple scores in this game, but kept finding ways to keep the Las Vegas Raiders in it. That all ended in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter when Ja’Quan McMillian highlight reeled Fernando Mendoza with a tip […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs for a fourth quarter touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos always find a way to make it interesting. They should have been up multiple scores in this game, but kept finding ways to keep the Las Vegas Raiders in it. That all ended in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter when Ja’Quan McMillian highlight reeled Fernando Mendoza with a tip and catch for the interception return for a touchdown to put the Broncos back out in front for good to move to 8-2 on the season. The Broncos have now scored 30, 28, 26, and 38 in their last four games. They are finding ways to put up a lot of points at a time when they need to keep winning to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West. Broncos vs. Raiders final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Las Vegas Raiders 0 10 7 7 24 Denver Broncos 3 14 7 14 38 First Quarter The offense took a few drives to get things going, but the Broncos’ defense and special teams were there to give them the time they needed. The biggest play being a blocked punt by Sai’vion Jones to setup the first points for Denver in the game. SAI'VION JONES BLOCKS THE PUNT pic.twitter.com/cyjMU808S1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 Jonathon Cooper added a sack and the defense held the Raiders’ on three drives to just 21 yards. Bo Nix and the Broncos’ offense got things going late in the first quarter and were knocking on the doorstep of the end zone when the quarter ended. Broncos 3, Raiders 0. Full first quarter recap . Second Quarter The Broncos offense would explode early in the second quarter. They would score a touchdown early on with a Nix pass to Adam Trautman. On their next possession, Nix would have a few big pass plays. The first being a 24-yard dart to Jaylen Waddle, then this flea-flicker to Marvin Mims Jr. down to the one yard line. FLEA FLICKER TO BIG PLAY MARVIN MIMS pic.twitter.com/Me3sZzt6KX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 That big play would lead to a Jonah Coleman touchdown two plays later to put Denver up 17-0 over the Raiders with still over 10 minutes to play in the second quarter. It was all Raiders after that with Ashton Jeanty ripping of runs of 45-yards and 68-yards with the latter being a house call to help Las Vegas get 10 points on the board before halftime. The Broncos did have a chance with a big time perfect throw from Nix to Troy Franklin… but Franklin must have lost sight of the ball cause it bounced off his helmet instead . Broncos 17, Raiders 10. Full second quarter recap . Third Quarter The momentum stuck around for the Raiders in the second half too and ended up tying up the game midway through the quarter, but the Broncos finally woke on offense up after that. They put together a 10-play, 72 yard drive that closed out at the end of the quarter with this Jonah Coleman touchdown to retake the lead. JONAH COLEMAN TOUCHDOWN X2 pic.twitter.com/MLdPionvaZ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 It just wouldn’t be a Broncos game without the game being close entering the final quarter. Broncos 24, Raiders 17. Full third quarter recap . Fourth Quarter The Broncos defense came up huge in the fourth quarter on the Raiders first drive after Denver’s touchdown drive. They would stop Vegas on a fourth down attempt near midfield and give the ball back to the Broncos’ offense. Nix would open things up with a pass to Evan Engam for a nice gain, then it was all Jonah Coleman from there. He would take every snap and finish with a seven yard touchdown run to put the Broncos back up by two scores for his third touchdown of the game. JONAH COLEMAN WITH THE HAT TRICK 3 RUSHING TOUCHDOWNS pic.twitter.com/TEtshWvf0Q — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 The touchdown run would put him over 100 yards on the day. After trading punts, the Raiders got a huge play on a bust coverage to get them into field goal range. A holding penalty set them back and put them into a third and five eventually after getting those yards back. Mendoza found an open tight end to the 10 yard line. They’d score to make it a one-score game once more. An untimely three-and-out gave the Raiders a chance for the comeback. At the two minute warning, Ja’Quan McMillian once again proved why he needs an extension with a pick six to seal the victory for the Denver Broncos. JA'QUAN MCMILLAN PICK 6 PAY THAT MAN pic.twitter.com/vi1YeYD5Hg — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 23, 2026 PAY THIS MAN TOO! Broncos 38, Raiders 24.

title: Broncos vs. Raiders third quarter recap
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders went into halftime down 17-10, but they had all of the momentum after scoring 10-unanswered points late in the second quarter against the Denver Broncos defense. Both scoring drives were powered by huge plays by Ashton Jeanty: one a 45-yard run and the other a 68-yard touchdown reception. That momentum took […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Jack Bech #18 of the Las Vegas Raiders catches a pass in front of Jahdae Barron #23 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders went into halftime down 17-10, but they had all of the momentum after scoring 10-unanswered points late in the second quarter against the Denver Broncos defense. Both scoring drives were powered by huge plays by Ashton Jeanty: one a 45-yard run and the other a 68-yard touchdown reception. That momentum took a bit of a hit to start the second half with the Broncos’ defense forcing an immediate three-and-out. With Matt Peart back in at left guard for the first time since the team’s second drive in the first quarter, Jonah Coleman fought his way through the middle for a seven yard gain on first down. He then backed it up with another two yard gain to bring up a third and short one yard. He looked like he would be stopped for a loss on third down, but side-stepped the would be defender for a six yard gain and a first down. Denver began throwing it from there with back-to-back receptions by Pat Bryant. The first for three yards, then another over the middle for a nine yard gain and a first down. Three plays later a dart to Evan Engram was stopped short by one yard of the first down marker at their own 39 yard line. They’d line up to go for it on fourth and short, but Bo Nix was stuffed just shy of the first down marker. The stop was a huge swing play in momentum and put the Raiders nearly in field goal range already to start their next drive. Back-to-back runs by Mike Washington got them well into field goal range inside the 30 yard line. Three plays later, Mendoza found a wide open receiver for the easy pitch and catch touchdown to tie the game up. Make that TWO TDs for Fernando Mendoza 🗣️ LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sgnbFG3sUr — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 Broncos 17, Raiders 17. Needing to flip the script since early in the second quarter, the Broncos were quickly faced with a third and five after a missed deep shot to Evan Engram. Nix would find Engram on third down anyway for a 19 yard gain across midfield to get things going. Then an end-around to Marvin Mims Jr. picked up another 11 yards and a first down. A dump off to Jonah Coleman picked up another seven yards, then gave it Coleman on the ground for another five yards and a first down at the Raiders 25. The drive was on the verge of stalling when Nix found Jaylen Waddle on a deep crosser for 18 yards to setup a first and goal at the four yard line. On the next play, Jonah Coleman punched it in to put the Broncos back out in front with the third quarter coming to an end. JONAH COLEMAN TOUCHDOWN X2 pic.twitter.com/MLdPionvaZ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 The touchdown would cap a 10-play, 72 yard drive. Broncos 24, Raiders 17.

title: Broncos vs. Raiders second quarter recap
summary: Facing a second and goal inside the five to start the second quarter, the Denver Broncos were looking to extend their lead over the Las Vegas Raiders. Maxx Crosby blew up their second down play that was going to be a wide open screen for a touchdown had he not been in Bo Nix’s face […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos scrambles during the first quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Facing a second and goal inside the five to start the second quarter, the Denver Broncos were looking to extend their lead over the Las Vegas Raiders. Maxx Crosby blew up their second down play that was going to be a wide open screen for a touchdown had he not been in Bo Nix’s face immediately. On third and goal from the four, Nix looked to Jaylen Waddle in the end zone but he was interfered with to setup a new set of downs at the one yard line. Adam Trautman would catch a pass from Nix on the very next play to put the Broncos up by two scores. TOUCHDOWN ADAM TRAUTMAN 🐟 pic.twitter.com/4a6mbO64gd — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 The touchdown capped a 12-play, 74 yard scoring drive. Broncos 10, Raiders 0. Fernando Mendoza tried to go deep to their speed guy on the very first play of their next possession, but Pat Surtain II was with him stride for stride. Asthon Jeanty was stuffed for no gain by Talanoa Hufanga to bring up third and 10 where Taylor Rapp blew up the pass attempt to force another punt. JL Skinner dang near blocked the punt attempt, but it got through to set the Broncos’ up with good field position anyway. Bo Nix hit Jaylen Waddle on the very first play for a 24-yard gain into Raiders territory. After a short scramble outside by Nix, he would find Evan Engram again on second down who turned it up field for a first down and into field goal range. From the 37-yard line, Nix after a flea flicker found Marvin Mims Jr. coming wide open at the end zone for the touchdown and the big play. They ended up calling Mims down at the one yard line, though. FLEA FLICKER TO BIG PLAY MARVIN MIMS pic.twitter.com/Me3sZzt6KX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 Two plays later Jonah Coleman would punch it in for the touchdown. JONAH COLEMAN TOUCHDOWN pic.twitter.com/jaXqDtLqm6 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 Broncos 17, Raiders 0. With just 21 yards of total offense, Mendoza and the offense finally got another first down on their next drive. They were faced with a third and three from midfield where someone left their gap assignment to let Ashton Jeanty break loose for a 45-yard gain to setup a first and goal at the five yard line. After stuffing Jeanty on first down and an offensive pass interference call on second down setup a screen pass back to Jeanty for a short gain. On third and goal from 10, Mendoza’s pass was too high and incomplete to force the field goal attempt. Broncos 17, Raiders 3. With a little over six minutes left in the half, Bo Nix and the Broncos took over at their own 35. They’d get some yards on first and second down, but on third and three the pocket collapsed from all sides for a rare sack of Nix to bring out the punt unit. On the Raiders first snap on their next drive, Alex Singleton was all over Mendoza on a blitz for a huge loss of 10 yards. Mike Washington gained a bit back, but Mendoza would still face a third and 13 where he found an open wide receiver on a deep crosser for the first down and a 19 yard gain. Jeanty would break loose again and this time make a house call on a wheel route beating Que Robinson for the 68-yard touchdown pass. Fernando Mendoza throws his FIRST career passing TD 🔥 LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Kse8UFzJpd — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 For whatever reason, Vance Joseph’s defense just cannot handle wheel routes from a running back. Broncos 17, Raiders 10. With less than three minutes to go in the half, the Broncos needed to find some way to take back the momentum the Raiders have taken in the game. In the most head-scratching way, the Broncos would be punting it back to Las Vegas. Bo Nix fired a perfect deep pass to an open Troy Franklin who stumbled and then had the ball bounce of his head somehow. Not ideal. Troy Franklin….let's a walk in touchdown bounce right off his helmet pic.twitter.com/A2fDXohlNm — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 22, 2026 The good news is the defense woke up a little to start their next drive with Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen converging on Mendoza for the first down sack. Denver already had one blocked punt and a near block after that one. They would come up again with Dondrea Tillman getting a block on that punt to give the Broncos the ball at midfield with 11 seconds left in the half. The Broncos could not convert the big play into points.
