full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs with the ball against Derrick Moore #8 of the Detroit Lions during the second quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (8-2) beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11, extending their win streak to six games and remaining atop the NFC North. This is the second time in the last four weeks that the No. 1 Defense in DVOA entered Ford Field and failed to slow a Lions offense firing on all cylinders. While the game ended 31-21, it wasn’t as close as the final score suggests, as the Lions defense continued to play complementary football and was willing to give up late-game points to drain the clock and secure a victory. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Jared Goff: 58 (100%) Josh Dobbs: 0 (0%) Another top defense and another stellar day from Goff. He completed 20 of 28 for 279 yards and two touchdowns, navigated the pocket at an MVP level, gained 12 yards on the ground, including converting three first downs, and even got the Lions into victory formation. “He should be in the MVP conversation, ” Lions center Juice Scruggs said of Goff post-game. “He’s been playing light-out all year, and I don’t think he gets enough respect in this league. He’s very underrated, and I think people are just starting to see how good he is.” Running back Jahmyr Gibbs: 43 (74%) Sione Vaki: 13 (22%) — 12 special teams snaps (48%) Jacob Saylors: 2 (3%) — 14 (56%) Gibbs has hovered around the 75% snap range for a while, but his touches are the number to watch. He had 27 in this game, which isn’t far from his “plan” for the season, but they’ll likely need to keep trying to find ways to take pressure off him as we head into the final seven games of the regular season. Vaki continues to roll as RB2, while Saylors found the field in victory formation. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown: 46 (79%) — 1 (4%) Jameson Williams: 45 (78%) Isaac TeSlaa: 23 (40%) — 1 (4%) Tay Martin: 2 (3%) — 15 (60%) DeAndre Carter: 0 (0%) — 8 (32%) For the first time since the early parts of the season, St. Brown saw more snaps than Williams. It’s not a major change, but when everything else played out close to what we have seen over the last two months, it’s the only notable shift. Tight end Sam LaPorta: 53 (91%) — 1 (4%) Brock Wright: 43 (74%) — 9 (36%) Tyler Conklin: 17 (29%) Collectively, this group all saw their snaps level up, as it was clear the Lions wanted the tight ends involved in this game, and they produced 122 yards on six receptions in this game. “Yeah, it’s pretty good. Yeah, (Tyler Conklin) Conk’s added that little layer for us this year where he is a third tight end, but he can run routes, he can get out of the backfield and do some things, and it was good to get him that one, off schedule,” Goff said of having three tight ends at his disposal. “And then Brock (Wright) and Sam (LaPorta) have just been so reliable. The seams were open today, and we hit them on a few of those. Thought Sam played so well, and he’s been deserving of getting more touches like that, and it was good to see him get the ball a little bit.” Offensive line LT Penei Sewell: 57 (98%) LG Christian Mahogany: 58 (100%) — 6 (24%) C Juice Scruggs: 58 (100%) — 6 (24%) RG Tate Ratledge: 57 (98%) — 6 (24%) RT Blake Miller: 58 (100%) — 6 (24%) LT/6th OL: Larry Borom: 1 (2%) — 6 (24%) LG Miles Frazier: 1 (2%) — 6 (24%) C Seth McLaughlin: DNP The Lions offensive line is in rhythm, and against the NFL’s second-highest blitzing team, they allowed only eight pressures and one sack, according to PFF. With the emergence of 13 personnel (three-tight-end sets), the Lions have almost entirely moved away from “Jumbo” (six-offensive-lineman formations). Interior defensive lin e 3T Alim McNeill: 54 (78%) — 4 (16%) DT Tyleik Williams: 30 (43%) — 3 (12%) 3T Skyler Gill-Howard: 28 (41%) — 3 (12%) — 3 offensive snaps (5%) DL Levi Onwuzurike: 20 (29%) 3T Mekhi Wingo: DNP ( Inactive ) With the Bucs rushing attack being their greatest offensive asset, we saw a bit more Tyleik Williams in this game opposite McNeill. Gill-Howard continues to see goal-line snaps on offense as an extra blocker, but it looked like he may have injured his leg on his final blocking attempt and needed to turn down post-game interview requests from Pride of Detroit to get treatment. On a short week, this will be worth keeping a close eye on. EDGE Rush End Derrick Moore: 55 (80%) — 4 (16%) Rush End DJ Wonnum: 49 (71%) — 4 (16%) Big End Tyler Lacy: 17 (25%) — 6 (24%) Big End Ahmed Hassanein: 12 (17%) Rush End Eric O’Neill: 6 (9%) — 12 (48%) EDGE Tyrus Wheat: DNP ( Inactive ) With Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve, speculation ran high about how the Lions would replace his snaps, but in their first game without him, the answer was simpler than expected: increase Derrick Moore’s playing time. Wonnum, Lacy, and O’Neill saw few changes to their snap counts, but Moore’s snaps increased significantly. Over the Lions’ first six games, Moore never saw more than 30% of defensive snaps, but that number climbed to 42% in Week 8, 58% in Week 9, 68% in Week 10—as a game replacement for Hutchinson—and 80% now that he’s a starter. He rewarded coaches with a half-sack, a team-leading seven pressures (per NextGen Stats), and a 19.4% pressure rate. Fan favorite Hassanein finally got to play in his first NFL game, and while he was quiet in his 12 snaps, it’s a valuable first step for the developing defensive end. Linebacker MIKE/WILL Malcolm Rodriguez: 55 (80%) — 13 (52%) SAM/MIKE Derrick Barnes: 53 (77%) — 7 (28%) WILL K.J. Britt: 25 (36%) — 9 (36%) OLB/PR Trevor Nowaske: 22 (32%) — 18 (72%) LB Joe Bachie: 0 (0%) — 15 (60%) LB Owen Pappoe: 0 (0%) — 6 (24%) LB Amen Ogbongbemiga: DNP ( Inactive ) The Lions linebacker carousel continues to rotate weekly. After losing Jack Campbell, the Lions leaned heavily on Barnes and Rodriguez in their first game without their leader. The following week, Barnes’ snaps stayed high, while Rodriguez stepped back and made way for Nowaske and Britt. This week, Rodriguez jumped Barnes in snaps for the first time this season, while Britt jumped Nowaske by a few reps. While there has been little consistency beyond Barnes playing at least 75% of snaps, the rotation is working. Rodriguez secured a sack, Barnes was key in run defense, Britt made an important fourth-down stop early in the game, and Nowaske delivered a delicious sack to help close things out. Cornerback CB/NB Roger McCreary: 65 (94%) — 1 (4%) CB Rock Ya-Sin: 63 (91%) — 1 (4%) CB Khalil Dorsey: 8 (12%) — 13 (52%) CB Nick Whiteside: 7 (10%) — 10 (40%) CB Ennis Rakestraw: DNP ( Inactive – Injury) CB D.J. Reed: DNP ( Inactive – Injury) Safet y S Chuck Clark: 69 (100%) — 1 (4%) S/NB Brian Branch: 68 (00%) S Kerby Joseph: 46 (67%) — 1 (4%) DB Andre Cisco: 5 (7%) — 6 (24%) DB Christian Izien: 2 (3%) — 12 (48%) DB Keith Abney: DNP ( Inactive ) With Kerby Joseph’s return at safety, the Lions shifted their secondary usage, keeping McCreary and Ya-Sin almost exclusively on the outside and letting the safeties handle the middle of the field. In base sets, the Lions leaned on Branch and Clark—now wearing the green communication dot and the “C” on his jersey—and in subpackage sets, Kerby took Branch’s deep role, while Branch shifted into the slot/box. “I think it actually slowed it down for me even more, just calmed the situation down,” Clark said of the returns of Joseph and Branch. “Two guys that have been in this system. I know it was some things out there on the field that we just talking about and it just naturally flow. Alright, cool. It felt good. Like I said, I kind of said this the other day, looking at the tandem of them to do all them from the outside being on different teams like, OK, them boys, they hooping. And…

title: Detroit Lions grades: Offense looking unstoppable vs. Buccaneers
summary: The Detroit Lions moved to 8-2 with an emphatic win over the underrated Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Let’s take a closer look at Detroit’s impressive performance with our Week 11 report card. Quarterback: A+ Jared Goff was absolutely phenomenal against a stingy Buccaneers defense. Through the air, Goff delivered some big-time throws, including his 57-yard bomb […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 22: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) looks for a receiver during a play during the second quarter of a regular season NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Detroit Lions on November 22, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions moved to 8-2 with an emphatic win over the underrated Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Let’s take a closer look at Detroit’s impressive performance with our Week 11 report card. Quarterback: A+ Jared Goff was absolutely phenomenal against a stingy Buccaneers defense. Through the air, Goff delivered some big-time throws, including his 57-yard bomb to Jameson Williams with Vita Vea right in his face. Despite being pressured on 46.7% of his dropbacks (fifth-highest of the week), Goff produced +0.39 EPA/ pass, the fifth-best production of the week. Goff was also surprisingly impactful with his feet. Whether he was avoiding a pair of sack attempts to find a Tyler Conklin for a big gain, scrambling for a third-and-9 conversion or moving the chains on a pair of third-and-1 sneaks, Goff’s mobility—yes, mobility—proved to be a huge factor during high-leverage plays. Running backs: B+ You wouldn’t think Jahmyr Gibbs had a very effective day running the football by looking at the box score. His 98 yards on 23 carries is far below his average, and even feels like it’s artificially inflated by a late 26-yard run (22 carries for 72 yards is 3.3 YPC). But Gibbs constantly kept the Lions ahead of the sticks with solid 4-5 yard runs on first down and short-yardage conversion. In the end, the Lions rushed for a 53.8% success rate (third best of Week 11) and +0.28 EPA/rush (highest of Week 11). This was against arguably the best run defense in football, by the way. Gibbs, to his credit, produced 76 rushing yards after contact (sixth most of Week 11) and his individual +6.1 EPA per rush was the best of the week. Wide receivers: B Jameson Williams was excellent against the Bucs, taking full advantage of the early injury to Bucs cornerback Jacob Parrish and destroying his matchup with backup Benjamin Morrison. It was a quieter day from Amon-Ra St. Brown and Isaac TeSlaa, who combined for just five catches for 37 yards and a touchdown (all from St. Brown). You could argue both had a drop or two, so this unit gets dinged a little. But I also think their lack of production had to do with Detroit’s game plan to attack the middle of the field with their… Tight ends: A The Lions clearly saw a mismatch in Tampa’s zone defense vs. their tight ends up the seams. Detroit’s tight ends combined for six catches and 122 yards—their best collective performance of the season. “The seams were open today, and we hit them on a few of those,” Goff said after the game .“Thought Sam played so well, and he’s been deserving of getting more touches like that, and it was good to see him get the ball a little bit.” On top of that, the tight ends all remain drastically important to the run game and pass protection, and I think the trio did a fine job in those duties as well. Offensive line: B+ On the surface, it doesn’t seem like a great day for the offensive line. I already mentioned the high pressure rate, and while Detroit’s running game was efficient, it was far from explosive. The yards gained were tough ones. Still, pass protection was good enough for Goff to average 3.06 seconds to throw (sixth longest of Week 11) and only incur a single sack on the day. And two of the biggest weaknesses facing the Lions rushing attack—poor short-yardage conversion and too many negative plays—were not an issue in this one. The Lions were stuffed on just 6.9% of rushes (third lowest percentage) and they were 7-of-11 on third downs. Defensive line: B Early on, the Lions’ defensive line was absolutely nails against the run. Bucky Irving had just 12 yards on nine carries at halftime. But in the third quarter, it felt like the Buccaneers were starting to find some creases up the middle. As far as pass rush, it was a mixed bag. Detroit produced a 34.9% pressure rate (12th), but turned that into four sacks (10.8% sack rate was sixth highest). For the third week in a row, Derrick Moore produced five pressures—and he had a half-sack to move to 4.5 on the season. But if we’re being honest, there was a clear Aidan Hutchinson void in creating consistent pressure. Linebackers: B K.J. Britt had an outstanding fourth-down stop, as he continues to get significant playing time and make the most out of it. Malcolm Rodriguez (0.5 sacks, pass defended) and Trevor Nowaske (1.0 sack, 2 TFLs) continue to do solid work and make plays in Jack Campbell’s absence. Meanwhile, it was more up and down for Derrick Barnes. Coverage continues to be a bit of an issue with this unit, as Tampa’s running backs combined for seven catches and 75 yards, although tight end Cade Otton was held to just one catch for 8 yards. Defensive backs: B I think we need to take a moment and appreciate just how impressive it is that Brian Branch does not look like he’s lost a step a year removed from his Achilles injury. He just about locked down the nickel position all day. And Chuck Clark—save a potential MA at the end of the first half—continues to be a difference-maker, showing why he didn’t go straight to the bench upon Kerby Joseph’s return. Joseph wasn’t much of a factor in his 2026 debut, as it looked like there was some rust to shake off. At corner, it wasn’t Rock Ya-Sin’s best day. While he was never torched in coverage, he couldn’t make plays against Ted Hurst (five catches, 56 yards, 2 TDs) when in-phase. On the other side, Roger McCreary wasn’t tested much, but only gave up three catches for 22 yards and tallied a pass breakup. For what it’s worth, I’m not docking this unit for the last drive and the pair of pass interference penalties. It’s garbage time. I do not care. Special teams: D Dave Fipp is not going to be happy this week. There were far too many penalties on this unit. Holding on Nick Whiteside changed starting field position from 32-yard line to 14-yard line Illegal formation on Malcolm Rodriguez cost 5 yards of field position Blindside block on Malcolm Rodriguez change starting field position from 30-yard line to 13-yard line That’s a total of 40 yards of field position impacted by special teams. Tack on a missed 53-yard field goal from Jake Bates, four kickoff touchbacks from Bates, and one from Jack Fox on a punt, and it just wasn’t a great day. Kudos to Bates for making up for his missed kick with a 56-yard bomb, but I have much higher standards for this unit. Coaching: B+ First off, we need to give the coaching staff a ton of credit for navigating the international travel for the last two games. The Lions had to deal with jetlag while the Buccaneers were coming in well-rested off a bye week, and Detroit matched—if not, exceeded—Tampa’s intensity and physicalness. Additionally, the gameplans were solid on both sides of the ball. On offense, Detroit leaned on the passing game to open up the run game, and it worked to near perfection. On defense, they keyed in on taking away the run early, and they nearly pitched a first half shutout because of it. However, I can’t give them an A, because I thought there were two key moments in this game that allowed the Bucs to hang around more than they should’ve. First, the defensive call in the final seconds of the first half was inexcusable. The only play for the Bucs there was to take a shot in the end zone, so there is no world in which Baker Mayfield should be able to find a one-on-one matchup for the score there. The other came on Detroit’s first second-half possession, when Detroit was facing a third-and-inches. The Lions did such a great job the rest of the game taking what Tampa was giving them on defense, and they got too fancy here with a play-action pass that the Bucs sniffed out. A QB sneak, which has been…

title: Lions vs. Bears odds: Detroit home underdogs on Thanksgiving
summary: As the Detroit Lions enter Thanksgiving week, they’ve won six straight games, are 8-2 overall, and are 2-0 in the division, sitting in first place in the NFC North. This Thursday, they’ll host the Chicago Bears, who also enter this game at 8-2, but are 0-2 in the division, putting them in second place. Despite […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) sacks Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As the Detroit Lions enter Thanksgiving week, they’ve won six straight games, are 8-2 overall, and are 2-0 in the division, sitting in first place in the NFC North . This Thursday, they’ll host the Chicago Bears, who also enter this game at 8-2, but are 0-2 in the division, putting them in second place. Despite the Lions’ better record and the game being at Ford Field in downtown Detroit, the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions +2.5 points . In Ben Johnson’s first year as head coach, the Bears went 11-6 and won the NFC North. They beat the Packers in the Wild Card but lost to the Rams in the Divisional round, ending a season that exceeded expectations. This offseason, the Bears made a few tweaks to their offense while overhauling half of their defense. On offense, priority No. 1 was replacing their center, Drew Dalman, who surprisingly retired. So the Bears traded with the Patriots for Garrett Bradbury, then drafted Iowa’s Logan Jones in the second round. At receiver, they traded away DJ Moore and replaced him with former Lion Kalif Raymond, who has stepped into a starting role in the slot and flashed. On defense, the Bears lost all four of their top safeties (Kevin Byard, Jaquan Brisker, Jonathan Owens, and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson), their top linebacker in Tremaine Edmunds, starting NT Andrew Billings, and EDGE Dominique Robinson. At safety, the Bears made two splash moves: drafting Dillon Thieneman in the first round and signing Coby Bryant in free agency, who unfortunately suffered a season-ending injury, but they also signed Cam Lewis, who has since stepped into a starting role. Former Michigan Wolverine Devin Bush was signed in free agency to fill an Edmunds-sized void at linebacker, and Neville Gallimore was brought in to start at nose tackle. When Gallimore struggled, Chicago made a significant in-season trade, sending two first-round picks to acquire NT Jeffery Simmons. The Bears opened the season by dropping 59 points on the Panthers and had Johnson talking about setting the NFL scoring record . The next week, the Bears scored only three points in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. Wins over the Eagles and Jets helped them regain rhythm, but they fell to the Packers in Week 5—their third consecutive loss to an NFC North rival dating back to last season when they lost to the Lions in Week 18. Since their 3-2 start to the season, the Bears have been on a roll, winning their last five games, rolling up over 30 points on the Falcons (31-23), Patriots (30-24), and Seahawks (34-17), but they have shown some kinks in the armor of late. Quarterback Caleb Williams was lucky to overcome a four-interception performance in Week 9 to beat the Bucs 27-24, and this past Sunday, he underwhelmed again , but Chicago’s defense delivered, and the Bears beat the Saints 21-13. title: Discussion: What’s more impressive: Detroit Lions’ pass game or run game?
summary: The Detroit Lions have won six games in a row and things are looking good ahead of a pivotal Thanksgiving Day showdown with the Chicago Bears. The defense has impressed for more than a month, stringing together stalwart performances despite losing many of their key contributors. The offense, meanwhile, has looked sharp of late, dropping […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs with the ball as Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions cheers in the background against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions have won six games in a row and things are looking good ahead of a pivotal Thanksgiving Day showdown with the Chicago Bears. The defense has impressed for more than a month, stringing together stalwart performances despite losing many of their key contributors. The offense, meanwhile, has looked sharp of late, dropping 35 points on the New England Patriots and 31 points on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Things have been so good for the Lions that two of their players are getting genuine Most Valuable Player consideration. Jared Goff has helmed one of the league’s best passing attacks, and aside from his two interceptions against the Patriots, has been playing near-flawless football. Jahmyr Gibbs, meanwhile, is putting up an extraordinary campaign out of the backfield, already breaking 1,000 rushing yards while also scoring an absurd 15 touchdowns across 10 games. The Lions offense is firing on all cylinders, but which aspect of the offense has impressed you the most so far? Today’s Question of the Day is: Have you been more impressed with the Detroit Lions pass game or run game? My answer: The run game. By all accounts, this was an impressive game for the Lions from top to bottom. That being said, I was really encouraged by how the run game persisted and eventually broke free. Early on, it was tough sledding for the rushing attack. At the half, Gibbs had seven carries for 20 yards, an average of just 2.9 yards per attempt, far below the Lions’ standard. It was shaping up to be a hard-fought grudge match. Some offensive play callers would shy away from their stalled rushing attack in the second half and opt to air it out instead. Drew Petzing had no qualms about letting Jared Goff uncork it, but it never came at the expense of the rushing attack. What has impressed me the most about Petzing is his adaptability and foresight. The Lions have such a good offense because they can take what isn’t working and spin it to their advantage. Vita Vea is dominating the interior of the offensive line and stonewalling any rushing attack? In the second half, they started to Gibbs moving horizontally and outside the tackle box more. The Buccaneers boast a good run defense, but by playing away from that strength, the Lions started turning gains of two or three into gains of four or five. Over the course of a game, that makes a difference. A running back like Gibbs is a ticking time bomb for defenses: it is not a question of if he’ll go off, but when and for how much. A lot of his yards on Sunday were tough yards—he rarely had a convoy blocking ahead of him. Instead, he is a master of earning those extra few yards on every down, whether it is with a quick juke or a well-time burst. Because of his explosiveness, he has the ability to turn almost any touch into a home run play. Not every play will be a home run, but opposing defenses cannot afford a single slip up against him. That is a high-wire act that few teams can manage. The NFL is still a passing-focused league, but the Lions are showing how important a rushing attack can be. I genuinely believe that the Lions can run on any team in the NFL. Between Gibbs toting the rock, Petzing calling the shots, and the offensive line, receivers, and tight ends paving the way downfield, it’s not hard to see why this rushing attack is difficult to stop. I think the notion of “running to set up the pass” is archaic because it makes the run game sound like a tacked-on part of a good offense. The Lions are running the ball not because they want to open things up for their passing attack—they are running the ball because they are pretty dang good at it.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 16. summary: Sunday of Week 11 closes out with a huge NFC matchup on “Sunday Night Football.” The 7-2 Minnesota Vikings are taking on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. If the 49ers win, they’ll hold onto the conference’s top seed. If the Vikings win, they’ll be one step closer to claiming the top seed […]
full_text: Fans arrive ahead of the NFL regular-season football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers at Banorte Stadium in Mexico City on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Yuri CORTEZ / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Sunday of Week 11 closes out with a huge NFC matchup on “Sunday Night Football.” The 7-2 Minnesota Vikings are taking on the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. If the 49ers win, they’ll hold onto the conference’s top seed. If the Vikings win, they’ll be one step closer to claiming the top seed themselves. For the Lions, both outcomes have mixed results for the Lions. If the 49ers win: That drops the Vikings into third place in the division, and it means Thursday’s game between the Lions and Bears will be for sole possession of first in the NFC North. However, it puts Detroit further away from the NFC’s No. 1 seed. If the Vikings win: The Lions will have temporarily taken the top seed in the NFC by virtue of a better conference record than the 49ers (7-1 vs. 7-2) and a head-to-head win over the Vikings. But that would also mean there are still three teams in the NFC North at 8-2. And it would be nice to create some separation in the division. title: 13 winners, 4 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: There was no jet lag for the Detroit Lions. A week after their overseas tilt in Munich, Germany, the Lions returned to home turf to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers were projected to be a Minnesota Vikings-esque team—a stout defense offset by a lackluster offense. However, with Baker Mayfield healthy enough to start […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions looks to pass the ball against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was no jet lag for the Detroit Lions. A week after their overseas tilt in Munich, Germany, the Lions returned to home turf to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers were projected to be a Minnesota Vikings-esque team—a stout defense offset by a lackluster offense. However, with Baker Mayfield healthy enough to start and Bucky Irving on a tear recently, it would not be an easy task for Detroit on either side of the football. Yet somehow, it was? After a scoreless first quarter, the Lions woke up on offense and stayed strong on defense. The offense dropped 31 points on the NFL’s best defense by Defense-adjusted Value Over Average, all while holding their own on defense. The Buccaneers finished with just 274 total yards on offense. All of a sudden, the Lions are clicking on both offense and defense: For the first time since 1976, the @Lions have held opponents to under 275 total net yards in four-straight games. #OnePride pic.twitter.com/BNkpYAQPfC — Detroit Lions PR (@LionsPR) November 22, 2026 Detroit faces a short week with Thanksgiving and the Chicago Bears on deck. Which players emerged from this game as winners or losers? Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winner: Jared Goff, QB Coming off a game versus the New England Patriots in which he threw two ugly interceptions, Goff faced a tough task versus the top-ranked Buccaneers defense. In spite of the pressure, Goff delivered arguably his best game of the year. Stat-wise, Goff has had bigger performances this season, but he was phenomenal against Tampa Bay in ways that don’t show up in the numbers. The offensive line was not at its best, largely due to a large Vita Vea up the middle, yet Goff navigated the pressure swimmingly. He survived a collapsing pocket to hit Tyler Conklin for an 18-yard gain. He had a 10-yard scamper for a first down. One of Goff’s best throws of the season came on his downfield shot to Jameson Williams with pressure in his grill: DOT. https://t.co/oRgyk62PRR pic.twitter.com/S87CfkVius — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) November 22, 2026 Goff was not afraid to chuck it downfield, also connecting on deep shots to Sam LaPorta (47 yards) and Brock Wright (27 yards), nor did he shy away from Williams or Amon-Ra St. Brown on intermediate routes. If anything, the Lions were going away from their usual short passing attack—Jahmyr Gibbs only caught four passes for 20 yards. Goff finished the game averaging 10.0 yards per attempt, the highest average of his season thus far. Winner: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB Lesser running backs would have been stonewalled by the Buccaneers defense, but Gibbs is simply too special. He is too fast and explosive to stop for an entire game. Early on, the Buccaneers admittedly had his number. However, Gibbs does the little things that make an impact over the course of a game. He ekes out any extra yard he can get. He can make defenders miss on a dime. Eventually, he can and will get his breakout plays—he is inevitable. Gibbs turned 23 carries into 98 yards and two touchdowns, and he earned every single one of those stats. We are so lucky to witness a player like him. Winner: Kelvin Sheppard, DC—Loser: Consistent pass rush On paper, the Lions defense walked away with four sacks, but I think that tally is misleading. The first sack, courtesy of DJ Wonnum and a few assists, was a legitimate pass rush win from the defensive line. The second sack was a key third-down sack from safety Chuck Clark. The third and fourth sacks came on back-to-back plays late in the game, one via a Trevor Nowaske spy and one via a seven-man blitz. Individually, these are great plays, but it masks the problem for the pass rush: consistency. Consistency was an issue even with Hutchinson in the lineup, but you could at least count on him to generate a half dozen pressures per game—he is too good to stop for an entire game. Without Hutchinson, the Lions are going to have to scheme up their pass rush wins more than rely on individual effort. I think Sheppard did a great job guiding a Hutchinson-less defense on Sunday. The Lions had timely blitzes. The run defense was solid for all but one drive. The secondary once again eliminated the big plays. The team looks far more cohesive and disciplined than when they started. However, I am still a bit concerned about the pass rush. Outside of those schemed plays, the Lions were not generating much pressure. The Buccaneers’ final drive of the first half exemplified that—Mayfield had too much time and delivered perfect passes despite tight coverage. Against better offenses, slow developing pressure is not enough. The Lions have guys with motor, certainly, but they need someone to consistently collapse the pocket without having to dial up a blitz or a stunt. Wonnum is steady and Derrick Moore is progressing (who added another sack to his resume), but the lack of Hutchinson is quite evident—I would like to see more one-on-one wins. Winner: Jameson Williams, WR I am really impressed with Williams’ growth this season. The deep ball remains his greatest strength, but he makes the most of every down. He is beginning to thrive on the intermediate routes as well, using his speed to bait defenders into covering deep. His hands have improved of late, and he has now has back-to-back games with toe-tap catches along the sideline. Coupled with his stout blocking for a receiver (especially one as skinny as him), there is a lot to love about how Jamo is playing right now. Winner: Sam LaPorta, TE LaPorta needed a game like this. Given how well the offense had been playing over the last month, they have not needed LaPorta to carry the offense—a few catches a game and some key blocks were more than enough for what Detroit needed. However, it was important for LaPorta to show that he can still be impactful in the receiving game, not only for his own confidence but as a reminder to the world that he is still a top-five tight end in the league. LaPorta finished with three catches for 62 yards, the biggest of which was his 47-yarder early in the game. This was his most receiving yards in a game since Week 5 versus the Arizona Cardinals. He also sealed the way for Jahmyr Gibbs’ second touchdown run of the game . Loser: Derrick Barnes, LB Last week, I thought that Barnes quietly had one of his best games of the year. This week, I think he quietly had one of his worst games of the year. Tackling was the biggest issue for Barnes, who struggled on multiple occasions to wrap up the ball carrier. The athleticism that shined last week was absent against Tampa Bay. Barnes has the potential to be a sideline-to-sideline type of linebacker that can also bring pressure, but both of those facets were lackluster. Too often he looked out of place. During the times he was in the right spot, a bad angle or tackling attempt gave Tampa Bay more yards. Considering that the Lions are getting good linebacker play out of their other linebackers, it might be time to dial back Barnes’ role on defense. Winner: Chuck Clark, S Clark earned the captaincy for his presence in the locker room, but has also earned it for his play on the field. Clark was a menace versus the Buccaneers, his first game donning the green dot (a role usually reserved for linebackers). He recorded a sack on a perfectly timed blitz in the second quarter. Shortly after, he blew up a Buccaneers receiver to force an incompletion. His tackling was steady too, as he was one of the few players able to wrap up Bucky Irving. On the day, he finished with eight tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss, and a pass…
author: John Whiticar

title: 5 takeaways from Detroit Lions’ 31-21 win against Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The Detroit Lions returned to Ford Field on a five-game winning streak entering Week 11. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers flew up and put up a fight, but it wasn’t enough, and they lost 31-21. The first half was low-scoring, but the offense exploded in the second half, and Tampa Bay couldn’t overcome it. Here are […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Chuck Clark #36 of the Detroit Lions steps over Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after a sack during the second quarter of the NFL football game at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions returned to Ford Field on a five-game winning streak entering Week 11. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers flew up and put up a fight, but it wasn’t enough, and they lost 31-21. The first half was low-scoring, but the offense exploded in the second half, and Tampa Bay couldn’t overcome it. Here are my five takeaways from the Lions’ victory against the Buccaneers. Front seven balled out We saw it against the Patriots last week, and again against the Bucs this week. Just because EDGE Aidan Hutchinson is out doesn’t mean this defensive line can’t still bring the juice. On the very first play of the game, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield got rocked and fumbled the ball on a sack by EDGE DJ Wonnum. DJ Wonnum starting the game off with the sack! pic.twitter.com/l1aqtbRDs0 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Mayfield faced pressure often, and he was more mobile than I expected with the foot injury, which made life more difficult for the Lions’ front seven. EDGE Derrick Moore continues to play at a high level, recording his fifth sack of the season. It wasn’t just the defensive line getting to Mayfield either, as linebacker Trevor Nowaske got a huge sack in the fourth quarter to help put this game out of reach for the Bucs. They also did a fair job with their run fits, holding Bucs running back Bucky Irving to 68 yards on 18 carries. It was strong in the first half, but just as the Bucs may have started to run on Detroit, the Lions got a lead too big for them to keep leaning on him to move the ball down the field. The tight ends found some exploits Every tight end for Detroit got involved on Sunday afternoon. The biggest name was Sam LaPorta, who finished with three catches for 62 yards. He was looked at often and helped move the chains most through the air. Just because LaPorta was targeted didn’t mean the others were forgotten. Backup Brock Wright had two catches for 42 yards, and third-string Tyler Conklin had an 18-yard catch. It was a day where the 12 and 13 personnel got their chances, and Tampa Bay couldn’t figure it out early on. Detroit was using them heavily and went away from it, which was odd. Usually, this offense finds a weakness and exploits it, and they seemed to take their foot off the gas in the second half. Shoutout K.J. Britt and Chuck Clark Before the season started, I wouldn’t have thought linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Chuck Clark would be helpful depth pieces on this team, but here we are. Britt was recently signed off the New England Patriots practice squad and was considered for intel in Week 10. He got some playing time against Tampa Bay and made some crucial tackles when the team needed it, finishing with four tackles, one for a loss. Clark was seen as a potential starter with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph out at the start of the year. With Branch and now Joseph back, Clark was seen as the odd man out, but not for long, as Clark was promoted to a team captain and got the green dot on his helmet. Clark got a sack on Mayfield on Sunday, recorded eight tackles and had a pass deflection. Players like Britt and Clark stepping up when needed are good to see, and show how much depth this team has all over. If one of Detroit’s best players is down, it’s a next-man-up mentality, and those players don’t let those chances slip. I love you Jamo, but don’t do that again You’d think after what happened last week with Hutchinson’s injury, the players would be more careful with their celebrations. Wide receiver Jameson Williams didn’t hear what head coach Dan Campbell said earlier in the week about players not flipping for celebrations. Williams is a fun character, and I get he brings a lot of energy to the team, but after what just happened to Hutchinson, it should’ve been a reminder not to be too crazy. Jameson Williams’ front flip celly 😭 (📺 Fox) pic.twitter.com/HWAARWtR2c — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 Despite a slow start, Gibbs has a strong performance Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was struggling to start the game, and it made sense; the Bucs defense is one of the best in the NFL. They’ve held teams to 79 rushing yards a game and have allowed the league’s fewest rushing touchdowns in three. Gibbs met a wall and had few successful runs early, but after the Lions’ passing game took over, the lanes opened up for him. Gibbs finished with 23 carries for 98 yards and two touchdowns, along with four catches for 20 yards. He not only scored twice against the Bucs, but he’s now tied with Lions legend Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns before turning 25. Jahmyr Gibbs vs Buccaneers: 23 CAR 98 YDS 2 TD Ties Barry Sanders for the most RUSH TD before turning 25. pic.twitter.com/EwfNSmUBjz — StatMuse (@statmuse) November 22, 2026 There are seven games left this season, and this is just another record for Gibbs to run up and make it even tougher for someone to break. Gibbs won’t be 25 until March, so he will have the final seven games to run up that total. He continues to tie or break records, with plenty of time to make it even crazier for him to win, at the very least, NFL Offensive Player of the Year, but again, he is showing MVP tendencies.
author: Brandon Knapp

title: Lions vs. Bucs recap, highlights: Detroit wins 6th straight with strong performance
summary: The Detroit Lions’ win streak is now at six after they disposed of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, 31-21. It was a strong day from the Lions offense, as they only punted twice all game. Jared Goff was excellent, completing 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns. And while the Lions’ run game […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Jameson Williams #1 of the Detroit Lions runs with the ball while being chased by Benjamin Morrison #21 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the third quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ win streak is now at six after they disposed of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, 31-21. It was a strong day from the Lions offense, as they only punted twice all game. Jared Goff was excellent, completing 20-of-28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns. And while the Lions’ run game wasn’t effective all day, Jahmyr Gibbs still managed to finish with over 98 yards and two scores. In total, the Lions offense put up 386 yards—a season-high allowed by the Buccaneers’ defense. Meanwhile, the Lions defense was outstanding against the run in the first half. And while Bucky Irving started to get going in the final two quarters, Detroit’s defense made enough plays in the second half to put the game away comfortably. With the win, the Lions will move to 8-2 on the season, maintain first place in the NFC North, and if the Vikings win on Sunday night, Detroit will hold the No. 1 seed in the NFC. First quarter The Lions won the toss and deferred, giving the ball to Tampa to start the game. After a touchback on the kickoff, Baker Mayfield started the opening drive at his own 35-yard line. Detroit was able to produce a quick three-and-out thanks to a sack from DJ Wonnum on the opening play. DJ Wonnum starting the game off with the sack! pic.twitter.com/l1aqtbRDs0 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 On third down, Derrick Barnes made a nice open field tackle on a Mayfield scramble that stopped him short of the first down. After a very nice punt, the Lions were forced to start at their own 14-yard line. But a huge play to Sam LaPorta shifted the field position immediately. Jared Goff found LaPorta up the seam for a 47-yard gain. JG dropped in a DIME to Sam LaPorta who took it for 47! pic.twitter.com/8JnGMZ3998 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 But two of the next three plays were Goff passes batted at the line of scrimmage, forcing the Lions to attempt a 53-yard field goal. Jake Bates pushed it wide right, though, keeping the game scoreless after one possession from both teams. Tampa took over with great field position, and they nearly took advantage. The drive was kickstarted by a wide screen to Kenneth Gainwell for 14 yards. Then, Mayfield converted a pair of third downs with a 5-yard pass to Tez Johnson, then an 8-yard receiver screen to Chris Godwin. Tampa then faced a fourth-and-1 from the Lions’ 9-yard line, but the Lions were all over it, and K.J. Britt got the tackle for loss to force the turnover on downs. The @Lions defense is holding strong 😤 TBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yy4g1meop0 — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 Detroit’s offense was able to get out of their own zone with a trio of Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 10 yards, then a pass to Jameson Williams for 16, following by another grab from LaPorta for 11. That set them up near midfield at the end of the first quarter. Second quarter Goff went right back to Williams for another 17 yards on the first play of the next quarter, pushing Detroit near field goal range again. Toe-tappin' Waymo! pic.twitter.com/aeoT13iBfl — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Gibbs then converted a third-and-1 with an outside carry for 2. Goff then quarterback sneaked to convert another third-and-1, setting the Lions up with a new set of downs in the red zone. On the next play, Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 15-yard touchdown and a 7-0 Lions lead. The JG-ARSB connection strikes for six! pic.twitter.com/ySlgujuaVq — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 The Bucs looked to answer with a methodical drive of their own. Mayfield converted another pair of third downs with a pass to tight end Cade Otton (8 yards) and Godwin (5). While Detroit was extremely stout against the run, Mayfield was able to dink and dunk his way down the field. But facing a third-and-13 after a delay of game, the Lions sent Chuck Clark on a blitz: he got to Mayfield for the team’s second sack of the half. CAPTAIN CLARK WITH THE THIRD-DOWN SACK pic.twitter.com/wOm3Tn801t — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 After a special teams penalty on the ensuing punt, Detroit was backed up at their own 14-yard line. On the first play, Goff somehow evaded two sack attempts and found Tyler Conklin for 18 yards. Oh my, Jared pic.twitter.com/NksGPZXREy — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Goff found Brock Wright up the seam for 27 yards into Bucs territory. But after a false start and a pass to Gibbs that went for -3 yards, Detroit was in a hole they couldn’t dig themselves out of. At the two-minute warning, they faced a third-and-11 from the Bucs’ 38-yard line. They didn’t convert, setting up Bates for a 56-yard field goal. This time, he made it. 10-0 Lions. With 1:48 left and three timeouts, the Bucs had an opportunity to get on the board before halftime. Mayfield scrambled for 14 yards on third-and-9 to avoid a three-and-out. An 11-yard completion to Ted Hurst and 16-yard pass to Irving moved the Bucs comfortably into field goal range. They only had time for one shot from the 23-yard line, but Mayfield connected with Hurst for the back-breaking score with just four seconds left. 10-7 Lions. The throw 🎯 The catch 🙌 📺: #TBvsDET on FOX pic.twitter.com/nLcoZh9l03 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 22, 2026 Third quarter The Lions started with the ball looking to add to their lead. But they went three-and-out after a play-action pass on third-and-inches fell incomplete. Detroit lined up to for it, but Tate Ratledge jumped, hoping to draw the defensive offsides. Instead, he was tagged with false start and Detroit punted. It appeared the Buccaneers had scored on an 80-yard run from Irving, but a holding call erased the play, and it put the Bucs in a first-and-20 hole, instead. A third-and-17 screen came up a couple of yards short, and Detroit got their three-and-out to match. The Lions drive started out with a promising 10-yard run from Gibbs. Then, Goff salvaged the drive with a 10-yard scramble on third-and-9. Jared "Wheels" Goff pic.twitter.com/n5Umgr7oFr — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 Two plays later, Goff, with Vita Vea in his face, hit Jameson Williams for a 57-yard score. 17-7 Lions. WAYMOOOOOO 57-YARDER pic.twitter.com/YcSKTBYX73 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 22, 2026 The Buccaneers responded with a long, sustained drive. Tampa started to get the run game going behind Irving, who had four rushes over 5 yards on the drive, including a 23-yarder to get Tampa into the red zone. Irving continued his dominant drive with a 9-yard reception, forcing a couple missed tackles along the way. Then, on first-and-goal from the 1-yard line, Irving scored. 17-14 Lions. Bucky Irving powers it through for the touchdown TBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jA4eksUBiV — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 After another special teams penalty, Detroit started the next drive inside their own 13-yard line. The Lions picked up a couple of quick first downs with a 15-yard connection to Wright. Goff converted a third-and-inches with a QB sneak to his own 39-yard line to end the quarter. Fourth quarter The Lions’ drive stalled there, after Goff took a sack on second-and-5, and he couldn’t connect with St. Brown on third-and-7. Tampa took over from their own 9-yard with a chance to take their first lead of the game. They went right back to Irving to lead them downfield. But after just one first down from Irving, the Bucs faced a third-and-12, and Mayfield’s pass was well wide of its target. Tampa was forced to punt, and Detroit took over with great field position—their own 41-yard line. Detroit got an early extension of the drive with a well-timed swing pass to Gibbs on a third-and-2…

title: Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers live discussion, chat
summary: The Detroit Lions will attempt to keep their five-game winning streak alive on Sunday, as they welcome the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to Ford Field for a big NFC showdown. The Lions, at 7-2, control most of their own destiny. While they’ll eventually need help if they want to get the No. 1 seed in the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is tackled by Al-Quadin Muhammad #96 and Tyrus Wheat #99 of the Detroit Lions in the fourth quarter of the game at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions will attempt to keep their five-game winning streak alive on Sunday, as they welcome the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to Ford Field for a big NFC showdown. The Lions, at 7-2, control most of their own destiny. While they’ll eventually need help if they want to get the No. 1 seed in the NFC, everything else is within their own power: another NFC North title, the No. 2 seed in the division, and I suppose even at 15-2 record for the second time in three years. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves, but the Buccaneers will be no pushover on Sunday. Tampa may only be 3-6, but their resume is much better than that. They actually have a positive point differential, because they haven’t lost a game by more than one possession. Additionally, all of their losses have come against teams who currently hold a playoff position. It’s been a brutal schedule for them, but despite that, they still boast a top-five defense and a top-10 rushing attack. That is enough to keep any team competitive each week, and I wouldn’t expect anything less from the Buccaneers this week. title: Green Bay Packers News: Here comes the cavalry
summary: When the Green Bay Packers take the field against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night, they expect to do so with some significant reinforcements returning to the field. And it couldn’t be coming at a more critical time. The next seven weeks will determine this team’s fate, with few games on the schedule being […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 24: Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers runs out from the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Green Bay Packers take the field against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night, they expect to do so with some significant reinforcements returning to the field. And it couldn’t be coming at a more critical time. The next seven weeks will determine this team’s fate, with few games on the schedule being contests that Packers fans can circle confidently as a game they expect to win. This Wednesday’s game against the Rams might actually be the most impactful single game remaining on the schedule from a playoff perspective, due to the Rams and Packers holding the same record at 6-4 and Green Bay appearing to be a ways back of the other teams in the NFC North. Thankfully, the couple of extra days off thanks to the bye week (and the odd Wednesday game) have bought a few injured players some extra time, and it looks like they should return to game action this week. The likes of Sean Rhyan, Zaire Franklin, and Kevin Zeitler seem ready to go, which should be a big help against a strong Rams running game and pass rush. And then, of course, there’s Micah Parsons, who is expected to make his season debut on Wednesday. His recovery has been a long time coming, but “better late than never” feels like the right approach to take at this point. Getting him back for arguably the biggest non-divisional game of the year should be an emotional boost, even if he doesn’t play much in his first game action in over 11 months. Packers getting healthier on both sides of the ball | Packers.com After the Vikings dismantled the Packers’ offensive line in Week 10, Rhyan and Zeitler should be a big shot in the arm. Packers LB Zaire Franklin Explains ‘Freak’ Injury That Sidelined Him for Month | SI.com Franklin finished two practice periods after suffering his injury and couldn’t really believe what had happened earlier in the day when he saw his X-rays. Packers LT Jordan Morgan wearing cast on hand ahead of matchup with Myles Garrett | Packers Wire Here’s perhaps the one bit of bad injury-related news coming out of practice this weekend. Morgan has easily been the Packers’ best offensive lineman this year (the occasional lowlight notwithstanding) and Jordan Love will need him at his best with an incredibly tough matchup ahead of him. Kaleb Johnson is giving Green Bay Packers run game hope now that he can block | Packersnews.com ($) Johnson didn’t pass protect at all in college, according to his own words. Now that he’s starting to pick up that facet of playing running back, he’s starting to take on a broader role in the backfield. On Sunday night, the 49ers did what the Packers couldn’t a week earlier: block the Vikings’ pass rush just long enough to let Brock Purdy get the ball out of his hands. Hero Wife Punches A Hippo Who Attacked Her Husband During Their Honeymoon And Saves His Life | Fashion Times I just got back from this very area last week and I am relieved to report that we didn’t run into any aggressive hippos. title: Packers vs. Rams odds: Opening lines for Week 12 matchup
summary: On Wednesday evening, two teams contending for playoff spots in the NFC meet in the NFL’s newest example of schedule creep. The night before Thanksgiving is now, apparently, a day for football, or so the league would have you believe, and they put an exciting matchup on the calendar for that evening. The game pits […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Rob Havenstein #79 of the Los Angeles Rams blocks Isaiah McDuffie #58 of the Green Bay Packers during the first half of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Wednesday evening, two teams contending for playoff spots in the NFC meet in the NFL’s newest example of schedule creep. The night before Thanksgiving is now, apparently, a day for football, or so the league would have you believe, and they put an exciting matchup on the calendar for that evening. The game pits the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams against one another in a game that will likely have massive playoff implications. The two teams are in a 3-way tie for the NFC’s 7th and final playoff spot heading into this week (with the Seattle Seahawks joining them at a 6-4 record), though the Packers win the tiebreakers at present and currently sit in that spot. However, the winner of Wednesday’s game will have a significant leg up for that spot, getting a big win over one of the other two contenders for that slot to go a game up with a head-to-head tiebreaker to boot. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium, giving the Rams home-field advantage (such as it is in southern California). As a result, the opening line has the Rams favored by a field goal, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , reflecting that this would truly be a toss-up on a neutral field. With the game taking place on a Wednesday, both teams got a bye in Week 11 — though it only gave them an extra three days of rest beyond a normal bye week. Still, that should help both teams get a few players back who have been dealing with less serious injuries. For the Packers, that could mean that players like Zaire Franklin and Sean Rhyan could return. Of course, Micah Parsons’ long-awaited return is also expected this week, though his playing time will surely be limited. All told, the books see a somewhat lower-scoring game in the cards here. Both teams’ defenses have been playing well, while the Packers have had plenty of issues all across their offensive line. Rhyan’s return would be a welcome one, as Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett were rounding into form just before the Rams’ bye. FanDuel has the game slated for an over/under of 44.5 total points, a number that puts the game very much in the middle of the pack in terms of points expectation this week. title: NFC Playoff Picture: Packers get a little help from the 49ers
summary: The Green Bay Packers weren’t the only team on a bye this week, with the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams also taking their rest week. All the 6-4 teams in the conference on a bye meant nothing much was going to change for the Packers in the standings. Green Bay is still seventh. But […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers weren’t the only team on a bye this week, with the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams also taking their rest week. All the 6-4 teams in the conference on a bye meant nothing much was going to change for the Packers in the standings. Green Bay is still seventh. But the Packers did gain a half-game on the team directly in front of them. The 7-2 Minnesota Vikings lost to the San Francisco 49ers, so Green Bay is now just one game (plus a tiebreaker) back of Minny. Green Bay plays the Rams on Wednesday night which will be very important in the long run of the Wild Card chase. The Rams have a better NFC record than Green Bay, too, so even a three-way tie won’t help the Packers. With that being said, there was some talk of Adams potentially returning from his hamstring injury for the Rams’ Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Plus, Micah Parsons is still on track. pic.twitter.com/dj7HYaonTC — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 22, 2026 Beyond just the receiver position, there are other players who are banged up for Los Angeles, despite coming off a mini-bye — like the Packers. The limited participants for the Rams on Sunday were edge defender Myles Garrett (knee) and running back Kyrien Williams (toe). The limited participants were offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring, usually the team’s starting left guard), safety Kam Curl (toe), center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring). The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had their entire active roster available to practice for the second day in a row. Considering how banged up the roster has been this season, that’s a massive win in itself. The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s injuries. Today, the Packers listed cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receiver Bo Melton (thigh), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) as limited participants. Cisse, Melton and Moore were unable to finish the game against the Minnesota Vikings last week, while Franklin, Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Zeitler never suited up. The only surprise on this list is that McDuffie is still dealing with a rib injury, as he missed just one snap of action against the Vikings and came back into the game. Guard Aaron Banks is listed with only a knee injury, instead of both a knee and groin injury like in previous weeks, and was a full participant on Sunday. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Banks is competing at both the left guard and right guard positions for playing time this week. If Banks doesn’t earn a starting role in practice, the assumption is that those gigs will go to Laken Tomlinson (left guard) and Kevin Zeitler (right guard). It’s also worth noting that teams are only allowed three padded practices from Week 12 to Week 18 of the NFL regular season. In preparation for their Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, the Packers decided to use a padded practice on Sunday. title: On this date: Packers lose to Colts in weird and wild game
summary: There’s no Packers game today, but that gives us plenty of time to crack open the history books and find some weirdness. We don’t have to look too far, either. On this date in 2020, the Packers found themselves on the wrong end of a high-flying game in Indianapolis. The Packers rolled into Indianapolis at […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 22: Aaron Rodgers #12 of the Green Bay Packers runs with the ball against the Indianapolis Colts during the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 22, 2020 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s no Packers game today, but that gives us plenty of time to crack open the history books and find some weirdness. We don’t have to look too far, either. On this date in 2020, the Packers found themselves on the wrong end of a high-flying game in Indianapolis. The Packers rolled into Indianapolis at 7-2 but in a bit of an inconsistent funk. They’d come out of their Week 5 bye flat against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and got slapped around, losing 38-10 in a grim foreshadowing of how their season would end. They beat the Texans, but fell to the Vikings at home 28-20 in an odd, wind-shortened game that saw both teams split a grand total of 15 possessions including a single-play kneeldown drive to end the first half. Then they’d handled the San Francisco 49ers, but struggled with the Jacksonville Jaguars. All in all, it was a confusing five-game stretch. It wouldn’t get better against the Colts. The Packers turned the ball over twice in the first quarter, but the defense held off Philip Rivers (in his first Colts stint) and the Indianapolis offense long enough for Aaron Rodgers and company to find their feet in the second quarter. They reeled off three straight touchdown drives to take a 28-14 lead into halftime. But true to form for that year, the offense bogged down in the third quarter. They went three and out twice in their only two third quarter possessions. Then, after return man Darrius Shepherd fumbled on a kickoff return early in the fourth quarter, the Packers would go on to turn the ball over on downs on their first drive of the final period. All of that opened the door for a Colts rally. They scored three field goals and a touchdown on four straight second-half drives to take a 31-28 lead early in the fourth quarter. And then things got really weird. Taking possession with just over eight minutes to go, the Packers navigated their way to the Colts’ 34-yard line, but decided not to play for a tie when facing a 4th-and-1 play. But Aaron Rodgers’ pass to Jamaal Williams fell incomplete, and the Colts had a golden opportunity to put the game away. But as is so often the case, the men in stripes had different thoughts. The Colts were flagged five times on their ensuing drive, including four holding penalties and one for illegal motion. But lest you think the refs were being one sided, the Packers were also flagged twice on the same drive, once when Preston Smith jumped offside and then, bizarrely, for having too many men on the field after the dead ball caused by Smith’s offside. At one point, there were penalties on one team or the other on five straight plays. Eventually, the Colts’ drive bogged down and the Packers took over for one last, desperate drive on beginning on their own six-yard line. Rodgers threw incomplete on first and second down, but facing a 3rd and 10 with just over a minute to go, he launched a moon shot to Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who somehow hauled it in for a 47-yard gain. Back in business, the Packers managed to get all the way to the Colts’ eight-yard line but couldn’t find the end zone. Mason Crosby converted a 26-yard field goal to tie the game, though, and the contest headed for overtime. The Packers won the toss, but it didn’t take long for everything to come undone. After a completion to Aaron Jones on first down, Marquez Valdes-Scantling fumbled a short pass, turning the ball over deep in Packers’ territory. Four plays later, the game was over. Valdes-Scantling’s fumble prompted a pointed, if a bit overly dramatic, question. “How can you live with Marquez Valdes-Scantling?” asked a beat writer of Matt LaFleur. The question did little but reflect fan outrage after the costly mistake, and make no mistake, fans were incensed. MVS reported receiving death threats after his costly mistake , which is a curious reaction considering the Packers wouldn’t have even made it to overtime had he not been the one responsible for a high-difficulty catch near the end of regulation. But nobody ever claimed being a sports fan is logical. And after a game as odd and disjointed as the one they witnessed that November day, you can at least understand why fans may have come out of it feeling a bit raw. Still, don’t threaten players. That’s too far.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Value of Things: By the numbers
summary: “I come to praise Caesar, not to bury hom.” — Marc Antony There has been a common refrain this year that the Texans defense is more to blame for their pedestrian record than their offense. After all, the offense is in the top ten in scoring and they are amongst the league leaders in fewest […]
full_text: “I come to praise Caesar, not to bury hom.” — Marc Antony There has been a common refrain this year that the Texans defense is more to blame for their pedestrian record than their offense. After all, the offense is in the top ten in scoring and they are amongst the league leaders in fewest turnovers. However, statistics (as we know) are sometimes deceiving. So, in this edition on by the numbers we are taking a very deep statistical deep dive into the defense. We will start by looking at the basic numbers everyone looks at. We will also break it down by Matt Burke and DeMeco Ryans to see if we have an uptick since Ryans took over play calling duties in week five. However, we also know that some games on the positive and negative end will drive those numbers up and down, so we will look at this through the prism of game by game to see how many games were actually good games and how many games were not so good. At the end, we will introduce some new numbers that might make us rethink how we look at this defense. PPG Rank YPG Rank RYPG Rank PYPG Rank TOPG Rank Total Defense 22.2 17 325.5 22 229.4 26 96.1 11 1.0 22 This defense looks pretty darn mediocre when you look at the numbers. Of course, as I am writing this, some teams are missing that tenth data point, so some rankings could fluctuate some, but they aren’t going to fluctuate a ton. This team is who they are. The points per game actually is almost dead ass average. However, let’s take a look at the Matt Burke circa numbers in just the basic categories above. PTS Yards Rushing Passing Turnovers Bills 36 409 86 323 0 Bengals 20 267 85 182 0 Colts 19 300 89 211 3 Cowboys 34 399 75 324 0 Total 27.25 343.75 83.75 260.00 0.75 There are two ways to look at these numbers. We can look at the average or we can look game by game. I would say in terms of game by game you are usually in good shape when you hold your opponent to 20 points or less. The Texans did that half of the time. They also surrendered more than 30 twice which is usually not a good thing. It was feast or famine. That would be the same as the total yards and the passing yards. They had two good games and two bad games each. Maybe even more important than the averages are how you would look at the game by game action. Below are what we have from DeMeco Ryans. Points Yards Rushing Passing turnovers Titans 3 187 57 130 2 Jaguars 31 412 109 306 1 Giants 27 420 188 232 0 Chargers 22 315 138 177 2 Browns 27 379 99 280 1 Colts 3 167 38 129 1 Total 18.83 313.33 104.83 208.50 1.16 I think if we were to say anything we would say that we have seen general improvement in the way they have defended the pass under Ryans. He allowed only one 300 yard game out of six and it is one of the people that is threatening to be an MVP candidate in Trevor Lawrence. Of course, you could say the same about Josh Allen and Dak Prescott to a lesser extent. I do give him some allowance for the running game given that much of the Giants rushing yards came in overtime and it is the only overtime game the Texans have played this season. In regulation, they are a considerably better defensive team under Ryans than they were under Burke. Of course, Burke defenders would be right to point out that those six games included the pathetic Titans (they have been less pathetic lately) and the now pathetic Colts. Take those two games out and the numbers look remarkably similar. That’s a fair point, but I would simply say Ryans deserves some credit for making bad football teams look bad. Now, comes the more interesting question. Is the Texans defense really to blame for the team’s losses? This is where things get more complicated. I start with a basic premise. The goal of a defense is to get off the field without allowing any points. The goal of the offense should be to possess the ball, score points, and limit the number of times the opposing offense has the ball. So, under both defensive play callers, we will look at the number of defensive possessions, yards per possession, and the percentage of times that the defense allowed points. Possessions YPP Punts TO 4th PCT Bills 10 40.9 2 0 1 70.0 Bengals 12 22.3 8 0 0 33.3 Colts 9 33.3 1 3 0 55.6 Cowboys 8 49.9 2 0 0 75.0 Total 9.75 36.6 3.25 0.75 0.25 56.4 So, when you look at things this way you would actually say that the Bengal game was their most successful defensive effort. They made the Bengals punt eight times. However, I would submit when you are giving Joe Burrow the ball two more times than any other opponent you are generally asking for trouble. The other three games saw them give up scoring drives on more than half of the defensive possessions. In particular, the Bills and Cowboys games could probably be labeled as defensive failures. All that being said, not every loss can be set at the hands of the defense. The defense probably did enough to win the Bengals and first Colts game. Possessions YPP Punts TO 4th PCT Titans 9 20.8 4 2 2 11.1 Jaguars 9 45.8 2 1 1 55.6 Giants 8 52.5 4 0 0 50.0 Chargers 13 24.2 4 2 2 38.5 Browns 11 34.5 5 1 0 45.5 Colts 6 18.6 3 1 1 16.7 Total 9.33 32.7 3.67 1.16 1.00 37.5 Context matters and these numbers provide a bunch of context. Pound for pound, the Giants game was likely the worst defensive performance of the season. They allowed the most yards per possession and the Giants scored 27 points on only eight possessions. On the flip side, the Chargers game was a better defensive effort than the basic numbers would let on. Any time you let any offense have the ball 13 times they are going to find a way to put points on the board. The Texans defense as a whole has gotten better at forcing punts and better at turnover over the other team under Ryans than they were doing under Burke, but it isn’t a noticeable difference. They also have been averaging nearly 0.5 fewer possessions per game as well. If you average between 30 and 35 yards per possession, than that alone accounts for 15 to 18 yards that the Burke defenses were surrendering. The most important thing is that if we agree that if a defense keeps you from scoring half of the time or better than you should have a good chance to win that game. Then, we would see that the defense has done that six times in ten games and five out of the last six. Perhaps, that number more than any other says that the defense is playing better football with Ryans calling the plays. They are 4-2 in these last six games and probably should be 5-1 if you follow the logic that you should win games when your defense holds them to zero points on 50 or more percent of their possessions. Furthermore, they did enough defensively to win the Bengals game and you could argue they did as well in the first Colts game. So, conservatively, this team should be 6-4 and maybe even as good as 7-3 with the defense they have been running out there every week. Would that make them a title contender? Of course not. The defensive has definitely not lived up to the Super Bowl level defense billing they had in the preseason. However, a 6-4 or 7-3 football team would be in line to go to the playoffs for a fourth consecutive season. As it stands, they will gave to hustle to get there and part of that probably requires that defense become the Super Bowl level defense we thought they would be.

title: Colts-Giants opening odds: A fresh start
summary: The Indianapolis Colts have continued to look different as the season has progressed. This Sunday against the Giants, they will look incredibly different. At the game’s most important position, the Colts will start a new quarterback. Daniel Jones is out. Anthony Richardson is in. Despite the quarterback change, FanDuel Sportsbook sees more of the same […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 08: A detailed view of the Giants helmet is shown during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and New York Giants on November 8th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have continued to look different as the season has progressed. This Sunday against the Giants, they will look incredibly different. At the game’s most important position, the Colts will start a new quarterback. Daniel Jones is out. Anthony Richardson is in. Despite the quarterback change, FanDuel Sportsbook sees more of the same as the Colts are 7-point underdogs. The money line comes in at +290 and the over/under is 42.5. The Colts are coming off another dreadful performance against the Texans. Thursday marked a fateful day for Jones as it was the straw that broke the camel’s back. The season’s failure cannot be blamed on Jones alone, but his play has had a lot to do with it. A swirl of rumors as the reason for his departure lingers over the franchise. The team will turn to Richardson, but if the rest of the offense that played in Houston shows up on Sunday, it won’t matter much. The Giants have been one of the surprises this year in the NFL. At 5-3-1, they are leading the NFC East. That division isn’t great, but beating the Jaguars goes a long way to providing them legitimacy. The Giants took the lead late in the first quarter and never looked back. J.J. McCarthy is the new man in town and looking to make a statement after being traded by the Vikings. Expect the Giants to put up a massive fight. The Colts’ season is done, but that doesn’t mean there is nothing to play for. Anthony Richardson and others up and down the roster are auditioning for next year either with the Colts or elsewhere. These players are professionals. Winning against the Giants would be a great step in the right direction. Let’s see if the Colts can get it done.
