title: Colts reportedly received ‘Day 3’ draft pick in trade offer for ex-QB Daniel Jones from Ravens
summary: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Baltimore Ravens recently offered a 4th round pick in exchange for former Indianapolis Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones and a conditional 5th round pick: Jones, who was rather shockingly cut this Friday after signing a historic 2-year, $88 million contract extension this past offseason, had remained with the Colts […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts and Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens meet on the field following the Ravens 41-23 win at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Baltimore Ravens recently offered a 4th round pick in exchange for former Indianapolis Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones and a conditional 5th round pick: The Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that the fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs. Minnesota also had interest in Jones. Indy held him, then released… https://t.co/8JGafh74Yr — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 22, 2026 Jones, who was rather shockingly cut this Friday after signing a historic 2-year, $88 million contract extension this past offseason, had remained with the Colts through the league’s Tuesday, November 10th trade deadline a few weeks ago even though there was some initial level of interest by potential suitors. That was also despite the Colts already selling off a number of other veteran pieces including DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, and Keenan Allen, as well as young wideout Josh Downs. The Minnesota Vikings also expressed some level of interest in Jones right near the trade deadline before acquiring and reuniting with ex-Las Vegas Raiders veteran starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, but reportedly never made a formal offer for Jones to Indianapolis beforehand—as talks never progressed. When you factor in that the Ravens are currently 4-6 and remain a long shot to make the playoffs, and that the Colts 5th round pick would thereby be included, then it’s not a meaningful draft capital haul to just trade up 25 spots for Indianapolis, but it’s also not nothing either. It’s additional draft capital value that the Colts would’ve otherwise received, instead of releasing Jones before the weekend and gaining nothing of extra value. I understand that a few weeks ago, the Colts were not shopping Jones . He still had the confidence of head coach Shane Steichen and the support of team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. At that time, with another year still under contract for 2027 too, the Colts considered Jones a viable bridge quarterback to the 2028 campaign. It was just a matter of him righting the ship and improving his play, the further he was removed from a torn Achilles. Again, wishful thinking, but we’ll look at it from both sides. However, per NFL Insider Tom Pelissero, it was actually Colts head coach Shane Steichen, who after another consecutive dismal Jones’ performance during this past week’s Thursday Night Football, decided to finally bench his struggling veteran starter—which was a move that was also supported by Irsay-Gordon. Rather than have Jones serve as the QB3, the Colts did right by their former veteran quarterback and granted his release, with the hopes that he may be able to latch on with a playoff hopeful team for the final stretch run. They also saved on a $10.5M injury guarantee and salary cap savings for both the 2027 and 2028 campaigns . Candidly, Jones should’ve been benched weeks ago and dealt before the league’s trade deadline. No one’s going to necessarily lose sleep on not taking this reported rendition of the Ravens offer, but at the same time, Indy clearly didn’t maximize Jones’ trade value—when they tried to maximize every one else’s who recently departed. The latest failed Colts quarterback was also struggling well before the trade deadline. The idea that Jones was going to suddenly improve without the Colts best offensive lineman up front, Quenton Nelson, and after trading their two best remaining wide receivers: Keenan Allen and Josh Downs was realistically very slim. Thereafter, he was throwing behind a worse Colts offensive line and a wide receiver room that more closely resembles something you’d see in preseason than a viable first team offense positional group. Hindsight of course is always 20-20, but it’s a bit of a head-scratcher that the Colts wouldn’t deal Jones at the trade deadline a few weeks ago, only to release outright for nothing just two weeks later.

title: Colts reportedly shutting down WR Alec Pierce for remainder of 2026 season
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly shutting down wide receiver Alec Pierce for the remainder of the 2026 season, prioritizing his long-term health as the organization prepares for another rebuilding period, according to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport. Pierce has been sidelined since aggravating a left heel injury during Indianapolis’ Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Alec Pierce #14 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Miami Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are reportedly shutting down wide receiver Alec Pierce for the remainder of the 2026 season, prioritizing his long-term health as the organization prepares for another rebuilding period, according to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport . Pierce has been sidelined since aggravating a left heel injury during Indianapolis’ Week 2 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, the same heel he underwent surgery on during the offseason. The 26-year-old receiver missed nearly all of training camp before returning to practice in late August, only to suffer another setback shortly after the regular season began. He has been on injured reserve since September, with head coach Shane Steichen repeatedly declining to provide a definitive timetable for his return. According to Rapoport, Pierce has been working extensively throughout his rehabilitation and had been pushing to return for the final few games of the season. However, the Colts are reportedly unwilling to risk another setback, instead focusing on having him fully healthy for the beginning of the 2027 campaign. While Pierce had hoped to return before the end of the year, the organization’s decision effectively brings his disappointing 2026 season to an end after just two appearances. The news comes during what has become an increasingly difficult season for Indianapolis, which has fallen to 3-8 following Thursday’s loss to the Houston Texans. With the Colts already having traded several established veterans, including wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, the organization has little incentive to rush one of its most important offensive players back onto the field during a season that is unlikely to produce a playoff appearance. Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million extension during the offseason following a breakout 2025 campaign in which he recorded 47 receptions for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns, leading the NFL in yards per reception for the second consecutive season. Expectations were understandably high entering 2026, with Pierce expected to become one of the central pieces of Indianapolis’ offense. Instead, he finishes the season with just five receptions for 72 yards, a frustrating outcome for a player who had established himself as one of the league’s most dangerous vertical threats. His absence also leaves the Colts with an extremely inexperienced receiving corps over the remainder of the season. Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and rookie Deion Burks are among the remaining options, placing additional pressure on the younger players to contribute as Indianapolis evaluates its roster for the future. With Anthony Richardson now back under center following the release of Daniel Jones, having Pierce available would have provided a much-needed downfield threat, although protecting his long-term health is clearly the more important consideration. From Indianapolis’ perspective, the decision makes plenty of sense. Pierce is under contract through 2029 and remains one of the few established offensive players who could realistically contribute to the franchise’s next competitive team. With significant changes expected during the offseason and a new general manager set to take over, ensuring Pierce returns fully healthy should be a much greater priority than attempting to squeeze a few additional games out of him during an increasingly disappointing season. After an injury-plagued year that never truly got started, the Colts will now hope that a full offseason of recovery allows Pierce to return to the level that earned him one of the NFL’s largest wide receiver contracts.

title: Jaguars Winners & Losers From Week 11: Miserable Day At MetLife Stadium
summary: There have been some historically bad Jaguars games through the years. Relative to expectations and current team trends, that one against the New York Giants has got to be up there. The Jacksonville Jaguars fell on the road at the Giants, 23-18, in sloppy conditions with even sloppier play. The Jags were overpowered along the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 22: Arvell Reese #52 of the New York Giants hits Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 22, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images There have been some historically bad Jaguars games through the years. Relative to expectations and current team trends, that one against the New York Giants has got to be up there. The Jacksonville Jaguars fell on the road at the Giants, 23-18, in sloppy conditions with even sloppier play. The Jags were overpowered along the offensive line, couldn’t throw the ball, and had an even tougher time not committing penalties as the team reverted to a weird form of itself that we saw briefly at the start of this season and even more often at the start of last season. The refereeing in that game will be the subject of discussion for months to come but the Jags should never have been in a position to be one touchdown away from winning or losing to a team with J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston at quarterback. The worst part is this game is largely for nothing. The Jags had far more to lose in the mid-afternoon slot against an NFC team than they ever had to gain. And boy did they ever lose. WINNERS Defensive Line Because I mostly feel emotionally obligated to have a winner from Sunday’s game, we will go with the defensive line. New York isn’t known for stellar offensive line play and the Jags outmatched that line for most of the game. McCarthy had guys in his face and despite just one sack from Josh Hones-Allen, this unit was overall impactful. Especially in the second half, it almost became hard to count how many times McCarthy was skipping balls to his receivers because he had so much pressure on him. In total, the Jags batted away nine passes. Travon Walker had two of those swats. The defensive unit had an up-and-down day but they certainly were more consistent than the offense. The defensive line did its part. Not many others can say that. Today is @JoshHinesAllen 's second game of the season with a sack and a forced fumble. Only one player in the NFL has more such games. pic.twitter.com/TY0hIBX6ru — JaguarsPR (@JaguarsPR) November 22, 2026 LOSERS Everyone Else Now on to the not-so-fun stuff that was the rest of that seemingly endless afternoon game. Jacksonville just never got going and every little thing this team did in New Jersey felt so difficult. Watching that offense try to execute felt like trying to stuff Jordan Davis through the eye of a needle. It was painful. Trevor Lawrence (and we will talk about him below) was out of sorts the entire day. He had a weird finger injury and then later suffered a seemingly rolled ankle. His offensive line did him no favors as he was harassed all game long. On almost every throw, Lawrence was heaving the ball off his back foot and being taken to the ground. Granted, the offensive line is patchwork at best currently and the Giants have a good defensive line but something has to be done to help this dude when clearly the rhythm is off. That didn’t ever materialize. Jacksonville ran fine at times (just 77 yards on the ground in total) but that part never got going either. You would think in the driving rain that the game plan would be to run the ball, but the Jags couldn’t get that aspect of their game going. It was just a brutal effort all around. Defensively, things were not much better. Ventrell Miller was busting skulls and Arik Armstead had a few good reps but everyone else looked to be asleep at the wheel, too. Sunday’s game reminded me of that Seattle Seahawks game from last year. Yes, the final was just a one-score difference at 20-12 but if you actually watched the game it was so much more lopsided than that. Seattle had seven sacks in that game, the Giants had three. The Jags committed 10 penalties against Seattle and 13 against New York. Neither game featured the Jags running the ball well. All-around bad day. And it only got worse as injuries piled up. "We lost a football game tonight… We know who we are, we just didn't play well tonight and if you don't play well – you get beat." Trevor Lawrence on turning the page and improving. pic.twitter.com/X3hVCRw190 — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 23, 2026 Trevor Lawrence Whatever the case may be, something was really off about Lawrence. He had undoubtedly his worst game of the year in MetLife after playing like a real MVP candidate for the earlier part of the season. His offensive line didn’t help, but it also didn’t seem like Lawrence was doing much to help himself. Yet again, red zone struggles plagued Jacksonville as the team kicked a handful of close field goals and turned the ball over at the New York 11. Despite not counting as an interception, Lawrence even threw a pick on a two-point conversion. It’s a real shame that that game will largely be the NFL’s perspective on Lawrence for the foreseeable future. With much of the country watching, the Jags laid an egg. Fair or not, a lot of blame will fall on the head of Lawrence. "I played really, really poorly today… It was nice to see the fight at the end of the game. We let our defense down today." Trevor Lawrence on #JAXvsNYG pic.twitter.com/0FZ4yIdJXQ — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 23, 2026 The Tackles Part of the reason the Jags had an awful day offensively was because tackles Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen got their asses handed to them. As previously mentioned, it’s no question New York has a solid defensive line but good golly they killed the tackles. Spin move after spin move, Abdul Carter was whipping up on anyone the Jags tried to block him with. It didn’t even look like Little and Van Lanen had ever played football before. To make matters worse, with Anton Harrison already sidelined, Little got hurt. He wasn’t carted off like Harrison but an injury to him further cuts into the already thin depth of the offensive line group. To go along with a handful of penalties committed ( or maybe not ) but the tackles, this group sucked it up. If there is a flaw on this team, it’s the offensive line group. Now Walker Little is injured. At some point "Next Man Up" shows up in a not so positive way. 4 of the Jaguars top 7 lineman coming into the season are hurt or out. — Amp Wigg (@ShopTalkingWigg) November 23, 2026 Montaric Brown While the Giants defense picked on Lawrence all day, McCarthy decided to pick on cornerback Montaric Brown on the other end. McCarthy and the Giants receiver room targeted Brown early and often and the veteran corner did little to help himself. With Jarrian Jones suffering an injury, it was up to Brown and Travis Hunter to man the outside. Who would you throw against in that scenario? Jones, Little and running back Bhayshul Tuten all got banged up against the Giants. As we saw with the offensive line, things are scary up there with injuries mounting. Now the defensive backfield took another hit. If the Giants can expose the Jags’ secondary with McCarthy throwing it, imagine what could happen with a better quarterback. The Refs There really is no use screaming into the ether about the ref show that we all saw Sunday . The Parker Washington no-touchdown call is truly one of the more baffling things anyone will ever see. Sure, some of those penalties committed by the Jags were legit as we do know they are liable to rack those up from time to time. But certainly not all of those calls were legit. "Talked to the NFL offices … They felt like there was not enough clear and obvious evidence to change the ruling on the field, which was an incomplete pass." – @GeneSteratore on Parker Washington's play in the back of the end zone pic.twitter.com/QOufBig3ET — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 23, 2026 The Jags couldn’t have beaten anyone yesterday. They were given an even smaller chance to win with the refs as involved as they were. We could get all conspiratorial about that, but what’s…

title: Giants’ Jevon Holland after win over Jaguars: ‘Shout out Vegas’
summary: Shoutout to Travis. In our staff roundtable previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Week 11 matchup against the New York Giants, he named referee Craig Wrolstad as an X-Factor. Little did we know how much his crew would impact the final score. I’m never going to say that the Jaguars lost because of the refs. In this […]
full_text: Nov 22, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants safety Jevon Holland (8) shakes hands with Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) after the game at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Shoutout to Travis. In our staff roundtable previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Week 11 matchup against the New York Giants, he named referee Craig Wrolstad as an X-Factor. Little did we know how much his crew would impact the final score . I’m never going to say that the Jaguars lost because of the refs. In this particular game, Trevor Lawrence threw 2 ugly interceptions, Liam Coen made questionable decisions, Bhayshul Tuten and Walker Little and Jarrian Jones were injured, the defense couldn’t get a stop when it mattered most… I could keep going. That said, Jacksonville certainly faced an uphill battle because of “improper” officiating. On New York’s first touchdown drive, Jameis Winston was awarded a touchdown on a 4th-and-1 QB sneak. You can see his helmet touch the goal line. I guess he hid the football inside his helmet? Jameis Winston inverts into the end zone "And no Baha Men callouts this time" – Jim Nantz pic.twitter.com/HYujuOV09c — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 22, 2026 On the game’s next possession, Chris Rodriguez Jr. picked up a 1st down. Then the spot of the ball was adjusted because of replay assist — even though that’s not what replay assist is meant for. After the game, Vice President of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth said in the official pool report , “It was an improper replay assist to short of the line to gain.” Coen had to burn a challenge to correct the spot. Later in the game, there was a sequence where two blatant offside penalties were missed, one by each team. I believe Abdul Carter and Wyatt Milum were the unpenalized players. This was a fun one. this was a false start on the Jaguars ¯_(ツ)_/¯ pic.twitter.com/n60izp4sD9 — Christian D'Andrea (@TrainIsland) November 23, 2026 By the fourth quarter, the officiating was a joke. Then the Parker Washington play happened. My thoughts on the Parker Washington play in #JAXvsNYG . What do you all think? pic.twitter.com/GUd5H2W3OU — Gene Steratore (@GeneSteratore) November 23, 2026 CBS Sports Rules Analyst and former NFL referee Gene Steratore said on the broadcast, “I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think that he lost possession of the football.” Steratore posted a poll on X that has 13,923 votes at the time of this writing. 92.3% of poll voters said it was a catch. So did the vast majority of Giants fans and general football observers from across the country. So did Giants safety Jevon Holland. “The game’s over — that might have been a catch,” Holland said postgame, via Dan Duggan. “That was a hell of a play. I thought he got his foot down, I was like, ‘Damn.’ But then they called it out and I was like, ‘Shit, all right.’ Shoutout Vegas. I don’t know.” Shoutout Vegas? SHOUTOUT VEGAS?!?! The saga continued after every player, coach, and media member exited MetLife Stadium. On Sunday Night Football between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings, receiver Mike Evans caught a touchdown that looked a lot like Washington’s. But Evans was awarded six points. Mike Evans is inevitable. What a TD catch! pic.twitter.com/bnp87P1jj3 — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 23, 2026 Coen said a referee told him “the ball switched hands” on Washington’s near-touchdown. WHAT. ARE. WE. DOING. HERE?!?!?!?!?! There are poor calls made in every single game. I get it. Making immediate decisions in such a fast-paced and emotional atmosphere can’t be easy. But GEEEEEE WHIIIIIIZ. Why is there such a disconnect in how different referee crews call games?! Washington’s touchdown being kept off the scoreboard is a shame — but it isn’t the problem. The problem is that Travis called it. Different referee crews have different tendencies for how often they call certain flags. For instance, Wrolstad’s crew called the most Defensive Pass Interferences of any crew entering this weekend. Remember the 37-yard penalty against Monatic Brown that set up Winston’s QB sneak? Again, the referees did not lose the game for Jacksonville. They had plenty of deserved penalties and self-inflicted mistakes. I’ll even give the Giants some credit for playing a good game. But for the love of all that is holy… Get a harness on these zebras, commish!

summary: Here are some predictions for what we’ll see today when the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 5-3-1 New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. full_text: Nov 15, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Travis Hunter (12) looks on before the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Here are some predictions for what we’ll see today when the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 5-3-1 New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the good guys are favored by 5.5 points. Prediction #1 Travis Hunter has been excelling as a cornerback this season. Through his first nine games of the season, he has 3 interceptions, 3 pass breakups, a 77.4 PFF coverage grade (ninth in the NFL), and a 0.0 passer rating allowed in man coverage (first in the NFL). He’s probably on pace to earn All-Pro recognition. Travis Hunter coverage on his INT pic.twitter.com/cXFVgRIKuF — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 15, 2026 That will be especially true if Hunter can shut down New York superstar Malik Nabers today. The Giants’ top wideout has been up and down this year as he works his way back from an ACL injury. According to NFL Pro, “Nabers has matched up with nine individual defenders at least 10 times each this season and has not gained 35 or more receiving yards against any of them.” In other words, when Nabers has been shadowed this season, he’s been clamped up. The prediction: Travis Hunter limits Malik Nabers to under 30 receiving yards Nabers’ receiving prop is set at 67.5 yards on FanDuel. Prediction #2 Only five teams have fewer sacks than Jacksonville this season (17). It’s not a significant issue — at least not yet — because the Jaguars rank 12th in pressure rate (37.5%) and first in average time to pressure (2.42 seconds). Anthony Campanile is one of the league’s best defensive coordinators at manufacturing pressure. So long as he’s in town, the pass rush shouldn’t be a potential pitfall. But man. It sure would be nice to see Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker take the quarterback to the ground a little more often! The expensive EDGE duo has combined for 5 sacks so far this season. Maybe Jordan Davis will give them more room to operate? So I’ll go ahead and speak it into existence for us all. The prediction: Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker each record a sack Hines-Allen and Walker each have +134 odds to record a sack on FanDuel. Prediction #3 The NFL is great because it’s not about any one individual. It’s very much a team sport. With that said… A lot of games in this league come down to which team has the better player under center. Jaguars vs. Giants is an intriguing matchup, especially with poor conditions expected at MetLife Stadium… but is Trevor Lawrence vs. J.J. McCarthy really going to be that close? The prediction: Trevor Lawrence passes for twice as many yards as J.J. McCarthy Lawrence’s passing prop is set at 240.5 yards on FanDuel; McCarthy’s is set at 214.5 yards. DUUUVAL! title: Revisiting the regular-season history of modern Chiefs-Bills rivalry
summary: Despite the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills being in separate divisions, the two franchises have found a way to make it an annual tradition to face off against each other, whether in the regular or post-season. The latest battle is as significant as any, with a big stage set on Thanksgiving night against two […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills being in separate divisions, the two franchises have found a way to make it an annual tradition to face off against each other, whether in the regular or post-season. The latest battle is as significant as any, with a big stage set on Thanksgiving night against two of the conference’s top teams. It’s the first matchup since last year, when the visiting Chiefs fell flat and never gained control of a 28-21 loss that preceded a disastrous end to the 2025 season in Kansas City. That was the latest in a stretch of five consecutive years in which the Bills beat the Chiefs in the regular season. 2025 Week 9: 28-21 Loss on the Road 2024 Week 11: 30-21 Loss on the Road 2023 Week 14: 20-17 Loss at Home 2022 Week 6: 24-20 Loss at Home 2021 Week 5: 38-20 Loss at Home The last time the Chiefs won in the regular season was during the COVID year in Buffalo, a “Monday Night Football” matchup that kicked off at 4:00 p.m. Arrowhead time and featured 204 rushing yards from a backfield consisting of Clyde Edwards-Helaire, Darrel Williams and Darwin Thompson. This year’s matchup will be the third straight regular-season matchup in Buffalo for the rivalry after the two played three consecutive games in Arrowhead Stadium. This seventh edition of the Chiefs-Bills rivalry will also mark the seventh time quarterbacks Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen have squared off in the regular season. Here are the stats for each player over the six games: Mahomes: 62% completion rate, 259 passing yards per game, 10 touchdowns, 8 interceptions, with 22 rushing yards per game. Allen: 64% completion rate,256 passing yards per game, 11 touchdowns, 3 interceptions, with 40 rushing yards per game and 5 rushing touchdowns. Mahomes and Allen are joined by Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, defensive tackle Chris Jones, kicker Harrison Butker, long snapper James Winchester, Bills left tackle Dion Dawkins and kicker Tyler Bass as the only notable players still with their teams in that first 2020 matchup. With the postseason matchups included — where Kansas City is undefeated — this will be the 11th time the franchises have squared off since each received it’s gift from God in the form of a franchise quarterback. This one should be as fun as ever.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Chiefs Week 11 snap count analysis: Hunter Nourzad emerges up front
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ snap counts in the 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ snap counts in the 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Kingsley Suamataia, C Creed Humphrey, RG Hunter Nourzad, RT Joshua Ezeudu, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Emmett Johnson, TE Noah Gray and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, NT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Nohl Williams, CB Mansoor Delane, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: N/A Inactive: QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), RB Kenneth Walker (groin), RG Trey Smith (concussion), DT Omar Norman-Lott (knee), DT Peter Woods (neck), CB Melvin Smith Jr. and RT Jaylon Moore (ankle) The big takeaway: Hunter Nourzad plays well at right guard Third-year lineman Hunter Nourzad was given the nod as the starting right guard against Arizona, marking his second career start — although last year’s season finale against the Las Vegas Raiders hardly felt like a regular-season game. He was one of two players (along with right tackle Joshua Ezeudu) to play every snap of the blowout win. He switched to center for the final five snaps of his day. . @Chiefs RG Trey Smith was out with a concussion, so KC asked Hunter Nourzad to deliver a similar level of violence. Nourzad had no problem delivering. pic.twitter.com/UemvDwTHRO — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 23, 2026 He moved defenders in the run game, but allowed just one pressure over 41 pass-blocking snaps. It was a strong first impression for Nourzad, who, after years of battling veteran Mike Caliendo, may have finally broken through in the rotation. The Offensive takeaway: Jake Briningstool’s role will only grow from here Last week, backup tight end Jared Wiley went down with a season-ending ankle injury, which shed light on a banged up position with the veteran Travis Kelce (ankle) appearing on the injury report over the last month. On Sunday, tight end Noah Gray left the game — and even fullback Ben VanSumeren went out with an injury. It sets up a challenge for second-year tight end Jake Briningstool, who played a season-high 27 snaps against Arizona. He didn’t see a pass come his way, but he’s coming off two games with multiple targets each; last week against the Atlanta Falcons , he gained 20 yards on a catch-and-run before Mahomes threw him a long-range pass. Get used to No. 88 in the Chiefs’ offense; he may see a lot of work against the Buffalo Bills on a short week. The Defensive takeaway: Chiefs are sharpening the rotation up front As Kansas City moves into playoff mode, it feels like the defensive line rotation is sharpening to maximize the strengths of its role players around edge rusher George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones. Second-year defensive lineman Ashton Gillotte continues to ascend as an every-down player, whether he lines up on the edge (24 snaps) or inside (23 snaps). However, fourth-year defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah remains the first-down starter opposite Karlaftis and is versatile up and down the front depending on the situation as well. He registered two quarterback hits in 18 pass rushes against the Cardinals. To round it out, rookie edge rusher R Mason Thomas is using his athleticism on pass downs, whether to get after the quarterback (1 pressure over 16 rushes on Sunday) or handle coverage (4 snaps). title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs beating the beaks off the Cardinals
summary: Listen, I know the Kansas City Chiefs are beating up on bad teams. But you can only play the teams on your schedule. And somewhere deep inside of me still lives the little kid who expects the Chiefs to play down to their competition and lose games they are supposed to win. But that’s not […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Listen, I know the Kansas City Chiefs are beating up on bad teams. But you can only play the teams on your schedule. And somewhere deep inside of me still lives the little kid who expects the Chiefs to play down to their competition and lose games they are supposed to win. But that’s not this team. They aren’t the best Chiefs team of the Mahomes era, but to steal a quote from former Arizona Cardinals head coach Dennis Green , the Chiefs are who we thought they were. And who we thought they were was good enough to cover a -15.5 point spread by a mile. Here are five things we learned from the Chiefs’ 34-7 victory over the Red Birds. 1. This is the farewell tour Kelce deserved last season We don’t know if this is Travis Kelce’s last season playing with the Chiefs. And although he may not be 100% the player he once was, he’s still better than 90% of the tight ends in the league, and smart and savvy enough to be more than just a productive player. He is still an offensive weapon. Kelce moved past former Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Rob Gronkowski to climb to third-place all time for most touchdowns by a tight end. He now only trails Tony Gonzalez and Antonio Gates for most touchdowns by a tight end. This isn’t a situation where Kelce is some battered old war horse, limping across the finish line — he is still a big part of this offense. Finishing this day with 74 yards and two touchdowns. If this is Kelce’s last year, this is the way he deserves to go out. 2. The Chiefs have two starting running backs Rookie running back Emmett Johnson continues to be the most impressive offensive rookie in the NFL this season. Amassing 143 total yards and a touchdown in this game. On any other team, we would be talking about him as the focal point of the offense. But the Chiefs are lucky enough to have two stud running backs. The Chiefs haven’t had a tandem this good since Christian Okoye and Barry Word. Per Next Gen Stats, #Chiefs RB @Emmett10Johnson has forced a missed tackle on 41.1% of his touches this season, the highest rate in the NFL entering Sunday Night Football in Week 11 (minimum 50 touches). #ChiefsKingdom — Rob Collins (@RobCollinsTV) November 23, 2026 Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has never had a running back room this good with the Chiefs. Sure, he’s had some good running backs, like Kareem Hunt—but nothing like this. On any given day, the Chiefs have the two best running backs on the field. 3. Josh Downs might be the key to unlocking this offense We don’t know which came first, the chicken or the egg. But what we do know is that since wide receiver Josh Downs joined this offense, the Chiefs have scored 30+ in back-to-back games, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes has surpassed 300 yards passing in both outings. Patrick Mahomes hitting an RPO Slant to an outside aligned Josh Downs pic.twitter.com/WqBX3Wm2xE — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 22, 2026 Is it just a coincidence that this surge in passing offense and scoring coincides with the arrival of Downs via a trade with the Indianapolis Colts ? Maybe. It also coincides with Emmett Johnson getting the start at running back. If Downs is the cause, what about his game has been so complementary that it’s allowed the receivers around him to pick up their game as well? Maybe it’s as simple as Mahomes just needing one more quality target to throw the ball to. Or maybe Downs is rubbing off on his fellow receivers. Maybe it’s as simple as Downs being a good football player. Either way, he seems to be the missing piece to this offense. 4. Nohl Williams is an All-Pro Beyond being the next WWE superstar, Nohl Williams has become one of the marquee cornerbacks in the NFL. In fact, he’s played so well this season that I would be hard-pressed to name another cornerback who’s played better through the first ten games. But if we’re being honest, Williams is just the next player up in a long line of stellar cornerbacks who set the tone and have helped build a reputation for the Chiefs’ defense. #AllProNohl 🧥 https://t.co/4nshKX4s1s — Sneed (@jay__sneed) November 22, 2026 I mean, just watch the clip above on repeat about 100 times and try to tell me that isn’t the baddest dude in the entire NFL. Then try to tell me he isn’t the best cornerback in the NFL. You can try to make that argument if you want, but you will be talking to the wall. 5. This defense is good enough to stop the Bills Maybe I’m drinking the Kool-Aid and putting too much stock in the Chiefs beating up on three straight bad teams. But winning games builds confidence, and I haven’t seen this team with this much swagger since former Chiefs edge rusher Frank Clark talked smack on Derek Henry immediately after the game. Patrick Mahomes was pulled early in the 3rd quarter after the @Chiefs went up 34-7. Since the shellacking in Seattle this is what Mahomes has done in his last 4 games: averaging 309 yards per game, 13 TD passes zero INTs. The offense is humming and here comes the 5 game stretch… pic.twitter.com/UY6Wnsnjxl — trey wingo (@wingoz) November 22, 2026 As far as regular season games go, it doesn’t get better than a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Buffalo Bills. A Chiefs victory would go a long way to proving that the Chiefs are more than schedule merchants. Only time will tell how good this team can be. I have a sneaking suspicion this team is better than we think.

title: Chiefs News: George Karlaftis continues impressive run of sacks
summary: Outside of one drive, the Kansas City Chiefs suffocated the Arizona Cardinals’ offense during the 34-7 victory in Week 11. That relentless effort was led by Mr. Relentless himself, defensive end George Karlaftis. He had 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and three other quarterback hits. He has now produced eight sacks this season, all since […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Outside of one drive, the Kansas City Chiefs suffocated the Arizona Cardinals ’ offense during the 34-7 victory in Week 11. That relentless effort was led by Mr. Relentless himself, defensive end George Karlaftis. He had 2.5 sacks, a forced fumble and three other quarterback hits. He has now produced eight sacks this season, all since Week 6. After the game, head coach Andy Reid was asked about what the secret sauce has been for Karlaftis this year. “He got married,” Reid joked. “His wife’s actually a better athlete than he is; we’ll sign his kids right now.” “Listen, George is all business,” Reid continued. “He’s smart, tough… relentless… he’s not the flashiest guy, but he’s going to keep breaking it on you. He’s developed some moves and some skill there that he’s worked hard at.” Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news How Chiefs’ George Karlaftis added to his impressive run with back-to-back sacks | The Kansas City Star At about the same time, Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton hit Johnson, too, for a split-sack: Karlaftis and Bolton would be credited with half a sack each on that particular play. But a few moments later, it was determined Karlaftis got there first, and the official stat sheet thus showed the sack belonging only to him. What did Bolton think of the ruling? “I’m not a fan of that one,” Bolton said with a chuckle. “But George has been working his (tail) off, so kudos to that guy. I’m proud of him.” Karlaftis is making it easy to be admired. One snap later, he made certain there would be no scoring decision needed — by recording a second straight sack. That brought his day’s sack total to 2 1/2, matching a career best. How Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce are leading Chiefs in ways you can’t see on TV | The Athletic “Even though I may know,” Downs said with a smile, “they’re telling me what to do.” Downs faces a huge challenge with his new team. He’s been dropped into a new playbook halfway through the season, which is like trying to learn a new language in a classroom of native speakers. The goal, Downs said, is to not have anyone adjust to him. It’s his job to learn it all and make sure he’s not a bother to others, and he’s felt good about his progress in a short amount of time. But just in case he’s shaky on any terminology, Kelce has had his back in the huddle, telling him what he needs to do on each play. NFL Week 11 grades for every team: 49ers earn ‘A+’ for dominating Vikings, Steelers nearly fail | CBS Sports It’s starting to look like the Chiefs might have found a diamond in the rough with Emmett Johnson. With Kenneth Walker out for the second straight game with an injury, the rookie running back stepped in and was the most electrifying player on the field. Not only did the fifth-round pick top 100 rushing yards for the second straight week, but he also added 38 receiving yards. Patrick Mahomes is also starting to heat up: After throwing for 348 yards last week, he nearly matched that total with 324 yards and three touchdowns against Arizona. Mahomes has been mixing it up over the past two weeks and he did a great job of that here with seven different players catching at least two passes. The Chiefs are peaking at the right time. This team looks ready for their Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills. 2 Super Bowl LIV champions visited the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday for entirely different reasons | A to Z Sports CBS Sports reporter Evan Washburn revealed during the game that former Chiefs sixth-round pick Laurent Duvernay-Tardif was in the building in an official capacity. “Guys, you never know who you’re going to run into on a sideline,” Washburn began. “Check this out. That’s Laurent Duvernay-Tardif, former Chiefs offensive lineman, now here in a medical capacity. If you remember, this is a great story: He left his professional football career to go become a doctor. He’s now here. That’s called a residency for the month, shadowing the medical staff. He’s part of the emergency response here on the sideline. 5 takeaways | Chiefs make easy work of Cardinals, schedule now gets tougher | KSHB 41 For the sixth time in the first 10 games this season, the Chiefs hit the 30-point plateau. That’s the most in a season since 2022, when the Chiefs scored at least 30 points eight times and topped forty points three times in the regular season. Kansas City managed eight 30-point games in the last three seasons combined — three times each in 2023 and 2025 and twice in 2024. The franchise record for 30-point games in a season is 12 in 2018, though the Chiefs were only 9-3 in those games. Around the NF L Former ESPN analyst and NFL linebacker Tom Jackson dies at 75 years old | Yahoo! Sports “All of us are stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet,” Berman said. “I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on ‘NFL Primetime’ and ‘NFL Gameday,’ now ‘Sunday NFL Countdown.'” “Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst,” he added. “There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson.” 49ers’ Brock Purdy beats Vikings blitz, hears ‘MVP’ chants in Mexico City | ESPN In two previous meetings — both losses — the Niners had moved the ball but averaged just 17 points per game. Still, Shanahan projected confidence that Purdy’s previous experience against Flores’ blitz-happy scheme would prove beneficial the third time around. He was right. With Flores blitzing Purdy on 20 of his 26 drop backs (77% is the highest rate he has faced in his career), the QB calmly stood in the pocket and delivered big completion after big completion. He finished 17-of-19 for 208 yards and two touchdowns when the Vikings sent more than four pass rushers after him. Jaguars denied TD after controversial no-catch ruling for Parker Washington | USA Today The play in question saw Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence throw a strike to Washington in the back of the end-zone. Washington appeared to secure the ball and get two feet down before going to the ground. However, the officials ruled Washington had not completed the catch. The Jaguars challenged the play, but the ruling on the field stood as called, much to the surprise of CBS Sports’ broadcast booth. Both play-by-play man Jim Nantz and game analyst J.J. Watt expressed their belief Washington had recorded a touchdown as the Jaguars’ challenge was announced. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Andy Reid gives 2 injury updates after Sunday’s big win The team appeared to escape the contest injury-free until late in the fourth quarter. Shortly before the game ended, Kansas City announced that tight end Noah Gray was questionable to return with a rib injury. A — minute later, fullback Ben VanSumeren — who was seen limping off the fiefld earlier — was ruled out with a knee injury. Head coach Andy Reid acknowledged both ailments in his postgame comments. “As far as the injuries go,” said Reid, “Noah Gray got hit in the ribs. We’ll just see how he does. Then, VanSumeren tweaked his knee, there. title: Chiefs preparation to face the Bills on Thursday begins Sunday night
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Arizona Cardinals by a blowout 34-7 margin. After their first possession, the Chiefs never led by less than a touchdown. Entering Sunday, there was concern among some Chiefs observers that the time might overlook Arizona with a Thanksgiving night showdown with the 9-1 Buffalo Bills looming in […]
full_text: (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Arizona Cardinals by a blowout 34-7 margin. After their first possession, the Chiefs never led by less than a touchdown. Entering Sunday, there was concern among some Chiefs observers that the time might overlook Arizona with a Thanksgiving night showdown with the 9-1 Buffalo Bills looming in four days. In his postgame comments, head coach Andy Reid made it clear sleeping on the Cardinals — arguably the league’s worst team over the last month — was never a possibility. “That comes from the locker room,” remarked Reid. “You have the veteran players there [with] that senior leadership. Those guys don’t let anything slide. They understand where we’re at in the season and the importance of it and that every game counts. And they hammer that point home. Coaches do a nice job with it, but hearing it from a peer, I think is important. Our guys, they don’t let anything slide there.” Now comes the challenge of preparing on a short week to face the Bills — widely considered Kansas City’s biggest rivals over the last decade. “When I’m done with you, I’m going back to the office,” revealed Reid. “It’s a short drive. You’re right there. Turn the page fast.” Quarterback Patrick Mahomes had another important group to meet with after speaking to the media: his children. But the league’s biggest star will also be putting in late hours on Sunday preparing for the Bills. “I’ll make it to bedtime when I put the kids down,” he stated, “and then I’ll be studying the Buffalo Bills. So, it’ll be a pretty quick process.” Players also face the challenge of getting their bodies right on an accelerated timeframe. “I’ll go home and get a little bit of treatment,” said defensive end George Karlaftis. “[I’ll] watch this game, flush it out and then right onto Buffalo tonight. It’s a short week; everybody has to be on point. We have a lot of respect for Buffalo.” The NFL’s best offensive weapon over the last two weeks is looking forward to his first experience with the quick turnaround. “It’s going to be great,” rookie running back Emmett Johnson predicted. “It’s a quick turnaround, so we have to go back and watch film. It’s going to be really exciting playing on Thanksgiving. It’s going to be a big spotlight game. Hopefully, [I’ll] get some good Thanksgiving food after.” The Chiefs will have their first practice — and issue their first initial injury report — on Monday.

full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Your Kansas City Chiefs made it look easy on Sunday, burying the Arizona Cardinals 34-7. They needed this one with the Thanksgiving matchup with Buffalo looming large over the next four days. The home team played as clean a game as I can recall, committing no turnovers, allowing only one sack and being called for just two penalties. This one was never in doubt and was exactly the kind of game we wanted to see on a short week. Here are a few who stood out on Sunday as the Chiefs stayed hot. 7 Winners Running back Emmett Johnson: The silver lining of Ken Walker’s injury is the opportunity it has afforded Emmett Johnson— the kid has been incredible. In three quarters of snaps, Emmett Johnson racked up another 143 yards and a touchdown. He should seriously be in the OROY conversation— and lots of conversations in the Chiefs’ offensive meetings over the next few months as they figure out how to employ Ken and Emmitt together down the stretch. Tight end Travis Kelce: Kelce’s first target of the day fell incomplete. But he made up for it with the next six catches, including two touchdowns. Another week, another throwback performance for the GOAT. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: When it clicks, it’s a thing of beauty. Mahomes continues to perform at an MVP level (another 300+ yards and 3 TDs) without having to play “hero ball.” He’s executing at a high level in the pocket, and burying teams early. Patrick Mahomes with a great running game and competent receivers is literally unstoppable. Defensive end George Karlaftis : Mahomes and Johnson will get the headlines, but Karlaftis was a spectacular counterpart on the defensive side of the ball. On Sunday, Furious George added five more QB hits, 2.5 sacks, and 2 tackles for loss to his season totals. Cornerback Nohl Williams : Two passes defended, a QB hit, and two of the biggest tackles of the game— one ended a drive with a stop right at the sticks on 4th down; the other hit was a WWE-style body slam. Nohl Williams is more than on pace for Pro Bowl/All Pro recognition in his second season. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: He wasn’t able to haul in that deep pass, but he did catch a short pass on a sprint out of the backfield and take it in for a score. Expectations for Worthy should be reset— Josh Downs and Rashee Rice should get more of the volume, but Xavier can be the new Mecole Hardman, which is a very useful player in the Chiefs’ offense. Kicker Harrison Butker: Give credit where it’s due. Harrison Butker came through on Sunday, hitting all four extra points and two field goals. He also had the touchdown-saving tackle on a kickoff return, allowing the Chiefs defense to make a stand (and they did, with the first three-and-out of the afternoon). It would be a great outcome if we can look back on the early part of Butker’s season as a slump that ended before Thanksgiving. 2 Losers Quarterback Justin Fields: Seeing Justin in the huddle this week was a very enjoyable experience, because we knew it meant that the game was in hand, and Mahomes was resting safe and healthy on the sidelines. It was an opportunity for Fields to make up for his recent fumble and help run the clock out with a first down or two. Instead, the Chiefs would have to punt twice, and we still haven’t really seen enough from the backup quarterback to feel comfortable with him taking snaps that count. The rest of the league: The Kansas City Chiefs are playing great defense, running the ball, creating explosive plays, and they’re doing it with a makeshift offensive line. They are heading into the toughest stretch of their schedule, getting healthier, and playing with an easy confidence that should keep other fanbases hating the Chiefs. It’s possible that the Chiefs are underrated right now, and they are getting better. That should be concerning to the rest of the league. Note: Applying the labels “winners” or “losers” is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.

full_text: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images | Getty Images Week 11 ended in a less-than-ideal way for the Los Angeles Chargers in more ways than one. Not only did the Chargers drop their Week 11 matchup to the New York Jets with a final score of 27-24; the team announced postgame that quarterback Justin Herbert will enter the concussion protocol. Herbert was able to play for the entire game, going 15 of 21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns, no picks, and he took six sacks, which begins to explain the concussion. The Chargers were in this one right up until the end, but the Jets did just enough to snap their five-game losing streak and keep the Chargers from establishing a win streak for the first time this season. The Chargers are technically not eliminated from postseason contention, but they are tied with the Dolphins and Titans for the worst record in the NFL at 1-9. And losing Herbert is unlikely to help. DJ Uiagalelei is the next man up on the Chargers’ QB depth chart. The second-year signal caller signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after spending time at Clemson, Oregon State, and Florida State in college. He spent the 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad, and signed a futures contract with the team last offseason. He competed for the Chargers’ backup position behind Herbert with Trey Lance, but won the job when Lance landed on injured reserve in October. In 2026, he’s attempted seven passes, completing two, for 24 yards and a touchdown. Trey Lance is currently on IR with a groin injury, but he is eligible to return at any point. There is no other quarterback on the Chargers’ active roster. We will monitor this situation and update as more information becomes available.

title: Rams best move of the offseason may be one they didn’t make
summary: Rumors and or reports came out during the 2026 offseason that the Los Angeles Rams had reached out to Philadelphia Eagles to inquire about adding wide receiver A.J. Brown, but that trade between L.A. and Philly never came to be. It may have been lucky, and perhaps the best move of the Rams’ offseason. Brown […]
full_text: Rumors and or reports came out during the 2026 offseason that the Los Angeles Rams had reached out to Philadelphia Eagles to inquire about adding wide receiver A.J. Brown, but that trade between L.A. and Philly never came to be . It may have been lucky , and perhaps the best move of the Rams’ offseason. Brown has done little to nothing for his new team in New England to justify their trade, and while L.A. is having receiver injuries and issues of their own, would Brown have added depth or another piece for Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford to utilize? Knowing what know now, no. Instead of helping, Brown would’ve been an even bigger question mark on a wounded Rams team that has enough question marks of its own without the injured Brown. Other notable Rams’ offseason trades for the 2026 season The Rams made a couple big trades over the offseason include trading for cornerback Trent McDuffie. You can make the argument that McDuffie was the best move by Les Snead this past year. Myles Garrett was another newsworthy move by the Rams leading up to the 2026 regular season, but Garrett’s been hurt. Aside from one dominant game against the Washington Commanders, Garrett hasn’t done too much on the field for L.A. As good as the McDuffie trade looks so far, can you imagine how much trouble the Rams would be in had they traded for Brown? Maybe Brown would’ve come to L.A. and stayed healthy, but if we accept that trade while keeping everything else the same, Brown would have been a disaster for the Rams. How has Brown done in 2026? Through the 2026 season, Brown has 11 receptions for 128 yards with only four games played. He’s been hurt, he’s been ineffective, he’s looked like a bad trade for the Patriots, and an addition by subtraction for the Philadelphia Eagles who moved on from him. It is unclear when Brown will suit back up for the Patriots this year as he continues to deal with injuries. Who/what would the Rams have given up for Brown? It was never quite clear or revealed what the Rams planned to trade for Brown or what the Eagles wanted, but one possibility was trading Davante Adams for Brown to the Eagles, or sending Adams elsewhere so the Rams could make room for Brown on their own roster. It was unlikely that the Rams would have been able to keep all of Puka Nacua, Adams and Brown due to cap space. Regardless of the exact trade details, Adams in comparison to Brown, has had a fine 2026 season despite his own injuries. Through 2026 Adams has 30 receptions, 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games played. This includes a massive 195-yard performance against the New York Giants. Adams has been having a stellar year when healthy, Brown has been having a down year whether he’s been healthy or not. As it stands, had the Rams sent some combination of Adams and or draft capital for Brown, then the Rams would likely be sitting with a worse record than 6-4, less draft capital, and an even murkier future with Brown being stuck on L.A.’s roster. In 2026, Brown has been out-played and out-produced by basically every other receiver on the New England’s roster including DaMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Romeo Doubs. It’s unclear if Brown will be able to return to the form that made him desirable via trade in the first place. The Rams got this one right McVay and Snead aren’t perfect, but they seemed to get this move right. Brown in 2026 would have been a liability to the Rams and not a boost. Sure, there’s a world where Brown looked great in 2026 and the Rams regretted not adding him, but this isn’t that world. Instead, we are in the world where the Rams clearly made two (maybe three) great offseason moves heading into 2026, and not adding Brown may be the best move the Rams made. Life isn’t all about saying “yes” , it’s knowing when to say “no” too, and we’ll continue to see how these moves and decisions age, but so far with regard to the Rams passing on Brown, so good.

High-powered passing attacks are great in September and early October. However, good defense and running the ball have always prevailed later in the season. A Rushing Attack Built for December Football That’s the type of football that the Rams were built for. Over the last month, the Rams rank second in rushing success rate and fifth in EPA per rush. They have the running back duo that can carry the offense. While the Rams are riding a four-game winning streak, much of the conversation this week has centered around Puka Nacua and his season-ending injury . Let’s get into that and more in this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook. Puka Nacua’s Suspension and Surgery Spark Controversy There’s no doubt that wide receiver Puka Nacua has been the topic of conversation this week. The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve before he was suspended by the NFL, and then it was later announced that he had undergone season-ending surgery.“ Seahawks’ Christmas Matchup Gets New Twist With Rams Injury Report (heavy.com) “The Rams’ official schedule places their Week 14 game at San Francisco on Dec. 13. The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries on Nov. 12 , a week before the NFL imposed its suspension. Like any player who lands on IR, Nacua had to sit out four games before he could return. By the time the suspension was announced, the length of that ban and his remaining time on IR were aligned. While that situation understandably turned heads, it’s worth noting that Nacua isn’t the first player to serve a suspension while on IR. To open the week, the Rams listed 14 players on Sunday’s injury report, though eight of them were full participants – including Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, Nate Landman and Kobie Turner. Myles Garrett is still limited by his knee injury, and Kyren Williams has a sore toe that caused him to be limited, but there doesn’t seem to be much concern about either player suiting up on Wednesday against the Packers.“ Seahawks, Rams Get Intriguing Playoff Outlook Ahead of Week 12 (sports.yahoo) “San Francisco is 9-1 and, barring a collapse on this final stretch of games, the 49ers are in the driver’s seat for the NFC West. full_text: The Los Angeles Rams remain out of the NFC playoff picture heading into their Wednesday night matchup against the Green Bay Packers. The Rams are on a bye in Week 11, so they couldn’t help or hurt their playoff chances this week and nothing else that happened on Sunday moved the needle either. The Rams are tied with the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks as all teams stand at 6-4 going into Week 12, with the Packers holding the final wild card spot. Therefore, if the Rams beat the Packers on Wednesday, L.A. will temporarily move into the 7-seed and the final wild card spot. However, if the Seahawks beat the San Francisco 49ers next Sunday, then Seattle will leapfrog the Rams and move into the 7-seed. On the other hand, if the Rams lose to Green Bay this week, that will be a damaging blow to L.A.’s playoff hopes. They will be 6-5 and sit a game behind the Packers in the race for a wild card berth. Here is where things stand after Sunday. NFC playoff standings during Week 11 The 49ers beat the Vikings on Sunday Night Football and they hold a one-game lead for the number one seed in the NFC, with a three-game lead in the NFC West. If the 49ers beat the Seahawks on Sunday, it will be nearly impossible for anyone in the division to catch them. The Rams have their rematch against San Francisco in Week 14. But L.A. can’t afford anymore slip ups and losing Puka Nacua for the rest of the season can’t be an excuse. The Rams hope to have back Davante Adams this Wednesday against Green Bay, a return that couldn’t come soon enough. The only team behind L.A. with a chance is the 5-6 Cowboys after Dallas romped the Titans 51-30. But the Cowboys are still two games back in the loss column and mostly fighting to win the NFC East. The Rams are far from out of it, but they will need to beat the Packers on Wednesday to really stay in it.

Now a new report confirms the four-to-five-month recovery will sideline him through the playoffs as well. MCL surgery timeline officially ends Puka Nacua’s 2026 campaign Nacua sustained the injury on the final offensive play of the Rams’ 20-13 win over Washington on Nov. 8. A violent hit during a five-yard rushing attempt left him with MCL and PCL sprains. He finished the match with 14 receptions for 150 yards and a touchdown.“ Sean McVay: Matthew Stafford is ‘extension’ of Rams coaching staff (sports.yahoo) “It’s not every year you see an NFL quarterback in his 18th season. Especially not one who just captured the NFL MVP Award the year prior. So it’s no surprise that Sean McVay is very grateful he has a quarterback like Matthew Stafford in Los Angeles. Stafford’s production isn’t quite as excellent this season as it was last year, but he’s still thrown for 2,623 yards and 19 touchdowns so far, keeping the Rams well within playoff contention. And when speaking about Stafford this week, McVay made it clear how big a role he plays in the Rams’ success in recent years.“ ‘I Know What He Can Do When He’s Healthy’ — Chad Johnson Backs Puka Nacua as Shannon Sharpe Argues Rams Shouldn’t Reset the Market for Injured WR (sports.yahoo) “While Nacua’s injury remains a big blow for the Rams, the situation became a topic of conversation on Saturday’s episode of the “Nightcap” podcast, hosted by NFL legends Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson. Chad Johnson Outlines Why Rams Should Pay Puka Nacua Nacua was placed on injured reserve on November 12, and he is also serving a three-game suspension connected to off-field incidents that recently resulted in disciplinary action under the NFL’s Personal Conduct Policy.“ Are the Rams playing today? NFL Week 11 schedule, next game, NFC West standings (usatoday) “The good news for the Rams is they won’t have to pick up all the pieces on Sunday due to their bye in Week 11. Tight end Terrance Ferugson will miss Wednesday’s Week 12 Thanksgiving eve matchup against the Green Bay Packers , but is expected to be activated off injured reserve before his 21-day practice windo w closes. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner, however, will be coming off IR and is expected to suit up against the Packers. Despite four straight wins, the Rams’ season outlook has dramatically plummeted over the last 48 hours. Here’s a look at their record, the NFC West standings and the Rams’ remaining schedule as the season continues.“ Los Angeles Rams vs. Green Bay Packers: How to watch, listen to and live stream Week 12 (rams.com) “The Rams and the Packers last faced off in Week 5 of the 2024 season, a 24-19 loss for Los Angeles at SoFi Stadium. Quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 260 yards with one touchdown against one interception. Stafford’s top target was wide receiver Jordan Whittington who had seven receptions for 89 yards. Wide receiver Tutu Atwell had six receptions for 52 yards and tight end Colby Parkinson had seven receptions for 52 yards. Running back Kyren Williams ran for 102 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries. Defensively, defensive end Kobie Turner had two sacks, a pass defended and a forced fumble. Outside linebacker Byron Young and defensive end Braden Fiske had four total tackles and a tackle for loss each. Safety Jaylen McCollough also added an interception. Kickoff for Wednesday’s game at SoFi Stadium is scheduled for 5 p.m. pacific time on Netflix.“ Los Angeles Rams host annual holiday giveaway in Watts (cbsnews) “The Los Angeles Rams hosted their annual holiday season giveaway in Watts on Saturday.” Why the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers should be furious with the NFL (nflspinzone) “The Green Bay Packers currently sit at a 6-4 record on the season. Things have gone about as well as the organization could have ever asked for, considering Josh Jacobs was out for the first stretch of the season, the offensive line fell apart and just about every unit has dealt with debilitating injuries. That said, there have been embarrassing moments sprinkled throughout the year in Green Bay, leading to a mixed bag of vibes for the squad. There are additional similarities between the teams, such as the fact that they both have a Week 11 bye. The interesting thing about that is the two franchises leave the rest week at the same time, as they play each other coming out of it. full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images While we already know that the Denver Broncos managed to get a win in Week 11, taking down the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on Sunday, the Broncos are still in a tight battle for first place in the AFC West with the Kansas City Chiefs. Also, we have to take a peek at what the Los Angeles Chargers are doing to see if there’s any drama at the bottom of the division standings. Chiefs vs. Cardinals Score: 34-7 Chiefs Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 27/39 (69.2%), 324 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Emmett Johnson: 23 carries, 105 rushing yards (4.6 ypc), 1 TD, 4 catches, 38 receiving yards TE Travis Kelce: 6 catches, 74 yards, 2 TDs EDGE George Karlaftis: 4 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 2 TFLs, 5 QB hits CB Nohl Williams: 3 tackles, 2 PDs, 1 QB hit This game was such a blowout that Mahomes barely even played in the fourth quarter, as Justin Fields got some reps off the bench. The Chiefs’ offense has been trucking along without Kenneth Walker III for the second week in a row, as the rookie, Johnson, has done a great job picking up the slack. Also, Kansas City’s defense has looked really sharp recently, allowing 13 or fewer points in each of the last three contests, while Karlaftis has really come alive as a pass rusher. The win allows the Chiefs to keep pace with the Broncos for first place. Denver has the advantage currently with a better record against common opponents, but this will be a battle of which team flinches first down the stretch. full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders lost their seventh game in eight tries, falling 38-24 to the Denver Broncos in Week 11. However, the Raiders are still alive in the race for the third AFC Wild Card spot or seventh seed in the division, especially with the Pittsburgh Steelers losing and entering the conversation. With that in mind, let’s take a look at the AFC Playoff Picture. [Editor’s note: The standings below are before the Cincinnati Bengals-Washington Commanders game on Monday Night Football. Silver and Black Pride will update when that game goes final.] AFC playoff standings during Week 11 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 2. Denver Broncos (8-2, 4-0 vs KC common opponents) 3. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2, 3-1 vs DEN common opponents) 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4, 2-1 AFCN) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4, AFCN 2-2) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7, 3-4 vs. AFC for tiebreaker over BAL) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7, 2-5 vs AFC) 12. New York Jets (3-8, 3-5 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8, 2-6 AFC) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9, 1-6 AFC) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-9, 1-6 AFC) 16. Meanwhile, the Steelers have lost back-to-back games and will host the Broncos next week on Black Friday. New England was also off this weekend, giving the Patriots some extra time to figure out their quarterback situation now that Drake Maye is expected to miss six weeks with a broken fibula. title: Raiders-Broncos: 19 things we learned
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders fought, but they simply couldn’t keep up with the Denver Broncos on Sunday, losing 38-24. The Raiders came back from 17-0 to tie the game, but saw Denver take over in the fourth quarter as it usually does. The Raiders are now 4-7 on the season after starting 3-0. Denver is […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders fought, but they simply couldn’t keep up with the Denver Broncos on Sunday, losing 38-24. The Raiders came back from 17-0 to tie the game, but saw Denver take over in the fourth quarter as it usually does. The Raiders are now 4-7 on the season after starting 3-0. Denver is 8-2 and has won six games in a row and have beaten the Raiders in five straight games. The Raiders have lost 19 straight games to teams with a winning record. Here are some key aspects to the game: Mendoza flashes, but also has some issues: In his second career start, Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza made strides. he threw three touchdown passes and was 18 of 37 for 267 yards. He did have some accuracy issues and he threw a Pick Six that sealed the win for Denver in the fourth quarter. But there was growth and when he gets tight end Brock Bowers healthy, that will be helpful as well. Defense gives up way too many points again: Las Vegas’ defense has allowed, at least, 30 points in seven of the past eight games. The Broncos were four for four in the red zone. Rob Leonard’s unit just isn’t good enough. Ashton Jeanty comes alive: Las Vegas running back Ashton Jeanty had a run of 46 yards and a catch for a 68-yard touchdown. It’s his best explosion since early in the season. The Raiders had 143 rushing yards, the first team they cracked 100 yards on the ground since Week 3. Run defense sags again: The Broncos had had trouble running the ball all season — until Sunday. They had 13 yards rushing and Jonah Coleman had three touchdowns on the ground. Denver takes over late: Denver has been excellent in the fourth quarter and the Raiders haven’t been. That trend continued. Penalties a problem: A week after not committing a penalty, the Raiders had nine penalties Sunday. Denver had two. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said at halftime that the officials needed to call penalties both ways. Tight ends without Bowers: Bowers was ruled out Sunday morning. Kubiak said after the game he is optimistic he can play next week. Las Vegas tight ends Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas combined for two catches for 23 yards and a touchdown by Thomas. Big game next week: Even though the Raiders are floundering, they are not out of the AFC playoff picture. They need to win at the 6-4 Browns on Sunday night, though. If not, Las Vegas may be buried. Injuries mount: The Raiders have had good health luck this season for the most part. But several players were banged up Sunday. Rookie defensive tackle Tim Keenan was banged up in the second quarter with a knee injury. Defensive tackle Adam Butler went down in the second quarter with a concussion injury. Special teamer Dareke Young suffered a stinger in the second quarter. Tight end Michael Mayer injured his back in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle JJ Pegues was banged up in the fourth quarter. They will be monitored through the week. Mendoza needs to be protected better: The Broncos sacked Mendoza five times. He has been sacked 11 times in two games. Teams will be coming after him until the Raiders can protect him better. Time of possession an issue again: This has been a season-long issue. Denver held the ball for 33:44 while the Raiders had it for 26:16. Not great. Bech shows up: After being very quiet this season, 2025 second-round pick, wide receiver Jack Bech had a big day. He had eight catches for 88 yards with a score. He needs to build on this game. Crosby has quiet day: Raiders’ defensive end Maxx Crosby had been hot, but he didn’t do much Sunday. He had just one tackle. He had, at least, one tackle for loss in five straight games and he had a sack in the past three previous games. Thin at defensive tackle: The Raiders began the game without injured defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway. Then, defensive tackles Tim Keenan (knee) and Adam Butler (concussion) left the game for good in the second quarter. Then, JJ Pegues was hurt in the fourht quarter. Bad move: Denver coach Sean Payton went form it on fourth and one from its own 39 in the third quarter and a Bo Nix sneak was stuffed. The Raiders took advantage of the flipped field and scored a touchdown to tie the game. McCoy makes first start: The Raiders’ continued their major flux at an outside cornerbacks spot as rookie Jermod McCoy started ahead of Darien Porter and Zeke Masses. Now, all three of these young players have have at the spot. McCoy, a fourth-round pick, got the starting nod after logging just nine defensive snaps last week. McCoy had a nice pass breakup in the end zone in the first quarter Punt blocked: Raiders’ punter AJ Cole had his first punt blocked of the season in the first quarter and it gave Denver the ball at the Raiders’ 24-yard line. Another Cole punt was tipped in the second quarter. Not great. Streak snapped: The Broncos were 0-or-28 on third down paly of 10 or more yards. But on their first drive of the game, they converted. Denver without safety: Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones missed the game with a hamstring injury. He was Denver’s only inactive starter. Thus, the Broncos, coming off their bye week, were most healthy Raiders’ opponents to start a game in several weeks.
