title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 11 loss to the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Miami Dolphins traveled to Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York on Sunday to take on the AFC East division leading Buffalo Bills. Many — myself included — predicted a very lopsided score in favor of the home team in this one, but the Dolphins played the kind of feisty football they’ve become known […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins reacts during the fourth quarter of the game against the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins traveled to Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York on Sunday to take on the AFC East division leading Buffalo Bills. Many — myself included — predicted a very lopsided score in favor of the home team in this one, but the Dolphins played the kind of feisty football they’ve become known for under new head coach Jeff Hafley — keeping the score relatively close for most of the contest before ultimately falling by a score of 26-9. There were some positives to take away from Sunday’s performance, particularly on the defensive side of the football. Unfortunately, the offense made sure those positives wouldn’t be enough to make this one a shocking upset for the Dolphins. As we do every week, let’s take a look at the good, bad, and ugly from Miami’s loss to Buffalo. GOOD Miami’s defense forces multiple turnovers If there’s one thing the Dolphins defense can hang its hat on after Sunday’s loss, it’s that they made life considerably more difficult for Josh Allen and the rest of the Bills offense than the final score might suggest. Miami forced multiple turnovers and did a respectable job of limiting the damage when Buffalo had the football. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez had an interception — as did safety Zayne Anderson. The Bills were held to mostly field goals — with kicker Tyler Bass connecting on 4 of 5 attempts. The Dolphins’ defense consistently prevented Buffalo’s offense from turning their possessions into touchdowns — with just one Allen passing touchdown and one James Cook rushing score on the day. Hafley has his defense playing inspired football, despite the loss of three quality players on the defensive line recently — Zach Sieler, Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips. Unfortunately, there’s only so much a defense can do when the offense isn’t pulling their weight. BAD Kyle McCord has dismal day against division rival Kyle McCord’s second NFL start left Dolphins fans with more questions than answers regarding his potential as a professional quarterback. Of course, playing in Western New York has historically proven difficult for this South Florida squad and his supporting cast could have given him significantly more help on Sunday (more on that later). Still, McCord completed just 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception — finishing with a brutal 32.6 passer rating. That type of performance isn’t going to earn you a victory 99 times out of 100 in this league. McCord is a young quarterback, and nobody should expect perfection from him. There will be growing pains, mistakes, and hopefully, plenty of lessons learned along the way. However, Sunday’s game was a reminder of just how difficult finding consistent quarterback play in this league can be — and why it’s so important Miami figures out their never-ending quarterback conundrum if they expect to compete for division titles in the future. UGLY Dolphins rookies have bad case of the dropsies against Bills The Dolphins have leaned heavily on the play of their rookie class this season — for better or for worse. On Sunday, at least on offense, their rookies let them down. Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas had 13 targets against the Bills. That doesn’t sound too bad, right? Except they turned those opportunities into just 3 receptions for 38 yards and FIVE drops. Douglas was responsible for four of those, but Bell’s drop was on a perfectly placed McCord deep-shot that would have put Miami into scoring position early on in the contest. No one is writing off either Douglas or Bell after Sunday’s bad performances, but the Dolphins’ coaching staff will surely be emphasizing the importance of helping out your quarterback and reeling in footballs when they hit your hands in the future. ___ Surprising no one, the Dolphins fell to the Bills on Sunday, bringing their record to 1-9 on the year. As they continue through the back half of their schedule, eyes are beginning to turn towards the potential incoming rookies to be had in the 2027 NFL Draft. Who do you have on your wishlist? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .

title: Miami Dolphins news: Reviewing Week 11’s loss to the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, falling to 1-9. The Dolphins were outmatched throughout the game, playing tough but not being able to avoid the mistakes and growing pains that come with a rebuild. The Bills took advantage of those issues and put away their AFC East rivals in the first […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass during the second quarter of a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, falling to 1-9. The Dolphins were outmatched throughout the game, playing tough but not being able to avoid the mistakes and growing pains that come with a rebuild. The Bills took advantage of those issues and put away their AFC East rivals in the first of two games between the clubs this year. Miami leaned on its defense in this game, with linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, edge rusher Chop Robinson, and safety Zayne Anderson all shining in the loss. Miami’s offense struggled to keep up, however, especially with multiple drops from wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell; quarterback Kyle McCord, playing in his second game in the NFL, had the up-and-down performance that should be expected of a younger player, throwing some beautiful passes but also showing some inaccuracy and forcing some passes where they should not have been thrown. The Miami special teams were more consistent this week than we have seen in recent games. New kicker Daniel Carlson connected on all three of his field goals, the Dolphins’ only points on Sunday, hitting from 27 yards and twice from 52 yards. Punter Jack Browning, filling in for the injured Bradley Pinion, kicked four times for an average of 41.3 yards. A couple of his punts were only 31 yards, but he also boomed a 50-yarder that could have been downed inside the five-yard line, but the coverage team reacted to the returner signaling for a fair catch and did not realize he was letting the ball go over his head. The Bills have the best record in the NFL, and they played like it on Sunday. The Dolphins have the worst record in the league and, while they play tough and do not quit, they have that record for a reason. This season is about improvement and growth. Can they show that improvement when they face the Bills again in six weeks? Today’s edition of the Splash Zone focuses on reviews of the Dolphins-Bills matchup. title: Dolphins vs. Bills final score, immediate reactions: Miami overmatched in Week 11
summary: On paper, the Miami Dolphins came into their Week 11 game against the Buffalo Bills as the last-place team in the AFC East, facing the division leaders. On the field, the performance looked much like a last-place team facing a first-place team. Miami showed fight and had flashes, but the Bills played a systematic game […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Jason Marshall Jr. #4 of the Miami Dolphins in the third quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images On paper, the Miami Dolphins came into their Week 11 game against the Buffalo Bills as the last-place team in the AFC East, facing the division leaders. On the field, the performance looked much like a last-place team facing a first-place team. Miami showed fight and had flashes, but the Bills played a systematic game from start to finish and looked like a team tied for the league’s best record. The Dolphins had no answer for Buffalo’s deliberate offensive attack and they could not find a way through the Bills’ defense to the endzone. Miami fought, but it was clear throughout the game that the Bills are simply a better team this year. The Bills kicked a late field goal in the game, which pushed the lead out to 17 points, covering the 16.5-point spread set for this game. Final Score Dolphins 9 – 26 Bills Immediate Reactions Snap Winners Zayne Anderson, safety. Anderson recorded an interception, a sack, and 11 tackles. He also defensed three passes. He was busy all over the defense and made plays all game long. Daniel Carlson, kicker. After last week’s miserable performance by Zane Gonzalez, including two missed field goals and a missed extra-point attempt, the bar was low for Carlson in his Dolphins debut. He connected on two kicks from 52 yards out and a third from 27 yards. He also assumed the kickoff duties, something Gonzalez had not been doing. Jacob Rodriguez, linebacker. A week after being held to just one tackle, Rodriguez rebounded in a big way this week. A long with an interception, Miami’s defensive rookie of the year candidate led the game with 13 tackles. Snap Losers Note: “Losers” is not a judgment on the talent or character of any individual. It is simply a categorization of the play in one game – no disrespect is intended or should be inferred . Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, wide receivers. Drops were a massive issue in this game. Douglas caught two passes for 30 yards on ten targets while Bell had one reception for eight yards on four targets. Some passes were of target, but there were just so many drops. Miami cannot afford to be giving up big plays because a receiver does not hold on to the ball. Just a rough day for both rookies. Kyle McCord, quarterback. Making his second-career appearance, McCord looked like a quarterback who had started only one game before. He was inaccurate at times, made questionable decisions, and didn’t look as comfortable with the offense as he did last week. He was not bad, but the learning curve he is facing was evident on Sunday. McCord finished the game 12-for-33 for 102 yards with an interception. Other thoughts All-aqua look. I know there are a lot of people who do not like the Dolphins’ current version of aqua or the logo. On Sunday, they went with an all-aqua look, matching their jersey to their pants. It is not their standard look when they wear the aqua jersey, usually opting for white pants. It really worked against the Bills. Maybe it was because Buffalo was using their all-white, icy “Cold Front” uniforms, giving a good contrast to the uniforms. I really liked the look today. Chop Robinson. I felt like Robinson had a really good day, but the box score is fairly empty for him. He had three tackles, one quarterback hit, and one pass defensed. I thought he played really well, getting into the backfield against the pass and setting edge well against the run. It might be worth rewatching the defensive snaps to see if Robinson played well and just did not come up with the numbers or if the numbers indicate that he only had a few flashes then disappeared for much of the game. Running game decisions. The Dolphins’ rushing attack was interesting. Gordon picked up several runs down the stretch to reach 11 carries, but at one point in the second half, both Gordon and Jaylen Wright had five carries each. Gordon finished with 11 carries for 69 yards, and Wright had five carries for 10 yards. It felt like the coaches wanted to get Wright involved, but it came at the cost of Gordon’s carries. That does not seem like the ideal plan for the Dolphins’ offense.

Miami enters the weekend with a 1-8 record and in last place in the division. The Bills are the opposite, coming in with an 8-1 record and atop the division. The Dolphins are in contention for the top overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, while Buffalo is fighting for the top spot in the AFC playoff picture. Can a Miami team trying to establish themselves in the image of new head coach Jeff Hafley stand up against the top team in the division? The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook do not seem to think there is much of a chance of that happening. The spread has remained constant all week, with Buffalo favored by 16.5 points. That massive line is indicative of just how far apart the two teams are in 2026. It is time for our weekly look at the spread for the Dolphins’ game and some prop bets to consider. Phins up! Dolphins at Bills (-16.5) That line is huge. It is the largest spread of the week, and it makes sense why it is so big. The Dolphins are tied for the worst record in the league. The Bills are tied for the best record in the league. They are on opposite ends of the contending spectrum this year. Miami has played teams tough this year, and the defense seems to be finding its form, but they will have to play their best game of the season today. But, again, that line is huge. I am going to say Miami covers, simply because 16.5 is such a big number. Prop Bets Kyle McCord passing touchdowns: 0.5 Over: -135 Under: +104 McCord is making his second start after making his NFL debut last week. He found the endzone last weekend, but it was on a scramble. He has yet to throw a touchdown pass. If Miami is going to stay close to Buffalo, they will need to throw the ball. McCord should get at least one passing touchdown. Dolphins first drive to catch a pass: Greg Dulcich Yes: +320 I like the +320 odds here. The tight end was held without a catch last week. He has to be a bigger part of the offense, providing McCord with an emergency option when needed. I think the Dolphins will purposely target him early in this game, so I will take the yes here. Tallysight does not include this prop in their widget. James Cook rushing yards: 92.5 Over: -113 Under: -113 Cook is averaging a ridiculous 107.9 yards per game this year, which is actually only good enough for third place right now (Jahmyr Gibbs 111.1, Kenneth Walker III 109.0). Holding him to 92.5 yards would actually be a really good accomplishment based on how this year has started for the Bills’ running back. Miami is allowing 118.4 yards per game on the ground this year. I will be a homer here and take the under, but I feel like this might be a tossup pick. Chop Robinson to record a sack Yes: +146 Sacking Josh Allen is tough. He moves so well in and out of the pocket and can turn pressure into a huge gain as he takes off downfield. Even when you hit him, he does not always go down. The Dolphins’ defense has to be disciplined and keep Allen in the pocket. If they continue to play as they have recently, they should be able to at least get pressure on Allen. I will take the yes here because, if the Dolphins are going to cover, I have to believe Robinson can pull down Allen at least once. All odds provides by FanDuel Sportsbook .

title: Vikes Views: Nincompoop of the Week: Vikings at 49ers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings were easily defeated by the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City. The build up to the game was energetic, but the Vikings’ 1st half performance was not. Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense put on a clinic. The Vikings offense was unable to keep up and a pair […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings is tackled by Ephesians Prysock #28 of the San Francisco 49ers during the fourth quarter at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings were easily defeated by the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday Night Football in Mexico City. The build up to the game was energetic, but the Vikings’ 1st half performance was not. Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense put on a clinic. The Vikings offense was unable to keep up and a pair of missed field goals didn’t help. The team was never able to get it close in the second half due to an early fumble and lack of offensive production. After the hot start, the team is 1-3 in the last four and quickly losing ground to the NFC contenders. Justin Jefferson Jefferson has 7 catches on 9 targets for 86 yards and overall wasn’t bad. He fumbled on a nice 29-yard catch and run on the first drive of the second half. When the team needed him most, he was unable to step up. Jefferson hasn’t been bad this year, but he seems to come up short when there is a play to be made. The fumble seemed to end any emotional momentum the Vikings were trying to build coming out of the half. Will Reichard Another missed 50+ yard field goal from Will Reichard. He is human and it doesn’t mean he’s done forever, but it wasn’t the best week. The free kick at the end of the half is a rare opportunity to make a difference. He came up a little short with no rush at a high altitude. It was the best setup in the history of the NFL. Reichard is great, but it wasn’t his best week. Kirk Cousins The Kirk Cousins we all learned to love/hate at the same time came through this week. The Vikings had the ball with a little over two minutes left in the 1st half, down by 11 and receiving the second half kickoff. The game was fine until Kirk tossed a vintage pick-six. They followed that up with a drive that went backwards seven yards and they had to punt before the half. My vote goes to Justin Jefferson this week. He’s the super star and he needed to step up.

Chat live throughout the game Enjoy fewer ads Jump easily between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for this week, and the Vikings are an early 6.5-point favorite over the Falcons for Sunday’s game. The over/under for this one has opened at 42.5 points. The Vikings were able to hang with the Niners early in their Sunday Night Football matchup in Mexico City, but a late second quarter touchdown pass from Brock Purdy followed by a pick-six from Kirk Cousins put the purple into a hole they couldn’t dig themselves out of as they fell 35-10. The Vikings’ defense had no answers for Purdy, who completed 21-of-26 passes on the night and threw three touchdown passes. The loss dropped the Vikings to 7-3 on the season, but Minnesota still has an inside track for a playoff spot in the NFC as things stand right now. The Falcons are coming off of their bye week, but they enter this game having lost five of their last six and with a record of 3-7 overall. . .which, in the NFC South, only puts them two games out of first place. Oddly enough, they’re the only team this season to defeat the 49ers, having dealt them a 29-20 loss in Week 7 to knock them from the ranks of the NFL’s undefeated. That’s also the only game the Falcons have won since October 5. They’ve lost their last three games by a combined score of 85-30, and that streak included a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers where the Buccaneers didn’t complete a single pass. The last time these two teams met was last season in Week 2 on Sunday Night Football. That game saw Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allegier rush for a combined 219 yards and a touchdown on 38 carries, while the Vikings turned the football over four times in a 22-6 loss at U.S. Bank Stadium. While this will be Cousins’ return to U.S. Bank Stadium in a Vikings’ uniform for the first time since he left following the 2023 season, it won’t be his first return to the Twin Cities since then. He came back with the Falcons in 2024 and threw for 344 yards, but he threw a pair of interceptions and had to watch Sam Darnold throw five touchdown passes as the Vikings blew the Falcons out, 42-21. What do you think of the opening line for this one, folks? Can the Vikings get themselves back on the right track on Sunday afternoon at the Falcons’ expense?

title: Vikings Week 11 Stock Market Report
summary: The Vikings lost the most important game of their season so far in a game in Mexico City that was never close. The Vikings defense was sliced and diced by the 49ers playmakers, mostly with quick game passing, but with some longer completions to Mike Evans as well. It was really a disappointing effort across […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Mike Evans #5 of the San Francisco 49ers is tackled by James Pierre #23 and Theo Jackson #26 of the Minnesota Vikings after catching a pass during the second quarter at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Agustin Cuevas/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings lost the most important game of their season so far in a game in Mexico City that was never close. The Vikings defense was sliced and diced by the 49ers playmakers, mostly with quick game passing, but with some longer completions to Mike Evans as well. It was really a disappointing effort across the board in prime time that made the Vikings look like they don’t belong among Super Bowl contenders. Final score was 35-10, but it was really over at halftime when the 49ers were up 28-10. The 49ers seemed to put more value in winning this game than the Vikings did, and it showed. They were ready for the game of the season and the Vikings seemed just happy to be there. One player not lacking in intensity was Kirk Cousins, but not enough of his teammates- on either side of the ball- shared that intensity. With that, here is the stock market report. Stock Up Kirk Cousins. He threw a pick six, and that was a big negative to be sure, but outside of that he was the driving force of the offense all night. He didn’t have much help from his supporting cast, including the defense, but he played relatively well under the circumstances and appeared ready for the big game atmosphere when most of his teammates and coaching staff were not. In many ways he seemed more prepared than his teammates despite having been with the team only two weeks. Myles Price. He didn’t play much as a wide receiver, but was the most productive with the snaps he had. He really deserves to be WR3 at this point. Jauan Jennings was okay, but Price is better and deserves more reps than he got. James Pierre. He replaced Isaiah Rodgers and allowed basically nothing in his coverage. T.J. Hockenson. He caught all six of his targets and was able to move the chains on a couple key plays in his first game with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Stock Down Justin Jefferson. What might have been a game changing play that may have gone for a touchdown or at least the deep red zone was blown with him holding the ball in one hand away from his body and sure enough, it resulted in a fumble and turnover. A stupid mistake and a costly one. FUMBLE ‼️ 49ers recover! MINvsSF on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qRIoGFuZWE — NFL (@NFL) November 23, 2026 Christian Darrisaw. This isn’t as much about Darrisaw’s performance as his durability. It’s been an issue ever since he came back from his knee injury. He lacks intensity and just seems more concerned about injuries than anything else and once again missed a lot of a big game with a shoulder injury. He just doesn’t seem like as much of a competitor at this point in his career. And when he’s as highly paid as he is, that’s not ideal. He’s needs to step up or not be the future at left tackle. Brian Flores. He didn’t have an answer for the 49ers quick passing game nor Brock Purdy’s focus on Mike Evans. That had to be an expected counter to his defense but there wasn’t much of a response or game plan for it. Kevin O’Connell. It’s O’Connell’s job to get his team ready for what was essentially a playoff-type game. And he didn’t. It was simply a poor effort and the game was quickly lost. This is where O’Connell needs to improve if the Vikings are to win a playoff game or make a deep run in the playoffs. Both Flores and O’Connell were outcoached by Kyle Shanahan in this game. Defensive Coverage. Outside of James Pierre, it was really a poor night for coverage, whether safeties, cornerbacks, or linebackers. Defending a quick passing game means being able to win more in coverage than the Vikings were able to do and that, more than anything else, allowed the 49ers and Brock Purdy to move the ball down the field and score on multiple drives. Sell The Vikings preparation for this game. The altitude wasn’t an issue or a disadvantage- the Vikings didn’t appear to be more fatigued than the 49ers- but the game planning and preparation was lackluster and showed from the first drive to garbage time. This was the biggest of four big games in a row for the Vikings and the second one on the road. I suspect they were tired mentally and perhaps emotionally as well going into this game and it showed. Buy The Vikings’ ability to rebound from this game. It’s been a tough four-game stretch for the most part for the Vikings and really one they weren’t well prepared for. Not having a decent quarterback and offense for the first half of this four-game stretch and trying to acclimate a new quarterback two weeks ago and then having two road games- the last against the best team they’ve faced this season- is tough to do midway through the season. But a couple home games against mediocre opponents in Atlanta and Carolina should help, followed by a road game against the Patriots. The goal of this three game stretch should be first to go 3-0- or 1-0 for three straight weeks- and rebuild the intensity and focus of the team in preparation for the next more important game against the Lions on December 20th. It’s been a tough month for the team to battle through but hopefully an easier schedule the next few weeks will allow them to rebuild stronger in preparation for the postseason- which will feature the same caliber of opponents as this past month. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Purdy, Niners Rip Vikings in Sunday Night Blowout
summary: Through the first ten weeks of the 2026 National Football League season, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense made some very good offenses look very average, and made some very good quarterbacks look anywhere from average to bad. In Week 11, they ran into Brock Purdy. Purdy showed why he’s one of the league’s leading candidates for […]
full_text: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers scores a touchdown reception against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through the first ten weeks of the 2026 National Football League season, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense made some very good offenses look very average, and made some very good quarterbacks look anywhere from average to bad. In Week 11, they ran into Brock Purdy. Purdy showed why he’s one of the league’s leading candidates for Most Valuable Player, as he completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three first-half touchdowns as the San Francisco 49ers put up a big first half lead and never looked back, blowing out the Vikings at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football by a final score of 35-10. The Niners got the football first in this one, as the Vikings won the opening coin toss and elected to defer to the second half rather than take the ball first as they had done several times in previous weeks. Brock Purdy and company got things moving for the San Francisco offense early, as he connected with the venerable Mike Evans on a 3rd-and-1 to put the Niners into Minnesota territory, and a run by Deebo Samuel picked up another first down for San Francisco early. Purdy then found Samuel again on a short pass that Samuel carried into the red zone to give the Niners an early scoring opportunity. They cashed in on that opportunity, as Purdy found George Kittle for a 17-yard touchdown pass, and the “home” team was very quickly up 7-0 less than four minutes into the contest. The Vikings started their first drive at their 35-yard line after a touchback, and Kirk Cousins led the offense onto the field for his second start since he was brought back at the trade deadline. The Vikings got a quick first down on a pass to the former Niner, Jauan Jennings, to put them near midfield, and then Cousins converted a big third down on a pass to T.J. Hockenson for 20 yards to put the Vikings into San Francisco territory. Another third-down pass for Jennings fell incomplete, and the Vikings called on Will Reichard to attempt a 55-yard field goal. Reichard’s kick had the distance, but it drifted wide to the left, leaving the score at 7-0 with seven and a half minutes left in the first quarter. The second drive looked more like the Vikings’ defense, as they forced the Niners’ offense into a three-and-out, punctuated by a sack of Purdy by Eric Wilson. The subsequent punt forced the Vikings to start at their own 10-yard line. After the Vikings picked up a quick first down to start the drive, Cousins found Justin Jefferson for a gain of 29 to put the ball back into San Francisco territory. Cousins then found Hockenson again on another third down to move the ball to the 25, and the Vikings then got another first down after Nick Bosa was called for roughing the passer on Cousins to give the Vikings another first down to the 11-yard line. Then, on second down, Aaron Jones decided that the Vikings needed to get on the scoreboard. Aaron Jones runs it in for 6️⃣ MINvsSF on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/I6EHmKgZnC — NFL (@NFL) November 23, 2026 The bulldozing 11-yard run by Jones evened things up at 7-7 with just over a minute left in the first quarter of play. The Niners quickly responded, with Purdy finding Evans for another big gain, this one a chunk of 34 yards down to the Minnesota 14 as the first quarter came to an end. Two plays into the second quarter, Kittle had his second touchdown catch of the night, as he hauled one in from eight yards out to make it 14-7 in favor of the Niners. The Vikings started their next drive at the 25 and picked up a nice first down on a screen pass to Aaron Jones. A third-down pass to Tai Felton was stopped short of the first down, leaving the Vikings with a 4th-and-inches at their own 47-yard line, and the Vikings converted it on a toss to Jones that moved the ball into San Francisco territory. Minnesota picked up some more yardage before the drive stalled out, and they called on Reichard again. This time, he was good from 48 to cut the San Francisco lead to 14-10 with 6:48 left before halftime. The Niners went right down the field on offense again, even after their starting right tackle, Colton McKivitz, suffered an injury that required him to be carted off the field. Purdy kept finding holes in the Minnesota defense and, eventually, found Evans again, this time for a one-handed catch in the back of the end zone from 4 yards out to put the Niners up 21-10 just ahead of the two-minute warning. A penalty on the ensuing kick return put the Vikings in a bit of a hole to start their next drive, and the Niners made the hole even deeper as Cousins’ pass was intercepted by Ji’Ayir Brown, who walked into the end zone for an 18-yard pick-six to make it 28-10 at the two-minute warning. Cousins never saw Brown coming, and he walked right in front of Felton for an easy score to set Estadio Banorte rocking. The Vikings went three-and-out on their next drive, and it looked like the Niners had a huge return, but the return was wiped out by a penalty on San Francisco to put them back inside their own 10-yard line. After an intentional grounding call on Purdy, the Niners were forced to punt, with Myles Price making the fair catch at the Minnesota 40-yard line. After the fair catch, Will Reichard was allowed a free kick from 71 yards out, which would have been a record had it gone through the uprights, but the kick was just short, leaving the score at 28-10 as the teams went into the locker room at halftime. Minnesota got the ball first to start the second half, and Cousins found T.J. Hockenson to get the ball to midfield to convert a first down. Cousins then found Justin Jefferson for what it appeared was going to be a big play, but Jefferson cut the ball back, changed his grip on the football, and had it knocked loose for a fumble that the Niners recovered for a turnover just when it looked like the Vikings were going to get back into things. To their credit, the Vikings’ defense responded with a three-and-out after the fumble, but the Niners managed to down the punt at the Minnesota 4-yard line, setting the Vikings up on a long field. The Vikings actually got the ball out to near midfield, but the offense stalled out and forced a punt, with Zemaiah Vaughn making an outstanding play to down the ball at the 2-yard line. But Purdy and the San Francisco offense got the ball moving again, as he continued finding receivers down the field and pushed the ball into Minnesota territory. Eventually, the drive found its way down to the Minnesota 5-yard line, and Christian McCaffrey capped a 98-yard touchdown drive by taking it in from five yards out to increase the San Francisco lead to 35-10 with thirteen and a half minutes left in regulation. The Vikings took their next possession into San Francisco territory and found themselves facing a 4th-and-13 at the Niners’ 20-yard line. Cousins got pressured and found DeeJay Dallas on a short pass with space in front of him, but he was stopped two yards short of the line to gain for a turnover on downs. We’ll be honest with you, folks. . .not a whole lot else happened after that. Both teams eventually pulled their starting quarterbacks, with Mac Jones coming in for San Francisco and Carson Wentz coming in to relieve Kirk Cousins for Minnesota. Nobody scored any more points, and the game ended with the Niners’ faithful in Mexico City celebrating a big victory on Sunday night. The big story of the game was Purdy and how he handled the Vikings’ blitz. Brian Flores did to Purdy what he does to every other quarterback, and Purdy handled it better than anyone else. He completed 17-of-19 pass attempts against the Vikings’ blitz for 208 yards and two of his three touchdowns. The Vikings just couldn’t get themselves right after…

(Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve got the results of our SB Nation Reacts poll about our Minnesota Vikings for this week, and we told you that we’d have the results for you before Sunday Night Football, so. . .here we go! Our first question of the week, as always, is whether or not you think the Vikings are moving in the right direction. Strangely enough, when you pair an actual, honest-to-goodness, functioning National Football League offense with the NFL’s best offense, fans start feeling a whole lot better about things than they had previously. We are now up to 89% of Vikings fans who feel that the Vikings are moving in the right direction, which is a new high for this season. Honestly, after what we saw against the Packers last week, it’s hard to blame anyone for feeling optimistic about this team, isn’t it? They broke the 30-point mark for just the second time this season, they completed the sweep against a hated rival, and it looks like they have a new lease on life going into one of the biggest games of the year. Speaking of that game, our other question this week had to do with how everybody feels about tonight’s big matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. It seems like a lot of people believe that the Vikings have a pretty good chance in a game that could serve to give them the upper hand in the race for the #1 overall seed in the NFC playoff race. Of those who responded to our poll, a full 70% believe that the Vikings will emerge victorious. We had 45% who think that the Vikings will win in a close one, by a margin of somewhere between 1-8 points, and another 25% who believe that they will win by more than a touchdown (and a two-point conversion). Only 30% of our respondents believe that the Vikings will take the “L” in tonight’s game, with 18% thinking the Vikings will lose by less than a score and 12% believing that they’ll lose by more. Honestly, as we’ve been saying all week, with this defense and, now, with an actual competent offense, this team can hang with. . .and beat. . .any team in the National Football League. The Niners are very impressive on offense, certainly, but the only thing that’s been shown to be able to slow down the Vikings’ defense this season is time of possession. If the Vikings’ offense can stay on the field, sustain drives, and keep the defense fresh, our squad can come out of this one at 8-2. Those are the results of our SB Nation Reacts poll for this week, ladies and gentlemen. title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. [UPDATE 11/17/2026] Appearing on local radio, Patriots safety Kevin Byard said that Maye was “probably out for the season.” [UPDATE 11/19/2026] Speaking to Scott Zolak in a 1-on-1 interview, Mike Vrabel referenced Maye’s injury being a “short term” issue : “I think he’s going to be unavailable here for the short time, and we’ll see how that goes down the road.” [UPDATE 11/20/2026] According to a report by ESPN, Maye suffered a fractured fibula without any ligament damage against the Lions. While no surgery will be necessary, the injury will sideline him deep into the season if not for the remainder of the year. [UPDATE 11/22/2026] Drake Maye’s injury will sideline him for at least six weeks , which does leave the door slightly ajar for a potential comeback later in the season. What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots won’t immediately add third QB, continue to back Tommy DeVito as starter
summary: The New England Patriots are expected to have interest in quarterback Daniel Jones following his release from the Indianapolis Colts, but a signing does not appear to be imminent. Instead, head coach Mike Vrabel continues to back Tommy DeVito as the Patriots’ starter with regular QB1 Drake Maye sidelined due to injury. “This is Day […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are expected to have interest in quarterback Daniel Jones following his release from the Indianapolis Colts , but a signing does not appear to be imminent. Instead, head coach Mike Vrabel continues to back Tommy DeVito as the Patriots’ starter with regular QB1 Drake Maye sidelined due to injury. “This is Day 1 of what we’re going to look like here going forward with Tommy,” Vrabel told WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. “We talked about [adding another quarterback]. I don’t think that that’s something that will happen today. But we’ll see. I don’t know that that’s something that we necessarily think. We have guys that have been with us, understand what we’re doing, and how we want to try to do it.” DeVito first arrived in New England as a waiver claim in August 2025, following his release from the New York Giants. He spent his first year with the club as the third-string quarterback behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs, and as a consequence saw no game action at any point throughout the season — a first in his three-year NFL career. Nonetheless, the Patriots were happy with DeVito’s development and signed him to a two-year, xx million contract extension in early March. Two weeks later, they released Dobbs. DeVito entered the 2026 regular season as the Patriots’ second-string quarterback between Maye and rookie Behren Morton, and as such appeared in two games before permanently taking over against the Detroit Lions in Week 10: when Maye suffered a broken fibula on the opening drive, New England turned to its backup. DeVito ended up completing 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each in a 35-10 loss. Now at 5-5, the Patriots are seemingly holding out hope for Maye to return at some point; he is reportedly expected to miss at least six weeks, which would leave the door open for a comeback down the stretch. For the time being, however, they are rallying behind DeVito. “We’ll see how he progresses and how long that takes,” Vrabel said about Maye. “I don’t think there’s any timetable right now. We’ll have to play and go here with ‘Two Chains’ and play good football, and find ways to win a game here.”

full_text: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is reportedly expected to miss “multiple weeks” due to the hamstring injury he suffered during the New England Patriots’ game against the Detroit Lions in Germany. On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed his status, at least for this week. “He won’t be out there today. I wouldn’t anticipate him playing this week,” Vrabel told WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . Brown hurt his hamstring in the third quarter of the Patriots 35-10 loss versus the Lions. He had to exit the game after a 21-yard catch and run, and shortly thereafter was ruled out. It was the third time the offseason trade acquisition has been banged up this year. Brown, who was brought in from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for first- and fourth-round draft choices in 2028 and 2027, respectively, suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 against Seattle. He missed four games on injured reserve before a return that was cut short to two weeks because of a knee flare-up. The 29-year-old did make a comeback against Detroit, but played only 28 snaps before departing again. Despite his bad injury luck, Vrabel remains optimistic. “I know he’s working hard to get back,” he said. “After the training camp that he had, I wouldn’t have anticipated anything. Injuries are part of the game. He gets rolled up on, and then gets dragged down the other day. That was unfortunate. We’ll just keep trying to get him healthy, and whenever he can get back out there to help us I know that he will.” Coming off their bye, the Patriots will travel to Los Angeles this weekend to take on the Chargers. Besides Brown, they also will be without starting quarterback Drake Maye, who suffered a broken fibula on the opening drive against the Lions.

title: Patriots expected to show interest in Daniel Jones, but there’s a catch
summary: With their season at a crossroads in light of the fractured fibula suffered by starting quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots are exploring the possibility of adding another passer to the mix. One name to keep an eye on is Daniel Jones, who was let go by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday. Jones, 29, […]
full_text: With their season at a crossroads in light of the fractured fibula suffered by starting quarterback Drake Maye, the New England Patriots are exploring the possibility of adding another passer to the mix. One name to keep an eye on is Daniel Jones, who was let go by the Indianapolis Colts on Friday . Jones, 29, was placed on waivers, meaning that any team has the opportunity to claim him. However, according to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, that is not expected to happen. And once he makes it through the wire and to the open market, the Patriots are among the teams expected to take a look at him. “The Patriots along with the Baltimore Ravens and maybe the Arizona Cardinals are expected to have interest in the recently-waived former Colts starter,” Rapoport said on the air on Sunday. “He goes on waivers. We find out 4 p.m. on Monday whether or not anyone claims him. Unlikely because of the $2 million due this year, $10 million guaranteed for injury next year.” With Maye potentially missing the next six weeks , if not more, the Patriots are looking at a starter-backup combination of Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton. Adding Jones to the mix would therefore make sense given his experience in the NFL and the fact that he has played some winning football previously in his career. However, there is a catch: the former first-round draft pick appears to be willing to wait for the right opportunity to come along. “If he clears [waivers], my understanding is that Daniel Jones is expected to wait,” Rapoport said. “Just to wait, see if there’s another quarterback injury. Of course, if there was, he would be the first call of any playoff team needing a quarterback.” If Jones is indeed in no rush to sign with a team, the Patriots’ interest might just start to evaporate. At 5-5 and the current eighth playoff seed in the AFC, they simply might not have time to wait for Jones. Instead, they might just try their luck with DeVito — who is in his second year in the system — rather than try to bring Jones aboard late and then try to get him up to starter-caliber speed. The Patriots, with DeVito currently atop their quarterback depth chart, will visit the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12.

full_text: The New England Patriots are entering Week 12 with significant questions at the quarterback position. So does their upcoming opponent. Los Angeles Chargers starter Justin Herbert was placed in concussion protocol following his team’s 27-24 loss to the New York Jets on Sunday. The two-time Pro Bowler did finish the game, completing 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and a pair of touchdowns. He also scored a rushing touchdown. However, Herbert was sacked six times during the game and tackled on an additional seven plays. Head coach Jim Harbaugh did not address his quarterback’s status during his postgame press conference. Herbert’s status will be one of the main stories heading into the Chargers’ upcoming game with the Patriots. Should he be unable to go, D.J. Uiagalelei is expected to draw the start this coming Sunday. Arriving in L.A. as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Uiagalelei spent his rookie campaign on the team’s practice squad. He entered his sophomore year as the third option on the depth chart behind Herbert and second-stringer Trey Lance, but moved up a spot when the latter was placed on injured reserve in October. So far in 2026, Uiagalelei has gone 2-for-7 for 24 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots, meanwhile, will be without their own starting quarterback in Week 12. Drake Maye suffered a fractured fibula during his club’s loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 10, and is expected to miss at least six weeks due to the ailment. Tommy DeVito replaced Maye against the Lions and projects as the next man up this week; rookie Behren Morton is in line move up into the backup spot. Kickoff between the Patriots and Chargers is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on Nov. 29. A rematch of last year’s wild card meeting between the two teams, it was originally set as a prime time contest but was flexed out after Maye’s injury and the Chargers’ 1-8 start.

full_text: The New England Patriots are on their bye this weekend, and it is a much-needed one. The team has struggled with injuries throughout the season, including most recently starting quarterback Drake Maye. While Maye’s outlook remains uncertain , the team as a whole is able to catch its breath after an excruciating 10 weeks of football. This means that we are also able to do that. And so, without further ado, let’s take a look at the football that is being played in Week 11 and who the Patriots and their fans should be rooting for. Before doing so, however, a quick explainer: as long as the Patriots are still theoretically alive in the race for the AFC East and a playoff spot, we will root with that possibility in mind. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Indianapolis Colts (3-7) at Houston Texans (3-6): Go Colts! The Colts have seemingly given up on the season, which in turn makes them far less a threat to a potential Patriots playoff run. And while the Texans have also not shined so far this year, they are a talented team capable of making a push over the second half of the season. | Prime Video Sunday 1 p.m. ET Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Buffalo Bills (8-1) : Go Dolphins! The Patriots’ chances of repeating as AFC East champions are slim, but until they are mathematically eliminated from the division race — as mentioned above — we will keep rooting against their rivals from Buffalo. To be fair, we would probably root against them in any scenario, but you get the point. | CBS Baltimore Ravens (4-6) at Carolina Panthers (4-5) : Go Panthers! The Ravens’ season has gone haywire after a 4-1 start, but they are still a theoretical player in the competition for playoff spots in the AFC. So, we will go with the classic NFC over AFC pick in this one. | FOX New Orleans Saints (3-6) at Chicago Bears (7-2) : Go Bears! There are two factors at play here. A Bears win would improve New England’s strength of schedule tiebreaker, and also help with the positioning of the 2027 sixth-round pick acquired from the Saints in the Ja’Lynn Polk trade. But don’t the Patriots also have Bears pick in the fourth round after sending them Garrett Bradbury? Yes, they do, but the higher of the two picks will transfer to Philadelphia as part of the A.J. Brown trade, so that selection essentially doesn’t matter. | FOX Tennessee Titans (1-8) at Dallas Cowboys (4-6) : Go Cowboys! Dallas losing would be fun, but the first overall pick in next year’s draft not going to an AFC East team would be as well. Hence, a pick against Tennessee in this one to keep them well-positioned in that particular race. | FOX Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) at Detroit Lions (7-2) : Go Lions! Four words: strength of schedule tiebreaker. | FOX Arizona Cardinals (3-7) at Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) : Go Cardinals! The Patriots need to get all the help they can get if they want to qualify for the playoffs, and their conference rivals losing what on paper is winnable games would be a good start. | CBS Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) : Go Eagles! See above. | CBS 4:05 p.m. ET New York Jets (2-8) at Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) : Go Jets! Welcome everybody to the Putrid Bowl. The Jets look destined to remain a non-factor in the playoff race even if they win in Los Angeles on Sunday, while a win would further remove them from the No. 1 draft pick. Meanwhile, the Chargers’ momentum after their first win of the season would be halted just before the Patriots come to town in Week 12. | FOX 4:25 p.m. ET Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) at Denver Broncos (7-2) : Go Raiders! The Patriots hold the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Raiders, so they shouldn’t worry too much about Las Vegas making up some ground — especially if it comes at the expense of a team currently in the playoff picture. | CBS Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) at New York Giants (5-3-1) : Go Giants! The Jaguars are likely to finish the season as AFC South champions, which in turn wouldn’t impact the Patriots’ own playoff outlook. That said, it’s b better to be safe than sorry when it comes to seeding and qualifying possibilities, so let’s go with the Giants here. | CBS 8:20 p.m. ET Minnesota Vikings (7-2) at San Francisco 49ers (8-1) : Go Vikings! There is one reason we are picking Minnesota here: the Vikings are on the Patriots schedule, and the 49ers are not. This is purely a pick with tiebreakers in mind. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) at Washington Commanders (3-5-1): Go Commanders! We are back in NFC over AFC territory for that one. | ESPN

title: One offensive positive from Saints loss to Bears
summary: The New Orleans Saints didn’t leave Soldier Field with the result they wanted against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, but there was at least one encouraging takeaway from Sunday’s loss. Despite another disappointing outcome, the Saints found success on third down against Dennis Allen’s defense that had made it one of the most difficult situations […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 22: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints takes off running in the first quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints didn’t leave Soldier Field with the result they wanted against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, but there was at least one encouraging takeaway from Sunday’s loss. Despite another disappointing outcome, the Saints found success on third down against Dennis Allen’s defense that had made it one of the most difficult situations for opposing offenses all season. New Orleans converted eight of 17 third-down attempts, finishing with a 47% conversion rate. That was the highest third-down percentage Chicago had allowed in a single game all season. Heading into Sunday’s matchup, the Bears were allowing opponents to convert just 22.8% of their third downs, the best mark in the NFL. The Saints more than doubled that percentage, finding ways to extend drives and keep their offense on the field against a defense that had consistently held their own in that department. For an offense that has struggled to find consistency, that kind of production is worth acknowledging and perhaps can lead to bigger developments. Obviously, converting third downs didn’t translate into the outcome the Saints needed. A strong performance in one area can’t make up for the other mistakes that ultimately contributed to the loss. That said, there is still something to build on from the performance. The Saints have more than plenty of issues to address moving forward, but there were certainly still some positives to takeaway from the loss. Now, the challenge is turning that production into more consistent offensive performances and, ultimately, wins.

title: Saints vs. Bears: The good, the bad, and the ugly from Week 11
summary: The Good: Defense All things considered the Saints defense played pretty well on Sunday. They held one of the better offenses in the NFL in the Bears to just 19 points and held Caleb Williams to 181 yards. The Saints defense also sacked Williams twice, and got four tackles for loss. They also got two […]
full_text: The Good: Defense All things considered the Saints defense played pretty well on Sunday. They held one of the better offenses in the NFL in the Bears to just 19 points and held Caleb Williams to 181 yards. The Saints defense also sacked Williams twice, and got four tackles for loss. They also got two takeaways, both through the efforts of Carl Granderson who tipped a pass that was intercepted by Danny Stutsman and forced a fumble that was recovered by Julian Blackmon. The Bad: Pass protection Tyler Shough was under duress all day as the Saints allowed 6 sacks. Shough had a hand in some of these as he left the pocket too early and scrambled into the defenders arms, but the Saints allowed Jeffrey Simmons to live in the backfield almost the whole game and allowed a total of 10 tackles for loss. The Ugly: More of the same Feels like I am writing the same thing every week, but the Saints continue to make no adjustments and simply nothing is changing. Once again they fell behind early, once again they turned the ball over multiple times, once again they squandered opportunities to get back in the game late, and once again they failed to adequately get the run game going. Travis Etienne Jr. actually became the first Saint to run for over 75 yards this year, but 46 of those yards came on one play. Take that away and he only averaged 2.3 yards per rush. They once again missed a field goal, and did not use Alvin Kamara in any meaningful way despite him scoring the only touchdown of the afternoon. The direction of the team is completely backwards and unfortunately, until changes are made, the results on the field will be the same.

title: ‘Great win’ shows that the NY Giants really are a good football team
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants’ 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars wasn’t pretty. It was nail-biting. It was more difficult than it needed to be. It ended up, though, being what some would call a signature victory. A victory over a 7-2 team that had won three straight games and scored 31 […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants’ 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars wasn’t pretty. It was nail-biting. It was more difficult than it needed to be. It ended up, though, being what some would call a signature victory. A victory over a 7-2 team that had won three straight games and scored 31 or more points in four straight. It was the Giants’ first victory over a team that currently has a winning record. Head coach John Harbaugh didn’t really want to sign off on the “signature victory” narrative on Sunday night. He just called it “a great win.” “I do respect it, definitely. I think that’s right, but I’m not going to say that because I don’t think we need to make it. We don’t really worry about that, we don’t really care what they think or what they say. It’s not our concern how we’re evaluated. It’s our concern how we play,” he said. “And that’s the thing I think our guys are so focused on. And if you keep the focus there, then you’ve got a chance to go out and play the way we played tonight, so I’m proud of the guys that way. But whatever you want to call it, it’s a great win. “I mean, I’m in the locker room saying that’s a real football win right there. That’s a real win. That’s a really good team. That’s a very well-coached football team. That’s a great quarterback (Trevor Lawrence). That’s a team that’s been playing excellent team football, all three phases, and we won it, so I’m proud of that win.” As he should be. Few prognosticators thought the Giants would pull it off. No one here at Big Blue View picked the Giants to win the game. “We heard everybody pretty much counted us out, that we pretty much had no chance, that we couldn’t stick with their offense. But we took that as disrespect, and we came out with a chip on our shoulder,” said edge defender Abdul Carter, who had the best game of his career on Sunday. “I think we proved that we are worthy. They keep saying we can’t beat these teams. We can’t beat them. I don’t know why they’re saying that, but what are they going to say now?” NFC East impact Let’s start by saying that Sunday was a massive step for the Giants toward winning their first NFC East title since 2011. Here are the current division standings: Giants 6-3-1 Dallas Cowboys 5-6 Washington Commanders 3-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles 3-7 Here is the Giants’ remaining schedule: at Indianapolis (3-8) vs. San Francisco (8-1) at Seattle (6-4) vs. Cleveland (6-4) at Detroit (8-2) at Dallas (5-6) vs. Philadelphia (3-7) Let’s say the Giants get to nine wins, which seems reasonable. Dallas would have to go 5-1 to get to 10. Washington, which plays Monday night against the Cincinnati Bengals, would have to go 6-2 to get to nine. We’ll know more by the end of the day as to whether they have a real chance to do that. Team Rankings now gives the Giants a 71.9% chance of winning the division and a 73.3% chance of making the playoffs. Resilience is this team’s hallmark All of the familiar issues we have seen with the Giants this season surfaced against the Jaguars. Placekicker Dominic Zvada missed a chip shot 32-yard field goal, yanking yet another kick wide left from the right hash mark. Cam Skattebo’s fumble was his fifth of the season and the Giants’ 18th. Only the lowly Los Angeles Chargers (19) have fumbled more often. It came when the Giants were threatening to turn Sunday into a rout, and made winning much more harrowing. The run game, with Skattebo carrying 14 times for 34 yards (2.4 yards per carry), bogged down to the point where the Giants mostly refused to use it. Over a four-possession, 13-play stretch where they managed just one first down late in the third quarter through the fourth quarter, the Giants ran the ball just one time. That is the exact opposite of what a team trying to protect a lead and bleed the clock would generally do. Yet, the Giants played through all of that. They played through a couple of critical penalties. They played through some questionable officiating that impacted both teams. They played through quarterback J.J. McCarthy having an up-and-down game and missing a couple of deep throws to Darnell Mooney that should have been touchdowns. “We had an opportunity early in the third quarter to put that game away, and we didn’t do it. We go down, and we miss the kick, we don’t score the touchdown, and then we miss the kick, and then we turned the ball over,” Harbaugh said. “But I will say this, how about the quarterback (J.J. McCarthy) going back and making that tackle on the turnover, right? Which saved us a touchdown right there. Which ultimately won us the football game. So, throughout the course of the game, there’s all those little plays, all those effort plays that make such a difference in the football game, the games that you find a way to win.” It isn’t often that a tackle by a quarterback can be considered the biggest play in a game. McCarthy hauling down Antonio Johnson after the Skattebo fumble qualifies. It prevented a touchdown, and the defense then prevented any Jacksonville points with a fourth-down stop, preserving the Giants’ 20-6 lead at the time. “At the end of the day, you have to do your job as a quarterback. When everything goes wrong, try to find a way to make it right. Don’t make a bad play worse,” McCarthy said. “And just being able to give that opportunity to our defense was the only thing that I was thinking about because they had a phenomenal game and obviously got it done in that moment.” McCarthy was also part of the game’s other resilient, defining moment. After watching the Giants’ second-half futility on offense, the Jaguars eschewed going for a potential game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion on fourth down and goal from the 8-yard line. Instead, they kicked a 26-yard field goal to close within five points with 3:43 to play. The Jaguars’ calculus was simple. Based on what they had seen, they did not believe the Giants’ offense could close the game out. A massive 19-yard completion from McCarthy to rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields, and two tough runs for a first down by Skattebo, proved Jacksonville wrong. “We took that personal,” McCarthy said. “It was really nice being able to close the game out with three minutes left,” Skattebo said. “We would wish to go back and close it out with seven minutes left, six minutes left, but we were able to get the job done when time called for it, and that’s what matters most.” The Giants also erased the memory of the Week 10 game against the Commanders that they should not have lost by winning a game most people said they weren’t supposed to win. “We definitely let that one get away last week, and so I think we just did a good job really just learning from that, turning the page, and just getting better throughout this past week,” said center Bryan Hudson. “The Jaguars are a good team, and they’ve won some games so far this season, but we’re a good team too, and I think today was another step for that, and just continuing to prove who we are and build on who we are, and I think we’re on our way.” Sunday’s victory wasn’t always pretty. It certainly wasn’t as easy as it could have been. It was, though, resilient. The hallmark of the 2026 Giants. Playoff-caliber defense Shhhhhhh!! Don’t anybody tell teams who will be searching for a head coach this offseason that they ought to talk to Giants’ defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Of course it helps when Carter plays like “the best in the world,” but Carter did not fly solo in an incredible defensive effort by the Giants on Sunday. The Jaguars came into Sunday having scored 31, 42, 33, and 40 points in their last four games. The Giants intercepted quarterback Trevor Lawrence twice. They sacked him three times and hit him 11 times. They had an amazing 14 passes defensed. They held the Jaguars to 1 of 6 (16.7%) in the red zone and 5 of 15 (33.3%) on third down. Jacksonville wide receiver Parker Washington had a season-high eight receptions, but it…

title: 11 winners, 2 losers, and some tweeners as the NY Giants outlast the Jaguars
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants didn’t do it the easy way, but they did manage to get a huge victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Let’s get to our ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ review. Kudos to … The defense as a whole — The Giants turned away the Jaguars again and […]
full_text: Abdul Carter rushing the passer Sunday night. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants didn’t do it the easy way, but they did manage to get a huge victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Let’s get to our ‘Kudos and Wet Willies’ review. Kudos to … The defense as a whole — The Giants turned away the Jaguars again and again on Sunday, refusing to let a missed field, a Cam Skattebo fumble, and an inconsistent day from quarterback J.J. McCarthy stand in the way of a signature victory for the Giants as they improved to 6-3-1, and moved a step closer to their first NFC East title since 2011. The Giants pressured a flustered Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence into his worst game of the season. Lawrence went 25 of 47 for 301 passing yards, but threw two interceptions, was sacked three times, hit 11 times, adn was chased endlessly by Giants pass rushers. The Giants got interceptions from Deonte Banks and Paulson Adebo. They had 14 passes defensed. They had a key fourth-down stop on fourth-and-1 at the Giants’ 11-yard line late in the third quarter after a Cam Skattebo fumble had given the Jaguars the ball at the New York 31-yard line. Now, let’s get to the individual honors. Abdul Carter — Flush with the excitement of a great performance in a huge victory for the Giants, Carter called himself “the best in the world.” Abdul Carter on what made him successful today: "I'm the best in the world" pic.twitter.com/npVCAEoPi9 — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 23, 2026 Carter has a long way to go before he can prove that, but he might well have been the best pass rusher in the NFL on Sunday. Carter said he played “real angry” after seeing some online criticism over the fact that he entered the game with just 2.0 sacks. Lawrence ended up feeling Carter’s anger in the second-year edge defender’s best game as a pro. Carter had two sacks, five quarterback hits, and a career-high 12 pressures, per NextGen Stats. This was the first multi-sack game of Carter’s career. Deonte Banks — Banks set up the Giants’ first points with an interception that put the ball at the Jacksonville 31-yard line. He also had three passes defensed, including one on a desperation throw into the end zone by Lawrence on a fourth-quarter pass from the 12-yard line. Paulson Adebo — The forgotten veteran cornerback was forced into action when the Giants lost starter Greg Newsome II to an ankle injury after just four snaps. Adebo was terrific. Adebo intercepted a Lawrence pass with 11:08 left in the game, putting the Giants at the Jacksonville 28-yard line and setting up a Dominic Zvada field goal. Adebo also had four passes defensed. Per Pro Football Focus, he gave up just one completion in eight targets while spending much of his day chasing Jacksonville’s Parker Washington. Per PFF, his passer rating against was 0.0. Adebo got a game ball from John Harbaugh. D.J. Reader — The big nose tackle’s job is to stuff the run. He certainly did that Sunday with a tackle for loss and, per PFF, three stops. Somebody forgot to tell him, though, that nose tackles not named Dexter Lawrence aren’t supposed to be impact pass rushers. Reader had a sack, two quarterback hits, and five total pressures. He continued to play at a Pro Bowl level. Reader celebrated with a simple social media post: And that’s another one for the good guys. — Dj Reader (@Djread98) November 23, 2026 Malik Nabers — I am honestly not sure about this one, but Nabers did have seven receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown. Through 29 career games, Nabers has caught 192 passes, the third-most through that many games in NFL history behind only Odell Beckham Jr. (199) and Puka Nacua (194). Xavier Gipson — The Giants’ new return man averaged 25.0 yards on five kickoff returns, including a 36-yarder, and had a 27-yard punt return. The Giants said they signed Gipson off the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad because they needed “a spark” in the return game. Gipson gave them one. Dru Phillips — Yeah, yeah. Phillips gave up seven completions on nine targets. Don’t care. I care about his three passes defensed, especially on fourth-and-1 from the Giants’ 11-yard line in the third quarter. Jordan Stout — The Giants’ punter averaged 60.3 yards on four punts, with a net of 54.5. The shortest punt Stout had was 57 yards. The amazing thing is that Stout manages to hit the ball that far while still getting enough hang time on his punts to give the Giants a chance to cover them. Zaire Barnes and Tyler Nubin — Barnes had four special teams tackles, added to the league-leading 14 he had entering the game. Nubin has not sulked about losing his starting safety job to Ar’Darius Washington. He had three special teams tackles. Wet Willies to … Second half offense — The Giants’ offense seemed out of sorts after Cam Skattebo’s fumble late in the third quarter with the Giants seemingly driving for what could have been a score that would have effectively put the game out of reach. After that the Giants got just one first down over their next four possessions, netting -20 yards of offense along the way. They played oddly for a team trying to run the clock and protect a lead. Over those four drives, they ran the ball only one time. Those four possessions took a total of just 3:44 off the clock, and continued to give Jacksonville opportunities to get back into the game. Micah McFadden — This was a rough night for McFadden. He made six tackles, and missed same number. Missed tackles have always been a bug-a-boo for McFadden, and this might have been his worst-ever game in that department. He missed a tackle in the backfield on a fourth-and-1 that went for a 21-yard run, and had a handful of chances to nab Lawrence in the backfield that he could not convert. Kwillies to … Cam Skattebo on the celebratory backflip after saying he’d retire it last week. #giants pic.twitter.com/9DJWFoM8qQ — Charlotte Carroll (@charlottecrrll) November 23, 2026 Cam Skattebo — Skattebo had a costly third-quarter fumble. He had just 34 yards on 14 carries, an average of 2.4 yards per attempt. After his third quarter fumble, the Giants seemed determined NOT to hand him the ball. Still, when the Giants needed a first down to ice the game, Skattebo delivered with two runs for 10 yards and a game-clinching first down at the two-minute mark. Skattebo also delivered a trademark backflip, a move he said he had retired, after the victory-sealing first down. “When energy calls for it, it calls for it,” Skattebo said. “I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team. I play this game with my heart and soul. When that happens it’s second nature. It’s hard to hold back from.” J.J. McCarthy — This was not McCarthy’s steadiest game throwing the ball. He went just 18 of 38 (47.4%) for 173 yards and a touchdown. McCarthy overshot a wide open Darnell Mooney on a couple of deep throws. He missed Mooney on a deep out where he was open. He failed to see an open Malik Nabers for what could have been a long touchdown. Yet, he made game-winning plays. His 8-yard touchdown pass to Nabers was a nice touch throw. He made a terrific 19-yard throw to Malachi Fields for a critical first down inside the three-minute mark. McCarthy used his legs to escape the pocket and pick up some key first downs. His play of the game, though, might have been his touchdown-saving tackle of Antonio Johnson after the Skattebo fumble. Cam Skattebo fumbles and the Jaguars carry it to the other side of the field pic.twitter.com/WbuSs1JpYd — Talkin’ Giants (@TalkinGiants) November 22, 2026 Dominic Zvada — The rollercoaster ride with the Giants’ strong-legged rookie placekicker continued on Sunday. He made field goals of 53 and 54 yards — from the right hash mark where all six of his misses had occurred this season. Then, Zvada missed a chip shot 32-yarder from that right hash early in the third quarter before adding a 43-yarder from the left hash mark for three critical points with 10:03 to…
