title: 4 things we learned from the Giants’ 23-18 victory over the Jaguars
summary: Sunday was the day the New York Giants’ Cinderella season carriage was going to turn back into the pumpkin of past season failures. That might yet happen – the road ahead is filled with difficult opponents. Today, though, the Giants for the first time established themselves as serious playoff contenders. They not only hung with […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Getty Images Sunday was the day the New York Giants’ Cinderella season carriage was going to turn back into the pumpkin of past season failures. That might yet happen – the road ahead is filled with difficult opponents. Today, though, the Giants for the first time established themselves as serious playoff contenders. They not only hung with the previously 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, they actually dominated a good part of the game. Things got dicey in the second half as the Jaguars started to move the ball and tighten up their defense, but the Giants held on for a 23-18 victory that solidified their hold on first place (on a day when the Cowboys and Eagles both won) and perhaps more importantly, suggested that they might be more than just a competent team that can squeeze out victories over the NFL’s bottom-dwellers. The NFL, which gambled that the Giants were for real by flexing their game into the national 4:30 window, won their bet with a thrilling game. What did we learn from the Giants’ 23-18 win over Jacksonville? The Giants have a playoff-caliber defense There’s been evidence of this since the start of the season, when Dennard Wilson’s aggressive approach proved a welcome change from the passive Shane Bowen defense in the Giants’ first game against Dallas. Still, most Giants games have been against poor to middling offensive teams, and when they faced a good offense, the Rams ran roughshod over them. Today it was the Jaguars’ No. 5 scoring offense in the NFL, one that had put 30 or more points up 6 times already this season. The 18 points they scored against the Giants today was their second lowest of the season, trailing only the 12 points they scored in Denver (which has one of the NFL’s best defenses). You have to credit the D as a whole. Trevor Lawrence did manage to put up 301 passing yards, but he only passed for 1 TD and was intercepted twice. Furthermore, the Jags’ potent running game only had 77 yards, though admittedly star running back Bhayshul Tuten left with an injury mid-game. The main reasons that was true today were: 1. Abdul Carter is officially a beast Carter has been having what by some metrics would be considered a breakout season, ranking high in a number of pass rush metrics such as pass rush win rate and time to pressure. What has been lacking are sacks. Today, though, Carter sacked Lawrence twice and hit or at least pressured him a handful of other times. Carter’s quickness and agility getting around blocks is other-worldly, and today he was finally rewarded for the work he’s been doing. Forget the stats, when J.J. Watt seems impressed, that’s good enough for me. Part of the reason Carter was effective was that he wasn’t alone. Kayvon Thobodeaux, as usual, did not get any sacks, but he was getting pressure from the other side as well (in addition to having a strong game against the run and intercepting a 2-point conversion attempt), and D.J. Reader was also getting pressure inside and had a sack of his own. There would have been more, but Lawrence is a pretty mobile QB for a guy his size, and the Giants had him running around a lot trying to escape and find someone downfield. The good thing is that the Giants did it without blitzing as much as they have in some recent games. 2. Welcome back, Paulson Adebo Part of the reason Lawrence had a long time to throw today (his longest of the season) was that the Giants did a pretty good job, all things considered, against the Jaguars’ potent receiving corps. Parker Washington, who has become one of the NFL’s best receivers, had 103 yards today, but that was on 17 targets, of which he only caught 8. Likewise, Jakobi Meyers had 85 yards, but again, on 10 targets of which he only caught four. Much of that was due to Paulson Adebo. The Giants’ big free agent signing last year, a disappointment then and relegated to the bench most of this year after being injured in Game 1, Adebo played perhaps his best game as a Giant. He held Washington to zero catches on three targets and Meyers to one 23-yard catch in five targets. He broke up four passes and also had an interception . Adebo entered the game after Greg Newsome left with an injury in the first quarter. If he is finally returning to his form of a couple of years ago when he was a Saint, that could be huge for the Giants, who will face some potent passing offenses in the coming weeks (he writes while watching Brock Purdy carve up the Vikings defense in the first half on Sunday Night Football). Meanwhile, Deonte Banks continues to play great ball. Banks only gave up two receptions in 10 targets for 21 yards and had his second interception of the season. To me, this was his best game of the season, even though he had the game-saving pick-6 against Arizona. It is such a remarkable development after watching him languish the past two seasons. Part of Lawrence’s problem tonight was that he couldn’t find open receivers. If this continues this could be the Giants’ best secondary since their 2022 playoff season. 3. The run defense is getting a little better In their first nine games, the Giants had five of them in which they gave up 163, 123, 202, 175, and 105 rushing yards. Today they gave up only 77 yards to a Jacksonville team that had rushed for over 100 yards in each of its last four games. The big news pre-game was that Darius Alexander was not active. That’s quite a fall from grace for the former high third round draft pick who had given the Giants a little interior pass rush but who had been a liability against the run. In his place the Giants played Bobby Jamison-Travis, who’s become a regular part of the rotation, and C.J. Okoye, who had missed the past three games. It’s worth watching going forward to see how IDL snaps are distributed and whether the Giants are able to hold up against formidable rushing teams that are coming up such as the 49ers and Lions. 4. The Giants don’t have a running game It can be frustrating to watch this Giants offense sometimes. J.J. McCarthy looked good early on, but he went downhill as the game progressed. To Matt Nagy’s credit, the Giants finally dialed up some downfield passes for McCarthy today. Unfortunately, he was pretty awful on those passes – 0 for 5 beyond 20 yards, with most of them sailing well beyond the receiver. The Giants might have put up more than 30 if he’d had better touch downfield. He was pretty good on downfield passes as a Viking, so let’s hope that today was just an aberration, because adding a downfield threat to their offense could be the difference between hanging with the good teams or being steamrolled by them. The problem is that they need for J.J. to be good, because their rushing game has been suspect. The Giants do not have good run blockers, especially on the interior offensive line. John Harbaugh and Greg Roman have been searching all season for a bellcow to help their offense run at maximum efficiency. One problem is that all their running backs fumble. Another problem is that they tend to get injured. Another problem is that none of them are elite running backs even when they are at their best. Cam Skattebo got the call again tonight with Tyrone Tracy still injured…and he fumbled again tonight at a critical juncture. With the Giants already up 20-6, with a first down at the Jaguars’ 33 and 4:01 left in the third quarter, once again Skattebo was stripped, his fifth of the season. Only a tackle by of all people J.J. McCarthy kept Antonio Johnson from returning it for a TD. That was really a turning point in the game. It went from a solid, bordering on easy, victory for the Giants to a nail-biter. Jacksonville got the momentum, and by the 3:43 mark in the fourth quarter, Cam Little’s field goal had gotten the Jaguars to within 23-18. Be honest – did you think the Giants were going to lose at that point? I did. Then something remarkable happened. After Skattebo ran for 3 yards, McCarthy completed a 19-yard pass to Malachi Fields to get the Giants to the…

title: Giants-Jaguars: Instant grades after New York’s victory over Jacksonville
summary: The New York Giants defeated the now 7-3 Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday to advance to 6-3-1. New York controlled the game, and Jacksonville was sloppy and undisciplined for much of the game. Still, the Giants’ inability to put down an opponent after establishing a lead caused some fear in the second half. New York was […]
full_text: The New York Giants defeated the now 7-3 Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday to advance to 6-3-1. New York controlled the game, and Jacksonville was sloppy and undisciplined for much of the game. Still, the Giants’ inability to put down an opponent after establishing a lead caused some fear in the second half. New York was up 20-6 at halftime, and was receiving the ball, but a missed Dominic Zvada field goal and a fumble by Cam Skattebo set an unfortunate tone for the offense throughout the second half. New York went three-and-out three times in the second half, and four-and-out once. The offense continues to struggle, but the defense responded well. New York went 4 of 15 on third down and finished with just 238 yards of offense, but 13 Jacksonville penalties, two turnovers, and constant pressure on Trevor Lawrence were enough for New York to earn the victory. Here are the immediate grades from the Giants’ sixth win of the season Quarterback The Giants offense struggled again. They were particularly bad in the second half. J.J. McCarthy finished 18 of 38 for 173 yards with a touchdown — a bad 4.6 yards per completion. McCarthy also missed some big-time throws to Darnell Mooney. He did have 33 yards on the ground and came up with a critical 19-yard pass to Malachi Fields to seal the victory after struggling throughout the second half; he went seven straight throws with an incompletion in the second half. It wasn’t pretty, but the offense did enough to get the win. Jameis Winston handled the red zone duties on the Giants’ first touchdown drive. He checked out of a run and threw a bad ball to Isaiah Likely that could have been caught. The Giants went for it on fourth down, and Winston scored on the tush push. Grade: C Running back New York struggled to consistently run the football. They averaged just 3.1 yards per carry, and that’s beefed up by McCarthy’s 4.7 YPC. Cam Skattebo — who had a costly fumble in the second half — had 14 carries for just 34 yards, but did catch three passes for 14 yards. Devin Singletary received snaps to spell Skattebo, but neither running back did much on the ground. The pass protection from Skattebo, though, was good, from what I could tell, once again. Grade: C Wide receiver The Giants’ receivers only had 173 collective yards; 55 were to Malik Nabers, who secured seven of 12 targets with a touchdown. Malachi Fields caught a key 19-yard dig route that helped the Giants secure the victory, but the offense — in general — was quiet for much of the game. We did see Jalin Hyatt catch one pass for 4 yards and Xavier Gipson had a catch for 6 yards. Darnell Mooney created a lot of separation, but could not secure any of his five targets — McCarthy missed him badly on a deep post route. Grade: C Tight end The Giants tight ends were not heavily involved. Isaiah Likely caught one pass for 35 yards, and Chris Manhertz caught one ball for 14 yards. Theo Johnson had a clutch 15-yard grab over the middle of the field on third down, but Skattebo fumbled on the next play. Grade: C Offensive line The Giants offensive line struggled early against Jacksonville; J.J. McCarthy faced two free rushers on the first two plays of the game. The pass blocking stabilized, and McCarthy was only sacked once, albeit there were too many free rushers. The offensive line struggled to create space at the point of attack, which is an annoying reality that has persisted for much of the season. Overall, the offensive line was less than stellar. Grade: C- Defensive line D.J. Reader picked up a first-quarter sack of Trevor Lawrence after a game shared with Abdul Carter, who spun back inside to help Reader finish the sack. New York’s defense was STOUT and shut down Jacksonville’s rushing attack. The defensive performance was an A+ overall, with Reader highlighted for four tackles and a sack, and C.J. Okoye with one STOP on early downs. Shelby Harris contributed three tackles. Grade: A Edge Abdul Carter told the world to WATCH and he SHOWED UP with a big-time first quarter sack and a second down sack in the second quarter, as well as some valuable pressures. He timed the snap magnificently and strung moves together all game. Carter was sensational. However, Jacksonville figured out his timing in the fourth quarter, and drew an encroachment penalty. Kayvon Thibodeaux was flying around the field and making important assisted tackles in short-yardage situations. He had a free run — as Dennard Wilson is one to dial up — at Trevor Lawrence, but could not get him on the ground. Dawuane Smoot had a sack negated, but continues to be a solid practice squad call-up. Grade: A+ Linebacker The Giants linebackers were flying all over the field. Arvell Reese remains a heavy hammer that punishes offensive players. Micah McFadden missed a key fourth-down tackle on the Jaguars’ first offensive drive, but he made several tackles throughout the game, including a few short-yardage stops. McFadden had Lawrence tee’d up multiple times throughout the game but struggled to get him down to the deck. McFadden was dinged up at the end of the game after missing a tackle in space against Chris Rodriguez Jr. Both McFadden and Arvell Reese had seven tackles; Zaire Barnes saw snaps and had four tackles. Grade: B+ Cornerback The Giants used multiple cornerbacks in the game, as Greg Newsome II and Tae Banks missed time during the contest. Tae Banks made an early impact by intercepting Trevor Lawrence on the Jaguars’ second offensive drive. Dru Phillips had a pair of HUGE pass deflections: one on a fourth-and-one route in the red zone and the other on third-and-goal with 3:43 left in the game, which prompted Cam Little’s fourth field goal. He did, though, miss a few tackles. Phillips did surrender a third-and-twenty on a deep corner versus Washington. Paulson Adebo received snaps after Newsome left and did not return; he made a great play on the football in Cover-4 on a deep post to Parker Washington on a first-down shot that went INC. And then, on the following play, Paulson Adebo intercepted Trevor Lawrence on a possible miscommunication with a Jaguars receiver. Grade: A+ Safety Jevon Holland set a tone early by dislodging the football from Parker Washington. Holland was around the line of scrimmage making tackles, and he almost came away with an interception in the end zone on Jacksonville’s second drive. Holland led the team with nine tackles, and Ar’Darious Washington had three. Grade: A Special teams Dominic Zvada is frustrating. He made a kick from the right hash! It started the Giants scoring, and then the rookie booted a 54-yard field goal at the end of the first half – AGAIN – from the right hash. It’s a positive development for the rookie kicker. However, Zvada then missed a 32-yard field goal from the right hash to start the third quarter, and made his fourth kick. He remains inconsistent and borderline unreliable. Jordan Stout averaged 60 yards per punt. He is very good at what he does. Xavier Gipson handled one punt and returned it for 27 yards, while also looking capable on his kickoff returns. The kick coverage failed on the first kickoff of the game, but Tyler Nubin made his presence known multiple times on coverage plays — he finished the game with three tackles and is becoming one of the best special teams players on the team. Grade: B+

title: Survey results – Giants fans still think the Cowboys are the biggest threat
summary: Few predicted that New York Giants would be the first place team in the NFC East as we get ready to sit down for Thanksgiving. Yet here we are, with the 5-3-1 Giants leading the division and in position to win it for the first time since 2011. That said, their perch atop the division […]
full_text: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo carries the ball against the Dallas Cowboys | Getty Images Few predicted that New York Giants would be the first place team in the NFC East as we get ready to sit down for Thanksgiving. Yet here we are, with the 5-3-1 Giants leading the division and in position to win it for the first time since 2011. That said, their perch atop the division was made significantly more precarious by their loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 10. That loss opened the door for both the Dallas Cowboys and the Commanders to overtake them for the division lead and knock the Giants out of the playoffs. This week we asked Giants fans which of the two teams is the bigger threat to the Giants’ control of the division, the 4-6 Dallas Cowboys or the 3-5-1 Washington Commanders. And while the poll was surprisingly close, Giants fans fear the Cowboys more than the Commanders. There’s a good argument that either division rival is a significant threat to the Giants’ playoff hopes. On one hand, Dallas has one of the most potent offenses in the NFL, which gives them a chance to win any game in which they play as long as they can turn it into a shootout. The Cowboys also only trail the Giants by 1.5 games (as of this writing), and the two teams still have a game against each other in Week 17. On the other hand, the Giants’ loss to Washington in Week 10 gives the Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Giants. So if both teams somehow wind up with the same record, Washington will win by virtue of their 1-0-1 record against the Giants. And while the Giants are entering the toughest stretch of their schedule, the Commanders have a much easier road, with games against the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons from November 29th to December 20th. It’s possible we could see Washington go on a four-game run after this week’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. The good news is that the Giants are still in control of their own destiny and are still the favorites to win the NFC East. As of this writing the Giants are -146 to make the playoffs this year, per FanDuel , and lead the NFC East in playoff odds. That said, they’re facing a tough stretch with games. They have matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, and Detroit Lions looming — as well as the Cleveland Browns and Cowboys. The Giants likely won’t be favored in any of those games, but they are opportunities to show that they deserve to be considered playoff contenders if they can come up with some wins as underdogs. Giants fans still believe in their team despite the Week 10 loss. The loss dented Giants’ fan confidence a bit, dropping it from the 97% of fans who were confident that the team was heading in the right direction a week ago. However, 90% of fans still being confident in the direction of the team is impressive considering how few fans were confident in the team a year ago. It will be interesting to see how the outcome of this week’s game against the Jaguars impacts fan confidence going forward.

title: New York Jets News: Fans are at Each Other’s Throats After win Over Chargers
summary: It’s a beautiful victory, Monday, New York Jets fans! I’m sure everyone is happy about this dub, right? Wrong. The fan base is fractured down the middle with this result. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what […]
full_text: Nov 22, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn hugs Los Angeles Chargers guard Kayode Awosika (74) following the game at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s a beautiful victory, Monday, New York Jets fans! I’m sure everyone is happy about this dub, right? Wrong. The fan base is fractured down the middle with this result. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what they describe as a frustrating loss to a crappy opponent that screwed up their draft positioning. “A Jets win that feels like a loss to many people in the fan base, and I don’t blame anyone who feels that way because I feel the same way. Watching the Jets go out there and win this game just leaves that sinking feeling in your stomach oh my God they have ruined the tank again. That’s the feeling many in the fan base have, and if you feel that way, you’re not a bad fan because you see the forest through the trees because you understand that a win over a one-win Chargers team could potentially do more damage than good. If you’re going to win games, you want it to be because your young players are playing great, not because 33-year-old Sterling Shepard is scoring two touchdowns on his only two touches of the game,” ESPN New York’s Jake Asman lamented. The Jets were not going to finish 2-15. Anyone who set that expectation set themselves up for failure. They have been in a ton of close games this season. A broken clock is right twice a day. A blind squirrel can find a nut. The Jets were eventually going to stumble into a victory, and who knows if this is the last one. There are still six games left in the 2026 regular season. For fans who like seeing their green and white team win regardless of circumstance, cheers to you today. We’ve only had three wins this year; enjoy them while you can. J-E-T-S! full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Safety Minkah Fitzpatrick #29 of the New York Jets makes a stop in the game between the Miami Dolphins vs the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets are now 3-8 on the season, in third place in the AFC East. The Jets scored on the opening drive of the game and never looked back. The Jets never trailed in the game. They scored every time they had the ball other than their last possession, when they ran out the clock to seal the win. The Jets offense bullied the Chargers defense all day. Defensively the Jets struggled, but David Bailey got another two sacks to get to 9.5 for the season and the offense was good enough to get the victory. The win over the Chargers left the Jets with a 3-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Dolphins’ only win this season came at the expense of the Jets a few weeks ago. full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 22: Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets scores a touchdown against Donte Jackson #26 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter at SoFi Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The game opened with the Jets on offense. They moved down the field with their running game and a completion to Adonai Mitchell before the drive bogged down. The Jets settled for a doinked 50 yard field goal that sneaked through the uprights for an early 3 – 0 Jets lead. The pattern of settling for field goals that persisted the last couple of weeks continued on the first drive of the game. The Chargers answered with a field goal drive of their own and the game was tied at 3 – 3 late in the first quarter. The Jets answered with a long drive featuring the running game. As the first quarter ended the Jets had a third and three at the Chargers 12 yard line. Three plays later the Jets were in the end zone as Geno Smith hit Breece Hall for the Jets’ first touchdown in 10 quarters. The Jets had a 10 – 3 lead early in the second quarter. After the Jets stopped the Chargers when David Bailey shut down the drive with a strip sack, the Jets offense took over. They quickly drove down the field with a nice mix of runs and passes. The drive ended when Geno Smith found Sterling Shepard, fresh off the practice squad, for a touchdown and a 17 – 3 Jets lead late in the second quarter. The Chargers closed out the second quarter with a drive ending in a Justin Herbert touchdown run as time expired in the first half. The drive was aided at the end by a bogus roughing the passer call on David Bailey. The Jets went into the locker room leading the Chargers 17 – 10. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. After the Jets shut down the Chargers with the help of another David Bailey sack, the Jets offense took over. They proceeded to grind out most of the third quarter as they put together an 18 play drive using almost ten minutes of clock before the Jets settled for a short field goal and a 20 – 10 lead with a little more than three minutes to go in the third quarter. The third quarter ended with the Chargers on the move in Jets territory and the score still Jets 20, Chargers 10. On the first play of the fourth quarter Omarion Hampton broke a 36 yard run to create a first and goal situation for the Chargers. A few plays later Justin Herbert found Ladd McConkey in the end zone for a touchdown to make the score Jets 20, Chargers 17 early in the fourth quarter. The Jets roared back, putting together a 62 yard drive highlighted by a 26 yard Breece Hall run. Geno Smith put the finishing touches on the drive with an improbable second touchdown pass to Sterling Shepard. The Jets had a 10 point lead with less than 10 minutes to play at Jets 27, Chargers 17. The Chargers came back. They put together a long drive ending in a touchdown pass from Justin Herbert to Ladd McConkey. The touchdown brought the Chargers within three points at 27 – 24, but the drive took up nearly eight minutes, leaving the Chargers less than two minutes to stop the Jets, get the ball back and drive to tie or win the game. The Jets needed one first down to ice the game. The Jets ran the ball down the Chargers’ throats for two first downs, one by Breece Hall and one by Braelon Allen. Game over, Jets win! Final score: Jets 27, Chargers 24. The win brought the Jets’ record to 3-8. The Jets are on the road next week against the Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins got their only victory of the season earlier this year against the Jets. The Jets hope to flip the script in Miami next week. After the Dolphins game the Jets get their bye week in Week 13.

title: Jets vs Chargers Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 1: Garrett Wilson #5 of the New York Jets runs onto the field prior to the NFL game against the Las Vegas Raiders at MetLife Stadium on November 1, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. Today, for the first time in three weeks, we’re not handing out a pre-blame ball. The Jets have a plausible path to victory against the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers, so pre-game ball it is. The pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Chargers goes to (drum roll please) – Garrett Wilson! The Chargers have a pretty good run defense. They allowed just 15 rushing yards last week against the Baltimore Ravens. They have held five of nine opponents under 120 yards rushing, and they have allowed just 3.9 rushing yards per attempt for the season. This could be a fairly difficult afternoon for the Jets’ running game. The passing game is a different story. The Chargers rank 28th in the NFL in net yards allowed per passing attempt. The Chargers also struggle to get to the quarterback, with just 15 sacks for the season. The top receivers on opposing teams have routinely excelled against the Chargers’ mediocre secondary. The loss of Derwin James at safety has badly hurt the Chargers’ secondary, and their mediocre cornerbacks have not been able to compensate. The Jets will be missing Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams against the Chargers, leaving Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell as the primary targets for Geno Smith in the passing game. With Wilson in the midst of his best season in the NFL, Smith is likely to look his way early and often against the porous Chargers secondary. This feels like a setup for a monster game for Wilson. Garrett Wilson, come on down! You’ve earned today’s pre-game ball for the Jets. Let’s see you torch the Chargers’ secondary on the way to a Jets victory today. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game or pre-blame ball to? Let us know in the comments.

title: Jets elevate veteran wide receiver ahead of Chargers game
summary: The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Sterling Shepard #87 of the New York Jets warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Sterling Shepard has been elevated to the active roster twice this season before today. He has been targeted twice by the Jets, with one reception good for three yards. The Jets needed another body at wide receiver with Cooper out. The team has Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell active, but behind those two are Tim Patrick and Malik McClain, who are unlikely to provide much value. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season. Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

title: Eagles-Steelers snap counts: Riq Woolen benched
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 11 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Tanner McKee INACTIVE: Cole Payton, Mac McWilliams, Smael Mondon, Lane Johnson, Ajani Cornelius, Jake Majors
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers spins with the ball against Riq Woolen #2 of the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 11 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Jordan Mailata is the only player who’s played 100% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps this season. He’s also played 11.76% of the Eagles’ special teams snaps. The Eagles’ starting offensive line configuration in each of their last five games has played 100% of the team’s snaps on offense. For all the talk about injuries, they’ve actually had strong in-game stability up front. Despite DeVonta Smith returning, Darius Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles wide receiver. And he led the team in receiving with four receptions for 59 yards. One of those receptions converted 3rd-and-13 and another converted 3rd-and-10 … on two different field goal drives. Dallas Goedert saw a single start, a season-low. But it resulted in a 38-yard reception. Makai Lemon played a good amount for a player who saw three targets for one reception and three yards. The 2026 first-round pick dropped two passes. If DeVonta was 100% healthy, I don’t think he’d only be playing 81% of the offense’s snaps. Saquon Barkley got banged up again in this game. He was productive when he was able to play. Will Shipley played more than the Eagles planned due to Barkley getting hurt. Second straight game where Johnny Mundt only played single-digit snaps on offense. There’s really no need for him to be on this roster, especially when the Eagles carrying four other tight ends. Zach Ertz might’ve had the quietest six snaps ever played. I can’t even recall seeing him on the field. Not sure he’s going to break the Eagles’ franchise record for receptions if he’s not even really playing, let alone getting targets. Cooper DeJean logged his first offensive snaps since Week 1 … the last time the Eagles lined up in victory formation. Britain Covey logged his first offensive snap since Week 18 last year. With Fred Johnson waived, the Eagles utilized John Ojukwu in a six offensive linemen package. Could be good to go with Willie Lampkin instead. DEFENSE Andrew Mukuba leads the Eagles in defensive snaps percentage played this season with 99.71%. For all his faults, it is at least good to see he’s been more durable? Jeremiah Trotter Jr. led the Eagles in tackles with 13 total, nine solo. Nice showing from both him and Jihaad Campbell at off-ball linebacker. Marcus Epps had a good showing as the top safety next to Mukuba in nickel packages. Quinyon Mitchell left the game in the fourth quarter due to a hamstring injury. It sounds like he might be able to play in Week 12 … but we’ll see how he fares on the injury report. In the aftermath of the Jordan Davis trade, Moro Ojomo played his second-highest snap count percentage this season. Riq Woolen was benched for Jonathan Jones after missing multiple tackles. Woolen later re-entered the game after Jones got banged up. Speaking after the game, Woolen said he was “annoyed” with the decision but expressed happiness that his team won. With Jones getting banged up, Woolen might have to play despite the fact the coaching staff clearly doesn’t prefer him to be out there. Jalyx Hunt had his first sack of the season wiped out by a penalty elsewhere on defense. Unfortunate development for him. This was Hunt’s highest snap count percentage played since prior to getting hurt in Week 5. Good to see him able to handle a bigger workload. Nolan Smith continues to show up in the box score with six sacks in his last eight games. Jonathan Greenard has two sacks in his last two games. This despite the fact he’s clearly playing through injury and playing on a pitch count. Arnold Ebiketie was traded to the Cincinnati Bengals … only for that deal to fall through and him to remain a rotational edge rusher and special teams contributor in Philly. Byron Young only played 22 defensive snaps but really made the most of them with two sacks and two TFLs. For context, Jordan Davis had 1.5 sacks and two TFLs in nine games with the Eagles before he was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. That’s wild. Ty Robinson logged his second-highest snap count percentage of the season despite getting banged up in the fourth quarter. Gabe Hall logged his first career sack in just eight snaps played on Sunday. Kelee Ringo was forced into action after both Mitchell and Jones got banged up at cornerback. He allowed a touchdown. Anferenee Orji, the Eagles’ only backup off-ball linebacker in this game, played three snaps while Campbell briefly missed time due to a finger injury. SPECIAL TEAMS Lame that Eli Stowers didn’t play at all on offense. How’s he supposed to get better? How are the Eagles supposed to evaluate him? I’m very confident that the Eagles don’t need both Mundt and Grant Calcaterra on this roster. They really don’t need either player. But if they really insist on having one of them, fine. Both of them? There’s just no good reason for it. Jaydon Blue is probably going to get waived again after fumbling as a kick returner. First game since Kenny Moore joined the Eagles that he did not play on defense. A.J. Epenesa has played zero defensive snaps and 13 special teams snaps over the Eagles’ last three games combined. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Tanner McKee INACTIVE: Cole Payton, Mac McWilliams, Smael Mondon, Lane Johnson, Ajani Cornelius, Jake Majors Guessing Mondon might miss another game after being ruled doubtful to play in Week 11. Tight turnaround to play against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. As a reminder, Johnson is set to remain on the Eagles’ roster until June 2027 , even though he retired.

title: Eagles News: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell lead inspired defensive effort
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Zack Baun now on injured reserve, the Eagles will get a look at the duo of Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell together over the next three games … if not longer. Baun has been a rare bright spot for […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. #54 and line backer Jihaad Campbell #11 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Zack Baun now on injured reserve, the Eagles will get a look at the duo of Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell together over the next three games … if not longer. Baun has been a rare bright spot for the Eagles this year … but maybe they can trade him in the offseason and move forward with their youth at off-ball linebacker? Something to consider. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Spadaro: 10 takeaways from the Eagles’ 19-16 victory over the Steelers – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Jeremiah Trotter sets the tone, and dominates With Zack Baun sidelined and on Injured Reserve, the Eagles went with Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell (7 total tackles, 1 for loss) at linebacker and both played extremely well. Trotter set the tone on the first possession, knifing into the hole and tackling running back Jaylen Warren for no gain, and the Eagles’ 40-yard line. Trotter ended up with 13 tackles, including 9 solos, and set the tone for a terrific defensive performance on that fourth-down stop. “I give the credit to my guys up front,” Trotter said. “They did their jobs and I did mine. I had a clear path to the ball and just did what I was supposed to do. We knew we had to stop the run today. We knew they ran the ball well, so we tackled well and got off blocks.” A note on the run defense: Pittsburgh came into the game averaging 116 yards per game on the ground and gained just 73 yards on 20 carries, including 29 from the not-nimble Rodgers on scrambles. Great job. 10 Eagles things I think I think following the win over the Steelers – BGN If the Eagles were facing a competent offense against a quarterback that wasn’t well past his prime, the outcome may have been different. Give credit to the offense for getting the field goal when they needed it and icing the game, but they had a stretch where they went 24 plays for 44 yards (1.8 yards per play). The ineptitude just happens way too often on offense to win games consistently. The Eagles were fortunate the Steelers never got anything going on offense until they were down 10 points in the final minutes. Byron Young, Eagles Defense DOMINATES Steelers For First Win In Two Months – PHLY Sports Super Bowl champion Vinny Curry joins the PHLY crew to break down the Eagles’ win over the Pittsburgh Steelers thanks to a forceful pass rush that included sacks from Jonathan Greenard, Gabe Hall and two from Byron Young in the first game since Jordan Davis’ departure. Joe Milton, Saquon Barkley and the Eagles offense did just enough to get the job done. Join Curry, Fran Duffy, EJ Smith, Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf for the lowdown. DK Metcalf has become the Steelers’ eye-poking disaster – SB Nation There’s something in the water when it comes to wide receivers in Pittsburgh that turns them into clowns. It’s been this way since the halcyon days of Hines Ward, as the team has managed, time and time and time again, to be saddled with problematic guys and know exactly when to part ways before the ticking time bomb explodes. Until DK Metcalf arrived. This is the organization’s big mistake, the whiff that is setting them back, and Sunday was a perfect example of how much of a disaster Metcalf has been for this team. It isn’t simply about losing to a hopeless Eagles team, or Metcalf getting ejected for poking Cooper DeJean in the eye, or even losing pace in the AFC North — it’s all of these things in concert, and the fact that they’re paying through the moon for this guy to actively hurt their team. Perhaps the worst part of all this is that anyone could see this was a HORRIBLE move for the Steelers when they made it. Steelers offensive woes continue, drop second straight game in loss to Eagles – Behind The Steel Curtain The Pittsburgh Steelers have now lost consecutive games for the first time this season, losing to the Philadelphia Eagles by the score of 19-16, dropping their record to 6-4 on the season. For the second straight week, the Steelers’ offense completely did them in. Their first four drives ended without points, the first of which saw a turnover on downs that led to an Eagles field goal. Their subsequent two drives were a pair of three-and-outs and then a six-play drive that ended in a punt. In total, they ran 16 plays for 17 yards in their first four drives. Meanwhile, the Eagles put together a 13-0 lead that the Steelers would never surmount. The Steelers entered halftime down 13-3, and Aaron Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt over the first two quarters, the lowest such number with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking air yards in 2006, per Brooke Pryor. From top-down, angry Eagles defensive front ‘whoop’ Steelers to halt losing streak – PHLY Eagles Moro Ojomo said it felt like winning the Super Bowl. He would know. To be clear, the Eagles‘ 19-16 win didn’t come with any trophy. There wasn’t confetti falling from the sky or stanchions dragged out to midfield or cigar smoke weighing down the air of the postgame locker room. What did exist was the weightlessness of a group adding to the win column for the first time since the Phillies were still playing baseball and the residual anger that it took that long to achieve it. That anger was palpable amidst the defensive line in the moments before the game. Ojomo broke his teammates down after pre-game warmups with a message he tried — and failed — to put “politely” in his locker stall a few hours later. “Whoop a motherfucker’s ass,” he said. An update on the Eagles’ projected compensatory pick for the loss of Jaelan Phillips – PhillyVoice However, there was always a possibility that the value of the compensatory pick for Jaelan Phillips could fall into a lower round tier if he didn’t hit playing time benchmarks. And certainly, that danger was higher for an oft-injured player like Phillips, who missed Weeks 7, 8, and 9 with a hamstring injury. If you look at OverTheCap’s compensatory formula chart, Phillips needs to play around 23 percent of the Panthers’ regular season defensive snaps to qualify for a third-round compensatory pick. Through 10 games, Phillips has played 336 of a possible 684 defensive snaps, or 49.1 percent. The Panthers are on pace to play 1,163 defensive snaps this season. If Phillips doesn’t play another snap and the Panthers stay on that pace, he will have played roughly 29 percent of the Panthers’ defensive snaps. There’s no moment where Phillips will “clinch” a third-round pick, but he should now safely be within that third-round tier at this point, even if he doesn’t play another snap this season. Losers No More – Iggles Blitz Braden Mann had a 70-yard punt that went out at the 4-yard line. The defense held and the offense got the ball near midfield. Milton completed a couple of passes that led to a FG. Darius Cooper made the key catch on that drive and played well overall. The Eagles were able to seal the win when Milton hit Smith on 3rd & 6 with a quick out that moved the chains. The Eagles weren’t pretty or efficient, but for once they were clutch. And that’s how you end a losing streak. The only downside to the game was more injuries. Quinyon Mitchell got hurt late in the game. With Dallas up on Thursday, you can’t afford to have him hurt. Barkley hurt his arm late in the game. You need him if the offense is going to have a chance in Dallas. Jonathan Jones also got hurt late. He was in for Riq Woolen, who got benched. We’ll see how all of this plays out. For now, enjoy the W. Roob’s Observations as Eagles’ defensive statement sparks win over Steelers – NBCSP This offense is so bad in…

While it was nice to see the Eagles’ defense turn in a good effort against the Steelers, the Cowboys’ offense is an entirely different monster. Case in point: Dallas dropped 51 points in a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Also, the Eagles could be banged up in the secondary with cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell and Jonathan Jones (who replaced a benched Riq Woolen) not finishing Sunday’s game due to injury. Although the Cowboys’ defense has been pretty bad, it’s not easy to imagine the Eagles keeping pace with their opponent’s scoring ability. The offensive numbers from Philly’s Week 11 win hardly point to an offense that turned the corner coming out of the bye week: The Philadelphia Eagles offense produced a 3rd percentile success rate in Week 11 They had the 2nd lowest success rate for a winning team this season, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) November 22, 2026 #Eagles had only 11 first downs (Steelers had 17) and only 14 (!) successful plays on offense the whole game (Steelers had 25) and still managed to win. Defense came up big just enough times to hang on. pic.twitter.com/xLPRGRW6e5 — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) November 22, 2026 Saquon Barkley also got banged up (once again) on Sunday, which doesn’t help the offensive outlook. The Eagles beating the Cowboys on Thanksgiving would be pretty delicious. It would also put them back in contention for the NFC East crown. I’m not counting on it happening. What say you?

title: 10 Eagles things I think I think following the win over the Steelers
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles won a football game! The result may not be want some fans wanted, but the seven-game losing streak is over. The Eagles secured a victory for the first time since September 20, beating the Pittsburgh Steelers in an ugly 19-16 victory. A win is a win. There are a lot of Eagles […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni argues with line judge Stephen Ray #99 during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles won a football game! The result may not be want some fans wanted, but the seven-game losing streak is over. The Eagles secured a victory for the first time since September 20, beating the Pittsburgh Steelers in an ugly 19-16 victory. A win is a win. There are a lot of Eagles playing for their jobs, so this victory does feel good after going more than two months without one. Getting a win to start a short week is encouraging given what’s coming on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys. This wasn’t the most impressive win, but the Eagles won’t apologize for it. The losing streak is over, and there are plenty of evaluations following this win. 1. This offense is a brutal watch No matter who the quarterback is, this offense can’t move the football consistently. The Eagles scored 13 points in the first quarter, netting points on all three drives. The rest of the game was brutal, as the Eagles had just 86 yards and averaged 2.4 yards per play. They averaged 1.9 yards per carry and 3.3 yards per attempt. Nick Sirianni and Sean Mannion may have been conservative after the 13-0 lead, but this offense just can’t move the ball. Here were the possessions after Saquon Barkley’s 38-yard touchdown that put the Eagles up 13-0 late in the first quarter. 3 plays, 8 yards, Punt 3 plays, 5 yards, Half 3 plays, -6 yards, Punt 6 plays, 20 yards, Field Goal 3 plays, -2 yards, Punt 6 plays, 19 yards, Punt 9 plays, 34 yards, Field Goal 5 plays, 7 yards, End of Game (two plays were kneeldowns) If the Eagles were facing a competent offense against a quarterback that wasn’t well past his prime, the outcome may have been different. Give credit to the offense for getting the field goal when they needed it and icing the game, but they had a stretch where they went 24 plays for 44 yards (1.8 yards per play). The ineptitude just happens way too often on offense to win games consistently. The Eagles were fortunate the Steelers never got anything going on offense until they were down 10 points in the final minutes. 2. Joe Milton looked better, for a quarter Wasn’t a surprise the Eagles scored 13 points in the first quarter with the way Joe Milton started the game. Milton had a nice 38-yard pass to Dallas Goedert that ended up being the highlight play of the paiing game, topping a quarter which he went 5-of-6 for 91 yards and averaged 15.2 yards per attempt. Milton struggled in the final three quarters, going 6-of-15 for 50 yards and averaging 3.3 yards per attempt (49.3 rating). The Eagles couldn’t get anything going on the ground either (20 carries, 37 yards, 1.9 yards per carry), which certainly isn’t ideal for a quarterback making his second career start. The Eagles were conservative with Milton, who avoided negative plays in spite of the offense failing to move the ball. He did have a fumble early, missed a deep throw to DeVonta Smith, and telegraphed a few balls throughout the game. Give credit to Milton for making the throw he needed to make to DeVonta Smith to ice the game, but the accuracy needs to improve. No matter how inconsistent Milton was, he did get his first win as a starter in the NFL. Something to build on. 3. How about Jake Elliott The Eagles don’t win this game without Elliott, who is having a fantastic season. Elliott’s future in Philadelphia was questioned this offseason, but Nick Sirianni gave him the vote of confidence he was still the kicker well before training camp. Elliott hit all four field goals in Sunday’s win, including a 53 and 55-yard kick in the second half. The 55-yard field goal put the Eagles up 19-9 with 4:24 remaining, massive in locking up their first win in over two months. Elliott has converted all four field goals from 50+ yards this season, making as many 50+ yard field goals as last year. The 100% field goal rate is a tremendous improvement over the 33.3% percent rate (5-of-15) on those kicks over the last two seasons. This season, Elliott is 11-of-12 on field goals this season — a career-best 91.7% conversion rate. He’s also 18-of-18 on extra point attempts. At 31 years old, Elliott is having an incredible bounce-back season. The Eagles’ faith in him paid off. 4. Braden Mann just shows up every week Jake Elliott has been fantastic this season, but he might not be the best player that kicks a football on the Eagles. That’s how good Mann has been all season, but Sunday’s win over the Steelers might have been his best performance of the year. Mann booted four punts for 237 yards, averaging 59.3 yards per punt. Two of those punts landed inside the 20-yard line and one inside the 10, pinning the Steelers at the 4-yard line with a kick that went 70 yards. He finished with 50.3 net yards per attempt, changing the starting field position by 21.8 yards. Mann is 15th in net yards per punt attempt (42.4) and 10th in punts inside the 20-yard line (45.3%). He’s fifth in the NFL in punts inside the 5-yard line (7.5%). The Eagles offense is consistently inefficient, so they need Mann to perform each and every week (he leads the NFL with 53 punts and 2,566 punt yards). Mann and Elliott have been two consistently good performers on the Eagles this season — and Rocco Underwood may be the third. 5. The impact without Jordan Davis was felt The first game the Eagles played since the Jordan Davis trade had a significant impact at defensive tackle, with the interior pass rush and the run defense. Byron Young was the No. 3 tackle, playing 22 snaps behind Jalen Carter (59 snaps) and Moro Ojomo (50 snaps). Young finished with 2.0 sacks, two TFL, and two QB hits in the win, while Gabe Hall added a sack and a QB hit. Young had more sacks on Sunday (two) than Davis had in nine games with Philadelphia this season (1.5), while Young and Hall combined for as many QB hits as Davis (three). The Eagles don’t have to use snaps on a nose tackle anymore and can go to a more traditional 4-3 look, which benefits the interior mass rush. Carter and Ojomo didn’t have standout games rushing the passer, but the rotational defensive tackles did. The run defense was excellent in the first game without Davis, as the Steelers had just 73 rushing yards and averaged 3.6 yards per carry. Aaron Rodgers was the leading rusher with 29 yards and the longest run given up by the run defense was a 12-yard scramble by Rodgers early in the game. The 76 rush yards allowed were a season-low for the Eagles, breaking the previous mark of 80 (which was last game). Quite impressive given this was the first game since the Davis trade. 6. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell might be the future at LB With Zack Baun on injured reserve, the Eagles are going to get a long look at both Campbell and Trotter Jr. over the rest of the season. This was the first game both Campbell and Trotter Jr. have started together since Week 4, and there were a lot of positive developments from the linebacker group. Trotter Jr. had a game-high 13 tackles (nine solo) and just seems to be in position every play. His instincts stand out pre-snap, which certainly helps out the second level of the field. He also had seven tackles on 16 designed runs, playing a major role in the Eagles having their best run defense of the year. Campbell was solid against the run too, but his performance in pass coverage was noticeable. He allowed three completions on three attempts, but only allowed 10 yards as Aaron Rodgers had just -3.0 air yards per attempt when targeting him. The Steelers’ pass offense isn’t very good, but Campbell has struggled against the pass all season. This is an encouraging sign for Campbell in his development, but he’ll get a significantly tougher…
author: Jeff Kerr

title: Eagles vs. Steelers: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: It looks like Nick Sirianni has his job for another week. It looks like the Eagles are heading towards a threepeat as NFC East champions, and another playoff run in 2026. Well, one of those statements may have a drop of truth to it after the Eagles snapped one streak and preserved another in a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Joe Milton III #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It looks like Nick Sirianni has his job for another week. It looks like the Eagles are heading towards a threepeat as NFC East champions, and another playoff run in 2026. Well, one of those statements may have a drop of truth to it after the Eagles snapped one streak and preserved another in a 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on an overcast Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak, their longest since 2012, during Andy Reid’s last season. The Eagles also continued their streak at home against Pittsburgh, winning for the 12th-straight time over the Steelers, who have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, (20–14 at Franklin Field), 61 years and two stadiums ago. Maybe the addition of former Eagles’ coach T.J. Paganatti as a consultant had something to do with the Eagles’ offensive line looking the best it has this season. The defense was strong, holding the Steelers to 73 yards rushing, 43 yards below their season average of 116 yards a game, and sacking 42-year-old relic Aaron Rodgers five times for minus-45 yards. Joe Milton was competent, moving the Eagles, especially in clutch situations, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards. Saquon Barkley made a brief appearance as Saquon Barkley rushing for a game-high 75 yards, the bulk of which came on a first quarter 38-yard touchdown run, while Jeremiah Trotter Jr. led the defense with a game-high 13 tackles, Marcus Epps had his best game this season with a season-high 8 tackles, and a bunch of guys who had received very little playing time making significant contributions like Byron Young’s two sacks, Jon Jones’ three defended passes, and Gabe Hall coming off the practice squad for a sack. The Eagles are 3-7. But are they suddenly cured of the slopfest they perpetrated over the first nine games—absolutely not. More proof is demanded. If the Eagles can somehow beat Dallas, in Dallas, on Thanksgiving, with the lowly tanking Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts following them, this nightmare of a season could have life, with the Eagles sitting at 6-7 in an NFC East Division up for grabs. Did Sunday’s victory resuscitate the Eagles or briefly camouflage a bad football team for one week and in the long run hurt its draft status? The answer may be four days from now in Dallas. The Eagles are no longer the proud owners of the NFL’s current longest losing streak, which has now been handed down I-95 to sinking Baltimore Ravens’ six-game skid after starting the season 4-1. For four days, everything will be right in Eaglesland. Sirianni is 6-0 after the bye week, Milton will no doubt stir comparisons by Eagles’ fans and podcasters to Randall Cunningham, and the true believers will begin making their reservations to Los Angeles for mid-February. There was a pile of good, some bad and smallest amount of ugly this season in the Eagles’ 19-16 win over the flailing Pittsburgh Steelers. The Good Joe Milton’s game-clinching third-down, seven-yard completion with less a minute to play to DeVonta Smith. The Eagles’ defense. They kept the Steelers to under 100 yards in the first half. Vic Fangio dialed up blitzes, stunts, and caused all kinds of problems for Aaron Rodgers. They sacked Rodgers five times for minus-45 yards and kept the Steelers out of the end zone for their first 10 drives before Max Hurleman’s 20-yard touchdown reception from Aaron Rodgers with 1:21 to play. Gabe Hall came up from the practice squad to sack Rodgers for the fifth time, taking the old river down for a nine-yard loss on the Steelers’ second drive in the fourth quarter. At the time,the Eagles sacked Rodgers five times for minus-45 yards. Milton had a knack for completing big passes in big situations. His nine-yard completion to Darius Cooper for a first down on a third-and-six on the Eagles’ first drive of the fourth quarter was one of them. It was just the second first down for the Eagles in their first five second half possessions. Milton later converted another third down by hitting Cooper for a 14-yard completion on a third-and-10 at the Steelers’ 31 on the Eagles’ second fourth quarter drive. Nolan Smith’s seven-yard sack on the Steelers’ second play of the fourth quarter, zapping Pittsburgh’s hopes of tying the game on a third-and-eight at the Eagles’ 35. More importantly, the Smith sack pushed the Steelers out of field goal range and forced a punt with 13:12 left to play. The problem was, the Eagles had not moved the ball since the first quarter, only gaining 30 yards since torching the Steelers’ defense for 128 yards of total offense in the opening frame. Safety Marcus Epps had his best game this season, coming up to make tackles for short gains. He stopped Germie Bernard on a second-and-10 in the third quarter, he came up and took down Rico Dowdle for a three-yard loss in the second quarter. He finished with a season-high eight tackles—all solos. Jake Elliott hitting field goals of 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards. Elliott is 11 of 12 on field goal attempts, and 18 of 18 on extra points. Elliott is 4-for-4 on field goals attempts of 50 yards or more. Hehas quietly had a great season. It makes you wonder why Nick Sirianni kept going for it on fourth down this season on the plus side of the field with Elliott kicking so well. Braden Mann’s 70-yard punt that pinned the Steelers at their four after a three-and-out on the Eagles’ second possession of the second half. Cornerback Jon Jones making a diving deflection on an Aaron Rodgers’ pass intended for Roman Wilson at the goal line on the Steelers’ second drive of the second quarter. Jones later came up to break up a fourth-quarter attempt to Wilson. Linebacker Jonathan Greenard’s 12-yard sack on the Steelers’ first drive of the second quarter on a third-and-19. Defensive tackle Byron Young’s nine-yard on the Steelers’ first drive of the second quarter. Young had his second sack late in the third quarter, pulling down old man Rodgers for seven yards on first-and-10. The first quarter. The Eagles scored a season-high 13 points after they had scored a total of 28 points in their first nine games in the first quarter. They had 128 total yards of offense to Pittsburgh’s 35 and five first downs to the Steelers’ one. The Eagles’ 13-0 lead was their largest this season. Saquon Barkey’s 38-yard sideline touchdown run for a 13-0 first quarter lead. It was classic Barkley, using his considerable speed to run away from TJ Watt trying to catch him from the backside and finding a rare hole. Milton hitting Cooper with a 29-yard rope down the sideline on a third-and-13 to the Steelers’ 28, and Dallas Goedert for a 38-yard pass on a great touch pass on a third-and-18 to the Steelers’ 13 on the Eagles’ second drive. Unfortunately, the Eagles were only able to get a Jake Elliott field goal out of it. The Eagles getting the Steelers off the field on Pissburgh’s first three drives for a total of 23 yards and no first downs. Of the Steelers’ first seven plays, the Eagles had two plays for zero and minus-1 yard, and an average of 2.3 yards a play. The Eagles held the Steelers on fourth-and-one, and had Pittsburgh facing a third-and-eight and third-and-14. Jihaad Campbell taking down Steelers tailback Jaylen Warren for a one-yard loss on the Steelers’ second drive at the Steelers’ 21. Jake Elliott nailed a 41-yard field goal with 10:01 left in the first quarter. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. slicing through on fourth-and-inches to bring down Warren down for no gain on the Steelers first drive at the Pittsburg 40. It was the utmost disrespect by Steelers’ coach Mike McCarthy, thinking he could convert a fourth-down gamble that early in the…
author: Joseph Santoliquito

title: Eagles-Steelers final score: Philadelphia snaps 7-game losing streak
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 3-7 after beating the Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday! Final score: 19 to 16. The seven-game losing streak is over! And Nick Sirianni finally has his first career win with the Eagles as home underdogs (1-9 in those situations now). Fans who wanted the team to tank for […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with fans after scoring a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 3-7 after beating the Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday! Final score: 19 to 16. The seven-game losing streak is over! And Nick Sirianni finally has his first career win with the Eagles as home underdogs (1-9 in those situations now). Fans who wanted the team to tank for better draft position won’t be happy with this win that probably eliminates Philly from No. 1 overall pick consideration in the 2027 NFL Draft. But if you’re holding out hope for the Eagles as extreme long shots to win the NFC East, well, here you go. Vic Fangio’s defense turned in an inspired effort and the Joe Milton-led offense did just enough, highlighted by Saquon Barkley’s 38-yard touchdown run. Is the offense fixed?! Hardly. They were pretty bad after their sole touchdown. But Jake Elliott pitched in with makes from 41, 29, 53, and 55 to give the Eagles enough to outpace the Steelers’ lackluster offense. The Steelers remain winless in Philadelphia since 1965. Next up for the Eagles: a quick turnaround as they travel down to Dallas to play the Cowboys this Thursday afternoon on Thanksgiving. Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, check me out on the PHLY Eagles postgame show! FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Steelers began at their own 31-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-4, Aaron Rodgers completed a pass to DK Metcalf just short of the sticks. Facing 4th-and-1, the Steelers kept their offense on the field and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. tackled Jaylen Warren short of the marker! Big stop to start the game. Check the timestamp: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. always looks like he knows exactly what the offense is running. Great anticipation. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) June 9, 2026 Trot with the stop pic.twitter.com/8F2S0Y0H2P — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 22, 2026 The Eagles took over at the plus 40-yard line. Saquon Barkley took a carry to the left edge for an easy first down run. Joe Milton then got strip-sacked … and just looked at the ball on the ground … before Jordan Mailata jumped on it for the Eagles to retain possession. What are you doing, Joe? Facing 3rd-and-8 after a completion to DeVonta Smith, Milton threw short of the sticks to Makai Lemon. Jake Elliott came in for the 41-yard field goal make. Five plays for 17 yards and three points. Might’ve been good to be more aggressive and try to get seven points by converting that 4th-and-5. EAGLES 3, STEELERS 0. Joe Milton just watched his fumble pic.twitter.com/cLOfmTFhTR — Jet (@_jetgaming) November 22, 2026 The Steelers took over at their own 20-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-8 after Jihaad Campbell made a nice run stop in the hole, Trot Jr. tackled Pat Freiermuth short of the sticks to force a Steelers punt. Strong start by Vic Fangio’s defense out of the bye. The Eagles took over at their own 31-yard line after a 17-yard Britain Covey punt return. Facing 3rd-and-13 after Milton was sacked on a blitz, Milton had a clean pocket but held onto the ball to invite pressure … and rolled left … to throw a strike on the move to Darius Cooper (who else but the birthday boy?) for 29 yards and a first down. Great ball. Barkley ran for another first down but it was called back due to an illegal shift on Dallas Goedert. Milton helped the Eagles pick up another first down through the air with a touch pass to Goedert for an over-the-shoulder grab for 38 yards. What is this offensive success?! Facing 3rd-and-9 after Barkley was tackled for a loss, Makai Lemon dropped a Milton pass short of the sticks and Mailata was flagged for illegal formation anyway. Elliott came in for the 29-yard field goal make. Bad to not get into the end zone but, hey, some signs of life! (The bar to clear is in hell.) EAGLES 6, STEELERS 0. Heck of a throw on the run from Joe Milton PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DWwabguGPB — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 The Steelers took over at their own 10-yard line after Pittsburgh’s kick returner muffed Elliott’s kickoff. Facing 3rd-and-9, the Steelers false started. Facing 3rd-and-14, the Steelers went with a quick pass to bring up a punt. The Eagles took over at the plus 48-yard line after Covey’s 13-yard punt return. Milton completed a pass to DeVonta Smith, who made a one-handed catch for 10 yards. Then Barkley went 38 yards to the house!Nicely blocked up for him, looked like 2024. Watch out! Second half of the season team! EAGLES 13, STEELERS 0. SAQUON HOUSE CALL! pic.twitter.com/e009d6X5H5 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 22, 2026 Saquon Barkley has scored rushing TDs in a career-best four consecutive games. #Eagles — John Gonoude (@john_gonoude) November 22, 2026 In their last game the Eagles had 220 yards and scored 11 points. In the 1st Qtr today the Eagles have 128 yards and 13 points. Fantastic start to the second half of the season. — Tommy Lawlor (@lawlornfl) November 22, 2026 The last time the Eagles scored on three consecutive offensive drives? November 23rd, 2025 in Dallas 364 days ago 🤯 — Drew Balis (@drewBbalis) November 22, 2026 The Steelers took over at their own 18-yard line. Rodgers ran for the Steelers’ first first down to end the first quarter. SECOND QUARTER Facing 3rd-and-7, the pocket collapsed on Rodgers and Jalyx Hunt got to the old ass quarterback for his first sack of the season. Except … there was an illegal contact penalty on Quinyon Mitchell. Very soft call by the refs to give the Steelers a first down at midfield instead of an Eagles stop. Facing 3rd-and-20 after Byron Young (first sack of the season!) sacked Rodgers, Jonathan Greenard chased down Rodgers in the backfield for another sack. Greenard followed up his first sack of the season in Week 9 with another here. Inspired defensive effort to limit the Steelers to 16 plays for 17 yards. JG tripping 'em up 💪 pic.twitter.com/ReVRNqFwxy — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) November 22, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 28-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-2, Milton had DeVonta streaking up the left sideline with a step on Jalen Ramsey but the quarterback missed his receiver with an overthrow. Dang. Hey, at least their first three-and-out didn’t come until middleish of the second quarter! Nick Sirianni opted to punt from 4th-and-2 at the Eagles’ own 36-yard line. The Steelers took over at their own 16-yard line. Pittsburgh picked up their third first down of the game. Jihaad Campbell got hurt, which forced Anfernee Orji onto the field. The Steelers picked up another first down on a screen. And another on a swing pass as Campbell returned to the field. Facing 3rd-and-1 after Rico Dowdle broke through a Riq Woolen missed tackle, Rodgers hit Germie Bernard on a short completion for yet another first down. Marcus Epps blew up a Steelers screen for a TFL. Facing 3rd-and-3, Campbell wasn’t able to get Dowdle down to allow yet another first down, this one into the red zone. Two short passes produced another Steelers first down, this one into goal-to-go. Rodgers missed a would-be touchdown to Bernard in the middle of the end zone with Cooper DeJean trailing. Facing 3rd-and-goal from the 7-yard line after the defense sniffed out a shovel pass, Jones broke up a pass into the end zone to bring up a Steelers field goal make. Big-time bend but don’t break drive by the Eagles, allowing just three points on a 17-play, 77-yard drive that lasted 8:22. EAGLES 13, STEELERS 3. The Eagles took over at their own 30-yard line with 0:54 on the clock and three timeouts to work with. A run by Barkley lost three yards and prompted the Steelers to take their second timeout. Another Barkley run…

title: Steelers WR DK Metcalf avoids accountability after ejection
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after a pair of unsportsmanlike penalties, the latter of which saw him reach into the facemask of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean for what appeared to be a poke in the eye. Metcalf left the stadium before the media had […]
full_text: (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles after a pair of unsportsmanlike penalties, the latter of which saw him reach into the facemask of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean for what appeared to be a poke in the eye. Metcalf left the stadium before the media had a chance to speak with him, but addressed the media on Monday back in Pittsburgh, where he denied poking DeJean in the eye. “I didn’t poke him in the eye,” Metcalf said via Nick Farabaugh . “I was telling him to stop pushing me.” When asked why he has struggled to maintain composure, Metcalf had an opportunity to take accountability for his actions. While it may not take back what he did or necessarily help him when it comes to his punishment, it would at least show some level of leadership on his part. Instead, he blamed those who pushed him to the point of getting ejected, “I think you got to ask the people that seemingly do that to me,” Metcalf said after being asked by Will Graves . Whether Metcalf will be suspended is yet to be known, but this has the potential to end very poorly for the Ole Miss product, who seemingly couldn’t care less what happens next.
