title: The Steelers need to cut DK Metcalf
summary: It turns out that shopping for used cars and players on the trade block are similar experiences. Both feature assets with some mileage to them, and a man at the top who will do anything he can to make you sign all the paperwork necessary to make the transaction official. Sometimes, both sides end up […]
full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It turns out that shopping for used cars and players on the trade block are similar experiences. Both feature assets with some mileage to them, and a man at the top who will do anything he can to make you sign all the paperwork necessary to make the transaction official. Sometimes, both sides end up happy. Take the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings, for example. In 2020, the Bills sent their first-round pick to the Vikings in exchange for Stefon Diggs. The star receiver had multiple All-Pro seasons in Buffalo and helped Josh Allen become the superstar quarterback we see today, while Minnesota used that pick from the Bills to draft Justin Jefferson. Other times, though, you have the great swindle that took place in March, 2025 when Seattle Seahawks GM John Schneider laughed all the way to the bank after selling a lemon to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Pittsburgh traded a second-round pick for DK Metcalf, and then immediately gave him a four-year, $132 million extension to be their No. 1 wide receiver. Less than two months later, they shipped George Pickens away to Dallas for a third-round pick. What has happened in the year and a half since has made the Steelers look like one of the most foolish franchises in the NFL. Metcalf has played in 25 games for the Steelers. In those 25 games, he has caught just 95 passes – less than four receptions per game – for 1,284 yards. Since the start of the 2025 season, there have been 127 receivers to run at least 250 routes – Metcalf ranks 93rd in target success rate. And while there was hope this summer during a very productive training camp for Metcalf to take a jump in Year Two as a Steeler, he has, instead, regressed to a point that has made him borderline unplayable. After 11 weeks, Metcalf is 50th in the NFL in receptions (36), 48th in yards (434), and 59th in touchdowns (2). He is also 51st out of 55 receivers in target success rate (min. 250 routes run) while his EPA per target is 46th and his reception percentage is 50th. Since joining the Steelers, Metcalf has just three games of 100+ yards, compared to 12 games of 45 yards or fewer – all while being the seventh-highest paid wide receiver in the league. This four-game stretch has been his most brutal to date. Over that span, Metcalf has caught six passes. In two of those games, he had fewer than five yards. The Steelers brought in Metcalf and got rid of Pickens because they felt Pickens was too much of a head case to give a long-term deal to. Since the start of 2025, Pickens has 55 more receptions, 925 more yards, seven more touchdowns, and an All-Pro selection to his name, while having one (potentially soon to be two) fewer suspensions. Which brings us to Week 11 in Philadelphia. Metcalf was ejected from the game after two skirmishes that both resulted in unsportsmanlike conduct penalties, the latter of which he reached into the facemask of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. It’s the second time in two seasons Metcalf has gotten into a physical altercation since joining the Steelers. Last season, he slapped a fan that was taunting him in Detroit during the team’s win over the Lions in Week 16. He was subsequently suspended by the NFL for the final two games of the regular season. Given his history, the league will likely view him as a repeat offender and give him another suspension of some kind. But what should the Steelers do? Should they get ahead of the league and suspend him internally for conduct detrimental to the team? I’ll do you one better – they should cut him. As Alan Saunders of Steelers Now points out, Metcalf doesn’t have any guaranteed money remaining on his contract after a restructure earlier this year. Should he be released between now and any point before the 2027 season begins, the Steelers would eat a dead cap hit of $37.5 million – and that’s what they should do. It would be one thing to deal with Metcalf’s temper if he was producing – he isn’t. He offers more problems than production.. His presence on the field does more harm than good. And it was proven in real time that anyone else can fill his role – and do it better. Undrafted practice squad receiver Max Hurleman made his NFL debut on Sunday and caught six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. He now has more games of five receptions and a touchdowns than Metcalf does this season. Everyone recognizes that Metcalf has one of the worst contracts in the league. And based on how Deshaun Watson is playing for the Browns right now, Metcalf may have the worst contract in the NFL. Send a message to the rest of the team, and future Steelers, as well. It doesn’t matter who you are or what you’re making. If you are more hurtful to the team than anything else, you’ll be shown the door. Admit your mistake, cut your losses, and get rid of the worst trade and contract the franchise has ever seen. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles
summary: The Steelers have entered their first losing streak of the season, failing to rebound from last week’s defeat in Cincinnati after a 19-16 loss to the 2-7 Eagles in Week 11. Despite a favorable matchup on Sunday, the Steelers still can’t seem to win in Philadelphia, dropping to 6-4 on the 2026 season. As always, […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Steelers have entered their first losing streak of the season, failing to rebound from last week’s defeat in Cincinnati after a 19-16 loss to the 2-7 Eagles in Week 11. Despite a favorable matchup on Sunday, the Steelers still can’t seem to win in Philadelphia, dropping to 6-4 on the 2026 season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had. 1. The Steelers’ offense can’t succeed in its current state The Steelers’ loss of left guard Mason McCormick has been rough for the offense. Not only is the team without one of its best players and a linchpin of the left side of the offensive line, but McCormick’s replacement, Spencer Anderson, did not look remotely close to an NFL starter in Sunday’s loss to the Eagles. Byron Young sacks Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/TLU4p3fdv8 — 𝐃𝐈𝐄-𝐇𝐀𝐑𝐃 🦅 𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐋 𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐀𝐓𝐄 (@Eaglesfans9) November 22, 2026 Anderson was the weakest link, but the Steelers’ line as a whole struggled to create push in the run game on Sunday afternoon. And in the passing game, they struggled in several aspects, whether it was against speed and power moves or simply looking unprepared and disorganized to Philadelphia’s blitzes. But making matters much worse was the fact that quarterback Aaron Rodgers can’t really handle pressure anymore. His mobility is poor although not completely gone (Rodgers actually led the Steelers in rushing with 29 yards), but his response to a collapsing pocket is a shell of what it used to be. He drops his eyes, his accuracy crumbles, and he often fails to find daylight when attempting to evade any sort of rush. Per PFF, Aaron Rodgers was under pressure on just 13 percent of his dropbacks, yet took 5 sacks for a pressure to sack rate of 71.4%! That number will come down some tomorrow when PFF reviews, but it's still going be unbelievably bad — Jon Ledyard (@LedyardNFLDraft) November 22, 2026 The end result? Rodgers was sacked five times for a total of 45 yards lost. His average depth of target in the first half, before the offense went into panic mode late, was a laughable 0.5 yards — a historically low number . The Steelers nearly left Philadelphia without a touchdown despite facing a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league against both the run and pass. The Steelers were consistently running late when getting to the line of scrimmage, and their veteran quarterback often seemed more frustrated than calm and collected. I don’t think it mattered how open or not open the Steelers’ pass catchers were on Sunday. Rodgers, playing the way he was under the pressure he was facing, probably couldn’t have gotten the ball to his receivers downfield either way. And the Pittsburgh ground game, which once looked like a sustainable foundation for the team’s offense, was stifled by a 25th-ranked Eagles run defense. The Steelers did not field a professional NFL offense on Sunday. And while past history would point to the team rebounding to some degree in later games, it’s hard to see Pittsburgh accomplishing much if Rodgers and Anderson remain playing on the level they did against the Eagles. (Also D.K. Metcalf, of course). 2. The D.K. Metcalf experience has been a disaster, but the wide receiver room is getting better… maybe? D.K. Metcalf has dead cap hits of $35.7 million and $23.8 million in the next two seasons, respectively. Even if he finishes 2026 without another catch, moving on from a player of his abilities with that contract verges on wildly irresponsible. But after Sunday’s showing against the Eagles, you have to at least think about it, right? Metcalf, who managed just one catch for two yards on four targets, was ejected after his second personal foul penalty of the game, when he appeared to try to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean’s eyes. DK Metcalf is poking Cooper DeJean in the eyes! He’s ejected! #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/1AJfkiZM17 — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) November 22, 2026 The resulting 15-yard penalty pushed a must-make Steelers field goal back 15 yards (Chris Boswell still delivered). Metcalf is the seventh-highest paid receiver in the NFL in terms of yearly average. He’s also 37th in the league in receiving yards, with more games under 50 yards than over, including three under 20. More than that, his rash of dropped passes, failed contested catches, and unnecessary penalties have at times made Metcalf more of a detriment to the team than even a low-end WR1 in recent games — something that was especially true versus Philadelphia. DK Metcalf today: • 2 receiving yards • 2 personal fouls • Ejected in the 3rd quarter Philly fans waved goodbye on his way out. https://t.co/S5DlOPtDch pic.twitter.com/8Ll1vkJdFF — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 22, 2026 As a player, Metcalf seems to have the yips, something he should be able to work his way out of eventually, especially if he ends up in a better environment in future seasons (I’ve maintained for a while that he and Rodgers have never been a good on-field pairing). But far more frustrating have been the wildly undisciplined moments from a veteran who should be a leader in an offense full of young skill players. There’s also some irony considering the Steelers essentially brought Metcalf in to replace the volatile personality of George Pickens, who has emerged as the much better player following the trade even if his on-field flare-ups haven’t died down in Dallas. Metcalf will probably be suspended by the NFL after seemingly going for DeJean’s eyes. That will make him a repeat offender as a Steeler, considering he missed critical games for Pittsburgh late last season after appearing to strike a fan during an altercation in Detroit. There has to be a line at some point, especially when managing the culture of a team in a transitional period such as the Steelers. And Metcalf might have crossed it. But while Metcalf’s horrendous day (and season) have headlined many of the Steelers’ struggles in the passing game, I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention former undrafted free agent Max Hurleman, who logged team highs in catches (six), yards (61) and touchdowns (one) in his first career game on Sunday. It’s always great to see a practice squad player such as Hurleman not only earn a helmet on game day, but actually look like he belongs on an NFL field. Hurleman ran some solid routes. He made tough catches. And most importantly, it looks like he has the trust of Rodgers. I’m by no means saying he’ll maintain Sunday’s level of productivity going forward, but Hurleman has certainly earned another elevation, at least, going forward. Elsewhere, getting Roman Wilson back from injured reserve against the Eagles gave the Steelers’ offense a much-needed vertical threat even if he and Rodgers didn’t always connect. Underneath, Germie Bernard continues to shine as a yards after catch option who is likely the team’s best and most reliable receiver at the moment. Michael Pittman Jr., another possession receiver, should also be back in the next week. Keep the first point of this article in mind — I’m not sure how much receiver play matters in this offense in its current state — but this wide receiver room might be in slightly better shape than most think in the coming weeks. Even if Metcalf does face a suspension, it is worth noting that the offense seemed to play its best with No. 4 off the field late against the Eagles. 3. Pittsburgh’s secondary is a mess The Steelers’ offense is once again the story of the loss, but the defense can’t be left completely off the hook. Despite giving up a respectable 19 points on the road, the Steelers secondary gave up several crucial third downs to Joe Milton in his second career start. Even from the TV copy, it was clear that the Eagles had plenty of open receivers downfield throughout the game, namely Devonta Smith, who Milton either didn’t always see or couldn’t always hit. summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers dropped their second straight game with a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. In a game where the offense again struggled for the majority of the game, the biggest storyline coming out is the ejection of their handsomely paid receiver. DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half of Pittsburgh’s […]
full_text: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers dropped their second straight game with a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. In a game where the offense again struggled for the majority of the game, the biggest storyline coming out is the ejection of their handsomely paid receiver. DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half of Pittsburgh’s Week 11 contest after a second personal foul attempting to poke Eagles corner Cooper DeJean in the eye. Just a few plays prior, Metcalf received his first personal foul of the contest for an altercation with several Eagles defenders. The receiver was seen exiting the stadium as the team was walking to the locker room after the game. Metcalf may have avoided having to speak to the media after the game, but his close friend and teammate Pat Freiermuth was not shy about offering his thoughts on the receiver’s ejection. “He knows that’s unacceptable,” Freiermuth said, via Alan Saunders . “He’ll be fine. But like I said, he’s one of my closest friends on the team, and he knows I have his back in those situations. But it just can’t happen.” Freiermuth has been vocal in his defense of Metcalf throughout the season, saying that the team had his back earlier this week amidst the receivers’ struggles. Unfortunately, today, it was about his extracurricular activites after the play rather than his play on the field that cost his team in a huge. Metcalf posted just one catch for two yards in the contest while also drawing two personal foul calls. The veteran is also subject to suspension from the league who will review the matter later this week. Freiermuth maintains that he has his friends’ back after his suspension, but also knows how much it cost the team in their second straight loss. His actions may very well cost the Steelers for longer than just this week. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers stock report after 19-16 loss to Eagles
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 0-12 in Philadelphia since 1965, as they fell to the Eagles 19-16 on Sunday. The Steelers were flat for much of the game and could not get anything going offensively until the game was effectively over. After sitting atop the AFC North after Week 8, the Steelers have lost two […]
full_text: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 0-12 in Philadelphia since 1965, as they fell to the Eagles 19-16 on Sunday. The Steelers were flat for much of the game and could not get anything going offensively until the game was effectively over. After sitting atop the AFC North after Week 8, the Steelers have lost two consecutive contests in their quest to defend their AFC North crown. Here is my weekly stock report after the Steelers’ shocking loss in Philadelphia. Stock Up WR Max Hurleman Max Hurleman was arguably the Steelers’ best player in his first career NFL game. His six catches for 61 yards led the team. The undrafted rookie was on the receiving end of the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown, as he made a great adjustment in the back of the end zone for a 20-yard score. Hurleman supplanted rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen as the Steelers’ primary return man, and given his performance today, it’s hard to imagine the Steelers have any plans to take Hurleman off the field for the foreseeable future. To this point, it looks like the Steelers may have a player in No. 84. K Chris Boswell We have to give Chris Boswell his flowers today, given he was the entirety of the Steelers’ offense. Boswell nailed field goals of 25 yards, 40 yards, and 52 yards. The veteran kicker kept the Steelers alive for as long as he could today. EDGE Alex Highsmith With Nick Hebrig ruled out earlier in the week, the Steelers were on pace to get the game they needed from veteran Alex Highsmith. The edge rusher recorded two early sacks on Eagles quarterback Joe Milton, but came up limping after his second sack. He spent an exorbitant amount of time in the blue medical tent and was even seen running around on the sidelines, but he did not return. Despite his early exit, Highsmith deserves some credit for the game he was having before his ankle injury derailed it. Stock Down WR DK Metcalf DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half after receiving his second personal foul for poking Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. I was honestly shocked by how the Steelers kept Metcalf in the game after his first personal foul, given how fired up he was. The receiver was unable to control his emotions, as he was ejected just a few plays later. There isn’t much to be said that hasn’t already been said about Metcalf. He is holding Pittsburgh’s offense back at this point. The team might actually be better off without his shenanigans and inability to control his emotions now that Hurleman has emerged and Roman Wilson is back. Metcalf could very well see an extended suspension from the league after his altercation in Philadelphia. Running Game Jaylen Warren entered the contest averaging 5.7 yards per carry on the season. He was held to 3.1 yards per carry today. Rico Dowdle was held in check as well, averaging just 3 yards per carry. The Steelers boasted one of the NFL’s best and most efficient running games through the first eight weeks of the season. They haven’t been able to get anything going in their last two games. Philadelphia came in ranked 25th against the run, making this performance even more frustrating for the Steelers. Offensive Line In case you were wondering just how important Mason McCormick is to this offensive line, look no further than the events of today. The run game was not nearly as efficient with the new-look offensive line. The pass protection was not much better, as Aaron Rodgers was sacked five times and was constantly on the move to avoid pressure. You have to wonder if the Steelers could look to replace Spencer Anderson, who has already been benched once this season, in the coming weeks. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers offensive woes continue, drop second straight game in loss to Eagles
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have now lost consecutive games for the first time this season, losing to the Philadelphia Eagles by the score of 19-16, dropping their record to 6-4 on the season. For the second straight week, the Steelers’ offense completely did them in. Their first four drives ended without points, the first of which […]
full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have now lost consecutive games for the first time this season, losing to the Philadelphia Eagles by the score of 19-16, dropping their record to 6-4 on the season. For the second straight week, the Steelers’ offense completely did them in. Their first four drives ended without points, the first of which saw a turnover on downs that led to an Eagles field goal. Their subsequent two drives were a pair of three-and-outs and then a six-play drive that ended in a punt. In total, they ran 16 plays for 17 yards in their first four drives. Meanwhile, the Eagles put together a 13-0 lead that the Steelers would never surmount. The Steelers entered halftime down 13-3, and Aaron Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt over the first two quarters, the lowest such number with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking air yards in 2006, per Brooke Pryor. Aaron Rodgers averaged 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half — the lowest air yards per attempt in a half with at least 20 attempts since ESPN began tracking AY in 2006, via @ESPNInsights 12/20 attempts were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage with his furthest… — Brooke Pryor (@bepryor) November 22, 2026 Overall, the offense failed to reach 300 yards for the second straight week, finishing with just 255 yards. The run game was never able to get going, as the Eagles made it clear they would not allow Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle to get going. It also helped Philadelphia that the Steelers were starting an unplayable guard in Spencer Anderson, who continues to prove he isn’t an NFL talent, and Brock Hoffman who continues to regress by the week. The Steelers finished the day with 73 rushing yards, and Aaron Rodgers led them with 29 yards on the ground. Defensively, the Steelers did everything that could have been asked of them. They allowed less than 20 points, held the Eagles to just 214 yards of offense, and they got off the field on nine of 13 third downs. Unfortunately, Pittsburgh’s offense was 5-of-17 on third downs themselves, and Rodgers took five sacks. The over-arching story of the game, though, was DK Metcalf. The seventh-highest-paid receiver in the league had another dreadful game, catching one pass for two yards before being ejected in the third quarter for an altercation with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. Metcalf poked DeJean in the eye, and he finished the game with as many yards as unsportsmanlike conduct penalties, and as many ejections as catches. A suspension likely awaits him, and his future in Pittsburgh becomes even more murky after a three-game stretch that has seen him catch four passes. In relief of Metcalf, though, Max Hurleman put on a tremendous show in his first NFL game, catching six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. To put that in perspective, Metcalf doesn’t have a game this season where he has five catches and a touchdown in the same game. The Steelers will now have a quick turnaround, as they’ll host the Denver Broncos on Black Friday as they hope to avoid going from 6-2 to 6-5 in the blink of an eye. title: Former Seahawks corner Riq Woolen benched by Eagles after missed tackles
summary: At Field Gulls, we keep tabs on former Seattle Seahawks players whether it’s going well or not, and there was one Week 11 game that went poorly for a couple of ex-‘Hawks. When the Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, one of the headlines was former Seattle Seahawks receiver DK Metcalf getting […]
full_text: ﻿Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At Field Gulls, we keep tabs on former Seattle Seahawks players whether it’s going well or not, and there was one Week 11 game that went poorly for a couple of ex-‘Hawks. When the Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, one of the headlines was former Seattle Seahawks receiver DK Metcalf getting tossed for two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties , the second of which was an attempted eye poke of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. Another notable ex-Seahawks in that game was Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, whose own day didn’t go a whole lot better. Woolen didn’t play on defense for almost the entire second half, only to eventually come back later in the game when Quinyon Mitchell suffered a hamstring injury. Jonathan Jones replaced Woolen in the lineup while Riq’s snaps were limited to special teams. In his post-game media availability, Woolen confirmed he was benched and it’s for an all too familiar reason for Seahawks fans and maybe the Seahawks organization. Hear what Riq Woolen had to say about being benched for missed tackles before returning late in the game amid a rash of Eagles injuries at cornerback. pic.twitter.com/9gfW5ItI1C — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) November 22, 2026 “I can’t say too much,” Woolen said. “It’s just the [coach’s] job. I mess up, they take me out. And I messed up, he took me out, and I just gotta be a great teammate just like how the next guy is. “It was just hard,” Woolen added. “I didn’t play the whole second half. To go in the last three, four minutes is tough. The DB position is a mental position more than physicality, so to be able to try to check back in mentally when you’ve been out so long is hard, but I have to be there for my guys no matter what. No matter how I’m feeling, it’s a team sport.” When asked if he was surprised if he was taken out, Woolen said he was not. “I had a talk with a coach before the game and then it was just basically saying I may be taken out a series just to help, you know, because I had a couple mental lapses. But it just turned into the whole second half and that’s how it went.” Putting two and two together, it looks as if this was the sequence that was the final straw for the Eagles coaching staff. This two-play sequence of missed tackles is presumably why the Eagles benched Riq Woolen, who confirmed that he was pulled from the lineup for almost the entire 2nd half before coming back in late for the injured Quinyon Mitchell. pic.twitter.com/JAc43a3yHl — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 23, 2026 “You know, we just wanted to reset there a little bit,” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said of Woolen’s benching. He also noted that Woolen did “a nice job responding” after injuries forced him back into the game. Woolen has been either benched or at least lost snaps in four consecutive seasons dating back to 2023. Tackling and effort issues resulted in a benching against the San Francisco 49ers and then scarcely playing against the Philadelphia Eagles. Under Mike Macdonald, Woolen sat for a series versus the Minnesota Vikings for an off-the-field team violation, and then last year saw his snaps reduced to effectively a split role with Josh Jobe after a horrible fourth quarter on opening day against the 49ers. After an encouraging start to Woolen’s Eagles career, ongoing penalty issues and tackling woes have not subsided on a new team. Having signed a one-year, $12 million “prove-it” contract in free agency, it doesn’t look like Riq is set to cash in with a major multi-year contract when he hits the market again in 2027. So if you’re so minded, Steelers-Eagles was distilled vindication for those who wanted to move on from Metcalf and/or Woolen. They both had plenty of positives in Seattle, but their negatives not only became persistent problems, they haven’t gone away elsewhere for either player.

full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are realistically out of the NFC West race after the San Francisco 49ers walloped the Minnesota Vikings 35-10 in Mexico City. Minnesota’s vaunted defense was shredded by a big Brock Purdy performance, while the Vikings offense committed some costly turnovers and was never really comfortable dealing with the 49ers defensive front. You can deny that the 9-1 49ers are elite and looking like the best team in the NFL, but the reality is San Francisco is playing like a juggernaut. As the Seahawks prepare for a Week 12 road trip to Santa Clara, they are three games back of their rivals in the NFC West standings. If there’s any solace in Minnesota’s performance, it’s the fact that they are now just a game ahead of Seattle in the Wild Card race. Take a look at the latest standings entering Monday Night Football : NFC playoff standings with the 49ers win 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 2. Detroit Lions (8-2, 2-0 NFCN) 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) 5. Chicago Bears (8-2, 0-2 NFCN) 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4, 4-4 NFC) 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4, 2-1 NFCW, 2-3 NFC) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4, 1-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7, 1-0 vs ATL+NO) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7, 1-1 vs TB+NO) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7, 0-1 vs TB+ATL, 1-5 NFC) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7, 1-6 NFC) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) Seattle needed a Vikings win to have an opportunity to pull within a game of the 49ers in Week 12. Now the best the Seahawks can hope for is being two games back of the 49ers with only five games to go. In the words of Deniece Williams, it’s going to take a miracle . But the 49ers-Vikings result doesn’t damage Seattle’s hopes of reaching the postseason. If the Seahawks beat the 49ers in Week 12 and the Green Bay Packers fail to beat the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, then Seattle will slot into a Wild Card spot heading into December. If the Seahawks get swept by the Niners then forget about the division title, and the Wild Card becomes a lot more uncertain. Week 12 is still about as close to a must-win as it gets for the Super Bowl champions.

full_text: There is no way around it: the Seattle Seahawks need a miracle to win the NFC West. Beyond the high probability of needing to win out (starting with Week 12 at the San Francisco 49ers), they’re going to need the 49ers to drop at least two other games… starting with Week 11 against the Minnesota Vikings. Yes, the final international game of the 2026 season is in Mexico City, and it’ll be the 49ers as the home team versus the Minnesota Vikings. It’s Kyle Shanahan’s offense against Brian Flores’ defense, except this time the Vikings have a shot to win because Kirk Cousins is the QB. Cousins can exact revenge on the 49ers after losing to them in his final start as a Las Vegas Raider just two weeks ago. If the Vikings win, the Seahawks can pull to within a game out of first place with a win over the 49ers in Week 12. If the Vikings lose, then the division race is probably over and Seattle is just looking to deny the 49ers top spot in the NFC and to improve its own Wild Card chances. Even a Vikings loss it not necessarily catastrophic for the Seahawks, as it would drag Minnesota into the Wild Card hunt and they’d only be a game up on Seattle. But we want a 49ers loss. DK and Aaron Rodgers seem like an incompatible match stylistically, but there is no quarterback who can work with Metcalf when he leads all NFL receivers with eight penalties committed and drops like these… DK Metcalf today: – 9 targets – 3 catches – 26 yards $33M a year. pic.twitter.com/foZlfOU3bG — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) September 13, 2026 Yet another drop for DK Metcalf!!!!! #yips #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/5LH7Dl7sSo — Steelers Depot 7⃣ (@Steelersdepot) September 20, 2026 DK Metcalf with a wide open drop that turns into an INT! 👀 #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/l5zZDo7Ppq — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) November 1, 2026 And even when he does catch the ball, he’s not been very effective picking up YAC. still shocked that Metcalf wasn’t able to get a first down here…. #NFL #Steelers pic.twitter.com/eNzpKtB1kl — The Standard (@TheStandard412) November 22, 2026 He has just 36 catches for 434 yards and 2 touchdowns with a sub-50% catch rate, all while his cap number is set to rise to over $38 million . Even if they didn’t win the Super Bowl last season, Nick Emmanwori looks to be a perennial elite defensive player for years to come, whereas Metcalf’s promising and productive start to his career is a distant memory. This is Year 8 for DK and he looks to be cratering. Sometimes the grass isn’t always greener.

title: Why the Seahawks freed up cap space with restructures
summary: The Seattle Seahawks sit at 6-4 and on the outside looking in when it comes to the 2026 NFL playoff picture. Yet, during their Week 12 bye, Seahawks general manager John Schneider kept the team in the headlines by restructuring the contracts of a trio of veteran players in Julian Love, Sam Darnold and Ernest […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Julian Love #20 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts after a play during the second quarter of an NFL divisional playoff football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks sit at 6-4 and on the outside looking in when it comes to the 2026 NFL playoff picture. Yet, during their Week 12 bye, Seahawks general manager John Schneider kept the team in the headlines by restructuring the contracts of a trio of veteran players in Julian Love, Sam Darnold and Ernest Jones. The restructurings created $9.88M of 2026 cap space for Seattle, and fans and observers immediately jumped to try and figure out what the moves meant. Did the team need the space for an impending signing of a big name free agent? Is the team going to extend the recently acquired Quenton Nelson or take care of Zach Charbonnet to prevent losing a starting running back for the second consecutive offseason? Maybe bring in Daniel Jones for the stretch run in case Darnold doesn’t return to 2025 form? Perhaps kick the tires on future former 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk? Well, Field Gulls is here to tell you that the reason for the restructurings is actually far more mundane and far less interesting than any of those potential ideas. For those who don’t wish to read several hundred words on the nuances of salary cap machinations, the simple reason why Seattle restructured those contracts is the exact same reason the team released Deven Eastern Monday and rolled through the bye week with just 52 players on the 53 man roster: The Seahawks were in danger of running out of cap space. To understand why the Seahawks were in danger of running out of cap space requires taking a step back and looking at the 2026 salary cap situation prior to the restructure. According to the only NFL salary cap site fans should ever peruse, OverTheCap.com, Seattle currently has $13,393,989 in available cap space after the restructures. Since the restructures created $9,880,000 of cap space, prior to the moves the team was sitting at just $3,513,989 of cap space. That’s certainly not an amount that represents an immediate threat to going negative, but between several factors it’s an amount that could quickly dwindle. The first and most prevalent item that could, and at some point in the coming weeks almost certainly will put a dent in the cap space available to the franchise is per game roster bonuses. When Seattle signs veteran players to second contracts, they contracts often include per game roster bonuses. For example, Julian Love has $680,000 in per game roster bonuses available in his contract for 2026, or $40,000 per game, and the CBA lays out exactly how those per game roster bonuses are accounted for. During the offseason and into the start of the regular season, the number of per game roster bonuses that count against the salary cap is determined by how many games in which the player appeared the prior season. Then, during the year once a player suits up for more games than they did in the prior season, the per game roster bonuses are added to their cap hit the day after the game. In the case of Love, he played in eight games during the 2025 regular season, so eight of the 17 available per game roster bonuses were included in his cap hit during the offseason and through Week 9. Then in Week 10 Love played was active for the ninth time in 2026, and thus a $40,000 per game roster bonus was recognized against the 2026 cap space for Seattle. Now, over the remainder of the regular season each week that Love is active will result in a $40,000 reduction in salary cap space for the Seahawks. Obviously, $40,000 is a number that is much lower than the $3,513,989 of cap space the Seahawks had prior to the restructures, and even should Love play every game through the remainder of the regular season and generate an additional $280,000 in per game roster bonuses, it’s still less than ten percent of the cap space the team had available. Of course, Love is far from the only veteran on the roster and not the only player who has per game roster bonuses available. Taking a peak at the entirety of the roster, here are the veterans with per game roster bonuses in their contracts and the cap impact each could have should they stay healthy for the remainder of the season. Player 2025 Games 2026 Games YTD 2026 Max Per Game Bonus Max Impact Julian Love 8 9 16 $40,000 $280,000 Jarran Reed 13 10 17 $30,000 $120,000 Derick Hall 14 10 17 $60,000 $180,000 Ernest Jones 15 10 17 $50,000 $100,000 Eric Saubert 11 10 17 $20,000 $120,000 DeMarcus Lawrence 16 10 17 $50,000 $50,000 Cooper Kupp 16 10 17 $30,000 $30,000 Total Potential Cap Impact N/A N/A N/A N/A $880,000.00 Certainly the maximum impact is $880,000 remains below the $3,513,989 of space Seattle had prior to the restructures, but it represents a quarter of the space the team had available and it’s not the only per game salary expenses the team will incur over the final seven weeks of the regular season. To that point, members of the practice squad earn between $13,750 and $22,850 per week, unless they are elevated to the gameday roster. When a player is elevated to the gameday roster their pay is bumped to somewhere the league minimum for a player of their experience, which is between $52,059 and $76,471 per game for the 2026 season. That difference between their practice squad salary and their gameday payment comes out of the salary cap, meaning if a team elevates two players per week it uses no less than $76,618 per week of cap space, oftentimes even more. Thus, if the Seahawks elevate two players from the practice squad per game over the final seven games of the season, that’s an additional $536,324 or so that will be taken out of that available cap space. Obviously, even combined $536,324 and $880,000 combined are still less than $3,513,989, so the question becomes where the does the risk of running out of cap space come from. The answer to that question is simple. Injuries. Using the amounts calculated above for the actual impact on the cap would leave the Seahawks with right around $2.1M of cap space left for the 2026 season. Certainly not a small amount, but an amount that would cover somewhere 27 and 40 games of injury replacements. Meaning that while a wave of injuries against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12 that lands four or five members of the roster on injured reserve is certainly extremely unlikely, it’s not out of the realm of possibility. Thus, rather than deal with the potential bean counters running out of beans to count should the roster be suddenly beset by injury when they have to travel to take on the Santa Clara Substation 49ers in Week 12, the Seahawks simply made the decision to go ahead and free up space in advance. That, of course, leads to the question of why they would free up space early, but that’s a different question for a different day.

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers lead grows to 3 games; Seahawks, Rams on bye
summary: That was a statement. The San Francisco 49ers walked into Mexico City on Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings, the defense allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game, and left with a 35-10 win that wasn’t that close. The big story is none other than Brock Purdy. He went 21-of-26 for 255 yards passing, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers in the locker room before the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Commanders 23-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images That was a statement. The San Francisco 49ers walked into Mexico City on Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings, the defense allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game, and left with a 35-10 win that wasn’t that close. The big story is none other than Brock Purdy. He went 21-of-26 for 255 yards passing, 9.8 yards per attempt, three touchdowns, and no interceptions, good for a 146.0 passer rating. This is against the best defense in the league. Brian Flores’ defense lives on pressure, and it got to Purdy once all night. Two of the touchdowns went to George Kittle and the other to Mike Evans, who finished with 109 receiving yards. The one sour note: right tackle Colton McKivitz left with an ankle injury, and Vederian Lowe finished the game. Lowe didn’t play bad at all, but now that he might be taking the starting job, defenses will be writing the book on how to get past him. The Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams are both on a bye, so this recap will be a bit brief. In short, the 49ers’ lead grew from 2.5 games to three. They have tough sledding, starting with the Seahawks in Week 11; if they can win that game, it might be time to start wondering when they can wrap this division thing up. Arizona Cardinals (3-8) Is there a game left on the schedule anyone can see the Arizona Cardinals winning? With rookie quarterback Carson Beck ailing, 40-year-old Josh Johnson, who signed off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad earlier this month, got the start against the Kansas City Chiefs. That makes his, like, 15th different team he started on in his career. Arizona’s lone touchdown, a 2-yard catch by wide receiver Simi Fehoko, came in the second quarter. It’s the only offensive touchdown the Cardinals have scored in three games. I guess you can call this progress, but with all the injuries the Cardinals are sustaining, it’s a matter of them getting out of the season without more injuries to the roster. Of course, the Cardinals defense is always there to pad out Patrick Mahomes’s stats; 324 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to tight end Travis Kelce. And the Sunday Night Football broadcast made sure you knew about it. The Chiefs got more than 400 yards of offense in a 34-7 win. One touchdown in three weeks plus one of the league’s worst defenses adds up to historically bad football, something 49ers fans know all to well, provided they can remember things a decade ago. The Cardinals were never going to be in contention this year, and their coaching is an upgrade over last year. It’s just a matter of time. Onto Week 12 The Rams kick off Thanksgiving week on Wednesday night, hosting the Green Bay Packers (6-4) at Levi’s South SoFi Stadium on Netflix. Green Bay is also coming off a Week 11 bye, so neither side has a rest edge—which is probably why they are playing on a Wednesday to begin with. I can’t believe I’m about to start rooting for the Packers, but here we are. The Seahawks visit Levi’s Stadium on Sunday. 49ers win here would push the lead to four games with six left. Drew Lock has won both starts since Sam Darnold went down. The Seahawks will be starting Darnold against the 49ers. Last time the Seahawks faced the 49ers at Levi’s was 2025’s Great Disappointment, so anything can be better than that. The Cardinals host the Washington Commanders, who were 3-5-1 going into Monday Night Football against the Bengals. Good luck, Cardinals? I mean, that’s all I got there. 1st: San Francisco 49ers ; Next: vs. Seattle Seahawks 2nd: Seattle Seahawks ; Next: at San Francisco 49ers 3rd: Los Angeles Rams ; Next: vs. Green Bay Packers (Netflix Thanksgiving Eve Game) 4th: Arizona Cardinals ; Next: vs. Washington Commanders

full_text: (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have Kirk Cousins’ number. So much so that they made history against the Minnesota Vikings quarterback on Sunday Night Football. Ji’Ayir Brown’s pick-six against Cousins was the second this month against Cousins. Jaden Dugger intercepted Cousins when he was with the Raiders to begin November. According to Sportsradar, Cousins is the first player to throw a pick six versus the same opponent with two teams in the same season. Kirk Cousins threw a pick 6 for #Raiders vs #49ers in Week 9 and for Vikings vs 49ers in Week 11. Per @sportradar , he's first player to throw a pick 6 vs same opponent with 2 teams in same season — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 23, 2026 Cousins was seen shouting at his offensive line on the sideline. He was not a happy camper. After the game, he said, “But it was hard to get explosives consistently today. Usually, when you can get those, that’s how you can score points and sustain drives. It was a little harder to do that today.” Cousins added, “I just think we didn’t finish drives. Certainly, when you don’t convert third downs, that’s how you don’t finish drives. But it felt like there were too many drives where we were moving the football and then stalled out and didn’t get any points.” His pick-six happened on one play. He didn’t see Brown, who baited Cousins to perfection, and that was the ball game after Brown strolled into the end zone. It was deja vu for the 49ers defense: Kirk Cousins has now thrown two pick-sixes to the 49ers this season on two separate teams pic.twitter.com/LvlUxVvfjz — NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) November 23, 2026 During the week, there were some sports talk radio that said Cousins would benefit from playing the 49ers a second time in two weeks. It sure did not play out that way on Sunday night. If anything, the Niners probably want to see Cousins a third time this season.

title: Colton McKivitz done for the year with ankle injury
summary: The dampener on the 49ers’ superb blowout win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night was the ankle injury suffered by starting right tackle Colton McKivitz, who was carted off amid emotional reactions from several teammates. NBC elected not to show replays of a gruesome injury, which has ended a hugely impressive season from McKivitz. […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers' offensive lineman #68 Colton McKivitz leaves the field after an injury during the NFL regular-season football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers at Banorte Stadium in Mexico City on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Yuri CORTEZ / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The dampener on the 49ers’ superb blowout win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night was the ankle injury suffered by starting right tackle Colton McKivitz, who was carted off amid emotional reactions from several teammates. NBC elected not to show replays of a gruesome injury, which has ended a hugely impressive season from McKivitz. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that the 49ers believed McKivitz had suffered a broken and dislocated ankle. And NFL Network and ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reported on Monday that the 49ers’ fears were correct, meaning they will have to turn to backup Vederian Lowe the rest of the way. Speaking in his postgame press conference, Shanahan said: “That was really crushing. Colton’s had an unbelievable year. We care about all of our guys.” Over the last two seasons, McKivitz has established himself as one of the best right tackles in football. As such, his injury stands as the biggest blow the 49ers have suffered this season, and places substantial pressure on veteran Lowe to ensure the drop-off in play at right tackle is not too steep. Behind Lowe, the 49ers may now look to open the practice window for Austen Pleasants, who started the season on injured reserve with a designation to return with a knee injury. Pleasants has previous experience filling in at both tackle spots and now looks to be the leading candidate to take Lowe’s spot as the swing tackle. The challenge for the 49ers will be to ensure McKivitz’s loss does not impact their remarkable offensive efficiency down the stretch as they look to lock up the one seed in the NFC. And running back Christian McCaffrey made it clear they will use an unfortunate turn of events as motivation to maintain their excellent form. “It’s brutal. He’s somebody that’s one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude,” McCaffrey said. “He’s the standard. And we’re going to really miss him. We all love him. We’re praying for him. It’s one of the worst parts about this game, stuff like that. But we love him, and we’re going to play for him at this moment here on out.”

title: Brock Purdy and Mike Evans overwhelm the Vikings in a 49ers blowout win
summary: The matchup featuring Brian Flores against Kyle Shanahan was all everybody talked about leading up to the week. Brock Purdy went 4-for-4 on his first drive with three double-digit gains to Mike Evans, George Kittle, and Deebo Samuel. Kittle caught a touchdown to cap off a 7-play, 72-yard drive that saw the Niners offense move […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The matchup featuring Brian Flores against Kyle Shanahan was all everybody talked about leading up to the week. Brock Purdy went 4-for-4 on his first drive with three double-digit gains to Mike Evans, George Kittle, and Deebo Samuel. Kittle caught a touchdown to cap off a 7-play, 72-yard drive that saw the Niners offense move the ball easily. And just like that, the San Francisco 49ers took an early 7-0 lead over the Minnesota Vikings. On the Niners’ first defensive drive of the game, CJ West made a tackle for loss. But on 3rd and 14, TJ Hockenson “mossed” Upton Stout for a 20-yard gain. After Fred Warner made a tackle for loss, Upton Stout broke up a pass intended for Jauan Jennings, forcing a 55-yard field goal. Will Reichard’s kick was wide left, gifting the 49ers a short field. Evans stumbled on first down. Christian McCaffrey lost two yards on second down. Purdy was sacked on third down, and the offense punted the ball right back to Minnesota in less than two minutes. Minnesota converted a third-down pass against Ephesians Prysock. Deommodore Lenoir came out of the game momentarily, and that was all the Vikings needed. Lenoir might as well have stayed on the sideline, based on his next rep against Justin Jefferson. He gave up an easy 29-yard completion. Nick Bosa followed that with a ticky-tack roughing-the-passer penalty. Aaron Jones ran over Lenoir to cap off a 90-yard drive to tie things at seven. Deebo Samuel returned the kick 33 yards. Purdy did the thing where he runs around and finds a receiver. He connected with Jordan Watkins for 19 yards. A couple of plays later, the Vikings had a free rusher, but Purdy looked the other way and found Evans down the seam for 34 yards. It was the exact type of play you need to make against the Vikings’ defense. Two plays later, Purdy zipped a ball into a tight window to Kittle for a 14-7 lead. The Vikings had another double-digit play drive, holding the ball for over seven minutes. They converted a 3rd & 10, then gained eight yards on 3rd & 9 before picking up a fourth-and-1. Raheem Morris threw a wrinkle on third down, putting Ji’Ayir Brown at dime linebacker. Brown stuck with TJ Hockenson to hold the Vikings to a field goal. That made it 14-10. When you settle for three points against this offense, you’re begging to lose. Purdy found Allen for 17 yards and Evans for 29 yards on the next drive. This came after an injury to Colton McKivitz, who suffered an ankle injury so bad the replay wouldn’t show it. Vederian Lowe replaced McKivitz. The offense overcame a false start by Lowe. Evans made a one-handed catch to put the offense up 21-10. If you walked away during the commercial break, you missed a Ji’Ayir Brown pick-six. He jumped in front of a Cousins throw to increase the lead to 28-10. The worry was how Purdy would hold up against the blitz. Purdy was 10-for-11 against the blitz for 145 yards, with a 13.18 yards per attempt and 0.89 EPA/pass. He was only sacked once in the first half, which might have been the most important number. On third down to begin the second half, Garrett Wallow was at linebacker. Stout was caught covering nobody and allowed Hockenson a first down. Lenoir gave up another big play to Jefferson, but he stuck with it and forced a fumble. So, instead of a potential red zone possession, the 49ers took over at midfield. However, the 49ers offense couldn’t do anything with the good field position, wasting a seven-yard gain on first down. Corliss Waitman’s 46-yard punt pinned the Vikings at the five. The Vikings picked up a couple of first downs, but Marques Sigle batted away a third-down pass to force a punt. The offense was backed up to the 2-yard line. Against the league’s best defense, could the Niners get out of their own end zone? Keenan Allen caught an 8-yard pass on 3rd & 4. Deebo took a reverse for 20 yards. Allen converted his second third down on the drive with a 13-yard catch on 3rd & 9. It was a back-breaking drive that resulted in a 98-yard touchdown, taking over seven minutes off the clock. It was the kind of statement drive you don’t forget. The 49ers made it clear who the NFC’s class was and broke the Vikings’ will to go up 35-10. Brock Purdy went 21-for-26 for 255 yards and three touchdowns. He was only sacked once. You know things are going well when Mac Jones enters the game late in the fourth quarter. Mike Evans went for 100 yards. Keenan Allen had multiple first-down receptions. George Kittle caught two touchdowns. Scoring as often as they did without needing much from Christian McCaffrey is what makes the 49ers unstoppable.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers vs. Vikings live discussion: Are we in for another high-scoring affair?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers average 31.2 points per game. The Minnesota Vikings defense allows just 14 points per game. Minnesota has dictated the pace of play for eight straight games. It’s been a low-possession, low-scoring game in those affairs. It’s hard to imagine a 49ers game being lower-scoring, regardless of the opponent. We just watched […]
full_text: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers average 31.2 points per game. The Minnesota Vikings defense allows just 14 points per game. Minnesota has dictated the pace of play for eight straight games. It’s been a low-possession, low-scoring game in those affairs. It’s hard to imagine a 49ers game being lower-scoring, regardless of the opponent. We just watched them score 38 and 46 points, albeit against two of the worst defenses in the NFL. But Brock Purdy and company got it done without Mike Evans. That won’t be the case on Sunday night against Brian Flores and company. Keenan Allen should help, too. Evans and Allen on third downs. Deebo Samuel and George Kittle on early downs. That makes for a nice mix of pass catchers. The latter two can help in the screen game, while the former can be your 1-on-1 winners. Add in Christian McCaffrey, and you can see why, even against the Vikings, the path for the Niners’ offense would come close to scoring what they do every game. As is the case with most games, this contest should come down to the red zone. Both teams are the best in the business in the red zone. Minnesota has held three above-average offenses to a combined 2-for-7 in the red zone in the past three games. If they can do that to a 49ers offense, they can escape with a victory. Based on everything we’ve seen this season from Kyle Shanahan’s offense inside the 20, the Vikings are a massive regression candidate.

title: 3 49ers-Vikings predictions: It’s all about red zone efficiency
summary: The San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings this weekend, looking to improve their 8-1 record as they get their toughest battle of the season on Sunday Night Football. Playing in Mexico City, the 49ers are considered three-point favorites on FanDuel, and should have Mike Evans back for the first time in a few […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers take on the Minnesota Vikings this weekend, looking to improve their 8-1 record as they get their toughest battle of the season on Sunday Night Football. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Playing in Mexico City, the 49ers are considered three-point favorites on FanDuel , and should have Mike Evans back for the first time in a few weeks as he’s been dealing with Achilles soreness. Last weekend, it was a shootout between two elite offenses, as the 49ers dropped 46 points with Brock Purdy throwing for 389 yards and three touchdowns over the Dallas Cowboys. This weekend, we’re getting the No. 1 offense vs. the No. 1 defense in an NFC heavyweight battle with a ton of implications for the No. 1 seed in the conference. Here are three predictions for the 49ers against the Vikings in Week 11. Niners will effectively stop the run game The Vikings have really struggled to get their run game going with Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones this season. They rank 26th in rush EPA per play and 27th in rushing success rate this season. While a lot of the blame (and deservedly so) was on quarterback play, this team’s run game hasn’t been very functional either. Last week, leading rusher Jordan Mason averaged 3.7 yards per game in a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers, while Aaron Jones averaged 4.3 yards per carry on his 11 rushes. Over the season, the Vikings just haven’t been efficient, averaging four yards per carry. They face a 49ers defense that ranks second in rush EPA per play allowed, and the Niners will be able to play heavier fronts and load the box more against this Minnesota team. The Vikings struggled when they were one-dimensional on offense earlier in the season, and the 49ers have a good chance to make that happen on Sunday night. Quick passing game rules With how much and how effective Minnesota’s blitzing is, this has to be a game to get the ball out quickly for Brock Purdy after the five sacks last week. I’m expecting a healthy dose of Christian McCaffrey. And if the 49ers bring in George Kittle to block and chip more as other teams do, Mike Evans could get peppered with quick targets. Kyle Shanahan will find the mismatches, but this is a game where it feels like Purdy will just have to take what he can get. On the flip side, I’m expecting the same with Kirk Cousins, who has played well this season and shone in his debut with the Vikings last weekend. Cousins has done a good job limiting sacks and getting the ball out this season. I’d expect the same game plan on Sunday night. Red zone efficiency It feels like this game is going to come down to the margins, and one of the biggest ones on Sunday night is the red zone battle. While the Vikings have excelled defensively over almost anybody, this is also an elite 49ers offense that has all its top weapons on Sunday. San Francisco has been elite in the red zone this season, scoring touchdowns at a higher than 82 percent clip. Meanwhile, the Vikings are easily the best red zone defense in the NFL, allowing touchdowns on just 25 percent of chances. On the other side, Minnesota’s offense ranks 27th in red zone touchdown rate, while the 49ers defense is 11th. It feels like touchdowns versus field goals are going to determine the game (as well as who actually hits the field goals). Whoever wins that battle with the opportunities they get feels like the one that’ll come out on top.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Buccaneers Week 11 Top Performers at Detroit Lions
summary: After a week of prep time to tweak an anemic passing offense and get healthy for a second-half desperation push, the Buccaneers still suffered from familiar issues in a 31-21 loss to the Detroit Lions. Dropping to 3-7, the Bucs face a déjà vu moment next week facing a must-win against the division rival (and […]
full_text: After a week of prep time to tweak an anemic passing offense and get healthy for a second-half desperation push, the Buccaneers still suffered from familiar issues in a 31-21 loss to the Detroit Lions. Dropping to 3-7, the Bucs face a déjà vu moment next week facing a must-win against the division rival (and leading) Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football. The last time this season it was truly “must-win,” they pulverized Carolina to the tune of 43-13 in Week 7. It’s probably not reasonable to expect a similar result, but it’s certainly a winnable game and the opener of the team’s easiest stretch of the year. Ultimately, it’s still a deeply flawed team that’s going to live and die week-to-week on the defense being the best version of itself and the run game driving the offense. Hard way to consistently win in the modern NFL. We’ll give some shoutouts and move onto the next one. Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving Even on a down day, Irving still served as the primary driver for the Bucs’ offense. He finished with 21 touches for 100 total yards and a touchdown, but it should’ve been much more if a needless holding penalty from Luke Goedeke didn’t erase an excellent 80-yard home run. Nevertheless, Irving continued his Pro Bowl worthy campaign, and he’ll need to mirror his dominance against the Panthers from last month (106 yards, 2 TDs) to give the Bucs a chance next week. Bucky Irving powers it through for the touchdown TBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jA4eksUBiV — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 Kenny Gainwell continued to be useful in his change-of-pace role, totaling 8 touches for 59 yards. Against a tough run defense in Detroit, both of the team’s top options delivered. Much fewer positive notes for the passing game (unsurprisingly). Baker Mayfield is a complete liability. You can blame the injuries or the coordinator or the receivers, and they all share some blame, but ultimately your $165 million QB shouldn’t be terrified at any remote sign of pressure and be able to execute some basic throws under duress. Mayfield’s pressure-to-sack ratio, which attempts to demonstrate how a quarterback’s sack percentage relates to an offensive line’s pressure allowed rate, was an egregious 36% Sunday. Out of 44 dropbacks, he was pressured only 11 times yet sacked 4 times. Too often the eyes are dropping when the pocket muddies and he attempts to turn into a fullback, and it simply isn’t winning football. He got the ball to rookie Ted Hurst quite a bit, and that was nice to see since Hurst has struggled mightily with drops. He reeled in 5 catches for 56 yards and 2 touchdowns, and hopefully this performance will do well to build the third-rounder’s confidence and take a stronger role in the receiver room. TED HURST OMG pic.twitter.com/7XqqtX0cQA — Pick 6 Pack (@Pick6PackFB) November 22, 2026 Defensive Top Performer: EDGE David Walker Not many highlights to speak of on defense, which held tough for three quarters but ultimately couldn’t remain sturdy against one of the league’s best offenses. Most notably, David Walker continued to be the team’s most reliable pass rusher. Toting one of the highest pressure rates in the entire league despite never starting, Walker recorded his team-leading 5th sack, the only one of the afternoon, when running the hoop on rookie tackle Blake Miller to take down Jared Goff. Perhaps the next coaching staff will let him be a starter next year. David Walker gets to Jared Goff for the sack #WeAreTheKrewe #TBvsDET pic.twitter.com/oUooKl8gLt — False Finish (@FalseFinishHQ) November 22, 2026 Losing Jacob Parrish early to a back injury crippled the secondary, but Zyon McCollum continued to play very well and kept top target Amon-Ra St. Brown quiet most of the afternoon — the latter netted just 5 catches for 37 yards and a touchdown, and his score came on the opposite side of the field with Benjamin Morrison in coverage. Speaking of whom, Morrison got absolutely dogwalked all afternoon long and then left with what must be his 5th 0r 6th hamstring issue since arriving in Tampa last year. If he and Parrish are both out next week, the Bucs could be facing a very dire situation at cornerback. Josiah Trotter continued to be a tackle machine, recording 14 total tackles on the afternoon. The coverage reps can be shaky, but he’s not a liability at least and that’s encouraging to see. A phantom facemask call put a damper on things at the end of the game, but such is life with NFL officiating sometimes. Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin Not much to note here. McLaughlin remained perfect on his kicks for the year, the only kicker in the league to do so. He attempted no field goals but made all three of his extra points, so hurray! McCollum made a nice play on Detroit’s first field goal attempt, jumping over the line to seemingly affect Lions kicker Jake Bates on a missed attempt. After his other excellent special teams play against the Bears, McCollum is making an impact everywhere.

title: Week 11 Game Recap: Bucs fall to 3-7; Behind coaching woes
summary: Knee deep in the midst of one of the most surreal playoff races that imaginable, the Buccaneers would be looking to collect a win against the Detroit Lions in week 11. Can Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and the Bucs’ bodacious defense pull together to upset Dan Campbell’s bunch on the road? First Quarter: It was […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Trevor Nowaske #53 of the Detroit Lions sacks Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Knee deep in the midst of one of the most surreal playoff races that imaginable, the Buccaneers would be looking to collect a win against the Detroit Lions in week 11. Can Bucky Irving, Baker Mayfield, and the Bucs’ bodacious defense pull together to upset Dan Campbell’s bunch on the road? First Quarter: It was Baker Mayfield’s ball first on Sunday and it was his chance to get sacked first— One play, three defenders getting off their blocks, and one sack of Baker Mayfield with a forced fumble to boot. The Bucs stayed in possession only to punt and play defense. Jared Goff’s second pass and first completion of the day took Detroit across midfield, but two batted balls in a three play sequence forced the Lions into a long field attempt and long field goal miss. The Buccaneers’ offense found a few completions, a few third down conversions, and more importantly a bit of their stride. Tampa Bay moved nearly 50 yards to the Detroit 10-yard line before having to make a decision. Facing a fourth and one, Todd Bowles neglected a short field goal opportunity and chose to leave his offense on the field. Zac Robinson opted for Bucky Irving running into traffic and that traffic did more than slow him down, it stopped him. Tampa’s failed fourth down attempt jump started Detroit’s next drive. Second Quarter: 50% of Tampa’s star cornerback tandem would leave the field on Detroit’s second drive and for Todd Bowles’ defense, no Parrish = no good. The Lions tagged Benjamin Morrison for a big play and tagged him again for a touchdown. While Morrison did struggle to fill the Jacob Parrish’s shoes, one of the early death nails for Tampa’s defense though the early moments has been thorough inability to keep the Lions out of third down and one and a subsequent inability to stop Detroit from converting those third downs into first downs. 7-0, Lions. Tampa’s next start was kicked off by a false start— No doubt they had been holding that in, going an entire quarter without one. The Bucs’ next drive no longer featured third down as an unconquerable foe third downs— First down Cade Otton, first down Chris Godwin, however, old habits die hard— All out blitz, sack, punt. With the seems as open as a 7/11 in New York City, Jared Goff picked apart Tampa Bay’s zones all the way into the final two minutes of the half and field goal range. 10-0, Lions. Rocking a bad thumb, a bad foot, and a bad offense Baker Mayfield had a 1:30 from the 35-yard line to cut into the Lions’ lead. One more big scramble from the Buccaneers’ injured quarterback and rare down the field throw to Bucky Irving planted Tampa Bay squarely in Chase McLaughlin’s range. The Buccaneers did not choose to settle, they took a shot at the end zone, trying for six. Baker Mayfield reared back and lofted a beautiful drop into the bucket to Ted Hurst III for a 23-yard touchdown strike. Hurst III’s second grab of the drive gave the Bucs’ a feeling of what could be, in a season where deep passes or a passing game with any consistent at all has been a needle in hay stack, Ted Hurst III’s score before half flashed a glimmer of what it could be if it all ever clicked. 10-7, Detroit. Third Quarter: Following a Detroit punt, the Buccaneers’ offense had the chance to capitalize on their end of half success— They did not. Their drive began with an 80-yard touchdown scamper by Bucky Irving (called back for a Luke Goedeke hold) and ended with a punt. After coming mere moments away from holding a lead over the Detroit Lions, the Bucs were back on defense and still trailing. Once again, no Parrish = no good. Jameson Williams ran by Benjamin Morrison like Ferrari passing a Hyundai at a stop light. Williams’ score gave the Lions their largest lead of the day (10 points)— 17-7, home town team. 8:56 left in the third, down 10, plenty of time to rally— Also plenty of time for a close game to become a rout. In a pinch, the Buccaneers’ offense turned to their backs. Bucky Irving on the ground and Kenny Gainwell through the air maneuvered Zac Robinson’s offense down the field and into the end zone for a second touchdown of the day— Bucky Irving’s score brought the Buccaneers back to whin three. 17-14, team awkwardly dressed like a Carolina Panthers spin off. Fourth Quarter: The game’s final 15 minutes were Detroit’s to start. Tampa’s defense notched their first sack of the day in order to force Detroit into a punt. Pinned deep at the nine, the Bucs needed some Mayfield magic to flip the scoreboard— Somebody might’ve miscalculated the formula on the magic because the Buccaneers finished their drive with a punt, a bad punt at that. Easy does it for the Lions’ offense, smooth sailing into the end zone for another touchdown— 24-14, Lions. With 5:24 remaining in the game, the Bucs found Emeka Egbuka to pick up a first down. That would be the only first down they would earn because Tampa Bay’s offense (in 2026) is to sacks like sand is to a beach. Tampa Bay’s turnover on downs segued into a nice undisciplined brawl (discipline falls on the coach) headed by Vita Vea and the Buccaneer’s weekly collapse was complete— Seven more points for Jahmyr Gibbs, 31-14, not Todd Bowles’ team. A hurt, beat down Baker Mayfield rallied the troops for one last gasp of air. Just under two minutes to go and the Bucs road penalty flags down to the red zone and Ted Hurst III across the goal line. 31-21, Detroit.

full_text: Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers can still make the playoffs. Yes, I’m telling you there’s a chance, however small. The Bucs are now 4-6, and they didn’t do themselves any favors in Week 11 with their 31-21 loss to the Detroit Lions. The Saints had a pretty typical New Orleans Saints performance against the now 8-3 Bears, and the Falcons couldn’t lose this week because they’re on the bye. The Panthers are now 5-5 and have a two-game lead in the NFC South, and now that the Buccaneers, Saints, and Falcons have the same 3-7 record, the Falcons move up to No. 3 because of their head-to-head tiebreaker over New Orleans. The Bucs remain in second place in the division. A Wild Card spot is pretty much off the table considering the weakness of the division, but the Panthers’ two-game lead in the standings isn’t insurmountable. The Bucs currently have +198 odds to make the playoffs, according to our friends at Fanduel Sportsbook , while the Panthers’ odds are +104. summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers return from their bye week Sunday as they take on the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, with some encouraging news surrounding quarterback Baker Mayfield. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo, Mayfield is expected to play despite dealing with a painful foot injury suffered during Tampa Bay’s Week 9 […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looks on before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers return from their bye week Sunday as they take on the Detroit Lions at Ford Field, with some encouraging news surrounding quarterback Baker Mayfield. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo, Mayfield is expected to play despite dealing with a painful foot injury suffered during Tampa Bay’s Week 9 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mayfield, who was listed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report, has reportedly been dealing with plantar fasciitis and spent portions of the bye week in a walking boot. The veteran quarterback returned to practice Thursday and Friday on a limited basis after sitting out Wednesday’s session. While the news surrounding Mayfield is encouraging, Tampa Bay will be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr., who was ruled out Friday with an ankle injury after missing all three practices during the week. The Buccaneers elevated safety J.J. Roberts from the practice squad Saturday to provide additional depth in Winfield’s absence. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also listed as questionable with a knee injury despite returning to full participation Friday but will suit up for the Bucs this afternoon. For Detroit, the Lions will be without center Cade Mays, who was placed on injured reserve Saturday with an ankle injury. The Lions also entered the weekend with several injury concerns in their secondary, including cornerbacks D.J. Reed, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Khalil Dorsey, who were all listed as questionable. Tampa Bay (3-6) will look to snap its losing streak against a Detroit team (7-2) that has won five consecutive games. The Buccaneers and Lions kick off at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX.
